definitions.note: Often written with an accent as « à ». Without the accent, « a » is also the verb form meaning « has » (from « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un a dans ce mot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an A in this word.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary to form compound past tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a déjà fini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has already finished.

definitions.note: Do not confuse with à, which usually means 'to' or 'at'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une voiture rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a red car.

definitions.note: Often used for lowering something physically, or lowering the level/amount of something (e.g., temperature, prices).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veuillez abaisser le volume, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please lower the volume.

definitions.note: Command form (to one person you address as “vous,” or to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abaissez le son, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn down the sound, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’accident, il a vécu un sentiment d’abandon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he lived with a feeling of abandonment.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mainly used in written narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après quelques minutes, il abandonna la recherche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a few minutes, he gave up the search.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il abandonne le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives up on the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils abandonnent le projet après deux mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They abandon the project after two months.

definitions.note: To leave someone/something (a place, an animal, a person) definitively or without care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va abandonner le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to abandon the project.

definitions.note: To stop trying or stop an activity/goal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle refuse d’abandonner malgré les difficultés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She refuses to give up despite the difficulties.

definitions.note: To stop using/maintaining something (a habit, a plan, a method).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont abandonner cette méthode inefficace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to drop this ineffective method.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu abandonnes le projet trop vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re giving up on the project too quickly.

definitions.note: Can be a command (to one person or to a group) or a present-tense form (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abandonnez cette idée !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give up that idea!

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural: used mostly in writing (stories, history), often corresponds to “they abandoned” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la tempête, ils abandonnèrent le bateau sur la plage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, they abandoned the boat on the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a été abandonné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was abandoned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bâtiment abandonné fait peur la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The abandoned building is scary at night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison abandonnée fait peur la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The abandoned house is scary at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les maisons abandonnées sont dangereuses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The abandoned houses are dangerous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’accident, ils se sont sentis abandonnés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, they felt abandoned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la nouvelle, il est resté abasourdi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he stayed stunned.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est restée abasourdie après la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remained stunned after the news.

definitions.native: bring down, knock down, cut down
definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or several people to do it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abattez cet arbre, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please cut down that tree.

definitions.native: to knock down, to bring down
definitions.note: Often used for knocking down a wall/building, or bringing down an animal (hunting) or a plane.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont abattre ce vieux mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to knock down this old wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of « abattre » (often used with « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a abattu l'arbre dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cut down the tree in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who feels very low or discouraged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est abattu depuis la mauvaise nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been downcast since the bad news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les vieux arbres ont été abattus après la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old trees were cut down after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une abeille butine sur les fleurs du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A bee is foraging on the flowers in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup d’abeilles dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of bees in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien aboie toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barks all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chiens aboient quand quelqu’un approche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dogs bark when someone comes close.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le gouvernement veut abolir cette loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government wants to abolish this law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a arrosé les plantes abondamment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She watered the plants abundantly.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nourriture est abondante pendant les fêtes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Food is abundant during the holidays.

definitions.note: Often used with à (e.g., abonné à un service) or as a noun meaning “subscriber.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis abonné à un journal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am subscribed to a newspaper.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis abonnée à ce magazine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am subscribed to this magazine.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « à bord » to mean being on a vehicle/ship/plane.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont déjà à bord, abord du train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are already on board, aboard the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant est bon et abordable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is good and affordable.

definitions.native: to approach, to come up to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau va aborder l’île au lever du soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat will approach the island at sunrise.

definitions.native: to bring up, to address (a topic)
definitions.note: Often used for starting or dealing with a subject in discussion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons aborder ce sujet demain en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to address this topic tomorrow in class.

definitions.note: Past participle of « aborder »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai abordé… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons abordé le sujet hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We brought up the topic yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien aboya toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barked all night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien aboyait toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was barking all night.

definitions.note: Used mainly for dogs (and sometimes figuratively for a person speaking aggressively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien va aboyer toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is going to bark all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a aboyé toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barked all night.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « s'abriter » (to take shelter) or « un abri » (a shelter/covered place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sont mis à l’abri de la pluie sous un arbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took shelter from the rain under a tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète des abricots au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying apricots at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la tempête, les habitants se sont réfugiés dans des abris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the residents took refuge in shelters.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "shelter from" (e.g., "abriter quelqu’un du vent").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet arbre abrite les oiseaux de la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That tree shelters the birds from the rain.

definitions.note: Insulting/derogatory.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est vraiment abruti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s really stupid.

definitions.note: Insulting and rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de faire l’abruti !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop acting like an idiot!

definitions.note: Insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des abrutis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re idiots.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son absence a été remarquée par tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His absence was noticed by everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est absent aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is absent today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est absente aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is absent today.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont absentes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are absent today.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont absents aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are absent today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le silence est absolu dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The silence is absolute in the room.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « absolu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une vérité absolue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an absolute truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as absolument raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are absolutely right.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong “yes” in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu viens demain ? — Absolument !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tomorrow? — Definitely!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette éponge absorbe beaucoup d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sponge absorbs a lot of water.

definitions.note: Past participle of « absorber »; often used with « être » to form the passive (e.g., « est absorbé » = “is absorbed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit est absorbé par les rideaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise is absorbed by the curtains.

definitions.note: Often used with « par » (absorbed in/by something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est complètement absorbée par son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is completely absorbed in her work.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: « abstenez-vous (de + infinitive) ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abstenez-vous de fumer ici, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please refrain from smoking here.

definitions.note: Often used in the reflexive form « s’abstenir (de) » (to abstain/refrain from doing something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais m’abstenir de commenter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to refrain from commenting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une idée assez abstraite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a rather abstract idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une idée absurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an absurd idea.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces arguments sont absurdes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those arguments are absurd.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « abus de confiance » (breach of trust) or « abus de pouvoir » (abuse of power).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet abus est inacceptable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This abuse is unacceptable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il abuse de sa position.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He abuses his position.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + noun/pronoun (e.g., "abuser de" = to abuse/misuse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils abusent de leur pouvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They abuse their power.

definitions.native: to abuse; to misuse; to take advantage (of)
definitions.note: Often used with "de" (abuser de + noun) meaning "to abuse/misuse" or "to take advantage of" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va abuser de ma confiance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to abuse my trust.

definitions.note: Past participle of « abuser ». In informal French, « C’est abusé ! » can mean “that’s crazy/way too much.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s’est sentie abusée par son patron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt abused by her boss.

definitions.note: Often used for physical damage (e.g., clothes, objects), but can also be used more generally (e.g., “ruin” a relationship).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ne faut pas abîmer ce livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You mustn’t damage this book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon téléphone est abîmé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un article académique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an academic article.

definitions.note: Often used to express being overwhelmed by emotion, work, or bad news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis accablé par cette mauvaise nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m overwhelmed by this bad news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime ton accent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your accent.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accepta la proposition sans hésiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepted the proposal without hesitating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette solution est acceptable pour tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is acceptable for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accepte mon invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepts my invitation.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present (they accept).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils acceptent notre invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accept our invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais accepter votre invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to accept your invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle acceptera notre proposition demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will accept our proposal tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « accepter » used with « tu » (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pourquoi acceptes-tu cette offre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you accepting this offer?

definitions.note: Used with "vous" (formal singular or plural "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acceptez-vous cette proposition ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you accept this proposal?

definitions.note: Present tense; can also be used as an invitation/suggestion (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acceptons les règles et avançons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s accept the rules and move forward.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai accepté l’offre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accepted the offer.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été acceptée à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was accepted to the university.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « accepter »; used with « être » in passive voice or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont acceptés dans cette école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are accepted at this school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gare est accessible à pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train station is accessible on foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est accessible aux débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is easy for beginners to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu un accident sur l'autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was an accident on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai supprimé le fichier accidentellement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accidentally deleted the file.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a souvent des accidents sur cette route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are often accidents on this road.

definitions.note: Past simple (literary) form; in everyday speech, French usually uses the passé composé instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand le chanteur entra sur scène, les fans acclamèrent très fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the singer came on stage, the fans cheered very loudly.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accompagnait sa sœur à l’école tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accompanied his sister to school every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle accompagne son ami à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanies her friend to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais t’accompagner à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to accompany you to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un agent de sécurité va accompagner les visiteurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A security guard is going to escort the visitors.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like helping or guiding someone through a project, change, or difficult period.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va accompagner son fils dans ses études.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to support her son in his studies.

definitions.note: Most often used with "tu" (present tense): "tu accompagnes" = "you accompany".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu accompagnes ta sœur à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You accompany your sister to school.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous accompagnez votre ami à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You accompany your friend to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est accompagné de sa sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is accompanied by his sister.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « accompagner »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est accompagnée de son frère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is accompanied by her brother.

definitions.note: past participle of « accomplir »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai accompli ma mission.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completed my mission.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle veut accomplir ses objectifs cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to accomplish her goals this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons trouvé un accord.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur accorda plus de temps aux étudiants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher granted the students more time.

definitions.note: Often used with musical instruments (e.g., accorder une guitare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avant le concert, il accorda sa guitare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the concert, he tuned his guitar.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur accordait plus de temps aux élèves qui en avaient besoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher used to give more time to the students who needed it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur accorde plus de temps aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher gives the students more time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accorde sa guitare avant le concert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tunes his guitar before the concert.

definitions.note: Often used with things like permission, time, or a favor (e.g., accorder la permission / du temps).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le directeur va accorder deux jours de congé à notre équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director is going to grant two days off to our team.

definitions.note: Used for tuning musical instruments (e.g., accorder une guitare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avant le concert, je vais accorder la guitare dans les coulisses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the concert, I'm going to tune the guitar backstage.

definitions.note: Formal/plural “you” form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accordez-vous quelques minutes pour réfléchir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give yourself a few minutes to think.

definitions.note: Formal/plural “you” form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accordez vos violons avant le concert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tune your violins before the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont signé deux accords importants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They signed two important agreements.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur m’a accordé plus de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher granted me more time.

definitions.note: Used especially for musical instruments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le piano est accordé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The piano is tuned.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « accorder »; often used in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une autorisation lui a été accordée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A permission was granted to her.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « accorder »; used for musical instruments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guitare est bien accordée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitar is well tuned.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of « accorder » (often used with « être » or to agree with a direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des bourses ont été accordées aux meilleurs étudiants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scholarships were granted to the best students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les points ont été accordés aux gagnants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The points were awarded to the winners.

definitions.note: used for a person (or animal) giving birth
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle accouche à l’hôpital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is giving birth at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va accoucher demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to give birth tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a accouché hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave birth yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est accro aux jeux vidéo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s hooked on video games.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accrocha son manteau au porte-manteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hung up his coat on the coat rack.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au dernier moment, il accrocha la corde et évita de tomber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the last moment, he grabbed onto the rope and avoided falling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il accroche son manteau au porte-manteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hangs up his coat on the coat rack.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux accrocher ton manteau ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can hang your coat here.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively: something “hooks” you (a story, a film, a detail).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film va t’accrocher dès la première scène.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie will hook you from the first scene.

definitions.note: Command (vous form); can also be used as “hold on” (on the phone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accrochez vos manteaux au porte-manteau, s’il vous plaît.
