definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whatever may happen, we will stay united.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre équipe a battu son adversaire en finale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team beat its opponent in the final.

definitions.note: Formal/literary; often used in fixed phrases like « quoi qu’il advienne » (“whatever happens”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Personne ne sait ce qui adviendra demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one knows what will happen tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in the general sense of “thing” or “issue” in everyday speech (e.g., une affaire importante).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une affaire importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important matter.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in set phrases like "les affaires" (business affairs, matters) or "des affaires" (things, belongings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois régler mes affaires avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of my affairs before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la randonnée, je suis affamé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, I’m starving.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun or subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la randonnée, elle est affamée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, she is starving.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la randonnée, nous étions affamés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, we were starving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit affecte ma concentration.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise affects my concentration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette décision va affecter beaucoup de personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision is going to affect a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette décision affectera beaucoup de personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision will affect a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il lui montre beaucoup d’affection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shows her a lot of affection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nouvelle l’a beaucoup affecté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news affected him a lot.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” (e.g., affecté à un service / à une ville) to mean assigned to a post, department, or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été affecté à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was assigned to Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’écran affiche la température.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The screen displays the temperature.

definitions.note: Often used for putting a notice or poster in a public place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il affiche une annonce sur le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts up a notice on the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des affiches dans le couloir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are posters in the hallway.

definitions.note: Often used to confirm something (e.g., in a formal tone, on the phone, or in radio communication).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Vous avez bien reçu le message ? — Affirmatif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Did you receive the message? — Yes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son affirmation est fausse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His statement is false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il affirme qu’il a raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He states that he is right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a affirmé qu’il viendrait demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stated that he would come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « affreux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette histoire est affreuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This story is awful.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify an adjective or adverb (similar to “really” but more negative/strong).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait affreusement froid ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s awfully cold this morning.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something unpleasant or very ugly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est affreux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is awful.

definitions.note: Often used for facing a difficulty, danger, or an opponent (in sports, debates, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle doit affronter un grand défi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to face a big challenge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a affronté le danger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He faced the danger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est africain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is African.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « agacer » (e.g., il/elle/on agace).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bruit m'agace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise annoys me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis agacé par ce bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by that noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bruit est vraiment agaçant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is really annoying.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette musique est agaçante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This music is annoying.

definitions.note: French normally uses a circumflex: « âge ». Here we use « age » to match the exact spelling you requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel age as-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How old are you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille dans une agence de voyages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in a travel agency.

definitions.note: In French, it commonly means a diary/planner (where you write appointments), not a political “agenda.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai noté le rendez-vous dans mon agenda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote the appointment down in my planner.

definitions.note: Often used for an agent representing someone (e.g., a literary agent or real estate agent), or a law enforcement agent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon agent m'a trouvé un nouvel appartement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My agent found me a new apartment.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « agent »; used for a woman (e.g., a police agent, a sales agent, a travel agent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’agente de police contrôle la circulation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer is directing traffic.

definitions.note: Plural form of « agent » (a person who acts for an organization, e.g., a representative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les agents de police sont arrivés rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officers arrived quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pluie aggrave la situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain worsens the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son état s'est aggravé pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His condition worsened during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a agi rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He acted quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with prepositions like “agir de” (to be about) or “agir sur” (to act on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut agir vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to act quickly.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « agir » (used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu agis vite quand il y a un problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You act quickly when there is a problem.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il agissait comme si tout était normal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was acting as if everything were normal.

definitions.note: third-person plural present (ils/elles) of « agir »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils agissent rapidement pour résoudre le problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They act quickly to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used when speaking to one person formally or to a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agissez vite, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Act quickly, please.

definitions.note: First-person plural present of "agir"; often used to suggest doing something together ("Let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agissons maintenant pour protéger la planète.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s act now to protect the planet.

definitions.note: Usually used with "il/elle" (he/she/it) as the 3rd person singular of "agir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il agit vite en cas d’urgence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He acts quickly in case of an emergency.

definitions.note: Present participle of « agiter »; often used after « en » to mean “by/while (doing something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parlait en agitant les mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was talking while waving his hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup d’agitation dans la rue ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of agitation in the street tonight.

definitions.native: to shake; to wave; to agitate
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va agiter la main pour dire bonjour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to wave her hand to say hello.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le café, je me sens agité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the coffee, I feel restless.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est agitée depuis ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been restless since this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À Pâques, nous mangeons de l’agneau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At Easter, we eat lamb.

definitions.note: Plural of « agneau ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les agneaux sont dans le pré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lambs are in the meadow.

definitions.note: Often means someone is dying (literally or figuratively) and suffering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vieux chien agonise depuis ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old dog has been dying since this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux me passer l’agrafeuse, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the stapler, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté l’agresseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the attacker.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il devient agressif quand il est stressé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He becomes aggressive when he is stressed.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces commentaires sont agressifs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These comments are aggressive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été victime d’une agression dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was the victim of an assault in the street.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « agressif ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un ton agressif et une attitude agressive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an aggressive tone and an aggressive attitude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été agressé dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was attacked in the street.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « agresser ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s'est sentie agressée dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt attacked in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon oncle est agriculteur et il travaille dans les champs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a farmer and he works in the fields.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les agriculteurs travaillent tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Farmers work early in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un endroit agréable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a pleasant place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons été agréablement surpris par la qualité du service.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the service.

definitions.note: Used to show realization, surprise, understanding, or mild emotion depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ah, je comprends maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ah, I understand now.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary form of « avoir » with many verbs in the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déjà mangé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already eaten.

definitions.note: Most often used with « j’ »: « j’ai » = “I have.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deux frères.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) of « aider », used mostly in writing (e.g., stories).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aida son ami à porter les valises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped his friend carry the suitcases.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing), 3rd person plural (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils aidaient leur voisin tous les week-ends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were helping their neighbor every weekend.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), describing an ongoing or habitual action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, il m’aidait avec mes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he used to help me with my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aide son frère avec ses devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She helps her brother with his homework.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural present tense of « aider ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils aident leurs voisins à porter les sacs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They help their neighbors carry the bags.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux m’aider avec mes devoirs ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with my homework?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aidera son frère avec ses devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will help her brother with his homework.

definitions.note: First person singular simple future ("I will help").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’aiderai demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will help you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional present (used for hypotheticals, polite requests, or reported speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aiderait son frère si on le lui demandait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would help his brother if he were asked.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present (tu) of « aider ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu m’aides avec mes devoirs ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you helping me with my homework?

definitions.note: Formal/plural “you” form (used with vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: S'il vous plaît, aidez-moi à porter ces sacs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please help me carry these bags.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (vous) of « aider »; mostly found in formal/literary French (often replaced by the present subjunctive « que vous aidiez » in modern usage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous aidiez votre sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to help your sister.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("nous") form, commonly used as a suggestion ("Let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aidons notre voisin à porter ses sacs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s help our neighbor carry his bags.

definitions.note: Past participle of "aider"; used with "avoir" or "être" (in passive voice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m’a aidé à porter les sacs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped me carry the bags.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « aider » (used with « avoir »; agrees with a preceding feminine direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai aidée à faire ses devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I helped her do her homework.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles ont été aidées par leurs amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were helped by their friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été aidés par leurs voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were helped by their neighbors.

definitions.note: Used with que + subjunctive (e.g., « il faut que… ») or as the imperative form meaning “have”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que j’aie terminé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Used as the imperative (command) form of « avoir » addressed to one person (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aie confiance en toi !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have confidence in yourself!

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form compound tenses (subjunctive form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu'ils aient fini avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They need to have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’ils aient le temps de finir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They need to have time to finish.

definitions.note: Used with "que" after expressions that trigger the subjunctive (e.g., "il faut que", "je veux que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu aies fini avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present subjunctive of « avoir »; often used after « il faut que », « pour que », etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu aies un billet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to have a ticket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un aigle vole très haut dans le ciel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An eagle flies very high in the sky.

definitions.note: Often used for tastes and smells (e.g., vinegar, lemon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce citron est trop aigre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This lemon is too sour.

definitions.note: Can describe a sharp, unpleasant tone of voice or comment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a répondu d’un ton aigre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replied in a bitter tone.

definitions.note: Often used for high-pitched sounds (e.g., a high note) or for sudden intense pain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une douleur aiguë au dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a sharp pain in my back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une aiguille pour recoudre ce bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a needle to sew this button back on.

definitions.note: Plural form of « aiguille ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des aiguilles pour coudre un bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought needles to sew on a button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai aiguisé le couteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sharpened the knife.

definitions.note: Often used for a sharp edge (knife) or a sharp mind/sense of observation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce couteau est très aiguisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: feminine form of « aigu »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une douleur aiguë au dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a sharp pain in her back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'oiseau a une aile blessée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird has an injured wing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’oiseau a de grandes ailes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird has big wings.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « aller », used after expressions of necessity, desire, doubt, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que j’aille à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go to school.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of « aller », often used after « que » (e.g., « il faut que… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu'ils aillent au travail demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have to go to work tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used after « que » with « tu » (present subjunctive of « aller »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu ailles à l’école demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to go to school tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déjà vu ce film ailleurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already seen this movie elsewhere.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past); most often found in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aima cette ville dès le premier jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He loved that city from the very first day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le serveur est très aimable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter is very kind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont très aimables avec les voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very kind to the neighbors.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third-person plural): “they” (or formal “you” plural) in the past, often for ongoing or habitual actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand ils étaient enfants, ils aimaient jouer dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were children, they loved (used to love) playing outside.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated actions or descriptions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais enfant, j’aimais beaucoup les histoires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I really liked stories.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), often used for habitual actions or ongoing states in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il était enfant, il aimait les histoires avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was a child, he liked stories before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person (especially a parent or partner): « un père aimant », « une mère aimante ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un père aimant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a loving father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis l’aimant sur le frigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the magnet on the fridge.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette fermeture aimante tient très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This magnetic clasp holds very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté deux aimants pour accrocher les photos au frigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two magnets to stick the photos on the fridge.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « aimer » (used with il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aime le chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes chocolate.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « aimer » used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils aiment la musique française.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They like French music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais aimer ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to like this movie.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular): he/she/it will love/like.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aimera ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will like this movie.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future of « aimer » (used with « je »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aimerai ce film, j’en suis sûr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will like this movie, I’m sure of it.

definitions.note: Conditional mood ("they" form): used to express a wish, preference, or polite request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils aimeraient aller en France cet été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would like to go to France this summer.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used to express a wish or polite request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aimerais un café, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used to express a wish, a polite request, or something that would happen under certain conditions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aimerait aller en France un jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would like to go to France one day.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu aimeras ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will like this movie.

definitions.note: Future tense (vous form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aimerez ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will like this movie.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (used for polite requests, wishes, or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aimeriez-vous un café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: Conditional form ("we would..."). Often used to express a polite wish or request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aimerions réserver une table pour deux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like to reserve a table for two.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu aimes ce film ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like this movie?

definitions.note: Present tense form of « aimer » used with « vous » (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aimez le chocolat ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like chocolate?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand vous étiez enfants, vous aimiez jouer dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were children, you liked playing outside.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of « aimer » (literary/very formal; in everyday French, « aimions » is most often the imperfect indicative: « we liked/loved »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que nous aimions ce quartier pour y rester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to like this neighborhood to stay there.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present tense of « aimer » ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aimons ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We like this movie.

definitions.note: Past participle of « aimer » (often used with « avoir » in the passé composé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a aimé ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He liked this movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un professeur très aimé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very well-liked teacher.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « aimer »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est aimée de tous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is loved by everyone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used to describe a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une amie aimée de tous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s a friend loved by everyone.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural feminine) of « aimer »; used with « être » in compound tenses, or to agree with a direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai aimées tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I loved them right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes aimés de tous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are loved by everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fais-le ainsi, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it this way, please.

definitions.note: Usually written with a circumflex: « aîné ». Often used for an older sibling/child.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est l’ainé de la famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is the oldest in the family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’air frais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need fresh air.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like « avoir l’air … » (“to look/seem …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a l’air fatigué aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks tired today.

definitions.note: Plural of « air »: can mean “airs” (attitudes/pretensions) or “tunes/melodies,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se donne des airs importants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on important airs.

definitions.note: Most often used in the expression « à l’aise » (“at ease, comfortable”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me sens plus à l’aise en français maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel more at ease in French now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me lave les aisselles tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my armpits every day.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal/literary way than "facile"; can also describe a person who is well-off depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail est aisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This work is easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il résout ce problème aisément.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He solves this problem easily.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of the auxiliary verb « avoir »; used in constructions like « qu’il/elle ait + past participle ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’il ait fini avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « avoir », used after expressions like « il faut que », « bien que », « pour que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’elle ait son passeport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to have her passport.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mostly in writing (e.g., literature, formal narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ajouta du sel à la soupe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He added salt to the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle ajoute du sucre dans le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adds sugar to the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais ajouter du sucre dans le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to add sugar to the coffee.

definitions.note: Usually used as “you add” when speaking to one person formally (vous), or to more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ajoutez un peu de sel, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a little salt, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai ajouté du sucre dans le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I added sugar to the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ajuste la chaise pour être plus à l'aise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I adjust the chair to be more comfortable.

definitions.note: « al » is not a standard standalone French word in contemporary usage. It most commonly appears as part of proper names (e.g., Arabic-derived names) or as a nonstandard/foreign element. If you meant the French contraction « au » (à + le), note that it is spelled « au », not « al ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le nom « al-Farabi », « al » est un article arabe translittéré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the name “al-Farabi,” “al” is a transliterated Arabic article.

definitions.note: Usually masculine in French: un album.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'écoute cet album tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listen to this album every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne bois pas d’alcool.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t drink alcohol.

definitions.note: Describes someone who is addicted to alcohol; can also describe things related to alcohol (e.g., "boisson alcoolique" = alcoholic drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon oncle est alcoolique et il a besoin d'aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is an alcoholic and he needs help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces alcooliques suivent un programme de soutien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These alcoholics are following a support program.

definitions.note: Usually used with words like « aux alentours » (around) or « dans les alentours » (in the area).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une pharmacie alentour ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there a pharmacy nearby?

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural: « les alentours ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un bon restaurant dans les alentours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a good restaurant in the nearby area.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to warn people of danger or an urgent situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alerte ! Il y a un incendie !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Alert! There’s a fire!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une alerte à la bombe dans la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a bomb alert at the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a été alertée, mais lui, il n’a pas été alerté à temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were alerted, but he wasn’t warned in time.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning “from Algeria”; the feminine form is “algérienne”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est algérien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Algerian.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma voisine est algérienne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Algerian.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont algériens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are Algerian.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les Algériens vivent en Algérie et ailleurs dans le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Algerians live in Algeria and elsewhere in the world.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a un alibi : il était au travail à l’heure du vol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has an alibi: he was at work at the time of the theft.

definitions.note: In everyday French, it can also mean “alien” (from outer space), but a more common word for that is « extraterrestre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet alien vient d'une autre planète.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This alien comes from another planet.

definitions.note: Plural form of « alien ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, des aliens envahissent la Terre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, aliens invade Earth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aligne les chaises contre le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lines up the chairs against the wall.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « industrie alimentaire » (food industry) or « habitudes alimentaires » (dietary habits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a de bonnes habitudes alimentaires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has good eating habits.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts for eating habits (e.g., healthy diet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une alimentation équilibrée est importante pour la santé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A balanced diet is important for health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons acheté des aliments frais au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought fresh food at the market.

definitions.note: Usually used with the verb "être" (e.g., "être alité").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est alité depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been bedridden since yesterday.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a woman or feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis l’opération, elle est alitée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the operation, she has been bedridden.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past), mostly used in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il alla au marché après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went to the market after work.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to talk about something that was going to happen (near future in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils allaient partir quand le téléphone a sonné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were going to leave when the phone rang.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils allaient à l’école à pied tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They used to walk to school every day.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to express the near future in the past (e.g., “j’allais + infinitive” = “I was going to …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’allais partir quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was going to leave when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « aller » (used for ongoing/repeated past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’allais à l’école à pied tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to walk to school every day.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to express the near future in the past (something that was about to happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il allait partir quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was going to leave when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « aller »; often used for ongoing actions in the past or for the near future in the past (e.g., « allait + infinitive »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il allait à l’école tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was going to school every day.

definitions.note: Present participle of « aller »; often used like “while going / when going”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En allant à l’école, je passe devant la boulangerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the way to school, I pass in front of the bakery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprend la langue allemande à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is learning the German language at school.

definitions.note: Usually capitalized in French when it refers to a person (un Allemand) or the language (l’allemand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je parle allemand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak German.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est allemande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is German.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes voisins sont allemands.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are German.

definitions.note: Plural noun; refers to German people (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les Allemands aiment souvent le pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germans often like bread.

definitions.note: Also used with another infinitive to express the near future, like "going to" in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux aller au parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go to the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une allergie aux noix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an allergy to nuts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des allergies au pollen au printemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have allergies to pollen in the spring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis allergique aux noix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m allergic to nuts.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to form the near future (futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous allez partir bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are going to leave soon.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a command to one formal person or to several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous allez à l'école en bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go to school by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les deux pays ont formé une alliance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two countries formed an alliance.

definitions.note: In French, une alliance commonly means a wedding band (distinct from une bague, a ring in general).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte une alliance en or.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wears a gold wedding ring.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to talk about the near future (le futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous alliez partir quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were going to leave when it started to rain.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form) of « aller ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous alliez souvent au marché le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You used to go to the market often on Saturdays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai vu un alligator au zoo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw an alligator at the zoo.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nous). Often used for ongoing actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous étions enfants, nous allions souvent au parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were children, we often went to the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La France est un allié important.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: France is an important ally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pays alliés ont signé un accord.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The allied countries signed an agreement.

definitions.note: Often used to answer the phone; can also be used to get someone's attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allo ? Qui est à l’appareil ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello? Who is speaking?

definitions.note: Can also mean “stretch out” (make something longer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'allonge la jupe de deux centimètres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lengthen the skirt by two centimeters.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), common in written stories and historical narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il allongea la corde pour atteindre le bateau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lengthened the rope to reach the boat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On peut allonger la robe de cinq centimètres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can lengthen the dress by five centimeters.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: s’allonger = to lie down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va allonger le bébé sur le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to lay the baby down on the bed.

definitions.note: Often used with drinks or sauces (e.g., with water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux allonger la sauce avec un peu d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can thin the sauce with a little water.

definitions.note: Command form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allongez-vous sur le canapé, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stretch out on the couch, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chat est allongé sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lying down on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une ombre allongée traverse la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An elongated shadow crosses the street.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est allongée sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lying down on the couch.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fille est allongée sur le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is stretched out on the bed.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to form the near future (le futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to leave now.

definitions.note: Can be used on its own as an invitation/suggestion (like “Let’s go!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allons au parc après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go to the park after school.

definitions.note: Also the “we” form of aller in the present tense (meaning “we go”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons à pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go on foot.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mostly used in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il alluma la lampe et regarda autour de lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lit the lamp and looked around him.

definitions.note: Used for switching on a device (a light, phone, etc.) or lighting something (a candle, a cigarette, a fire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il allume la lumière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turns on the light.

definitions.note: Used for turning on devices (lights, TV, phone) and for lighting a fire/candle/cigarette.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux allumer la lumière, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn on the light, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cherche une allumette pour allumer la bougie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a match to light the candle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a plus d’allumettes dans la boîte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no more matches in the box.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or several people to turn something on/light something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allumez la lumière, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn on the light, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « allumer »; used with « avoir » in compound tenses (e.g., « j’ai allumé… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai allumé la lumière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light.

definitions.note: Often used for something that is switched on (like a light or a screen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le téléphone est allumé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is on.

definitions.note: Informal; used to describe someone who seems a bit crazy or weird.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est un peu allumé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a bit crazy.

definitions.note: Used for something (often a light, lamp, screen, etc.) that is on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lampe est allumée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp is on.

definitions.note: Informal: said about a person (or an idea) to mean a bit crazy/strange.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est complètement allumée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s completely crazy.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les lumières sont allumées dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are on in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Used for things like lights, screens, devices, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les phares sont allumés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The headlights are on.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used to describe people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont un peu allumés, mais très sympas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re a bit crazy, but very nice.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about how fast someone/something is moving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marche à une allure rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walks at a fast pace.

definitions.note: Common in expressions like « avoir de l’allure » (to look good / have style).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe a beaucoup d’allure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress has a lot of style.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « faire allusion à » (“to allude to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait une allusion à son ancien travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made an allusion to his former job.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person plural (“we”). Mostly used in writing and storytelling; in speech, French usually uses the passé composé (“nous sommes allés”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allâmes au village avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went to the village before nightfall.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in writing (stories, history), not in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils allèrent au village après le déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went to the village after lunch.

definitions.note: Past participle of « aller »; commonly used with « être » in the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est allé au cinéma hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went to the movies last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « aller » (used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est allée au cinéma hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went to the movie theater last night.

definitions.note: Often refers to a walkway/driveway lined with trees (like an avenue in a park or garden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se promènent dans l’allée du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are walking along the garden path.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « aller », used with « être » (e.g., « elles sont allées… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont allées au cinéma hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went to the movie theater last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le journaliste enquête sur ces allégations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist is investigating these allegations.

definitions.note: Often used for loyalty to a person, a cause, a country, or a ruler.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a juré allégeance au roi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swore allegiance to the king.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « aller », used with « être » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont allés au cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went to the movie theater.

definitions.note: Used especially when answering the phone (or to get someone’s attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allô ? Qui est à l’appareil ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello? Who is speaking?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'étais étudiant alors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was a student then.

definitions.note: often used at the beginning of a sentence in conversation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alors, tu viens ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So, are you coming?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants apprennent l’alphabet à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children learn the alphabet at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons deux alternatives : partir maintenant ou attendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two alternatives: leave now or wait.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons plusieurs alternatives pour résoudre ce problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have several alternatives to solve this problem.

definitions.note: Used as a title of address for royalty (e.g., ‘Votre Altesse’ = ‘Your Highness’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Votre Altesse, le carrosse est prêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your Highness, the carriage is ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À cette altitude, l’air est plus froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this altitude, the air is colder.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange des amandes au goûter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat almonds for a snack.
