definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought an antique table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont visité des ruines antiques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They visited ancient ruins.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette statue date de l’Antiquité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This statue dates from antiquity.

definitions.note: Plural: items (often old furniture or objects) sold as antiques.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vendent des antiquités au marché aux puces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell antiques at the flea market.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « antécédents médicaux » (medical history) or « antécédents judiciaires » (criminal record).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin note mes antécédents médicaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor notes my medical history.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est anxieuse avant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is anxious before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis anxieux avant l'examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m anxious before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai de l’anxiété avant les examens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have anxiety before exams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le village a été anéanti par l’incendie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village was destroyed by the fire.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « anéantir »; often used figuratively (e.g., emotionally devastated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la nouvelle, elle était anéantie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, she was devastated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En août, beaucoup de Français sont en vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In August, many French people are on vacation.

definitions.note: Often used for suddenly noticing something (sometimes with « s’apercevoir de » = to realize).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais apercevoir quelqu’un dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to notice (catch sight of) someone in the street.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « apparaître » (3rd person plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les étoiles apparaissent quand la nuit tombe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stars appear when night falls.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le soleil apparaît derrière les nuages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun appears behind the clouds.

definitions.note: (also: to show up; to come into view)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une silhouette semble apparaître dans le brouillard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A silhouette seems to appear in the fog.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive or clause to express how something seems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il paraît apparaître plus confiant aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems to appear more confident today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet appareil photo est très cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This camera is very expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les appareils sont éteints.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The devices are turned off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apparemment, le train a du retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently, the train is delayed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son apparence a beaucoup changé cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His appearance has changed a lot this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les apparences peuvent être trompeuses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Appearances can be deceiving.

definitions.note: Often used for people who are related (by family ties), or things that are closely connected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont apparentés par le sang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are related by blood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son apparition a surpris tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His appearance surprised everyone.

definitions.note: Often used for a ghost-like figure or a sudden supernatural sighting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils disent avoir vu une apparition dans le château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say they saw an apparition in the castle.

definitions.note: Informal abbreviation of « appartement ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai trouvé un nouvel appart près du métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a new apartment near the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'habite dans un appartement au troisième étage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in an apartment on the third floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous cherchons des appartements près du métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for apartments near the subway.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing state or habitual situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette maison appartenait à mes grands-parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This house belonged to my grandparents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous appartenez à cette équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You belong to this team.

definitions.note: Usually used with an indirect object: appartenir à + person/thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre va appartenir à Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is going to belong to Marie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces clés appartiennent à mon frère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These keys belong to my brother.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (e.g., "appartenir à quelqu’un").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu m'appartiens !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You belong to me!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre appartient à Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book belongs to Marie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un problème est apparu hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A problem appeared yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « apparaître »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est apparue soudainement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She appeared suddenly.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; in everyday French you more often use the passé composé (a apparu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soudain, un homme apparut dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, a man appeared in the street.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a phone call.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai reçu un appel de mon amie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a call from my friend.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing and storytelling, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il appela son ami dès son arrivée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called his friend as soon as he arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past); can also mean “were named” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais petit, ils m'appelaient tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, they used to call me every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle appelait son amie tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She used to call her friend every evening.

definitions.note: Often used for calling someone (by phone or to get their attention), and for calling/naming something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais t’appeler ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call you tonight.

definitions.note: Used with “vous” (you plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appelez-moi ce soir, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me tonight, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous appeliez souvent vos grands-parents le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You used to call your grandparents often on Sundays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m'appelle tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls me every day.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « appeler », used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils appellent leur ami ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They call their friend tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle t’appellera ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will call you tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’appellerai ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will call you tonight.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form of « appeler » in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu appelles ta mère tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You call your mother every day.

definitions.note: This is a common misspelling of « appelez » (from « appeler »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sur le formulaire, vous avez écrit « appellez » au lieu de « appelez ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, you wrote “appellez” instead of “appelez.”

definitions.note: 1st person plural present ("nous"); often used as an invitation or suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appelons le restaurant pour réserver une table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's call the restaurant to reserve a table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai reçu beaucoup d’appels aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a lot of calls today.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in written storytelling/history.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils appelèrent le médecin immédiatement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called the doctor immediately.

definitions.note: Past participle of « appeler ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a appelé sa mère hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called his mother last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « appeler »; used with « être » or as an adjective (e.g., « Elle est appelée… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est appelée Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is called Marie.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « appeler »; it often agrees with a feminine plural noun (or with a direct object placed before the verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les candidates ont été appelées pour un entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candidates were called for an interview.

definitions.note: Past participle of « appeler »; often agrees in gender/number when used with « être » or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont appelés par le professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are called by the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a applaudi le chanteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He applauded the singer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la chanson, le public va applaudir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the song, the audience is going to applaud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À la fin du spectacle, il y a eu de longs applaudissements.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the show, there was long applause.

definitions.note: Formal/plural "you" form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Applaudissez les artistes, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Applaud the artists, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le public applaudit le chanteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauds the singer.

definitions.note: Often used for software/apps, but can also mean an application (a request/form) for a job, program, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai téléchargé une application pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I downloaded an app to learn French.

definitions.note: Often used for applying something to a surface (e.g., putting on cream, paint).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle applique de la crème sur son visage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She applies (puts on) cream on her face.

definitions.note: Often used with "appliquer quelque chose" (apply something) or "appliquer quelque chose à/sur" (apply something to/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va appliquer de la crème sur son visage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to apply cream to her face.

definitions.note: Used with "vous" (you plural or formal), in the present tense or as a command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appliquez cette crème sur votre visage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apply this cream to your face.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai appliqué la crème sur ma main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I applied the cream on my hand.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a student who works seriously and carefully.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un élève appliqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a hardworking student.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) of « apporter », used mostly in writing and formal storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apporta une bouteille de vin au dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brought a bottle of wine to dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « apporter » (often used meaning to bring something to someone or to a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apporte une bouteille de vin pour le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brings a bottle of wine for dinner.

definitions.note: Often implies bringing something to a place or person (similar to “bring over” or “bring to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux apporter ton passeport, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring your passport, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle apportera le dessert ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will bring the dessert tonight.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of « apporter ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu apportes le dessert ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you bringing dessert tonight?

definitions.note: Command form (vous) or present tense for "you" (plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apportez vos documents, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bring your documents, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « apporter » (used with « avoir » in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai apporté du pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought some bread.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il apprenait le français, il écoutait des podcasts tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was learning French, he listened to podcasts every day.

definitions.note: Present participle of « apprendre »; often used after « en » to mean “while/by learning.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En apprenant le français, tu vas gagner en confiance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By learning French, you’ll gain confidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprend le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He learns French at school.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of « apprendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle apprendra le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will learn French at school.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’apprendrai le français cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will learn French this year.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu apprendras le français avec de la pratique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will learn French with practice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like learning French.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., “apprendre quelque chose à quelqu’un” = to teach someone something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va apprendre la musique aux enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to teach music to the children.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous apprendrez le français plus vite avec de la pratique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will learn French faster with practice.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu apprends le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You learn French at school.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense; also used as a polite singular (formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprenez ces mots pour le test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn these words for the test.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, often used after expressions like « il faut que » or « je veux que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que j'apprenne le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to learn French.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) present tense of « apprendre »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils apprennent le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They learn French at school.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous apprenons le français ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learn French together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est apprenti mécanicien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an apprentice mechanic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai appris la nouvelle ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned the news this morning.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense) of « apprendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprit la nouvelle hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He learned the news yesterday evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le projet a reçu l’approbation du directeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project received the director’s approval.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le train approchait de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train was approaching the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons choisi une approche simple pour résoudre le problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We chose a simple approach to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Can mean someone/something is getting nearer (physically or in time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bus approche de l’arrêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is approaching the stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les oiseaux approchent de la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds are coming closer to the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais approcher de la fenêtre, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to come closer to the window, please.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (to one person you address with « vous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Approchez, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come closer, please.

definitions.native: let's come closer, let's get closer
definitions.note: First-person plural ("nous") form used to make a suggestion ("let's …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Approchons-nous de la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's get closer to the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a fait une analyse approfondie du problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She did an in-depth analysis of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette tenue n’est pas appropriée pour le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This outfit isn’t appropriate for work.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces vêtements sont appropriés pour l’hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These clothes are suitable for winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le directeur va approuver le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director is going to approve the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais approuver ta proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to endorse your proposal.

definitions.native: agree to; accept (a plan, measure, law)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le Parlement doit approuver la loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Parliament must approve the law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le directeur a approuvé le budget.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director approved the budget.

definitions.note: Often used for estimates or not exact information (numbers, times, descriptions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce chiffre est approximatif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This figure is approximate.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes a habitual action or an ongoing state in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il était enfant, il appréciait beaucoup les histoires avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was a child, he really liked stories before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “likes” in everyday French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprécie beaucoup ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He really likes this movie.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils apprécient beaucoup ce restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They really like this restaurant.

definitions.note: Often used for recognizing the value or merits of something/someone; can also mean “to be grateful for.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’apprécie ton aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate your help.

definitions.note: Common in polite/formal contexts to express that you like something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’apprécie ce restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this restaurant.

definitions.native: to assess; to judge; to gauge
definitions.note: Used for evaluating something (often more formal/technical).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut apprécier la situation avant d’agir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to assess the situation before acting.

definitions.note: Often also means “will like” in everyday French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis sûr qu'elle appréciera ce cadeau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sure she'll appreciate this gift.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu apprécies ce film ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like this movie?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espère que vous appréciez ce cadeau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you appreciate this gift.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person plural (“we”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous apprécions beaucoup ce restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We really enjoy this restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai apprécié ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I enjoyed this movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très appréciée par ses collègues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very appreciated by her colleagues.

definitions.note: Past participle used with a feminine plural noun (often with être or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chansons sont très appréciées en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These songs are very appreciated in France.

definitions.note: Often used in police/news contexts to mean someone was arrested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le suspect a été appréhendé hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was arrested last night.

definitions.note: Can describe something you were worried about happening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le moment tant appréhendé est enfin arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The much-dreaded moment has finally arrived.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of help or backing (e.g., moral or political support).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin de ton appui pour ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your support for this project.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., a button) or with "sur" (e.g., appuyer sur un bouton).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il appuie sur le bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He presses the button.

definitions.note: Often used with "sur" to mean leaning/resting on something for support.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle appuie sur le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She leans on the wall.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense) of « appuyer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il appuya sur le bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pressed the button.

definitions.note: Often used with "sur" (appuyer sur) to mean pressing/pushing on something (like a button).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois appuyer sur le bouton, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to press the button, please.

definitions.note: Can mean to support something or to lean on something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va appuyer son dos contre le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to lean his back against the wall.

definitions.note: Often used in instructions as the formal/plural command form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appuyez sur le bouton, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Press the button, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « appuyer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai appuyé sur le bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pressed the button.

definitions.note: Used for fishing or hunting; also figuratively for something used to lure someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pêcheur met un appât sur l’hameçon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman puts bait on the hook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le dîner, nous allons nous promener.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, we are going for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew an ace.

definitions.note: Informal: someone who is very good at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un as en maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s an ace at math.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in the passé composé (tu as + past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as fini tes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have finished your homework.

definitions.note: Form of the verb «avoir» used with «tu» (you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as un stylo ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a pen?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends l’ascenseur jusqu’au cinquième étage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the elevator up to the fifth floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux ascenseurs dans cet immeuble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two elevators in this building.

definitions.note: Noun (plural): refers to people from Asia.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les Asiatiques représentent une grande diversité de cultures et de langues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Asians represent a great diversity of cultures and languages.

definitions.note: Usually refers to protection granted by a country (political asylum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il demande l’asile en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is seeking asylum in France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime cet aspect du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this aspect of the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons discuter des différents aspects du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to discuss the different aspects of the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai passé l'aspirateur dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I vacuumed the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je cours, j’aspire profondément.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I run, I inhale deeply.

definitions.note: Often used with « à »: « aspirer à » + noun/infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aspire à devenir médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She aspires to become a doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à la tête, je vais prendre une aspirine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a headache; I’m going to take an aspirin.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., un regard assassin = a deadly/killer look).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m’a lancé un regard assassin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a killer look.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police cherche l’assassin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for the murderer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police cherche les assassins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for the assassins.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le journaliste a été assassiné hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was assassinated last night.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été assassinée dans son appartement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was murdered in her apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été assassinés pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were murdered during the night.

definitions.note: Often used for an official or formal gathering (e.g., a legislative assembly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’assemblée vote la nouvelle loi demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The assembly votes on the new law tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used as a transitive verb (sit someone down), but it can also be used reflexively: "s’asseoir" = to sit down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur fait asseoir les élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher has the students sit down.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite/plural command, especially with “-vous” (e.g., “Asseyez-vous”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Asseyez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down, please.

definitions.note: Often placed before an adjective/adverb to mean “quite,” and after a verb or amount to mean “enough.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis assez fatigué aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm quite tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille assidûment pour réussir son examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works diligently to pass her exam.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the reflexive pronoun: « assieds-toi » (informal) / « asseyez-vous » (formal or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assieds-toi ici, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down here, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mets la salade dans une assiette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the salad on a plate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons acheté quatre assiettes pour la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought four plates for the kitchen.

definitions.note: Past participle of « asseoir »; often used with « être » (e.g., « je suis assis »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis assis sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used after être: « être assis ». Not related to English “assist.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis assis sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est assise sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « asseoir » (used with être, e.g. « elles sont assises »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont assises sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « assis ». Often used with « être » to describe people who are sitting down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont assises sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sitting on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour votre assistance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Usually means an assistant (a person who helps someone in their work), not the AI tool.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’assistant du professeur prépare la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher’s assistant prepares the classroom.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’assistante du médecin prend les rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor’s assistant schedules the appointments.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (e.g. "assister à un cours" = to attend a class).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il assiste à la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He attends the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g. "assister quelqu’un"), and can sound more formal than "aider".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle assiste son collègue aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She helps her coworker today.

definitions.note: Often used with « assister à » + event (e.g., assister à une réunion). This is a common false friend: it looks like English “assist” but usually means “attend.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais assister à une réunion cet après-midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to attend a meeting this afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: « assister quelqu’un » (more formal than « aider »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin va assister le patient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is going to assist the patient.

definitions.note: Usually used with "à" (e.g., "assister à" = to attend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai assisté à la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I attended the meeting.

definitions.note: Less common than "aider" for "help" in everyday French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai assisté mon ami pendant le déménagement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I helped my friend during the move.

definitions.note: Past participle used as an adjective (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ville est assiégée depuis trois semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city has been besieged for three weeks.

definitions.note: Often used for a nonprofit group/organization (similar to “association” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle fait partie d'une association de quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is part of a neighborhood association.

definitions.note: Often used for a business partner (e.g., in a company or firm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon associé et moi avons créé cette entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My business partner and I created this company.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group). Often used to mean business partners or members/associates of a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les associés signent le contrat demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The partners will sign the contract tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for business partners (e.g., people who own a company together).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes associés et moi avons signé le contrat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My partners and I signed the contract.

definitions.note: Imperative form of the verb « asseoir » used with « tu » (informal singular): « Assieds-toi » can also be written/spoken as « Assois-toi » (familiar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assois-toi et écoute-moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down and listen to me.

definitions.note: Past participle of « assommer »; often used like an adjective to describe someone who is dazed or unconscious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le coup, il est assommé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the blow, he is knocked out.

definitions.note: Less common spelling of « asseyez » (imperative « vous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assoyez-vous, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sit down.

definitions.note: Often means taking responsibility/owning up to something. It does not usually mean “suppose” (that’s more often "supposer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que j’assume mes erreurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take responsibility for my mistakes.

definitions.native: to take responsibility for; to own up to; to accept (the consequences)
definitions.note: Commonly means taking responsibility for something (not just ‘to suppose’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais assumer mes erreurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take responsibility for my mistakes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai une assurance pour ma voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have insurance for my car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle avec assurance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks with confidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons des assurances pour la voiture et la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have insurance for the car and the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il assure la sécurité des enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ensures the children’s safety.

definitions.note: In the insurance sense (to provide insurance coverage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette assurance assure ta voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This insurance policy insures your car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux assurer la sécurité de tous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ensure everyone's safety.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (person) or with “que”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais t’assurer que tout ira bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to reassure you that everything will be fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu m’assures que tout va bien ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You assure me that everything is fine?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous assurez la sécurité des enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You ensure the children’s safety.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce colis est assuré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This package is insured.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un ton assuré quand elle parle en public.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a confident tone when she speaks in public.

definitions.note: Used especially in contexts like insurance (a person or item that is covered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce conducteur assuré a déclaré l’accident à son assureur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This insured driver reported the accident to his insurer.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (past participle), often used with être
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est assurée de réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s sure she’ll succeed.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (past participle), often used with être
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture est assurée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is insured.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très assurée quand elle parle en public.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very confident when she speaks in public.

definitions.note: Fairly formal; often used to emphasize agreement or certainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assurément, c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Certainly, it’s a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère a de l’asthme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother has asthma.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon rêve, c’est de devenir astronaute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dream is to become an astronaut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici une astuce pour apprendre le vocabulaire plus vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here’s a tip for learning vocabulary faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est astucieux et trouve toujours une solution.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is clever and always finds a solution.

definitions.note: Used for an artist’s or craftsperson’s workspace; also used for a workshop class or session (e.g., a writing workshop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille dans un atelier de peinture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in a painting studio.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet athlète s’entraîne tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This athlete trains every day.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces athlètes s’entraînent tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These athletes train every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon oncle est athée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is an atheist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’adore l’atmosphère de ce café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love the atmosphere of this café.

definitions.note: Often used for a strength that helps you succeed in a situation (in everyday speech and in contexts like work, sports, games).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parler anglais est un atout pour trouver un travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speaking English is an asset for finding a job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses atouts sont sa patience et son expérience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His strengths are his patience and his experience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était un crime atroce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an atrocious crime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été atrocement blessé dans l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was atrociously injured in the accident.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; common in writing and stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attacha son vélo devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He attached (tied) his bike in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attache sa ceinture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fastens his seatbelt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux attacher ta ceinture, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you fasten your seat belt, please?

definitions.note: Plural of « attache ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des attaches pour fermer le sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some fasteners to close the bag.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally, or several people, to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attachez votre ceinture, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fasten your seatbelt, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « attacher »; often used with « avoir » to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a attaché son vélo devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fastened his bike in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bouton est attaché à la chemise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The button is attached to the shirt.

definitions.note: Often used with « être attaché à … » to express emotional attachment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très attaché à ma famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very attached to my family.

definitions.note: Can also mean “emotionally attached” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La petite fille est très attachée à sa mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little girl is very attached to her mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’attaque a commencé à l’aube.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attack began at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attaque son adversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He attacks his opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils attaquent le château à l’aube.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They attack the castle at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien va attaquer le facteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is going to attack the mail carrier.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a task or activity (e.g., work, a project).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va attaquer le travail à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to start work at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les attaques ont commencé à l’aube.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attacks started at dawn.

definitions.note: Can also mean “to tackle” a task/problem; here it’s the “you” (plural or formal) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attaquez maintenant !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Attack now!

definitions.note: Present tense (nous form); can also be used as “let’s …” to make a suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attaquons ce problème étape par étape.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s tackle this problem step by step.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a attaqué le facteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacked the mail carrier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été attaquée dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was attacked in the street.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "attaquer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les villes ont été attaquées pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cities were attacked during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été attaqués pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were attacked during the night.

definitions.note: Often used with "être" to mean you’re running late.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Désolé, je suis attardé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I'm running late.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il atteignit le sommet avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reached the summit before nightfall.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in literature; equivalent to “we reached” in everyday English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après trois heures de marche, nous atteignîmes enfin le sommet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After three hours of walking, we finally reached the summit.

definitions.native: will reach, will achieve, will attain
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle atteindra le sommet avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will reach the summit before noon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous voulons atteindre le sommet avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to reach the summit before nightfall.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) future tense of « atteindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous atteindrons le sommet avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will reach the summit before nightfall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il atteint le sommet en une heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reaches the summit in one hour.

definitions.note: Often used with être (e.g., « il est atteint de… ») to talk about being affected by an illness or condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est atteint d’une maladie rare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is affected by a rare disease.

definitions.note: Often used with « atteinte de » to say someone is suffering from an illness or condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est atteinte d'une maladie rare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is suffering from a rare illness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attend le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waits for the bus.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils attendaient le bus depuis vingt minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’attendais devant le cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was waiting for you in front of the movie theater.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of the reflexive verb "s'attendre (à)" (to expect). Often used with "à" + noun/infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je m’attendais à une meilleure note.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was expecting a better grade.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle attendait le bus devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was waiting for the bus in front of the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils attendent le bus devant l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are waiting for the bus in front of the school.

definitions.note: Usually used with “vous” (you, formal/plural) as a command or instruction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attendez ici, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait here.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous attendiez le bus depuis vingt minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

definitions.note: Used in the reflexive form: « s’attendre à » = to expect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vous attendiez à une réponse rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were expecting a quick response.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous attendions le bus sous la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were waiting for the bus in the rain.

definitions.note: From the reflexive verb s’attendre (often used with à): s’attendre à + noun/infinitive = to expect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nous attendions à une mauvaise nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were expecting bad news.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « attendre »; often used in written storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attendit le bus pendant une heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waited for the bus for an hour.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of « attendre » (used with « nous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attendons encore cinq minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s wait five more minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il t’attendra devant le cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will wait for you in front of the movie theater.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of « attendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’attendrai devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will wait for you in front of the train station.

definitions.note: Often a false friend with English “attend” (which usually means “go to”); in French, attendre means “to wait (for)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu attendras ici cinq minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will wait here for five minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais attendre devant le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to wait in front of the café.

definitions.native: to expect (to wait for something to happen)
definitions.note: Often used when you’re waiting for an event, result, or moment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons attendre la réponse du médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to wait for the doctor’s reply.

definitions.note: More formal/literary English equivalent; French usage is common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont attendre l’arrivée du train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to await the train’s arrival.

definitions.note: Often used with “attendre” + direct object or “attendre” + “que”. Not the same as English “attend” (= to go to an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous attendrons le bus devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will wait for the bus in front of the train station.

definitions.note: Often used to tell someone to pause or wait (can be present tense “you wait” or the imperative “wait!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attends-moi une minute !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait for me a minute!

definitions.note: Often used to mean “wait!” / “hold on!” in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attends-moi !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait for me!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai attendu le bus pendant vingt minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for the bus for twenty minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous n'avons pas attendu une réponse si rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We didn’t expect such a quick answer.

definitions.note: Past participle of « attendre » (feminine singular). Often used in passive constructions like « est attendue ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réponse est attendue demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is expected tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les réponses attendues sont arrivées ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The expected answers arrived this morning.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (masculine plural), especially in passive or adjective-like uses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les résultats sont attendus demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The results are expected tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup d’attente à l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of waiting at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des attentes élevées pour ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have high expectations for this project.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in fixed phrases like « salle d’attente » (waiting room).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les attentes à la caisse sont longues aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waits at the checkout are long today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très attentif en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very attentive in class.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves sont attentifs pendant la leçon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are attentive during the lesson.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning (e.g., on signs or to alert someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention ! Il y a une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! There’s a car.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning or to ask people to be careful: « Attention ! » = « Watch out! »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention, il y a une voiture qui arrive !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, there’s a car coming!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un ami attentionné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a thoughtful friend.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « attentif ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très attentive en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very attentive in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écoute attentivement les instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Listen carefully to the instructions.

definitions.note: Past participle of « atterrir ». Commonly used with « être » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion a atterri à 18 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane landed at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Used mainly for planes/helicopters (and also for people/objects that “end up” somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion va atterrir dans dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to land in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Used especially for airplanes (and spacecraft).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’atterrissage a été très doux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The landing was very smooth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion atterrit à 18 h 30.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane lands at 6:30 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used about physical appearance, but can also describe something appealing (an idea, an offer, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une ville très attirante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very attractive city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je trouve cette robe très attirante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find this dress very attractive.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est très attirante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very attractive.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces produits sont très attirants pour les clients.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These products are very attractive to customers.

definitions.note: Often a form of « attirer » meaning “to attract/draw”; it is not related to English “attire” (clothing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette affiche attire beaucoup de monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This poster attracts a lot of people.

definitions.note: Often used for attracting people/attention (attirer l’attention) or physically pulling something toward you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette affiche peut attirer beaucoup de gens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This poster can attract a lot of people.

definitions.note: Past participle of « attirer »; often used with « être » (e.g., « je suis attiré par… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis attiré par la musique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m attracted to music.

definitions.note: Often used with « par » to say what someone is attracted to (e.g., « attiré par … »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis attiré par cette idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am attracted to this idea.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (past participle) of « attirer »; often used with « être » to mean “to be attracted/drawn to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est attirée par la musique classique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is attracted to classical music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont attirés par la musique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are attracted to the music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime ton attitude en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your attitude in class.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form; mostly used in writing (stories, books), not in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attrapa la balle au dernier moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He caught the ball at the last moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attrape le ballon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He catches the ball.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils attrapent le ballon avant qu’il tombe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They catch the ball before it falls.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essaie d’attraper le ballon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to catch the ball.

definitions.note: Command (imperative) or “you” form (plural/formal) of the verb “attraper.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attrapez le ballon !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Catch the ball!

definitions.note: Past participle of « attraper »; used with « avoir » (j’ai attrapé…) or « être » in the passive (il est attrapé…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai attrapé un rhume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught a cold.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of « attraper »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les souris ont été attrapées par le chat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mice were caught by the cat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont déjà attrapés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re already caught.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est très attrayante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very attractive.

definitions.note: Most often used with "à" (e.g., attribuer quelque chose à quelqu’un).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur attribue des points supplémentaires aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher awards extra points to the students.

definitions.note: Past participle of « attribuer ». Often used in passive forms (e.g., « est attribué » = “is assigned/awarded”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix a été attribué à une jeune chercheuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prize was awarded to a young researcher.

definitions.native: to the, at the, in the
definitions.note: Contraction of à + le; used before masculine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais au marché ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the market this morning.

definitions.note: Often used for simple lodging in the countryside; also common in the phrase “auberge de jeunesse” (youth hostel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On passe la nuit dans une auberge près du lac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re spending the night in an inn near the lake.

definitions.note: Usually used with negation (ne...aucun). Can also mean “none” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai aucun argent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any money.

definitions.note: Often used with « ne » in negative sentences (e.g., « Je n’en ai aucun. »). It can also mean “no” before a noun (e.g., « aucun problème »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y en a aucun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There aren’t any.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "aucun"; used before a feminine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle n’a aucune idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has no idea.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « aucun »; it agrees with the noun it refers to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai aucune idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu l’audace de contredire son patron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had the audacity to contradict his boss.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une idée audacieuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a bold idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un choix audacieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a bold choice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa voix est à peine audible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His voice is barely audible.

definitions.note: Also commonly means a formal meeting/hearing (e.g., an audience with a president, a court hearing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le public applaudit à la fin de l’audience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauds at the end of the show.

definitions.note: Used mainly in tech/commerce contexts (e.g., audio equipment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un câble audio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought an audio cable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le cortex auditif traite les sons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The auditory cortex processes sounds.

definitions.note: Often used for actors, dancers, musicians, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle passe une audition demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an audition tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’auditoire écoute attentivement le professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience is listening carefully to the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu une augmentation des prix cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was an increase in prices this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix augmente chaque mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price increases every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prix augmentent chaque année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices increase every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prix vont augmenter cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices are going to increase this year.

definitions.note: Often used for increasing something (like a price, salary, or volume).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chef va augmenter le salaire de ses employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is going to raise his employees' salary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix augmentera l’année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price will increase next year.

definitions.note: Past participle of « augmenter ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix a été augmenté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price was increased.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aujourd'hui, je travaille à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today, I’m working from home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habitais à Lyon auparavant, mais maintenant je vis à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to live in Lyon before, but now I live in Paris.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (auprès de) to mean "near" or "close to" a person or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habite auprès de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live near the school.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (auprès de) to mean being with someone or in their company, especially in more formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis resté auprès de mon ami toute la soirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed with my friend all evening.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun; masculine singular form (used for things, not people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici le document auquel je pensais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is the document I was thinking about.

definitions.note: Auxiliary form of « avoir », used to form compound future tenses (e.g., the future perfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aura fini ses devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will have finished her homework before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aura vingt ans demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will be twenty tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular (je) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, j'aurai plus de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will have more time.

definitions.note: First-person singular (je) in the simple future of «avoir».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, j’aurai plus de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will have more time.

definitions.note: Conditional form used with a past participle to talk about what would have happened (often in reported speech or hypotheticals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils auraient aimé venir, mais ils étaient malades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have liked to come, but they were sick.

definitions.note: Conditional mood, 3rd person plural (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils auraient oublié le rendez-vous sans ton message.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have forgotten the appointment without your message.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "avoir", used as an auxiliary (often to form the conditional past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si j’avais su, j’aurais appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had known, I would have called.

definitions.note: Conditional present form of « avoir »; often used to express a hypothetical past (e.g., « j’aurais aimé… » = “I would have liked…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aurais besoin d’aide, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would need help, please.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the conditional perfect (conditionnel passé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aurait fini plus tôt, mais il était fatigué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would have finished earlier, but he was tired.

definitions.note: Conditional present of « avoir » (used to express a hypothetical or reported past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aurait oublié son rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would have forgotten his appointment.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect ("will have done").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu auras terminé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Future tense of « avoir » (used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu auras le temps demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future form of « avoir »; often used as an auxiliary to form the future perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aurez terminé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will have finished before noon.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aurez besoin de votre passeport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will need your passport.

definitions.note: Conditional present (used as an auxiliary with a past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous auriez dû me prévenir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should have warned me.

definitions.note: Second person plural (vous) conditional present form of « avoir »; often used to form the conditional past (e.g., « vous auriez fait » = « you would have done »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous auriez plus de temps si vous partiez plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would have more time if you left earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aurions fini plus tôt si nous étions partis à l’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have finished earlier if we had left on time.

definitions.note: Conditional present, 1st person plural (nous). Used to talk about something we would have (often in a hypothetical situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aurions plus de temps si le train n'était pas en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have more time if the train weren’t late.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the future perfect (e.g., « nous aurons fait » = « we will have done »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aurons terminé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will have finished before noon.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) future tense of « avoir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous aurons assez de temps demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will have enough time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ils/elles) simple future of « avoir ».
