definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils auront assez de temps demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will have enough time tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime aussi le chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I also like chocolate.

definitions.note: used in comparisons with « que »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est aussi grande que sa sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is as tall as her sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aussitôt, il a compris le problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Immediately, he understood the problem.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons with "que" ("autant que" = "as much/many as").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas autant de temps que toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have as much time as you do.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet auteur a écrit un roman célèbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This author wrote a famous novel.

definitions.note: Plural of « auteur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les auteurs signent leurs livres après la conférence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authors sign their books after the talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce tableau est authentique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting is authentic.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces bijoux sont authentiques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These pieces of jewelry are authentic.

definitions.note: In French it can describe a person with autism; it can also be used more loosely/negatively in some contexts, which can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon cousin est autiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin is autistic.

definitions.note: Informal/short for « automobile ». Common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai garé mon auto devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I parked my car in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends l’autobus tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai demandé un autographe à l’actrice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked the actress for an autograph.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porte est automatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is automatic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porte se ferme automatiquement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door closes automatically.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En automne, les feuilles tombent des arbres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn, the leaves fall from the trees.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun, especially in phrases like « industrie automobile » or « secteur automobile ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il travaille dans l’industrie automobile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works in the automotive industry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon oncle a acheté une automobile neuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle bought a new car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis qu’elle vit seule, elle est plus autonome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since she started living alone, she is more independent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a pratiqué une autopsie pour déterminer la cause de la mort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor performed an autopsy to determine the cause of death.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une autorisation pour entrer dans ce bâtiment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need permission to enter this building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur autorise les étudiants à utiliser un dictionnaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher allows the students to use a dictionary.

definitions.note: Often used to say something is permitted (e.g., « C’est autorisé » = “It’s allowed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes autorisé à entrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are authorized to enter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’accès est autorisé uniquement aux employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Access is authorized only for employees.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « autoriser »; often used with « être » in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ne sont pas autorisés à entrer ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are not allowed to come in here.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ne sont pas autorisés à entrer ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are not authorized to enter here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’autorité a fermé la route après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authority closed the road after the accident.

definitions.note: Plural: can refer to government/public officials or the relevant official bodies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les autorités ont ouvert une enquête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authorities opened an investigation.

definitions.note: In France, this often refers to major high-speed roads, many of which are toll roads (à péage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On prend l’autoroute pour aller à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take the highway to go to Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En France, les autoroutes sont souvent payantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In France, highways are often toll roads.

definitions.note: Often used with de: « autour de » = around, about (a place/thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants courent autour du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are running around the garden.

definitions.note: Often used with « de »: « autour de » = around (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des arbres autour de la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are trees around the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux un autre café, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want another coffee, please.

definitions.note: Often used with an article (e.g., « un autre », « les autres ») to refer to another person or thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux un autre café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want another coffee.

definitions.note: Used to refer to a different person or thing (often with a determiner: "un autre", "l'autre", "d'autres").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux un autre, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want another one, please.

definitions.note: More literary/old-fashioned than "avant"; often used in stories or historical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Autrefois, les gens écrivaient souvent des lettres à la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, people often wrote letters by hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dépêche-toi, autrement on va être en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, otherwise we’re going to be late.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai d’autres questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have other questions.

definitions.note: Plural form (used before a plural noun: « d'autres idées », « les autres personnes »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux voir d'autres options.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see other options.

definitions.note: Plural form of « autre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les autres arrivent demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The others are arriving tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural form of the pronoun « autre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Certains préfèrent le thé, d’autres préfèrent le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some prefer tea, others prefer coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au zoo, nous regardons des autruches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo, we watch ostriches.

definitions.note: Used mainly in set phrases like « autrui » = people other than oneself; it doesn’t take an article (not *l’autrui*).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut respecter autrui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to respect others.

definitions.note: Contraction of à + les; used before plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parle aux enfants après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is speaking to the children after dinner.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "auquel"; used after a plural masculine antecedent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les projets auxquels il participe sont importants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The projects he takes part in are important.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/background past situations or habitual actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils avaient déjà mangé quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had already eaten when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (3rd person plural) of "avoir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils avaient un chien quand ils étaient petits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had a dog when they were little.

definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form of the auxiliary verb « avoir »; used on its own or to form compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’avais déjà fini quand tu es arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already finished when you arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing states/habits in the past, or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais petit, j'avais un chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I had a dog.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of the auxiliary verb « avoir » (used to form compound past tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle avait déjà fini quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had already finished when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form of « avoir » (he/she/it had).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avait un chien quand il était petit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a dog when he was little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avale une pilule avec un verre d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swallows a pill with a glass of water.

definitions.note: literal; also used figuratively (e.g., to swallow one’s pride)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va avaler le comprimé avec un verre d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to swallow the pill with a glass of water.

definitions.note: to swallow quickly, often in large mouthfuls
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la course, elle a dû avaler une grande gorgée d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the race, she had to gulp down a big sip of water.

definitions.native: to swallow up / to take in (a lot)
definitions.note: figurative: to absorb, consume, or “take up” (time, money, distance)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce projet va avaler tout notre budget.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This project is going to swallow up our entire budget.

definitions.note: informal; to eat very quickly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a préféré avaler son déjeuner et retourner travailler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He preferred to scarf down his lunch and go back to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a avalé une pilule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swallowed a pill.

definitions.note: Often used for money given before the full amount is paid (e.g., an advance on salary or a down payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai payé une avance de 200 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid a 200-euro down payment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le projet avance vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is moving forward quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils avancent lentement dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They move forward slowly in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons avancer lentement dans la file d’attente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to move forward slowly in the line.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu avancer la réunion à demain ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you move the meeting up to tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used for progress made, or money paid in advance (an advance payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les travaux ont bien avancé : nous avons déjà fait de grandes avances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The work has gone well: we’ve already made a lot of progress.

definitions.note: Often used as an instruction or request to one person formally (vous), or to several people (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avancez, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move forward, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bus a avancé de quelques mètres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus moved forward a few meters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce cours est avancé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This course is advanced.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective mainly in set phrases like « la partie avant » (the front part) or with vehicle parts (e.g., « roue avant »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La roue avant est crevée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The front tire is flat.

definitions.note: Used before a noun or pronoun to indicate something happens earlier in time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me lave les mains avant le repas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hands before the meal.

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression (e.g., avant midi = before noon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu avant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him before.

definitions.note: Used mainly to refer to the front part of something (especially a boat, vehicle, or building).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'avant du bateau est endommagé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The front of the boat is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu avant-hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him the day before yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet avantage est important pour notre équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This advantage is important for our team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail a plusieurs avantages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job has several advantages.

definitions.note: Often used to criticize someone who doesn’t like spending money or sharing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est avare et ne veut jamais payer sa part.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is stingy and never wants to pay his share.

definitions.note: Often used for a profile picture or a character representing someone online; can also mean a person’s incarnation in a game or virtual world.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai changé mon avatar sur l'application.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my avatar on the app.

definitions.note: Used as a Latin greeting/salute (not a common modern French word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ave, César !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hail, Caesar!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je viens avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux construire un meilleur avenir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to build a better future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils racontent leur aventure en montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tell the story of their adventure in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils racontent leurs aventures de voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tell stories about their travel adventures.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une aversion pour le mensonge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an aversion to lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai averti Paul du danger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I warned Paul about the danger.

definitions.note: Often used with "avertir quelqu’un" (warn someone) or "avertir quelqu’un de" (warn someone about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais t’avertir si le train est en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll let you know if the train is late.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “advertise”; it means “warn,” not “advertise.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’avertis : il va pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m warning you: it’s going to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as reçu un avertissement pour excès de vitesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You received a warning for speeding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a plusieurs avertissements sur l’emballage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several warnings on the packaging.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle avertit son frère quand le train arrive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She warns her brother when the train arrives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est aveugle depuis sa naissance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been blind since birth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont aveugles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are blind.

definitions.note: Often used in legal/police contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les aveux du suspect ont surpris tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect's confessions surprised everyone.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous): used for “you (plural)” and also as the polite/formal “you (singular)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous avez une question ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a question?

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense of « avoir » (used with « vous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous avez une minute ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a minute?

definitions.note: Usually followed by de + noun/infinitive: avide de savoir, avide de nouvelles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est avide de nouvelles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is eager for news.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form); used as an auxiliary to form compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aviez déjà fini quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had already finished when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous aviez déjà un billet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already had a ticket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends l’avion demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking the plane tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les avions décollent à l’heure ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The planes are taking off on time this morning.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the past perfect (plus-que-parfait).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avions déjà terminé quand tu es arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had already finished when you arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect form used with “nous” (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous étions petits, nous avions un chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were little, we had a dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À mon avis, c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my opinion, it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Often used with "aviser quelqu’un" (to notify someone) or "aviser quelqu’un de quelque chose" (to inform someone about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’avise mon collègue du changement d’horaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I inform my coworker about the schedule change.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is practical and makes good judgments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un homme avisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a shrewd man.

definitions.note: Often means “wise” or “shrewd,” not “advised” (a common false friend with English “advised”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très avisée et elle prend toujours son temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very wise and she always takes her time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon avocat me conseille de ne rien dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My lawyer advises me not to say anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange un avocat au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat an avocado for breakfast.

definitions.note: Feminine form; refers to a woman who is a lawyer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon avocate prépare le dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My lawyer is preparing the case file.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les avocats parlent avec leurs clients.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyers are talking with their clients.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète des avocats au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying avocados at the market.

definitions.note: Main verb meaning possession or relationship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux avoir une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to have a car.

definitions.note: Used with many verbs to form compound past tenses; the auxiliary appears as a conjugated form of avoir in real usage, but this example includes the exact infinitive "avoir" as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais avoir mangé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will have eaten before noon.

definitions.native: to have (to do something) / to need to
definitions.note: In expressions like "avoir à" meaning "to have to" or "to be required to."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quelque chose à avoir à faire avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something I have to do before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais avoir une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to have a question.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the passé composé (perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons déjà fini nos devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have already finished our homework.

definitions.note: Present tense (nous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons deux chiens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two dogs.

definitions.note: Usually insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il l’a traité d’avorton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called him a runt.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form, mostly used in writing (e.g., literature, formal narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avoua son erreur au juge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admitted his mistake to the judge.

definitions.note: Used for the present tense and also as the imperative (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’avoue que j’ai peur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admit that I’m scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois t’avouer quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to admit something to you.

definitions.note: Often used to ask someone to be honest or acknowledge something (e.g. « Avouez ! » = “Come on, admit it!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avouez que vous avez oublié.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admit that you forgot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai avoué la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admitted the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon anniversaire est en avril.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in April.

definitions.note: Used mostly in writing as the present participle of « avoir », often to introduce a participle clause (e.g., « Ayant + past participle »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayant fini ses devoirs, elle est sortie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished her homework, she went out.

definitions.note: Present participle of « avoir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayant fini ses devoirs, il regarde un film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished his homework, he’s watching a movie.

definitions.note: Used with “vous” (plural or formal “you”), often as a command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayez terminé avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have it finished before noon.

definitions.note: Formal or plural command form (used with vous); also used in set phrases like « Ayez confiance » (“Have confidence”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayez patience, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have patience, please.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, used after expressions like « il faut que », « pour que », « bien que », etc.; often used as an auxiliary to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que nous ayons fini avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to have finished before noon.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive of « avoir », commonly used to make suggestions (often with « que »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayons un peu de patience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s have a little patience.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « aérer » (used for letting fresh air in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aère la chambre tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I air out the bedroom every morning.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like transport (e.g., “transport aérien” = air transport) or space (e.g., “espace aérien” = airspace).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le transport aérien est rapide, mais souvent cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Air travel is fast, but often expensive.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons pris la ligne aérienne la plus rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the fastest airline route.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les compagnies aériennes proposent des vols directs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Airlines offer direct flights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l’aéroport en taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the airport by taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les aéroports sont très fréquentés pendant les vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Airports are very busy during the holidays.

definitions.note: Often used for the older/eldest sibling or child (e.g., "le frère aîné", "la fille aînée").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère aîné habite à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My older brother lives in Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon aîné est à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My oldest child is at university.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for an older/oldest sister, daughter, or woman in a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon aînée est déjà à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My oldest daughter is already at university.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form of « aîné »; used for a group of female older siblings/children (often in relation to younger ones).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes aînées habitent à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My older sisters live in Lyon.

definitions.note: Plural form; often refers to people older than you, especially in a family or group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons respecter nos aînés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must respect our elders.

definitions.note: An exclamation used to react to sudden pain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aïe ! Je me suis coupé le doigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ow! I cut my finger.

definitions.note: Often indicates direction (to) or location/time (at).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à Paris demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to Paris tomorrow.

definitions.note: the letter "b" (pronounced "bé" in French)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En français, le mot « bonjour » commence par b.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In French, the word "bonjour" starts with B.

definitions.note: Used as the name of the letter; also appears as an abbreviation in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En français, la lettre b se prononce « bé ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In French, the letter b is pronounced “bay.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bébé cherche son baba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is looking for his pacifier.

definitions.note: Often said as « baba au rhum ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au dessert, je prends un baba au rhum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dessert, I’ll have a rum baba.

definitions.note: Often used for a large open container (e.g., a storage bin or a washing tub).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mets les jouets dans le bac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the toys in the bin.

definitions.native: high school diploma, high school final exam
definitions.note: In France, « le bac » is short for « le baccalauréat ». It refers to the final exam and, by extension, the diploma.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle passe le bac cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is taking the high school final exam this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange du bacon au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat bacon for breakfast.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des bactéries sur tes mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are bacteria on your hands.

definitions.note: Often used for an ID badge or name badge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois porter mon badge au travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wear my badge at work.

definitions.note: Plural of « badge ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les badges des employés sont sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees' badges are on the table.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m’a donné une baffe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a slap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je récupère mon bagage sur le tapis roulant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m picking up my luggage from the baggage carousel.

definitions.note: Usually plural in French when talking about your luggage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Où sont mes bagages ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is my luggage?

definitions.note: Usually means a physical fight (a brawl), often informal in tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu une bagarre devant le bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a fight in front of the bar.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: « se bagarrer » = to get into a fight (often a physical fight).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont bagarrer souvent à la sortie de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to brawl often outside the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un bagel au saumon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm having a salmon bagel.

definitions.note: Informal (slang).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai garé ma bagnole devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I parked my car in front of the house.

definitions.note: Usually a piece of jewelry worn on a finger.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il lui a offert une bague en or.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave her a gold ring.

definitions.note: Plural of « bague ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte deux bagues en or.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing two gold rings.

definitions.note: A long, thin loaf of French bread.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais acheter une baguette à la boulangerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to buy a baguette at the bakery.

definitions.note: Plural of « baguette »; in everyday French this most often refers to long French loaves of bread.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète deux baguettes à la boulangerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying two baguettes at the bakery.

definitions.note: Used to show indifference, disbelief, or mild annoyance (similar to “meh” or “bah” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bah, ce n’est pas si important.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Meh, it’s not that important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange une baie rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating a red berry.

definitions.note: Used for a body of water; not to be confused with "bail" in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nous baignons dans une baie calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We swim in a calm bay.

definitions.note: Plural form of « baie ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ajoute des baies dans mon yaourt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I add berries to my yogurt.

definitions.note: Often refers to a swim for pleasure (in the sea, a river, a lake, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va faire une baignade dans la mer cet après-midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to go for a swim in the sea this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il baigne le bébé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bathes the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau bouge beaucoup aujourd’hui.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing or habitual action).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meat is boiled.

definitions.note: Often refers to soft, cooked foods (like baby food) with a mushy texture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fais bouillir de l’eau, s’il te plaît.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le boulanger prépare du pain frais tous les matins.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai encore fait des boulettes au travail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il était bouleversé après la nouvelle.

definitions.note: Informal (everyday spoken French).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a reçu un bouquet de fleurs pour son anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She received a bouquet of flowers for her birthday.

definitions.note: Informal; often means a (usually old or ordinary) book.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a great book at the bookstore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a commandé un bourbon au bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ordered a bourbon at the bar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a mis de la bourre dans le coussin.

definitions.note: Informal; can sound slangy.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bourse a fermé en baisse aujourd'hui.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une boussole pour trouver le nord.

definitions.note: Often used for a small, stylish shop (e.g., clothing, accessories).

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont braves malgré la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are brave despite the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des vaches dans les champs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are cows in the fields.

definitions.note: Borrowed from Japanese (as in “-chan” after a name) in informal/anime fandom contexts; used as an affectionate suffix, not standard French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci, Sakura-chan !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks, Sakura!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai de la chance aujourd'hui !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m lucky today!

definitions.note: Common in expressions like « une chance de + infinitive » (“a chance to…”) and « donner une chance (à quelqu’un) » (“to give (someone) a chance”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai une chance de te revoir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a chance to see you again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for certain high-ranking government or state officials (e.g., Germany’s head of government: le chancelier).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chancelier a annoncé une nouvelle réforme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chancellor announced a new reform.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as de bonnes chances de réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have a good chance of succeeding.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « chanceux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis chanceuse d'avoir une famille gentille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am lucky to have a kind family.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont chanceuses d’avoir un si bon professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are lucky to have such a good teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis chanceux d’avoir des amis comme toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m lucky to have friends like you.

definitions.note: Common in Canadian French; in France, you often hear "pull" for "sweater."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il met son chandail parce qu’il fait froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on his sweater because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’allume une chandelle quand il n’y a plus d’électricité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I light a candle when there’s no more electricity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’allume deux chandelles sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I light two candles on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il change de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changes jobs.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), most common in writing rather than everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il changea de place pour mieux voir la scène.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changed seats to see the stage better.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense form of « changer » (can mean “I was changing” or “you were changing” in informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je changeais de travail quand j’ai déménagé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was changing jobs when I moved.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing, repeated, or background action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il changeait de travail tous les deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changed jobs every two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce changement est important.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This change is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de changements cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of changes this year.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they change).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils changent de voiture chaque année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They change cars every year.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with « nous »; can also be used as an imperative meaning “let’s …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Changeons de sujet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s change the subject.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais changer de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to change jobs.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (il/elle/on) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il changera de travail l’année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will change jobs next year.

definitions.note: Conditional present (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je changerais de travail si je trouvais quelque chose de mieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would change jobs if I found something better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec plus de temps, elle changerait d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With more time, she would change her mind.

definitions.note: Simple future tense (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu changeras d’avis demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will change your mind tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu changes souvent d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You often change your mind.

definitions.note: Used with "vous" (formal singular or plural) and also for commands (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Changez de place, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please change seats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai changé d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my mind.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « changer »; often used with « être » (e.g., « elle est changée »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a changé de travail, et maintenant elle est vraiment changée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She changed jobs, and now she’s really changed.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « changer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les règles ont été changées hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rules were changed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les plans ont été changés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plans have been changed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime cette chanson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime écouter des chansons françaises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like listening to French songs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime ce chant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), most common in writing (stories, literature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il chanta une chanson et tout le monde l’écouta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sang a song and everyone listened to him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été arrêté pour chantage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested for blackmail.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past), 3rd person plural: “they” (or sometimes “you” plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous arrivions, ils chantaient dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrived, they were singing in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je) of « chanter »: used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past or background description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je chantais sous la douche tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sang in the shower every morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past or background situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je suis arrivé, elle chantait dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, she was singing in the kitchen.

definitions.note: present participle (often used like “while singing” or “by singing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En chantant, il se détend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By singing, he relaxes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle chante très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sings very well.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) present tense of « chanter »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils chantent dans la chorale de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sing in the school choir.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime chanter sous la douche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to sing in the shower.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, je chanterai avec la chorale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will sing with the choir.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "chanter" used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu chantes très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sing very well.

definitions.note: Usually a male singer (or used generically); for a female singer, you often see « chanteuse ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce chanteur est très populaire en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This singer is very popular in France.

definitions.note: female singer
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette chanteuse est très célèbre en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This singer is very famous in France.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chantez avec nous !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sing with us!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chantier est fermé aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The construction site is closed today.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense ("vous" form): used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais enfant, vous chantiez souvent le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, you often sang in the evening.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense ("nous"): used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous étions enfants, nous chantions tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were children, we sang every evening.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « chanter » used with « nous »; it can also be used as an invitation meaning “let’s …” (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chantons ensemble !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s sing together!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime ces chants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these songs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai chanté une chanson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sang a song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est le chaos dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's chaos in the street.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaparde a pris mon portefeuille dans le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief took my wallet in the subway.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to congratulate someone or express admiration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chapeau ! Tu as réussi du premier coup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hats off! You succeeded on the first try.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un chapeau noir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a black hat.

definitions.note: Plural of « chapeau ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils portent des chapeaux en hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wear hats in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons visité une petite chapelle près du château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited a small chapel near the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lis un chapitre chaque soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read one chapter every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre a vingt chapitres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book has twenty chapters.

definitions.note: Used with a singular noun (e.g., « chaque jour », « chaque personne »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chaque étudiant a un livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each student has a book.

definitions.note: A military armored vehicle. (Not the same as English “car,” which is “voiture” in French.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un char traverse la ville pendant le défilé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A tank drives through the city during the parade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le charbon est noir et salit les mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Coal is black and it makes your hands dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une grande charge pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a big responsibility for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte une lourde charge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is carrying a heavy load.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: « frais et charges » (fees and charges).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des charges supplémentaires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are additional charges.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il charge les valises dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He loads the suitcases into the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle charge son téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She charges her phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chargement de la page est très lent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The page loading is very slow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va charger les cartons dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to load the boxes into the car.

definitions.note: Often used for charging a phone/device or charging money for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois charger mon téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to charge my phone.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le serveur chargera la page en quelques secondes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The server will load the page in a few seconds.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular): “I will …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je chargerai mon téléphone ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will charge my phone tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for regular costs you have to pay (e.g., rent, utilities, building fees).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les charges sont comprises dans le loyer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The charges are included in the rent.

definitions.note: Can also mean “charge” (e.g., charge a phone) or “accuse/blame,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chargez les valises dans le coffre, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Load the suitcases into the trunk, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « charger »; often used with « être » (e.g., « est chargé » = “is loaded”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le camion est déjà chargé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is already loaded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très chargé aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very busy today.

definitions.note: Often used for something carrying a lot (physically or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le camion est chargé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is loaded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La camionnette est chargée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The van is loaded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une journée très chargée aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a very busy day today.

definitions.note: Often used for something carrying a lot (a bag, a truck, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture est chargée de bagages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is loaded with luggage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les camions sont chargés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trucks are loaded.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "être chargé de" + noun/infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont chargés de l'organisation de l'événement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are in charge of organizing the event.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pousse le chariot dans le supermarché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushes the cart in the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle donne de l’argent à une charité locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gives money to a local charity.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge they don’t really have (especially in medicine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce médecin est un charlatan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That doctor is a quack.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un quartier charmant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a charming neighborhood.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très charmante avec tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very charming with everyone.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont très charmants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very charming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a beaucoup de charme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of charm.

definitions.note: Often refers to the load-bearing wooden/metal structure of a roof or building.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La charpente du toit est en bois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof frame is made of wood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le charpentier répare la charpente du toit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The carpenter is repairing the roof frame.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like "être en charrette" (to be swamped/rushing to meet a deadline).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont chargé le foin dans une charrette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They loaded the hay into a cart.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chars avancent dans la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tanks are moving forward in the city.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais enfant, mon grand-père chassait tous les dimanches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, my grandfather would go hunting every Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chasse est interdite dans cette forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hunting is forbidden in this forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il chasse le dimanche matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hunts on Sunday morning.

definitions.note: Often used with "chasser" + direct object (e.g., chasser quelqu’un/un animal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien chasse les pigeons du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog drives the pigeons out of the garden.

definitions.note: Used with "ils/elles" (they); often appears after expressions that trigger the subjunctive (e.g., "il faut que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’ils chassent les moustiques de la chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have to chase the mosquitoes out of the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aime chasser le sanglier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to hunt wild boar.

definitions.native: to chase away, to drive away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien veut chasser les oiseaux du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog wants to chase the birds away from the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu chasses le lapin dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hunt the rabbit in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu chasses le chat de la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You chase the cat out of the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chasseur marche dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter is walking in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural form of "chasseur".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chasseurs partent tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunters leave early in the morning.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the formal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous chassez le dimanche ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you hunt on Sundays?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le renard a été chassé par les chiens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fox was chased away by the dogs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été chassés du village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were driven out of the village.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cat is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chaton dort sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitten is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chatons jouent dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kittens are playing in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette plume chatouille mon nez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This feather tickles my nose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne va pas chatouiller mes pieds !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t tickle my feet!

definitions.note: Plural of « chat ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux chats dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two cats in the garden.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « chat ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma chatte dort sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My female cat is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.note: Plural of "chatte" (female cat). In informal/slang, "chatte" can be a vulgar term for female genitals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chattes du voisin sont très gentilles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbor’s female cats are very nice.

definitions.note: Used for things that are physically hot or warm (food, drinks, weather, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le café est chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is hot.

definitions.note: Often used with the article (e.g., « le chaud »), especially in expressions like « le chaud et le froid » (“heat and cold”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la randonnée, ils se sont assis au chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, they sat in the warmth.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "chaud".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La soupe est chaude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is hot.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « chaud ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mains sont chaudes après le sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hands are warm after the workout.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaudière est en panne, il n’y a plus d’eau chaude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boiler is broken, there’s no more hot water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sorcière mélange une potion dans un chaudron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witch mixes a potion in a cauldron.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of « chaud »; used to describe masculine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les cafés sont chauds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffees are hot.

definitions.note: Often refers to a building’s heating system or the heat being used (e.g., central heating).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chauffage est en panne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heating is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chauffage chauffe bien aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heating is working well today.

definitions.note: Often used for heating a room, food, or a vehicle (e.g., « chauffer la voiture »).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m heating up water for tea.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drivers are waiting in front of the hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cherche une chaussette propre.

definitions.note: Plural.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought black socks.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my slippers when I get home.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai acheté de nouvelles chaussures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought new shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad is bald.
