definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "commercial".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une offre commerciale intéressante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an interesting commercial offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le commerçant vend des fruits et des légumes au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shopkeeper sells fruit and vegetables at the market.

definitions.note: Usually used with something negative (e.g., a crime, an error).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il commet une erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He commits a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu commets une erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You make a mistake.

definitions.note: Most often used with things like a crime, an offense, or a mistake (e.g., commettre un crime / une erreur).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va commettre une erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to make a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a commis une erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed a mistake.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « commettre », often used for mistakes or crimes; it agrees with a preceding feminine direct object (e.g., « l’erreur… commise »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’erreur qu’elle a commise est grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mistake she committed is serious.

definitions.note: In everyday French, often refers to a police commissioner or an official appointed to oversee a task.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le commissaire interroge les témoins au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commissioner questions the witnesses at the police station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les commissaires ont présenté leur rapport ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commissioners presented their report this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais au commissariat pour déposer une plainte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the police station to file a report.

definitions.note: Often refers to an official committee or group formed for a specific purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une commission étudie la nouvelle loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A commission is studying the new law.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), used mostly in writing/storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il commit une grave erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed a serious mistake.

definitions.note: False friend: in English, “commode” often means a toilet; in French, une commode is furniture with drawers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rangé mes vêtements dans la commode.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put my clothes away in the dresser.

definitions.note: Often used in the fixed phrase « une commotion cérébrale » = a concussion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu une commotion dans la rue après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a commotion in the street after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons un objectif commun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a common goal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette communauté est très accueillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This community is very welcoming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons une passion commune : la musique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a shared passion: music.

definitions.note: In France, a commune is the smallest administrative division (a town or village and its local government).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La commune a construit une nouvelle école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The municipality built a new school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La communication est importante dans une équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communication is important in a team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les communications sont interrompues à cause de la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communications are interrupted because of the storm.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the Christian sacrament (receiving bread and wine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va à la communion dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to Communion on Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je communique avec mon équipe par e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I communicate with my team by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils communiquent par e-mail tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They communicate by email every day.

definitions.note: Often used with "avec" (with) or "à" (to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais communiquer avec mon équipe par e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to communicate with my team by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le communisme a marqué l’histoire de plusieurs pays au XXe siècle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communism shaped the history of several countries in the 20th century.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon grand-père était communiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a communist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce roman, les communistes organisent une réunion dans le quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this novel, the communists organize a meeting in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "commun".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons des intérêts communs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have common interests.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used to talk about gossip as a general thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne supporte pas les commérages au bureau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand gossip at the office.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often means a woman’s romantic partner (girlfriend/wife) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma compagne habite à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My partner lives in Paris.

definitions.note: Often used for a business/company (and also used in fixed expressions like "en compagnie de" = "in the company of").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette compagnie embauche de nouveaux employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company is hiring new employees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces compagnies aériennes proposent des vols moins chers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These airlines offer cheaper flights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon chien est mon compagnon de tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dog is my everyday companion.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic partner (especially someone you live with), without necessarily implying marriage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle vient avec son compagnon ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s coming with her partner tonight.

definitions.note: Plural form of « compagnon »; can refer to people you’re traveling/living/working with, or your partner (especially male).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voyage avec mes compagnons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m traveling with my companions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette comparaison n’est pas juste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This comparison isn’t fair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il compare les prix avant d’acheter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He compares prices before buying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils comparent les prix avant d’acheter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They compare prices before buying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais comparer ces deux offres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to compare these two offers.

definitions.note: Formal/informal: this form is used with "vous" (plural or polite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comparez les deux photos, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compare the two photos, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je laisse ma valise dans le compartiment au-dessus de mon siège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave my suitcase in the compartment above my seat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le train, il y a plusieurs compartiments.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the train, there are several compartments.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai comparé les deux photos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I compared the two photos.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « comparer »; used with « avoir » when the direct object is feminine and comes before the verb, or in passive forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai comparée à l’originale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I compared it to the original.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces deux modèles sont souvent comparés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These two models are often compared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a montré beaucoup de compassion envers les victimes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed a lot of compassion toward the victims.

definitions.note: Often used to express that you feel sorry for someone: « Je compatis (avec toi) ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je compatis avec toi : ça doit être vraiment difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sympathize with you: it must be really difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis fier d’aider mes compatriotes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud to help my fellow citizens.

definitions.native: to compensate, to make up for
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois compenser mon retard en travaillant ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to make up for my delay by working tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dossier est complet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The file is complete.

definitions.note: A masculine noun meaning a (usually men's) suit (jacket and trousers). Not the adjective “complete.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte un complet gris pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s wearing a gray suit for the interview.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les dossiers sont complets.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The files are complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un problème complexe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a complex problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a un complexe à cause de son accent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a complex because of his accent.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with a plural noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces règles sont trop complexes pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These rules are too complex for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’opération, il y a eu des complications.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the operation, there were complications.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est complice dans cette affaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an accomplice in this case.

definitions.note: Often used with "être complice de" (to be involved in / share responsibility for something wrong).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont complices de cette injustice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are complicit in this injustice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté le voleur et son complice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the thief and his accomplice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle m’a fait un compliment sur ma tenue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave me a compliment about my outfit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle reçoit souvent des compliments sur sa robe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She often receives compliments on her dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça complique les choses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That complicates things.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ne faut pas compliquer les choses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must not complicate things.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un problème compliqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a complicated problem.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situation est compliquée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is complicated.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les règles sont compliquées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rules are complicated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces exercices sont compliqués.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These exercises are complicated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a découvert un complot contre le gouvernement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police uncovered a plot against the government.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "complet".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La liste est complète.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The list is complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle complète le formulaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fills out the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis complètement d’accord avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completely agree with you.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les informations sont complètes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The information is complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu compléter ce formulaire, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you fill in this form, please?

definitions.note: Imparfait, 3rd person plural of « comporter » (to include/contain). Used for what things used to include or what they contained in the past.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents included three appendices: a table, a map, and a glossary.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes what something used to include/contain or what it was including at that time.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract included several important clauses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce contrat comporte une clause importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This contract includes an important clause.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail comporte beaucoup de responsabilités.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job involves a lot of responsibilities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son comportement est exemplaire en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior is exemplary in class.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural present of « comporter »; used for what something has/contains/includes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces documents comportent plusieurs pages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These documents include several pages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail comporte beaucoup de responsabilités.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job involves a lot of responsibilities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce prix comportez-il les taxes ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Does this price include taxes?

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « se comporter » (to behave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vous comportez très bien en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You behave very well in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il compose une chanson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He composes a song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va composer une chanson pour son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to compose a song for her friend.

definitions.note: Used especially with a phone number: composer un numéro.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais composer le numéro et attendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to dial the number and wait.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce compositeur a écrit la musique du film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This composer wrote the film’s music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les compositeurs travaillent souvent la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Composers often work at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La composition de cette chanson est magnifique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composition of this song is beautiful.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « être composé de » meaning “to be made up of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mot est composé de trois syllabes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word is made up of three syllables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’équipe est composée de dix personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team is made up of ten people.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je): used for past habitual/ongoing actions or descriptions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne comprenais pas la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for an ongoing state/habit in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais petit, je ne comprenais pas, mais maintenant je comprenait mieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I didn't understand, but now I understood better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle comprend la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understands the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il comprendra la leçon demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will understand the lesson tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future of « comprendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je comprendrai mieux demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will understand better tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional present, 1st person singular (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je comprendrais mieux avec un exemple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would understand better with an example.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (often used for polite requests or to express a hypothesis).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pensais qu’il comprendrait la situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he would understand the situation.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu comprendras quand tu seras plus grand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will understand when you are older.

definitions.note: Infinitive form; used after a conjugated verb or another infinitive (e.g., "Je dois comprendre").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux comprendre la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to understand the question.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous comprendrez mieux après le cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will understand better after the class.

definitions.note: Conditional present, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si vous aviez plus de temps, vous comprendriez mieux la leçon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils comprendront la leçon demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will understand the lesson tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « comprendre » (used with « je » or « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu comprends la question ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.note: Second-person plural present (used with "vous" and sometimes as a polite singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous comprenez la question ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.note: Usually used with « vous » (you) in the imperfect subjunctive; common in formal writing or set phrases like « je voulais que vous compreniez ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voulais que vous compreniez la règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted you to understand the rule.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « comprendre » (used after expressions of doubt, necessity, emotion, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je comprenne la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to understand the question.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils comprennent la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They understand the question.

definitions.note: Used with "tu"; this form is often found in the subjunctive after expressions like « il faut que », « je veux que », « pour que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu comprennes la règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to understand the rule.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense: “we understand.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous comprenons la leçon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We understand the lesson.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a medicine tablet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un comprimé après le repas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a tablet after the meal.

definitions.note: Usually refers to medicine in tablet form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenez deux comprimés avec un verre d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take two tablets with a glass of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai compris la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood the question.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « y compris » (“including”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le petit déjeuner est compris dans le prix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breakfast is included in the price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons trouvé un compromis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found a compromise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ton explication est claire et compréhensible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your explanation is clear and understandable.

definitions.note: Describes someone who shows empathy and is willing to forgive or accept (not “comprehensive”).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour votre compréhension.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your understanding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille dans la comptabilité de l’entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in the company’s accounting department.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon père est comptable dans une grande entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad is an accountant at a big company.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for an ongoing/repeated action in the past.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was counting the coins on the table.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle comptait les pièces sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was counting the coins on the table.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « payer comptant » (to pay cash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je paie comptant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying in cash.

definitions.note: Used when paying immediately with cash (as opposed to by card, check, or on credit).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to pay in cash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comptant jusqu’à dix, il essaie de se calmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Counting to ten, he tries to calm down.

definitions.note: Most often used for a bank account or an online account.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a bank account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je compte jusqu’à dix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I count to ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je compte venir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They count to ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sais compter jusqu’à cent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know how to count up to one hundred.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to leave tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les comptes ne sont pas bons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The calculations aren’t right.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You count to ten.

definitions.note: Usually the counter in a shop, bar, or bank, where you stand to be served.

definitions.note: Usually means “we count” (present tense) in context; it can also be used as an imperative meaning “let’s count.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai compté jusqu’à dix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I counted to ten.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « Le temps est compté » (time is limited).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le temps est compté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time is limited.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « compter ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tous les votes sont comptés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the votes are counted.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « Les jours sont comptés » meaning “the days are numbered.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces points sont comptés dans le total.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These points are counted in the total.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a beaucoup de compétence en informatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of skill in computer science.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a de bonnes compétences en informatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has good computer skills.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très compétente dans son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very competent at her job.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très compétente dans son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very competent at her job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s'entraîne tous les jours pour une compétition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She trains every day for a competition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle participe à plusieurs compétitions cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is taking part in several competitions this year.

definitions.note: A noble title; feminine: « comtesse ». Not the same as the verb « compter » (“to count”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le comte habite dans un château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The count lives in a castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comtesse arrive au château ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The countess is arriving at the castle tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce comté est très rural.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This county is very rural.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to the cheese, especially when talking about food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends 200 grammes de comté, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take 200 grams of Comté, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On peut parfois voir une comète dans le ciel la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can sometimes see a comet in the sky at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On regarde une comédie ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a comedy tonight.

definitions.note: Male form; the female form is « comédienne ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce comédien joue dans un film très connu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This actor acts in a very well-known movie.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar insult in French; avoid in polite conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été vraiment con de dire ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was really stupid to say that.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and insulting in French (a strong swear word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne l’écoute pas, c’est un con.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t listen to him; he’s an idiot.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se concentra sur son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He concentrated on his work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin de concentration pour étudier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need concentration to study.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form: « se concentrer » (to concentrate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me concentre sur mon travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m focusing on my work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'essaie de me concentrer sur mon travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to focus on my work.

definitions.note: Used with "tu" (informal you) in the present tense or in the subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu te concentres sur ton travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You focus on your work.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): said to one person formally or to a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Concentrez-vous sur la leçon, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Focus on the lesson, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce jus d’orange est très concentré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This orange juice is very concentrated.

definitions.note: Describes someone who is paying close attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est concentrée pendant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is focused during the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très concentrée sur son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very focused on her work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces jus sont concentrés, alors ajoute un peu d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These juices are concentrated, so add a little water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce concept est facile à comprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This concept is easy to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le concepteur a créé une nouvelle application.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The designer created a new app.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La conception du nouveau site web est presque terminée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The design of the new website is almost finished.

definitions.note: Often used for the moment a baby is conceived (when a pregnancy begins).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont parlé de la date de conception du bébé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They talked about the baby's date of conception.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Concernant ton dossier, je te réponds demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regarding your file, I’ll get back to you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cela ne me concerne pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That doesn’t concern me.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “involved” or “affected” by a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne me sens pas concerné par ce problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel concerned by this problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va au concert ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the concert tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce mois-ci, il y a beaucoup de concerts dans la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This month, there are a lot of concerts in the city.

definitions.note: In French, often refers to the person who looks after an apartment building and can handle maintenance or residents’ needs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le concierge a réparé la porte d’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The caretaker fixed the front door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai conclu un accord avec eux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reached an agreement with them.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enquête est enfin conclue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigation is finally concluded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous pouvons conclure que cette solution est la meilleure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can conclude that this solution is the best.

definitions.note: Can be used to mean “to decide/determine” after thinking about something (e.g., “I conclude that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je conclus que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I conclude that you are right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En conclusion, je pense que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In conclusion, I think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Plural of « conclusion ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses conclusions sont claires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His conclusions are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je coupe un concombre pour la salade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cutting a cucumber for the salad.

definitions.note: Plural form of « concombre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète des concombres au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying cucumbers at the market.

definitions.note: Often used in a formal context, especially with "avec" (e.g. "concorde avec").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette réponse concorde avec les faits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This answer matches the facts.

definitions.note: Often used for an official competitive exam or selection process (e.g., for schools or jobs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle prépare un concours pour entrer dans une grande école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is preparing for a competitive exam to get into a prestigious school.

definitions.note: Past participle of « concourir », usually used with « avoir » (e.g., « a concouru »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a concouru pour une bourse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She competed for a scholarship.

definitions.note: often historical; refers to a woman in a long-term relationship with a man without being married to him
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans l'Antiquité, il avait une épouse et une concubine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In ancient times, he had a wife and a concubine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise fait face à une forte concurrence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company faces strong competition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos concurrents baissent leurs prix cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our competitors are lowering their prices this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le procureur demande au juge de condamner l'accusé à deux ans de prison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prosecutor asks the judge to sentence the defendant to two years in prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beaucoup de citoyens veulent condamner la violence et les discours de haine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many citizens want to condemn violence and hate speech.

definitions.native: to doom; to make unavoidable (often with à)
definitions.note: Often used with "condamner à" (to doom someone/something to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignorer ce problème, c'est condamner le projet à l'échec.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ignoring this problem is to doom the project to failure.

definitions.note: Past participle of « condamner »; often used with « être » (e.g., « a été condamné ») to mean someone was found guilty and given a sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été condamné à deux ans de prison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to two years in prison.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who has been found guilty in court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est condamné pour vol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is convicted of theft.

definitions.note: Can also mean being officially judged as unacceptable or destined to a bad outcome (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bâtiment est condamné et doit être démoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building is condemned and must be demolished.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette offre est valable sous certaines conditions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This offer is valid under certain conditions.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette aide est conditionnelle à la présentation d’un justificatif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This assistance is conditional on presenting proof.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « conditions générales » (general terms and conditions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’accepte les conditions du contrat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept the terms of the contract.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (mes/tes/ses condoléances).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vous présente mes condoléances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you my condolences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le conducteur s'arrête au feu rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver stops at the red light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les conducteurs doivent respecter les limitations de vitesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drivers must respect the speed limits.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La conductrice conduit prudemment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver drives carefully.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular): “he/she/it will …” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle conduira les enfants à l’école demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will drive the children to school tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular (I) in the simple future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, je conduirai jusqu’à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will drive to Lyon.

definitions.note: Often used for driving a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sais conduire une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know how to drive a car.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « conduire » used with « je » or « tu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je conduis jusqu’à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drive to the school.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils conduisaient trop vite sur l’autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were driving too fast on the highway.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense form (could be “I” or “you” informal, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je conduisais quand tu m'as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was driving when you called me.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past ongoing or habitual action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il pleuvait, elle conduisait très lentement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it was raining, she drove very slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu conduisant sur l’autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him driving on the highway.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (conduisant à...) to mean "leading to" or "resulting in".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette décision, conduisant à plus de travail, n’a pas plu à l’équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision, leading to more work, didn’t please the team.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the present subjunctive (e.g., « que je/tu/il/elle conduise »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je conduise prudemment ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to drive carefully tonight.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « conduire » for « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils conduisent jusqu’à Paris ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are driving to Paris tonight.

definitions.note: Used after « que » in the present subjunctive (e.g., « Je veux que tu conduises... »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux que tu conduises plus lentement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to drive more slowly.

definitions.note: Used with "vous" (formal singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conduisez prudemment, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drive carefully, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mostly used in literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conduisit jusqu’à Paris sans s’arrêter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drove to Paris without stopping.

definitions.note: Verb form of « conduire ». Not the English noun “conduit”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conduit une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drives a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le conduit d’aération est bouché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The air duct is blocked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La conduite en ville demande beaucoup d’attention.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Driving in the city requires a lot of attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son professeur a remarqué sa bonne conduite en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her teacher noticed her good behavior in class.

definitions.note: Past participle of « conduire » (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les camions ont été conduits par des chauffeurs expérimentés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trucks were driven by experienced drivers.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mainly used in written/literary French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pâtissier confectionna un gâteau pour l’anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pastry chef made a cake for the birthday.

definitions.note: Often used for making/producing items (especially clothing) in a careful or artisan way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il confectionne un costume sur mesure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He makes a custom-made suit.

definitions.note: Often used for making something carefully or by hand (e.g., clothing, food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va confectionner une robe pour sa sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to make a dress for her sister.

definitions.note: Past participle of « confectionner »; often used for items that are made (sometimes in a careful or crafted way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sac est confectionné à la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is made by hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je confesse que j’ai oublié ton anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confess that I forgot your birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va confesser la vérité à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to confess the truth to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait une confession à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a confession to the police.

definitions.note: Often used for the Catholic sacrament of confessing sins.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à la confession dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to confession on Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a tout confessé à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed everything to the police.

definitions.note: Usually plural in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y avait des confettis partout après la fête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was confetti everywhere after the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai confiance en toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis confiant avant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am confident before the exam.

definitions.note: Often used either for telling someone something private (confide) or giving someone responsibility for something (entrust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lui confie un secret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confide a secret to him/her.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” + person: confier quelque chose à quelqu’un (to entrust something to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te confier un secret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to entrust you with a secret.

definitions.note: Often used for government-imposed stay-at-home restrictions (especially during the COVID-19 pandemic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant le confinement, beaucoup de gens ont travaillé à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the lockdown, many people worked from home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’attends la confirmation de votre rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waiting for confirmation of your appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je confirme le rendez-vous de demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confirm tomorrow’s appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pouvez-vous confirmer votre adresse, s’il vous plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you confirm your address, please?

definitions.note: Also used to mean “verify” in many contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Confirmez-vous votre réservation ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you confirming your reservation?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a confirmé le diagnostic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor confirmed the diagnosis.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone is skilled/established in something (e.g., un cuisinier confirmé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un joueur confirmé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s an experienced player.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunion est confirmée pour demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is confirmed for tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Used for sweet fruit spreads (often with pieces of fruit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends de la confiture de fraises au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have strawberry jam for breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’ai confié un secret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confided a secret to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le conflit a duré plusieurs années.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conflict lasted several years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il confond souvent les prénoms.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often mixes up the names.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne dois pas confondre les deux dossiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must not mix up the two files.

definitions.note: Often used with « confondre X avec Y ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On ne peut pas confondre le sel avec le sucre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t mistake salt for sugar.

definitions.native: to baffle; to perplex; to throw off
definitions.note: Less literal: to leave someone confused.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette explication risque de confondre les débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This explanation might confuse beginners.

definitions.native: to expose; to catch (someone) out; to prove (someone) guilty/wrong
definitions.note: In the sense of unmasking or showing the truth (e.g., a lie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le témoin a pu confondre le suspect pendant l’interrogatoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness was able to expose the suspect during the interrogation.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « confondre » (used with tu/il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu confonds mon frère et moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You confuse my brother and me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai confondu les deux dates.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mixed up the two dates.

definitions.note: Often used with “se conformer à” (to comply with / conform to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons nous conformer aux règles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must comply with the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après une longue journée, j’ai besoin de confort à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a long day, I need comfort at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce canapé est très confortable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sofa is very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes assis confortablement sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are sitting comfortably on the couch.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaussures sont très confortables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very comfortable.

definitions.note: Often used with a person or issue, or with "à" to mean "confront (someone) with (something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois confronter mon collègue à propos de ce problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to confront my coworker about this problem.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine singular), often used with « être » or adjectivally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est confronté à un problème difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is confronted with a difficult problem.

definitions.note: Usually used with « à »: « confronté à » = confronted/faced with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est confronté à un problème difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is faced with a difficult problem.

definitions.note: Often refers to an organized religious or traditional group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a rejoint une confrérie locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He joined a local brotherhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis confus à propos des règles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am confused about the rules.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « confus ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis confuse, tu peux répéter ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m confused; can you repeat?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu de la confusion pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was confusion during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’assiste à une conférence sur le climat ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m attending a talk on climate tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à des conférences sur l’histoire de l’art.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to conferences (talks/lectures) about art history.

definitions.note: Often used for a large formal meeting of delegates or professionals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le congrès a lieu à Paris cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conference is taking place in Paris this year.

definitions.note: Often used for leave from work (paid leave, sick leave, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un congé demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm taking a day off tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (congés), especially for paid leave or vacation days.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis en congés la semaine prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m on leave next week.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will know the answer tomorrow.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form: contagieux (feminine: contagieuse).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This virus is very contagious.

definitions.note: Often used for a fairy tale or traditional story (e.g., un conte de fées).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce conte est très connu en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tale is very well-known in France.

definitions.note: Often used for looking at something for a long time, quietly or thoughtfully.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to gaze at the landscape from the window.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « contemporain ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s a very well-known contemporary artist.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing/habitual past action or a past description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La boîte contenait des lettres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The box contained letters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette boîte peut contenir dix livres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This box can hold ten books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très content de te voir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very happy to see you.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « content » (used with a feminine noun or a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est contente de te voir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is happy to see you.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: « contenter quelqu’un » = to satisfy someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette décision contente les parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision satisfies the parents.

definitions.note: Often used in the reflexive form « se contenter de » meaning “to be satisfied with” / “to make do with.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce cadeau va contenter les enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This gift will please the children.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont contentes de te voir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are happy to see you.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun (se contenter de) meaning “to be satisfied with” (e.g., contentez-vous de…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Contentez vos clients avec un bon service.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Satisfy your customers with good service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis contents de vous voir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am happy to see you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le contenu de ce cours est facile à comprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The content of this course is easy to understand.

definitions.note: Usually refers to short fictional tales (e.g., fairy tales).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le soir, ma grand-mère nous racontait des contes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening, my grandmother told us stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle conteste la décision du juge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She challenges the judge’s decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans contexte, cette phrase est difficile à comprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without context, this sentence is hard to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces boîtes contiennent des biscuits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These boxes contain cookies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette boîte contient des biscuits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This box contains cookies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit est continu pendant les travaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise is continuous during the construction work.

definitions.note: Often the simple past (passé simple) of « continuer », mostly used in writing and stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il continua à marcher malgré la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He continued walking despite the rain.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (3rd person plural). Often translates as “were continuing,” “kept,” or “used to continue,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils continuaient à parler malgré le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were continuing to talk despite the noise.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il continuait à parler malgré le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept talking despite the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle continue à travailler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She continues to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils continuent à travailler malgré la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They continue to work despite the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais continuer demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to continue tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle continuera demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will continue tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu continues à apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You continue learning French.

definitions.note: Addressed to “vous” (one person formally or multiple people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Continuez à parler, je vous écoute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep talking; I’m listening to you.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form, often used as a suggestion or prompt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Continuons notre travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s continue our work.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural: used mainly in written narration (e.g., stories, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après une courte pause, ils continuèrent leur route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a short break, they continued on their way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a continué à marcher malgré la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He continued walking despite the rain.

definitions.note: Often used about going around an obstacle, or (figuratively) getting around a rule or difficulty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va contourner le village pour éviter les embouteillages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to bypass the village to avoid traffic jams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La contraception permet d’éviter une grossesse non désirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Birth control helps prevent an unwanted pregnancy.

definitions.note: Often used with illnesses (contract a disease) or with muscles (a muscle contracts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il contracte une grippe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He contracts the flu.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant l’accouchement, elle a eu des contractions régulières.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During labor, she had regular contractions.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’agit d’une obligation contractuelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is a contractual obligation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une contradiction entre ce que tu dis et ce que tu fais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a contradiction between what you say and what you do.

definitions.note: Can be the present tense form (3rd person singular) of « contraindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette règle contraint les employés à porter un uniforme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule forces employees to wear a uniform.

definitions.note: Can be the past participle of « contraindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis senti contraint d'accepter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt forced to accept.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of « contraindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont contraints de partir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are forced to leave tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est le contraire de ce que je pensais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the opposite of what I thought.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le contraire de "chaud" est "froid".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The opposite of “hot” is “cold”.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone is a bit upset or disappointed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis contrarié par cette nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m upset by this news.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est contrariée parce que son train est en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is upset because her train is late.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont contrariées par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are upset by the news.

definitions.note: Often used for being bothered or disappointed by something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont contrariés par le retard du train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are upset about the train delay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai signé un contrat de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I signed an employment contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons signé deux contrats hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We signed two contracts yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis contre cette idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m against that idea.

definitions.note: Often used in sports, debates, and comparisons (e.g., France contre Allemagne).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce soir, c’est Lyon contre Marseille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight, it’s Lyon vs. Marseille.

definitions.note: Used to show physical contact or leaning against something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il appuie son vélo contre le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leans his bike against the wall.

definitions.note: Used to express opposition (being opposed to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis contre cette idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m against that idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il contredit souvent son professeur en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often contradicts his teacher in class.

definitions.note: A supervisor (often in a factory, workshop, or on a construction site).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le contremaître vérifie le travail de l’équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The foreman checks the team's work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout le monde peut contribuer au projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone can contribute to the project.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” or “pour” to mean giving money, time, or help toward something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle peut contribuer à la collecte de fonds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can chip in to the fundraiser.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci à tous les contributeurs du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks to all the contributors to the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour votre contribution au projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your contribution to the project.

definitions.note: Often used for a required payment, especially to an organization or in a collection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chaque membre paie une contribution annuelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each member pays an annual fee.

definitions.note: Past participle of « contribuer »; often used with « avoir » to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a contribué au projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She contributed to the project.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision controversée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a controversial decision.

definitions.note: Often used for an official check/inspection (e.g., ticket check, identity check).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un contrôle des billets à l'entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a ticket check at the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used for an ID/ticket check or an inspection; also used in phrases like « contrôle de sécurité » (security check).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le policier contrôle les papiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer checks the documents.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils contrôlent les billets à l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They check the tickets at the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used for verifying or examining something (documents, tickets, work, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais contrôler tes devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check your homework tonight.

definitions.note: Can mean to control or manage something (a machine, a situation, emotions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaie de contrôler sa colère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s trying to control his anger.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who checks tickets or compliance (e.g., on public transport) or someone who supervises/controls a process.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le contrôleur a vérifié nos billets dans le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inspector checked our tickets on the train.

definitions.note: Usually addressed to one person formally (vous) or to more than one person (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Contrôlez vos réponses avant de rendre la copie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check your answers before handing in the test.

definitions.note: Past participle of « contrôler »; often used with « avoir » in compound tenses (e.g., « j’ai contrôlé »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai contrôlé les billets à l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the tickets at the entrance.

definitions.note: Often a more literary/old-fashioned way to say "raconter" (to tell a story).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a conté son voyage à ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told his friends about his trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son argument est très convaincant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His argument is very convincing.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son explication est convaincante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her explanation is convincing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle te convaincra de venir avec nous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will convince you to come with us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essaie de convaincre mon ami de venir ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to convince my friend to come tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis convaincu que ça va marcher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m convinced that it’s going to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis convaincu que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m convinced that you’re right.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is convinced that everything will be fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont convaincus que c’est la bonne décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are convinced that it’s the right decision.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After his operation, he needs a few weeks of recovery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette tenue est convenable pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This outfit is appropriate for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut s’habiller convenablement pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to dress properly for the interview.

definitions.note: Past participle of « convenir »; often used with « avoir » to mean “agreed (on)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons convenu d’un rendez-vous à 15 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on an appointment at 3 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons eu une conversation intéressante après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had an interesting conversation after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont eu plusieurs conversations hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had several conversations last night.

definitions.note: Often used with « avec » (to talk with someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime converser avec mes amis après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to chat with my friends after dinner.

definitions.note: Often used both for a strong belief and for a criminal conviction, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle avec conviction.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks with conviction.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses convictions sont très fortes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her beliefs are very strong.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has two criminal convictions on his record.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These times suit us.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally as “ça/il convient de …” meaning “it is appropriate to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette date te convient ?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a noté des convulsions pendant la nuit.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This app was designed for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange un cookie au chocolat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète des cookies au chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying chocolate cookies.

definitions.note: Informal; borrowed from English and commonly used in spoken French.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really cool.

definitions.note: Informal.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cool! Let’s go.

definitions.note: Describes a person, attitude, or way of working; the feminine form is « coopérative ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very cooperative in class.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cooperation between the two teams is essential.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to cooperate to finish this project on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le coordinateur du projet organise les réunions chaque semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project coordinator organizes the meetings every week.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural to mean someone’s contact info (address, phone number, email, etc.).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m meeting up with my girlfriend tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes copines arrivent à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) friends are arriving at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai copié le texte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I copied the text.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le coq chante tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rooster crows early in the morning.

definitions.note: Often refers to a hard outer covering (e.g., an eggshell) or the hull/body of a boat or vehicle.
