definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ta réponse est correcte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is correct.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « correct ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ta réponse est correcte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is correct.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réponds correctement à la question, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Answer the question correctly, please.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tes réponses sont correctes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answers are correct.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (e.g., correspondre à = correspond to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce numéro correspond à ton dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This number corresponds to your file.

definitions.note: Often used for written communication (letters, emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois répondre à ma correspondance ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to reply to my correspondence tonight.

definitions.note: Used for things that line up or match (e.g., a name and a number).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une correspondance entre le nom et le numéro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a match between the name and the number.

definitions.note: Often used for a journalist reporting from a particular place, or for a person you write to (a contact).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our correspondent in Tokyo sent an article this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chiffres correspondent à la réalité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These figures match reality.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « corriger » (also used for the imperative “correct!” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur corrige les devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher corrects the homework.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur corrigeait les devoirs après le cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher was correcting the homework after class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais corriger tes devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to correct your homework tonight.

definitions.note: Usually used to address one person formally (vous) or more than one person (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Corrigez ces erreurs, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Correct these mistakes, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai corrigé l’exercice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I corrected the exercise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’argent corrompt certaines personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Money corrupts some people.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This politician is corrupt.

definitions.note: masculine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The corrupt politicians were arrested.

definitions.note: Usually refers to dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in power.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La corruption est un grave problème dans certains pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Corruption is a serious problem in some countries.

definitions.note: A small naval warship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La corvette patrouille près de la côte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The corvette is patrolling near the coast.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning “Korean” (from Korea); agrees with the noun it describes (coréen/coréenne/coréens/coréennes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est coréen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Korean.

definitions.note: Used as a noun for a Korean man; the feminine form is « coréenne ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est coréen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Korean.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est coréenne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Korean.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for people or things that are solid and hard to break.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce carton est costaud, il ne se déchire pas facilement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This box is sturdy; it doesn’t tear easily.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a business suit (jacket and matching trousers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte un costume bleu pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s wearing a blue suit for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour la fête, ils portent des costumes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the party, they are wearing costumes.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « avoir la cote » = to be popular / to be in favor.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce chanteur a la cote en ce moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That singer is popular right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette chemise est en coton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shirt is made of cotton.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont loué un cottage près du lac pour le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rented a cottage near the lake for the weekend.

definitions.note: Often written « côté » (with an accent) in standard French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De quel coté est la gare ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which side is the train station on?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a mal au cou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His neck hurts.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past) form, mostly used in literature and formal writing; in speech you usually use passé composé (a couché).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle coucha l'enfant à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She put the child to bed at eight o’clock.

definitions.native: was going to bed, was lying down

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went to bed late on Saturday night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois changer la couche du bébé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change the baby's diaper.

definitions.note: Verb form of « coucher ». Not the noun « couche » (“layer/diaper”). It can look like English “couch” but the meaning is different.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je couche les enfants à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the children to bed at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: coucher un enfant = to put a child to bed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais coucher les enfants à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to put the children to bed at eight o'clock.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: se coucher = to go to bed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais me coucher tôt ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go to bed early tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On doit acheter des couches pour le bébé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy diapers for the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le gâteau a trois couches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake has three layers.

definitions.note: Often used with "tu" (you) in the present tense: "tu couches".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu couches les enfants à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the kids to bed at eight o’clock.

definitions.native: go to bed, put to bed
definitions.note: Present tense form of « coucher » used with « vous » (and as a polite command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Couchez les enfants à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the children to bed at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai couché le bébé à 20 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the baby to bed at 8 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est déjà couché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s already in bed.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « coucher » (often used with « être », e.g. « elle est couchée » = she is lying down / in bed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est déjà couchée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is already in bed.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with a feminine noun/person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est couchée sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants sont couchés depuis huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids have been in bed since eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Informal and friendly greeting (often used when you arrive or to get someone’s attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coucou ! Ça va ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi! How are you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle coud un bouton sur sa chemise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sews a button onto her shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My elbow hurts after the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sais coudre un bouton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know how to sew a button.

definitions.note: Very vulgar slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s'est pris un coup dans les couilles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got hit in the balls.

definitions.note: Vulgar and insulting; avoid in polite conversation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop being an idiot!

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tears were running down his cheeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’eau coulait sous le pont.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water was flowing under the bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau coulait après la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat was sinking after the storm.

definitions.note: Present participle of « couler »; often used like an adjective to describe something that is flowing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On entendait de l’eau coulant sous le pont.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We could hear water flowing under the bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'eau coule du robinet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is running from the tap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il fait chaud, l’eau peut couler longtemps dans la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it’s hot, the water can flow for a long time in the river.

definitions.note: Often used for boats/ships (and things that end up underwater).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant la tempête, le bateau a commencé à couler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the storm, the boat began to sink.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of « couler ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’eau coulera doucement dans la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water will flow gently into the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle est ta couleur préférée ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your favorite color?

definitions.note: Plural of « couleur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime les couleurs vives dans cette peinture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the bright colors in this painting.

definitions.note: Used especially for theater/TV/cinema, or more generally for what happens out of public view.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actors wait backstage before going on stage.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hallway is long and dark.

definitions.note: Plural form of "couloir".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school hallways are very noisy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau a coulé pendant la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat sank during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rivière a coulé toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flowed all night.

definitions.note: This is an English word, not French. If you meant the French word, it’s usually “pays” (meaning “country”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: This is a country.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ceci est un pays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a reçu un coup sur la tête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took a blow to the head.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « un coup de chance » (a stroke of luck) or « un bon coup » (a good move/idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était un bon coup !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a good move!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is guilty of that crime.

definitions.note: Used as a noun to mean the person who is guilty (the culprit).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les coupables ont été arrêtés par la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The culprits were arrested by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a gagné la coupe du tournoi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She won the tournament trophy.

definitions.note: Often used for a hairstyle or the act/result of cutting (e.g., a haircut).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your haircut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il coupe le pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cuts the bread.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils coupent le gâteau en parts égales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They cut the cake into equal pieces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais couper le pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to cut the bread.

definitions.note: Second-person singular ("tu") form of « couper ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took several blows.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cut on my finger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a des coupures sur les doigts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has cuts on his fingers.

definitions.note: Often used for services being interrupted (like electricity, water, internet).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are power outages tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai coupé le pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon doigt est coupé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My finger is cut.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut it in half.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective (used with a feminine noun).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les fleurs sont déjà coupées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers are already cut.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « couper »; often used with « être » in the passive or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les câbles sont coupés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cables are cut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants jouent dans la cour de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are playing in the school courtyard.

definitions.note: Often refers to the king’s/queen’s court in historical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cour du roi est à Versailles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king’s court is in Versailles.

definitions.native: hang in there, you can do it, good luck

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a eu le courage de dire la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had the courage to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très courageuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very brave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très courageux, même quand il a peur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very brave, even when he is scared.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (describes an ongoing or habitual past action).

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je l’ai vu, il courait dans le parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I saw him, he was running in the park.

definitions.note: Used especially about speaking a language.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks English fluently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une erreur courante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a common mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un fort courant dans cette rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a strong current in this river.

definitions.note: Used to talk about a current of ideas (for example in art, politics, or philosophy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce peintre appartient à un courant artistique moderne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painter belongs to a modern artistic movement.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « courant ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une pratique courante en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a common practice in France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sur le graphique, la courbe monte rapidement.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are running in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a runner and he trains every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les coureurs commencent la course à neuf heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The runners start the race at nine o’clock.

definitions.note: Plural form of « course ».

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le crocodile nage dans la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crocodile swims in the river.

definitions.note: plural of « crocodile »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des crocodiles dans cette rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are crocodiles in this river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le loup montre ses crocs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wolf is showing its fangs.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « croire » (used after expressions of doubt/necessity, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux que tu le croie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to believe it.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense ("they").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils croient que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think you’re right.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « croire » used with « tu » (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu croies vraiment à cette histoire ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you really believe that story?

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croira ton histoire demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will believe your story tomorrow.

definitions.note: First person singular ("I") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te croirai si tu me montres une preuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will believe you if you show me proof.

definitions.note: Conditional form (je/tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te croirais si tu me montrais une preuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would believe you if you showed me proof.

definitions.note: Conditional present (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croirait tout ce que tu dis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would believe everything you say.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu croiras ce que tu voudras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will believe what you want.

definitions.note: Often used with "croire que" (to believe/think that) or "croire en" (to believe in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais croire que c’est vrai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to believe/think that it’s true.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense form of « croire ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous croirez cette histoire demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will believe this story tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple future tense (3rd person plural) of « croire ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils croiront ton histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will believe your story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je crois que c’est vrai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe it’s true.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of "croiser"; often corresponds to "crossed" in English narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croisa les bras et resta silencieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crossed his arms and remained silent.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing (arms/legs) or crossing paths (meeting someone by chance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croise les bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crosses his arms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le croisement est dangereux la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The intersection is dangerous at night.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing streets/roads/bridges, or for crossing one thing over another (e.g., arms, legs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux croiser la rue ici ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you cross the street here?

definitions.note: Future tense ("I will...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je croiserai mes voisins au marché demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will meet my neighbors at the market tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a type of military ship (un navire de guerre).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le croiseur entre dans le port.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cruiser enters the harbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous partons en croisière en Méditerranée cet été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going on a cruise in the Mediterranean this summer.

definitions.note: Often used for economic growth (e.g., “croissance économique”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La croissance de l’entreprise est rapide cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company’s growth is fast this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un croissant avec mon café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a croissant with my coffee.

definitions.note: Plural of "croissant" (a crescent-shaped buttery pastry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends deux croissants, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have two croissants, please.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of « croître ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au printemps, les plantes croissent rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the plants grow quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai croisé les bras pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crossed my arms during the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used to mean meeting someone by chance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai croisé Marie au supermarché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into Marie at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often used for things positioned one over the other (e.g., legs, arms, straps).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est assise avec les jambes croisées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is sitting with her legs crossed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sont croisés dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ran into each other in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont les bras croisés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have their arms crossed.

definitions.note: Often followed by « que » (that) or « en » (in), depending on the meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croit que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thinks you are right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une croix sur le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cross on the wall.

definitions.note: Usually refers to small breaded, fried bites (often potato, meat, or fish). In the plural, it can also mean dry pet food (kibble), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On commande des croquettes de poulet en entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re ordering chicken croquettes as a starter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a fait un croquis du paysage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She made a sketch of the landscape.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for animal droppings. Also used in expressions like « c’est de la crotte » (“it’s crap”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention, il y a une crotte de chien sur le trottoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, there’s dog poop on the sidewalk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces pommes de terre sont bien croustillantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These potatoes are really crispy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La baguette est croustillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baguette is crispy.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les frites sont croustillantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fries are crispy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son histoire est tout à fait croyable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story is completely believable.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third-person plural): used for ongoing past states/habits or background description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils croyaient que le magasin était ouvert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed that the store was open.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « croire » (used for ongoing or habitual past, or background descriptions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je croyais que tu étais déjà parti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you had already left.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croyait que tout allait bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believed that everything was going well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa croyance en la justice est très forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her belief in justice is very strong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses croyances sont importantes pour elle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her beliefs are important to her.

definitions.note: Present participle of « croire »; often used like “by/in believing …” or “while believing …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En croyant à cette histoire, il s'est fait avoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By believing that story, he got fooled.

definitions.note: Usually refers to someone who believes in a religion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce village, beaucoup de croyants vont à l’église le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this village, many believers go to church on Sunday.

definitions.note: Formal or plural form ("vous") of "croire" in the present tense; also used for polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Croyez-vous à cette histoire ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you believe that story?

definitions.note: Second-person plural imperfect subjunctive of « croire » (used with « que », after doubts/feelings/necessity, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il voulait que vous croyiez en vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted you to believe in yourselves.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of « croire » (used with « nous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous croyons que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We believe that it’s a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La population de cette ville croît rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The population of this city is growing quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for more formal contexts (e.g., population, profits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La population de la ville continue de croître.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city's population continues to grow.

definitions.note: Often refers to the crust of bread, or the hard outer layer that forms on food or a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’aime pas la croûte du pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like the crust of the bread.

definitions.note: Past participle of « croire » (used in compound tenses like « j’ai cru » = “I believed/thought”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai cru que tu étais déjà parti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you had already left.

definitions.note: Often used for food (e.g., meat, fish, vegetables) that isn’t cooked.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je préfère les légumes crus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer raw vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cruauté de cette histoire m’a choqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cruelty of this story shocked me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle verse de l’eau d’une cruche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pours water from a pitcher.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « croire »; used with a feminine subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle m’a crue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believed me.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « cru » (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne mange pas de viande crue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t eat raw meat.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a river rising (e.g., after heavy rain or snowmelt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après les fortes pluies, la crue de la rivière a inondé des champs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the heavy rain, the river flood flooded some fields.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est trop cruel pour les enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is too cruel for children.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "cruel".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette histoire est cruelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This story is cruel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été cruellement puni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was cruelly punished.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses remarques étaient cruelles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her remarks were cruel.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form (used with masculine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces mots sont vraiment cruels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those words are really cruel.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of « croire » (used with « avoir » when the direct object is plural, or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai crus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed them.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "cru"; often used for food (e.g., eggs, vegetables, fish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les légumes sont meilleurs crus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vegetables are better raw.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form, mostly found in literature or formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il crut entendre son nom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believed he heard his name.

definitions.note: Often used in computing/IT contexts (e.g., encrypted message, encrypted connection).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce message est crypté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This message is encrypted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le crâne est un os important du corps humain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The skull is an important bone in the human body.

definitions.note: In France, often refers to a daycare for very young children (a nursery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre fille va à la crèche trois jours par semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our daughter goes to daycare three days a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais une crème au chocolat, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a chocolate cream, please.

definitions.note: Often used for things like a tire: « Un pneu crève » = “A tire goes flat.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon pneu crève encore !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My tire is going flat again!

definitions.note: Colloquial/informal way to say someone dies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il crève seul dans sa chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dies alone in his room.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), used mainly in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En 1998, elle créa sa propre entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1998, she created her own company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce créateur de mode présente sa nouvelle collection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fashion designer presents his new collection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très créatif et trouve toujours de nouvelles idées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very creative and always comes up with new ideas.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces étudiants sont très créatifs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These students are very creative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La création de ce site a pris trois mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The creation of this website took three months.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très créative.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very creative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette créature vit dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This creature lives in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les créatures vivent dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the creatures live in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son histoire est crédible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story is believable.

definitions.note: Often refers to money you can borrow (e.g., via a credit card, a loan, or store credit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai plus de crédit sur ma carte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any credit left on my card.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est trop crédule : il croit tout ce qu’on lui dit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s too gullible: he believes everything people tell him.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « créer » (e.g., il/elle/on crée).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle crée un nouveau compte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is creating a new account.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they create).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils créent une nouvelle application.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They create a new app.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aime créer des jeux vidéo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes to create video games.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes rentrés au crépuscule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We came home at dusk.

definitions.note: Insult; can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne sois pas un crétin !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be an idiot!

definitions.note: Insulting and informal; can be quite rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrêtez, bande de crétins !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop it, you bunch of idiots!

definitions.note: Past participle of « créer »; often used with « avoir » to form the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a créé une nouvelle application.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She created a new app.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise a été créée en 2010.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company was created in 2010.

definitions.note: Past participle of « créer », masculine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les documents ont été créés hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were created yesterday.

definitions.note: Thin French-style pancakes; plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous mangeons des crêpes au sucre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We eat crêpes with sugar.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont cubains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are Cuban.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je coupe le fromage en cubes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the cheese into cubes.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « cueillir » (used with je/il/elle/on). Often used for picking flowers, fruit, mushrooms, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle cueille des fleurs dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She picks flowers in the garden.

definitions.note: Past participle of « cueillir » (often used with « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai cueilli des pommes ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked some apples this morning.

definitions.note: Used for picking things like flowers, fruit, or mushrooms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons cueillir des pommes au verger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to pick apples in the orchard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai besoin d'une cuillère pour manger ma soupe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a spoon to eat my soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a trois cuillères sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are three spoons on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sac est en cuir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is made of leather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais cuire des légumes ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to cook some vegetables tonight.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « cuire » (usually with « je » or « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cuis des légumes pour le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cook vegetables for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisine est petite, mais très pratique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is small but very practical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’adore la cuisine française.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love French cooking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cuisine tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cooks every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime cuisiner le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to cook in the evening.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « cuisiner » (used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu cuisines souvent le soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you often cook in the evening?

definitions.note: Usually said to one or more people (e.g., “you cook!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuisinez les légumes pendant dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cook the vegetables for ten minutes.

definitions.note: Often refers to a (male) professional cook; the feminine form is « cuisinière ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le cuisinier prépare le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cook is preparing dinner.

definitions.note: Feminine form; can refer to a woman whose job is cooking or someone cooking a meal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisinière prépare le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cook is preparing dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisinière prépare le dîner ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cook is making dinner tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisinière est allumée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stove is on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le poulet est déjà cuisiné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chicken is already cooked.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), mostly used in writing; in everyday speech, French usually uses the passé composé instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier, tu cuisis le poisson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, you cooked the fish.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple) form, mostly used in literature and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cuisit le pain au four.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cooked the bread in the oven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à la cuisse après le sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My thigh hurts after sports.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la randonnée, j’ai mal aux cuisses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, my thighs hurt.

definitions.note: Often used for the process or time of cooking (e.g., “temps de cuisson”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisson des pâtes prend dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cooking the pasta takes ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pain cuit au four.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread cooks in the oven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le gâteau est cuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is cooked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le poulet est bien cuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chicken is well cooked.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les légumes sont cuits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vegetables are cooked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette bague est en cuivre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ring is made of copper.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal in most contexts; common in everyday speech but not polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est assis par terre et s’est fait mal au cul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat on the ground and hurt his butt.

definitions.note: Informal: used to criticize someone for being brazen or shameless.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a le culot de me demander de l’argent après ça !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has the nerve to ask me for money after that!

definitions.note: Often refers to women's underwear; can also be used more generally for underwear depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une nouvelle culotte noire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought new black underwear.

definitions.note: Plural form; in everyday French, often refers to underwear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des culottes au magasin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some underwear at the store.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: « culpabiliser quelqu’un ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaie de culpabiliser sa sœur pour qu’elle change d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s trying to make his sister feel guilty so she’ll change her mind.

definitions.note: Can also be used without an object: « culpabiliser » = to feel guilty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux culpabiliser quand je ne réponds pas tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel guilty when I don’t reply right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle ressent de la culpabilité après avoir menti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels guilt after lying.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle cultivait des tomates dans son jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was growing tomatoes in her garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle cultive des tomates dans son jardin.

definitions.note: Describes someone who is well-educated and knowledgeable (often about arts, literature, etc.).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime découvrir la culture française.

definitions.note: Plural of "culture".

definitions.note: Often used to mean greedy for money or possessions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis curieux de savoir comment ça marche.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a hug.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want cuddles.

definitions.note: Plural form; usually used in the plural in French as well.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I add capers to the salad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cède sa place à une personne âgée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives up his seat to an elderly person.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple) form, used mainly in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sous la pression, il céda et accepta l’accord.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Under pressure, he gave in and accepted the deal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fini par céder et accepter notre proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ended up giving in and accepting our proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va céder sa place à une personne âgée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to give up her seat to an elderly person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a cédé sa place à une personne âgée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave up his seat to an elderly person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je coupe du céleri pour la soupe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm chopping celery for the soup.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun too (un/une célibataire) to mean “a single person.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis célibataire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m single.

definitions.note: Plural form; used for men or mixed groups (feminine plural: célibataires).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are all single this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant est célèbre dans tout le quartier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je célèbre mon anniversaire avec mes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I celebrate my birthday with my friends.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These artists are famous all over the world.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons célébrer ton anniversaire ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to celebrate your birthday tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette célébrité arrive au festival ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This celebrity is arriving at the festival tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de célébrités à ce festival.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of celebrities at this festival.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense; often used as an invitation (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Célébrons cette victoire ensemble !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s celebrate this victory together!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont célébré leur anniversaire hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They celebrated their birthday last night.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in French, especially for breakfast cereal.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat cereal for breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cérémonie commence à dix heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ceremony starts at ten o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous habitons sur la côte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live on the coast.

definitions.note: In cooking, you often see it in dishes like « côte de bœuf » (rib of beef / rib steak).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à une côte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My rib hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal aux côtes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ribs hurt.

definitions.note: Refers to the coastline of a region or country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons longé les côtes de la Bretagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drove along the coast of Brittany.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « à côté de » (= next to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le café est juste à côté de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café is right next to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De quel côté es-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which side are you on?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les deux côtés de la rue sont très bruyants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Both sides of the street are very noisy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal au cœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My heart hurts.

definitions.note: Plural of « cœur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sur cette carte, il y a des cœurs rouges.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this card, there are red hearts.

definitions.note: Common informal spoken form of "cela".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comment va ça ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How is it going?

definitions.native: this, that, it (informal/typographic variant of « c’ »)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The typist types quickly.

definitions.note: Informal slang, usually used with “que” (e.g., “que dalle !”) to mean “absolutely nothing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qu’est-ce que tu as trouvé ? — Que dalle !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What did you find? — Nothing at all!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont posé une dalle de béton dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They laid a concrete slab in the garden.

definitions.note: Often a polite or formal way to refer to a woman, especially an older one.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une dame m’a demandé son chemin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A lady asked me for directions.

definitions.note: Plural of « dame ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mesdames et messieurs, bienvenue !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un danger ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a danger here.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette route est dangereuse la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This road is dangerous at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conduisait dangereusement sur l’autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was driving dangerously on the highway.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « dangereux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces routes sont dangereuses la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These roads are dangerous at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est dangereux de traverser ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s dangerous to cross here.

definitions.note: Plural of « danger ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des dangers sur cette route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are dangers on this road.

definitions.note: A noun for someone from Denmark; the feminine form is "Danoise".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Danish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je parle un peu danois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak a little Danish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le livre est dans le sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is in the bag.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple); mostly used in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dansa toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He danced all night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third-person plural: “they”).

definitions.note: imperfect (past) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier soir, je dansais dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, I was dancing in the living room.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for an ongoing action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dansait toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was dancing all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime la danse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like dance.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dances very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils dansent dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They dance in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime danser le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to dance on the weekend.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of « danser ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu danses très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You dance very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est danseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a dancer.

definitions.note: feminine form (a female dancer)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma sœur est danseuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a dancer.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les danseuses répètent avant le spectacle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dancers rehearse before the show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous dansez très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You dance very well.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present (used to mean “let’s …” or “we …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dansons ensemble !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's dance together!

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mostly used in literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils dansèrent toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They danced all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai dansé toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I danced all night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the date today?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This document dates from 2010.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète des dates au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying dates at the market.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelles sont les dates du voyage ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are the dates of the trip?

definitions.note: Plural form of "datte" (the fruit).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are date palms in the oasis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dauphin nage près du bateau.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We often see dolphins near the boat.

definitions.note: Often used with a verb to mean “more” (not “plus” in the sense of addition).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to travel more this year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A glass of milk, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Paris.

definitions.note: Often used in business contexts; borrowed from English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont signé un deal avec l’entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They signed a deal with the company.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a drug dealer near the train station.
