definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté deux dealers près de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two dealers near the train station.

definitions.note: Often used after the verb (e.g., « être debout » = to be standing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis debout depuis six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been up (standing) since six o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reste debout pendant tout le concert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stays standing up throughout the concert.

definitions.note: Often used as an instruction or encouragement (like “Up!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debout ! Il est déjà huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get up! It’s already eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with « être »: « être debout » = to be standing. Can also be used as an instruction: « Debout ! » = Get up!
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis debout depuis six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been up since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “inside (it/them)” or “in there.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a quelqu’un dedans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s someone inside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait 30 degrés aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s 30 degrees today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait froid dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside.

definitions.note: Often used after verbs like « aller », « sortir », « être » to mean being outdoors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants jouent dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are playing outside.

definitions.note: This is not standard spelling in French; it is normally written as two words: “de la”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je viens dela gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the station.

definitions.note: Mostly used in the fixed expression « l’au-delà » (the beyond/the afterlife).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’au-delà fascine beaucoup de gens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The afterlife fascinates many people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pars demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm leaving tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À demain !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you tomorrow!

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), used mostly in writing (stories, novels) to mean a completed past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il demanda son chemin à un passant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked a passerby for directions.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; in everyday French, people usually use the passé composé (j’ai demandé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je demandai au professeur de répéter la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked the teacher to repeat the question.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je demandais toujours la même chose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was always asking for the same thing.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il demandait toujours de l’aide quand il en avait besoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was always asking for help when he needed it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une demande à te faire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a request to make.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like supply and demand (economics) or demand for a product/service.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La demande pour ce produit est très forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Demand for this product is very high.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il demande de l’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asks for help.

definitions.note: Can also mean “asks (a question)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle demande pourquoi tu es en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks why you are late.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils demandent de l’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ask for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais demander de l’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to ask for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle demandera de l’aide si elle en a besoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will ask for help if she needs it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te demanderai demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will ask you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional present (je): used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te demanderais bien de m’aider, mais je sais que tu es très occupé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to ask you to help me, but I know you are very busy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai reçu plusieurs demandes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received several requests today.

definitions.note: Often used with "tu" (informal singular): "tu demandes" = "you ask." Not the same as English "demand" (which is usually "exiger" in French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pourquoi tu demandes ça ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you asking that?

definitions.note: Formal or plural form: “you ask” / “ask!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demandez au professeur si vous avez une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask the teacher if you have a question.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form of "demander" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous demandons de l’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ask for help.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; common in writing and stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils demandèrent de l’aide au voisin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked the neighbor for help.

definitions.note: Often a false friend: French « demander » usually means “to ask (for)”, not “to demand”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a demandé de l'aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked for help.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « demander » (used with « être » in compound tenses or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette aide a été demandée hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This help was requested yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in a somewhat formal or literary way (e.g., a large or notable home).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils habitent dans une vieille demeure à la campagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in an old home in the countryside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Malgré les difficultés, elle demeure calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the difficulties, she remains calm.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; can also mean “continue to be.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la réunion, ils demeurent dans la salle pour discuter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meeting, they remain in the room to talk.

definitions.note: Can sound formal or old-fashioned compared with "restez" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demeurez ici pendant que je reviens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here while I come back.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (and can be invariable in some set phrases), e.g. « une demi-heure ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais une demi-baguette, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like half a baguette, please.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like "un demi" (a half-pint of beer) or "à demi" (halfway/partly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais un demi, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a half-pint (of beer), please.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned or formal; today often replaced by « mademoiselle » (also becoming less common in official contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette demoiselle attend son amie devant le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This young lady is waiting for her friend in front of the café.

definitions.note: Plural form of « demoiselle ». Often used for young women; can sound old-fashioned or formal depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mesdemoiselles, vous pouvez entrer maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Young ladies, you may come in now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La forêt est dense et sombre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The forest is dense and dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à une dent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a toothache.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des soins dentaires réguliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get regular dental care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai oublié mon dentifrice à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my toothpaste at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais chez le dentiste demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the dentist tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of « dent ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me brosse les dents deux fois par jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brush my teeth twice a day.

definitions.note: Used with a starting point in time (or sometimes place): “since” + date/event; “for” + duration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habite ici depuis 2021.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lived here since 2021.

definitions.note: Used to express a starting point in time or how long something has been happening (often with the present tense in French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habite ici depuis 2020.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lived here since 2020.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “most recent” (e.g., le dernier film = the latest film).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est mon dernier jour ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my last day here.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of « dernier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont les derniers jours de l'année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the last days of the year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « dernier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est ma dernière chance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my last chance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai été très occupé dernièrement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been very busy recently.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « dernier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont les dernières places disponibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the last available seats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chat est derrière la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is behind the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien est juste derrière toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is right behind you.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s'est assis sur son derrière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat down on his butt.

definitions.note: contraction of de + les, used before a plural definite noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il revient des montagnes demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is coming back from the mountains tomorrow.

definitions.native: of the, from the, about the
definitions.note: Contraction of "de + les" (used before a plural noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle des étudiants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is talking about the students.

definitions.note: Plural indefinite article; it is often omitted in natural English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai des amis à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some friends in Paris.

definitions.note: plural form of the indefinite article (from "un/une"), used before plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai des amis à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some friends in Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il descend les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes down the stairs.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (family lineage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a transmis cette maison à sa descendance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He passed this house on to his descendants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En descendant l'escalier, j'ai vu mon voisin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While going down the stairs, I saw my neighbor.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, often used after « que » (e.g., « Il faut que je descende. »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je descende tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go down right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils descendent l’escalier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They go down the stairs.

definitions.native: go down, come down, get off
definitions.note: Usually used as a command to one person (formal) or to several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Descendez à la prochaine station, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get off at the next station, please.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il descendit l’escalier en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went down the stairs in silence.

definitions.native: let’s go down, let’s come down
definitions.note: Often used as an imperative meaning “let’s …” (suggestion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Descendons les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go down the stairs.

definitions.native: to go down, to come down, to descend; to get off (a bus/train)
definitions.note: Infinitive form required in the example. Used for going down (stairs, a hill, etc.) and for getting off public transport ("descendre de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais descendre du bus à la prochaine station.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get off the bus at the next stop.

definitions.native: go down, come down, get off
definitions.note: Present tense form of “descendre” (also used for “you go down/come down” or “I go down/come down,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu descends à la prochaine station ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you getting off at the next station?

definitions.note: Past participle of « descendre ». It can also mean « got off / got out (of a vehicle) » depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est descendu du bus à la prochaine station.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got off the bus at the next stop.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « descendre » (used with « être » for motion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est descendue du bus à la prochaine station.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got off the bus at the next stop.

definitions.native: gone down, come down; gotten off
definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « descendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont descendus du train à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got off the train in Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La descente est dangereuse quand il pleut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The descent is dangerous when it’s raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a une description du suspect.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have a description of the suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime le design de cette chaise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the design of this chair.

definitions.note: Often used for loosening something that is tight (like a screw, a tie, or a grip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux desserrer la vis ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you loosen the screw?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un dessert après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a dessert after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait un dessin de mon chat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a drawing of my cat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle dessine un chat sur la feuille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She draws a cat on the sheet of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aime dessiner des animaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes to draw animals.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « dessiner » (often used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dessines un chat sur la feuille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You draw a cat on the sheet of paper.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (“Draw!”) or as “you draw” (formal/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dessinez un chat, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a cat, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les dessins des enfants sont sur le frigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children's drawings are on the fridge.

definitions.note: Past participle of « dessiner »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai dessiné » = “I drew / I have drawn”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai dessiné un chat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew a cat.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte une robe avec des fleurs dessinées dessus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a dress with flowers drawn on it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chat est dessous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is underneath.

definitions.note: Often used with an article (e.g., « le dessous ») to mean the underside/bottom part of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dessous de la table est sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The underside of the table is dirty.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (« des dessous », « les dessous ») to mean underwear/lingerie.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des dessous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some underwear.

definitions.note: Often used with en: « dessus » = « on (top of) it », « en dessus » = « on it ». Also appears in expressions like « au-dessus » (“above”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mets le livre dessus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on it.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: « le dessus de … » = “the top/surface of …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dessus de la table est sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The top of the table is dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je crois au destin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe in fate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre destination, c’est Marseille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our destination is Marseille.

definitions.note: Past participle of "destiner"; often used with "être" (e.g., "être destiné à").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est destiné aux débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is intended for beginners.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” (destiné à + noun/infinitive) to say what something is meant for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est destiné aux débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is intended for beginners.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette lettre est destinée à mon professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This letter is intended for my teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croyait que sa destinée était déjà écrite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believed that his destiny was already written.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective; often used with “à” (intended for) or “à + infinitive” (meant to…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces cadeaux sont destinés aux enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These gifts are intended for children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La destruction de la forêt inquiète les habitants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The destruction of the forest worries the residents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une dette envers la banque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a debt to the bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a des dettes depuis l’an dernier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has had debts since last year.

definitions.note: Used for the period or state of mourning after someone’s death (e.g., "être en deuil").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la mort de son père, elle est restée en deuil pendant un an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After her father’s death, she stayed in mourning for a year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai deux frères.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est mon deuxième jour à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my second day in Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Premièrement, nous devons vérifier les prix ; deuxièmement, nous devons réserver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First, we need to check the prices; secondly, we need to book.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (they); often expresses obligation or what was expected in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils devaient partir tôt ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had to leave early this morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect of « devoir » used to talk about an obligation in the past (ongoing/habitual/background).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je devais partir tôt ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to leave early this morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je/tu): used for an ongoing past obligation or something you were supposed to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je devais partir tôt, mais j’ai raté le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to leave early, but I missed the bus.

definitions.note: Imperfect form; often expresses obligation in the past (or a planned/expected action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il devait partir à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to leave at eight o'clock.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « devoir » (used for past habits/ongoing situations, or to set background in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il devait partir tôt, mais il a raté le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to leave early, but he missed the bus.

definitions.note: This appears to be a misspelling of “devant”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une voiture juste devanr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a car right in front.

definitions.note: Can be used as a preposition (devant + noun) or as an adverb meaning “in front.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il attend devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is waiting in front of the station.

definitions.note: Often used with a place or person: devant la maison (in front of the house), devant moi (in front of me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture est juste devant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is right in front.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, often with an article (e.g., « le devant ») to mean the front part/side of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le devant de la maison est bleu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The front of the house is blue.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « devenir » (used for ongoing actions or descriptions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je devenais de plus en plus confiant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was becoming more and more confident.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (he/she/it was becoming).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec le temps, le ciel devenait plus sombre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time, the sky was becoming darker.

definitions.note: Formal or plural “you” form (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devenez membre dès aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Become a member today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux devenir médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to become a doctor.

definitions.note: Past participle of « devenir » (often used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est devenu médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He became a doctor.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « devenir » (used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est devenue médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She became a doctor.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « devenir »; used with « être » or « se » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont devenues amies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They became friends.

definitions.note: Past participle of « devenir »; often used with « être » (e.g., « ils sont devenus… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont devenus amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They became friends.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous devez partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must leave now.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense of « devoir » (used with « vous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous devez partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il deviendra médecin plus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will become a doctor later.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je deviendrai médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will become a doctor.

definitions.note: Conditional (present) form of « devenir »; often used for hypotheticals or polite/uncertain statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans aide, il deviendrait difficile de finir à temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, it would become difficult to finish on time.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu deviendras médecin plus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will become a doctor later.

definitions.note: Third-person plural future tense of « devenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils deviendront médecins après leurs études.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will become doctors after their studies.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « devenir » (used after expressions of desire, necessity, doubt, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux que tu deviennes médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to become a doctor.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of « devenir » (used with ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec le temps, ils deviennent plus patients.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With time, they become more patient.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu) of « devenir »; often used after expressions like « il faut que », « je veux que », « pour que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux que tu deviennes médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to become a doctor.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « devenir » used with « je » or « tu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu deviens très bon en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re becoming very good at French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il devient médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He becomes a doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous deviez partir plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were supposed to leave earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devine combien de personnes viennent ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess how many people are coming tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for guessing the answer or figuring something out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux deviner la réponse ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess the answer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu devineras la réponse en une minute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will guess the answer in one minute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu devines la réponse ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you guessing the answer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une devinette pour toi : qu’est-ce qui est jaune et qui attend ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a riddle for you: what is yellow and waiting?

definitions.note: Used to ask or tell someone (informal or formal) to guess something; often said as a prompt like “Guess what?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devinez qui est là !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess who’s here!

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in literature and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils devinrent amis après ce voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They became friends after that trip.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 1st person singular of « devenir »; used mostly in writing (stories, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À cet instant, je devins courageux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that moment, I became brave.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form; used mainly in writing (stories, books, formal history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il devint médecin à trente ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He became a doctor at thirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deviné la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guessed the answer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nous): expresses an obligation in the past, often ongoing or not completed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devions partir tôt, mais on a raté le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were supposed to leave early, but we missed the train.

definitions.note: Used in phrases like « devise étrangère » (foreign currency).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont changé des euros en devise locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They exchanged euros into the local currency.

definitions.note: Often refers to an official motto (e.g., of a country, school, or organization).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La devise de cette école est « Travail et respect ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The motto of this school is “Work and respect.”

definitions.note: Noun: a responsibility or obligation (often used in the plural: "les devoirs" = homework).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est mon devoir de dire la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is my duty to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Noun (usually plural): "les devoirs" refers to schoolwork assigned to do at home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois faire mes devoirs avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do my homework before going out.

definitions.note: Verb: to be indebted to someone ("Je te dois ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te dois dix euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I owe you ten euros.

definitions.note: Verb (conjugated): expresses obligation or necessity; dictionary form is "devoir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pense que je vais devoir partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think I’m going to have to leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai beaucoup de devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est mon devoir de t'aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's my duty to help you.

definitions.note: Noun: a responsibility or obligation (often moral, civic, or professional).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est mon devoir de dire la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is my duty to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Noun (usually plural: les devoirs): schoolwork to be done at home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai beaucoup de devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework tonight.

definitions.note: Verb: to be indebted; to owe someone money or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te dois dix euros, mais je ne dois rien d’autre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I owe you ten euros, but I don’t owe anything else.

definitions.note: Verb (impersonal obligation/necessity): « devoir » + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois le faire parce que je dois respecter les règles, mais c’est un devoir pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must do it because I have to follow the rules, but it is a duty for me.

definitions.note: Plural form; very often used in the plural in French to mean school assignments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai trop de devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have too much homework tonight.

definitions.note: First-person plural present of « devoir » (nous). Often expresses obligation/necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to leave now.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We train at the dojo every Wednesday.

definitions.note: Most often refers to the U.S. dollar, but can also refer to other currencies called “dollar” (e.g., Canadian dollar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas de dollars sur moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any dollars on me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça coûte vingt dollars.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It costs twenty dollars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sujet est en dehors de mon domaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That topic is outside my field.

definitions.note: Often used for a large property, especially a vineyard or country estate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils visitent un domaine viticole en Bourgogne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are visiting a vineyard estate in Burgundy.

definitions.note: Often used for things related to the home or household (e.g., chores, animals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais les tâches domestiques le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do the household chores on Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le domestique prépare le petit-déjeuner tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The domestic servant prepares breakfast every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons des animaux domestiques à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have domestic animals at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les domestiques préparent le dîner pour la famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The household staff prepare dinner for the family.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/administrative contexts to mean your official place of residence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai changé de domicile le mois dernier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my home address last month.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette équipe, elle est très dominante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this team, she is very dominant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette équipe domine le championnat cette saison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That team dominates the league this season.

definitions.note: Often used in the set phrase « C’est dommage » to express regret or disappointment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est dommage, je ne peux pas venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pity, I can’t come.

definitions.note: Used to express regret or disappointment (often like “that’s a shame”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dommage, je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Too bad, I can’t come tonight.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in legal/insurance contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a demandé des dommages après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked for damages after the accident.

definitions.note: Often used for a natural talent or ability (e.g., avoir un don pour...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un don pour la musique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a gift for music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour votre don.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your donation.

definitions.note: Used as a title placed before a woman’s first name in Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dona Maria arrive demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Doña Maria is arriving tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a result, conclusion, or consequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pleut, donc je reste à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining, so I’m staying home.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il donna son manteau à son frère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave his coat to his brother.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person singular; mostly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lui donnai la clé et je partis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave him the key and I left.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), 3rd person plural (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils donnaient des bonbons aux enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were giving sweets to the children.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (je/tu form), often describes an ongoing or habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je donnais des cours de français le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to give French lessons in the evening.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): ongoing/repeated action or background description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me donnait toujours des conseils.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was always giving me advice.

definitions.note: Present participle of « donner »; often means “while giving” or “by giving,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En donnant un coup de main, tu gagneras du temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By giving a hand, you’ll save time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est à toi de faire la donne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s your turn to deal.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « changer la donne » (“to change the situation”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nouvelle loi change la donne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This new law changes the situation.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « donner »; also used in some contexts for commands (e.g., « Donne-moi… » = “Give me…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me donne un cadeau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives me a present.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they give).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils donnent des cadeaux à leurs amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They give gifts to their friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te donner un coup de main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to give you a hand.

definitions.note: Third-person singular simple future of « donner ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me donnera un coup de main demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will give me a hand tomorrow.

definitions.note: First person singular future tense (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te donnerai mon numéro demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give you my number tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional present (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te le donnerais si je l’avais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would give it to you if I had it.

definitions.note: Conditional present (often used for hypothetical situations or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il donnerait tout pour te revoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would give anything to see you again.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) simple future of « donner ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me donneras ton adresse demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will give me your address tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) in the future tense; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous donnerez votre réponse demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will give your answer tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils donneront leur avis demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will give their opinion tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "donner" used with "tu" (you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me donnes ton numéro ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me your number?

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural) or formal singular command/present form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Donnez-moi votre adresse, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me your address, please.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) present tense; often used to make a suggestion ("let's...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Donnons un coup de main à nos voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's give our neighbors a hand.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural ("they"); mainly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils donnèrent leur argent à une association.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave their money to a charity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai donné à ma sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have given it to my sister.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « donner » (it agrees with a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réponse est déjà donnée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is already given.

definitions.note: Past participle of « donner » (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les instructions ont été données hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions were given yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les données sont stockées sur le serveur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data is stored on the server.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « donner ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les documents ont été donnés au professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were given to the teacher.

definitions.note: Plural of « don ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour vos dons à l’association.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your donations to the organization.

definitions.note: Relative word that replaces "de + which/whom" (e.g., "le livre dont je parle" = "the book (that) I’m talking about").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une femme dont j’admire le courage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s a woman whose courage I admire.

definitions.note: Used mainly as a relative word to replace “de + [something]” (e.g., “la fille dont je parle” = “the girl I’m talking about”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est le livre dont j’ai besoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s the book I need.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun used to replace something introduced by « de » (e.g., parler de, avoir besoin de).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est le livre dont je t’ai parlé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the book I told you about.

definitions.note: slang
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vend de la dope.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sells drugs.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je suis arrivé, ils dormaient déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, they were already sleeping.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dormais quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was sleeping when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je suis arrivé, il dormait déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, he was already sleeping.

definitions.note: Participe présent of « dormir ». Not the same as English « dormant » (= inactive) in most cases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai vu mon chat dormant sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw my cat sleeping on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dort et elle dort, mais mon bébé dorme très peu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sleeps and she sleeps, but my baby sleeps very little.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « dormir » used with « ils/elles ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants dorment déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are already sleeping.

definitions.note: Used with tu ("you") in the present subjunctive, often after que (e.g., "il faut que tu dormes").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu dormes un peu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to sleep a little.

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form used with "vous".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous dormez déjà ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you sleeping already?

definitions.note: Past participle of « dormir », used with « avoir » in compound past tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai dormi huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slept eight hours.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je suis arrivé, vous dormiez déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, you were already sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois dormir tôt ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to sleep early tonight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular in the simple future (il/elle/on dormira).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, il dormira tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, he will sleep early.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in written French (stories, literature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le long voyage, ils dormirent immédiatement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long trip, they slept immediately.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dormis mal cette nuit-là.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slept badly that night.

definitions.native: slept (simple past, literary) / was sleeping (historical present context)
definitions.note: 3rd person singular of « dormir » in the passé simple; used mainly in literature and formal narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le dîner, il dormit profondément.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, he slept deeply.

definitions.note: In narrative style, « dormit » can imply that someone spent the night sleeping or that they went to sleep, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Épuisée, elle dormit sans entendre l’orage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Exhausted, she fell asleep without hearing the storm.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of « dormir » (used with « nous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous dormons encore une heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re sleeping for another hour.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "dormir" used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dors déjà ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you sleeping already?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dort déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is already sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves dorment dans un dortoir pendant le voyage scolaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students sleep in a dormitory during the school trip.

definitions.note: Often a shared sleeping room (e.g., in a school, hostel, or camp).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves dorment dans un dortoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students sleep in a dormitory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux dortoirs dans cette auberge de jeunesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two dormitories in this youth hostel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte un collier doré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a golden necklace.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte une robe dorée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a golden dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dorénavant, je travaillerai de chez moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From now on, I will work from home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal au dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My back hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a augmenté la dose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor increased the dose.

definitions.note: Often refers to a set of documents about a person or topic (e.g., an application file or case file).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai mis les documents dans ton dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the documents in your folder.

definitions.note: Common in administrative/legal contexts: a set of documents about a specific matter.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le juge étudie le dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge is reviewing the case file.

definitions.note: Often used for a folder (physical or digital) containing documents about a topic or person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai rangé les dossiers dans l'armoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the files in the cabinet.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to say what someone/something is endowed or equipped with: "doté de".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est doté d'une grande patience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is endowed with great patience.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to say what something is equipped/provided with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette salle est dotée d’un projecteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room is equipped with a projector.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont dotés d’un excellent sens de l’humour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are endowed with an excellent sense of humor.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the customs service/authorities, especially at borders and airports.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois passer par les douanes avant de sortir de l’aéroport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go through customs before leaving the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux une portion double, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a double portion, please.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday contexts like ordering food/drinks (e.g., un double café).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais un double, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a double, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je double la recette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I double the recipe.

definitions.note: Often used for passing another vehicle on the road (especially in driving contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veut doubler un camion sur l’autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to overtake a truck on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont doubler la production cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to double production this year.

definitions.note: Most often used for the inner fabric layer of clothing, bags, curtains, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette veste a une doublure chaude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This jacket has a warm lining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai doublé la recette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubled the recipe.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « doux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une voix douce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a soft, gentle voice.

definitions.note: Often used to tell someone to slow down or be careful (like “easy!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parle doucement, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak softly, please.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « doux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces fraises sont très douces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These strawberries are very sweet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime la douceur de cette confiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the sweetness of this jam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une douche le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a shower in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: « se doucher » = to take a shower.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me douche tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shower every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais me doucher avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to shower before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des douches au gymnase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are showers at the gym.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une douleur au dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have pain in my back.

definitions.note: Plural form of « douleur »; often used for physical pain or emotional suffering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des douleurs au dos depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had back pain since yesterday.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « douloureux ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette blessure est douloureuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This injury is painful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce massage est un peu douloureux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This massage is a little painful.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), first-person singular: “I was doubting / I used to doubt.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je doutais de ses intentions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubted his intentions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un doute sur la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a doubt about the answer.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + noun/infinitive ("douter de..."), or with "que" + clause ("douter que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je doute de sa version des faits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt his version of the facts.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + noun or infinitive: "douter de quelque chose", "douter de faire quelque chose".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais douter de sa sincérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to doubt his sincerity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai des doutes sur cette histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have doubts about that story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce contrat semble douteux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This contract seems dubious.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with vous (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne doutez pas de vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't doubt yourself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai douté de ton histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubted your story.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural: les douves (around a castle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le château est entouré de douves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle is surrounded by a moat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce pull est très doux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sweater is very soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime le chocolat doux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like sweet chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une douzaine d’œufs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a dozen eggs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont acheté des douzaines d’œufs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought dozens of eggs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai douze ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twelve years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est le douzième chapitre du livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the twelfth chapter of the book.

definitions.note: Often used with "pour" + noun/verb to say someone is talented at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très douée pour la musique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very talented at music.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très douée en maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very gifted at math.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine, or mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces étudiants sont très doués en maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These students are very gifted at math.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Doña Carmen lives in Madrid.

definitions.note: Written abbreviation of « docteur » (doctor).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dr. Martin arrives at 3 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chevalier combat un dragon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knight is fighting a dragon.

definitions.note: Plural of "dragon".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette histoire, les dragons protègent le village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this story, the dragons protect the village.

definitions.note: In everyday French, this usually means trying to pick someone up romantically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va draguer une fille au bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going to flirt with a girl at the bar.

definitions.note: Can mean “theatrical” or “very serious/tragic,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une situation dramatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a dramatic situation.

definitions.native: to dramatize, to make a big deal out of
definitions.note: Often used to mean exaggerating a problem or reacting too strongly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ne faut pas dramatiser la situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We shouldn't dramatize the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce dramaturge a écrit une pièce très célèbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This playwright wrote a very famous play.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film raconte un drame familial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie tells a family drama.

definitions.note: Usually means a bed sheet (e.g., “drap de lit”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des draps blancs pour le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought white sheets for the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le drapeau français est bleu, blanc et rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The French flag is blue, white, and red.

definitions.note: Plural of « drapeau ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des drapeaux devant l’hôtel de ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are flags in front of the city hall.

definitions.note: Usually refers to bed sheets.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais changer les draps ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to change the sheets tonight.

definitions.note: Literary simple past (passé simple) of « dresser »; often means to train an animal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dressa le chien en une semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trained the dog in a week.

definitions.note: Literary simple past (passé simple) of « dresser ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle dressa une tente près de la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She put up a tent near the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle dresse une tente dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sets up a tent in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for training animals (e.g., a dog).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dresse son chien à s’asseoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trains his dog to sit.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase « dresser la table » (to set the table).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais dresser la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to set the table.

definitions.note: Used for making something like a list, report, or inventory.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle doit dresser une liste des invités.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to draw up a list of the guests.

definitions.note: Often used for training an animal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont dresser leur chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to train their dog.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in writing (stories, history), less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils dressèrent une tente près de la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They set up a tent near the river.

definitions.note: Often used for trained animals (e.g., a trained dog).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce chien est bien dressé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dog is well trained.

definitions.note: Used for something set upright or set up (e.g., a statue, a tent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La statue est dressée au centre de la place.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The statue is erected in the center of the square.

definitions.note: Often used for illegal drugs; in plural (des drogues), it can also refer to drugs/medicines in general depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a trouvé de la drogue dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found drugs in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a trouvé des drogues dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found drugs in the car.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “addicted” in everyday speech; can be informal or pejorative depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il était drogué et ne savait plus où il était.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was drugged and no longer knew where he was.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean someone is high or addicted to drugs; can be insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle avait l'air droguée après la soirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked drugged after the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce mur est droit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This wall is straight.

definitions.note: Masculine form (feminine: droite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le gant droit est sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The right glove is on the table.

definitions.note: Used as an adverb of direction (often with verbs like aller, continuer, marcher).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go straight ahead, then turn left.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: « les droits » = rights.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout le monde a le droit de s’exprimer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has the right to express themselves.

definitions.note: In this sense it often refers to the field of law (e.g., « étudier le droit »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle étudie le droit à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies law at university.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used with feminine nouns (e.g., la main droite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’écris avec la main droite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I write with my right hand.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used in expressions like « une ligne droite ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une ligne droite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a straight line.

definitions.note: Usually used with the preposition « à » (e.g., « à droite » = on/to the right).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tournez à droite au prochain carrefour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn right at the next intersection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pharmacie est à droite de la banque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is to the right of the bank.

definitions.note: Often used in math and geometry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trace une droite sur la feuille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a straight line on the sheet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis droitier, donc j’écris avec la main droite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m right-handed, so I write with my right hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les murs sont droits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The walls are straight.

definitions.note: Plural of « droit ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants ont des droits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children have rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un drone survole la plage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A drone is flying over the beach.

definitions.note: Plural of « droïde ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les droïdes aident les héros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the droids help the heroes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment drôle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really funny.

definitions.note: Informal; often used to emphasize an adjective or adverb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait drôlement froid aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s really cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces histoires sont vraiment drôles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These stories are really funny.

definitions.note: contraction of de + le
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le toit du garage est rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof of the garage is red.

definitions.note: used before a masculine singular noun, often with uncountable things
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais du fromage avec le pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like some cheese with the bread.

definitions.note: contraction of de + le before a masculine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le toit du garage est neuf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof of the garage is new.

definitions.note: A noble title; the feminine form is "duchesse".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le duc habite dans un grand château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The duke lives in a big castle.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the historical expression « le Duce », the title used for Benito Mussolini in Fascist Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mussolini se faisait appeler le Duce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mussolini had people call him the Duce.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La duchesse arrive au château ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The duchess is arriving at the castle tonight.

definitions.note: Very informal and insulting (vulgar slang).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de faire le ducon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop acting like an idiot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sont battus en duel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fought a duel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce duo de chanteurs est très populaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This duo of singers is very popular.

definitions.note: Past participle (also used adjectivally) of « duper »; agrees in gender/number (dupé, dupée, dupés, dupées).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis fait dupé par un faux vendeur en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got fooled by a fake online seller.

definitions.note: Can describe something physically hard or difficult (e.g., a hard task).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce pain est dur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread is hard.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it modifies a verb (e.g., travailler dur = to work hard).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il travaille dur pour réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works hard to succeed.

definitions.native: the hard part, the tough part
definitions.note: Used as a noun, often in the expression « le dur » meaning “the hard/tough part.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dur, c’est de rester motivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hard part is staying motivated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film dura deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasted two hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaussures sont durables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are durable.

definitions.note: Often used in environmental contexts (e.g., “développement durable” = “sustainable development”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous voulons une énergie durable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want sustainable energy.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal writing; in everyday speech, people very often use "pendant" instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durant la réunion, je n’ai pas parlé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the meeting, I didn’t speak.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « dur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette chaise est dure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is hard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film dure deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasts two hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été durement puni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was punished harshly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaussures durent longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes last a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film va durer deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will last two hours.

definitions.note: Often used to say how long something takes or will take.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Est-ce que ça va durer longtemps ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is it going to take a long time?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film durera deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will last two hours.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "dur".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaises sont dures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These chairs are hard.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of « dur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces exercices sont vraiment durs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These exercises are really hard.

definitions.note: Plural noun form of « dur »; often refers to people who are tough or strict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette équipe, les durs ne se plaignent jamais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this team, the tough ones never complain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film a duré deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasted two hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La durée du film est de deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie’s duration is two hours.
