definitions.note: Masculine plural form (past participle/adjectival use) of « devoir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces frais sont dus au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These fees are owed to the owner.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past form (passé simple) of « devoir »; common in writing, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dut partir immédiatement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to leave immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un dvd hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a DVD yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une équipe dynamique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a dynamic team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont trouvé de la dynamite dans le bâtiment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found dynamite in the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin suspecte une dysenterie après son voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor suspects dysentery after his trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est dyslexique, alors il lit plus lentement que les autres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dyslexic, so he reads more slowly than the others.

definitions.note: Used with time (and sometimes place) to mean “starting at/starting from.” Often appears in phrases like “dès que” (as soon as).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis disponible dès demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m available starting tomorrow.

definitions.note: A small cube used in games; plural: dés.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jette le dé, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw the die, please.

definitions.native: to wander; to stroll; to amble around
definitions.note: Usually means walking about without a specific destination, often leisurely (sometimes aimlessly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le déjeuner, nous aimons déambuler dans les rues du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch, we like to wander around the streets downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais déballer les cartons ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to unpack the boxes tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il débarque du train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets off the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le camion débarque les marchandises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck unloads the goods.

definitions.note: Used for getting off a vehicle (train, plane, boat) or coming ashore.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons débarquer du train à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to get off the train in Lyon.

definitions.note: Past participle of « débarquer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont débarqué du bateau à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got off the boat at noon.

definitions.note: Often used as « se débarrasser de » = “to get rid of (something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me débarrasse de ces vieux papiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting rid of these old papers.

definitions.native: to clear (away), to get rid of
definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "to get rid of (something)" (e.g. "se débarrasser de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois débarrasser la table après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to clear the table after dinner.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to address one person formally or several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Débarrassez la table, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clear the table, please.

definitions.note: Often used with objects (e.g., a table) or with “de” to mean “free of / rid of” something. Not the same as English “embarrassed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai débarrassé la table après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleared the table after dinner.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « débarrasser », often used with « être » + « de » to mean being free of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis débarrassée de ces papiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve gotten rid of those papers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le débat commence à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The debate starts at eight o'clock.

definitions.note: Often used with de: débattre de quelque chose = to debate/discuss something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont débattre de ce sujet en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to debate this topic in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sujet a été débattu hier en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The topic was debated yesterday in class.

definitions.note: Informal; can be insulting (used to call someone stupid).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce commentaire est vraiment débile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment is really stupid.

definitions.note: Informal and offensive insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de faire le débile !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop acting like an idiot!

definitions.note: Can be used literally (e.g., a door/phone) or figuratively (e.g., a situation/problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il débloque son téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unlocks his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le verre déborde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is overflowing.

definitions.note: Often used to say you have too much to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis débordé au travail cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m overwhelmed at work this week.

definitions.note: Past participle of « déboutonner »; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai laissé mon manteau déboutonné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my coat unbuttoned.

definitions.note: Often used for unplugging an electrical device (pulling the plug).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il débranche le chargeur avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unplugs the charger before leaving.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (vous form) or as a polite instruction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Débranchez l’appareil avant de le nettoyer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unplug the device before cleaning it.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun “se” (se débrouiller) meaning “to manage/get by.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se débrouille tout seul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He manages on his own.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais débrouiller les fils avant de les ranger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to untangle the wires before putting them away.

definitions.native: to sort out, to figure out
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « se débrouiller » meaning “to manage, to get by (on your own)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va débrouiller ce problème ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to sort out this problem together.

definitions.native: will sort out, will figure out
definitions.note: Simple future (il/elle/on). Often used in expressions like “se débrouiller” = to manage, to get by.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle débrouillera le problème demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will sort out the problem tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular future ("I will...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je débrouillerai les fils plus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will untangle the wires later.

definitions.native: manage, get by, figure it out
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: « se débrouiller » (to manage on one’s own).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne t’inquiète pas, tu te débrouilles très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, you’re managing very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai débrouillé le problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sorted out the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le début du film est très drôle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The beginning of the movie is very funny.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple); mainly used in writing (stories, history), not in everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le concert débuta à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert began at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis un débutant en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am a beginner in French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce cours est parfait pour les débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This class is perfect for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film débute à 20 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie starts at 8 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le concert débutera à 20 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert will begin at 8 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used for moving an appointment, deadline, or schedule to a later time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va décaler la réunion à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to postpone the meeting until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bourreau va décapiter le condamné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The executioner is going to behead the condemned man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le roi a été décapité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king was beheaded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été décapités par le bourreau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were beheaded by the executioner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon anniversaire est en décembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in December.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette décennie a été très importante pour la technologie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decade has been very important for technology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces changements se sont produits au fil des décennies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These changes happened over the decades.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte une tenue décente pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s wearing a decent outfit for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai ressenti une grande déception après le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great disappointment after the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment décevant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really disappointing.

definitions.note: Means “disappoint,” not “deceive” (French for “deceive” is « tromper »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous me décevez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You disappoint me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne veux pas te décevoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to disappoint you.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “deceive” (French for “to deceive” is “tromper”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si je promets ça, je te décevrai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I promise that, I will disappoint you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ville a fermé la décharge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city closed the landfill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais décharger le camion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to unload the truck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le policier va décharger son arme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer is going to discharge his weapon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déchargé le camion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I unloaded the truck.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut trier les déchets.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to sort the waste.

definitions.note: Often used for decoding writing (handwriting, a code) or understanding something difficult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n'arrive pas à déchiffrer son écriture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't decipher his handwriting.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), third person singular; common in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle déchira la lettre et la jeta à la poubelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tore up the letter and threw it in the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle déchire la page du cahier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tears the page out of the notebook.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce groupe déchire !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This band rocks!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais déchirer cette feuille par erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to tear this sheet by mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon pantalon est déchiré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My pants are torn.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), used mostly in written French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après quelques secondes, elle décida de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a few seconds, she decided to leave.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person singular; mostly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je décidai de partir tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to leave right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il décide de partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decides to leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais décider ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to decide tonight.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + infinitive: décider de faire quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons décider de partir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to decide to leave tomorrow.

definitions.native: to rule / to decide (a case, an issue)
definitions.note: Formal or legal usage: décider une affaire, décider d’un litige.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le juge va décider l’affaire lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge will decide the case on Monday.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will decide).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle décidera demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will decide tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils décideront demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will decide tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « décider » used with « tu » (you, singular informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu décides maintenant ou tu attends ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you deciding now, or are you waiting?

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form used with “vous” (you plural or formal you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Décidez maintenant, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Decide now, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person plural (“we”). Mostly used in writing, stories, or formal history.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après une longue discussion, nous décidâmes de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a long discussion, we decided to leave.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing (stories, novels, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils décidèrent de partir tôt le lendemain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to leave early the next day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai décidé de partir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to leave tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a l’air très décidé à réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems very determined to succeed.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est décidée à réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to succeed.

definitions.note: Often used to express the speaker’s judgment or mild frustration (like “honestly” or “seriously”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Décidément, tu arrives toujours en retard !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Honestly, you’re always late!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un moment décisif pour notre projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a decisive moment for our project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision difficile à prendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a difficult decision to make.

definitions.note: Plural of « décision ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons pris plusieurs décisions importantes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We made several important decisions today.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le témoin déclara qu’il avait tout vu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness stated that he had seen everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait une déclaration à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a statement to the police.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., to declare something officially or to state something publicly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle déclare qu’elle est prête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She states that she is ready.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., declaring income, declaring something to the police).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il doit déclarer ses revenus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to declare his income.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with "tu" (informal singular "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu déclares tes revenus en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You declare your income online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a déclaré ses revenus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He declared his income.

definitions.note: Often used for starting an event or reaction (an alarm, a process, a crisis, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette photo peut déclencher une vive réaction.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This photo can trigger a strong reaction.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’alarme s’est déclenchée et a déclenché une évacuation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The alarm went off and triggered an evacuation.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il déclina l’invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He declined the invitation.

definitions.note: Often used for politely refusing an invitation or offer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais décliner l'invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to decline the invitation.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (administration, customer service): “décliner son nom / son identité”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veuillez décliner votre nom et votre adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please state your name and your address.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a décliné l’invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He declined the invitation.

definitions.note: Used in grammar to say a noun/adjective changes form (cases, endings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En latin, ce nom est décliné au génitif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Latin, this noun is declined in the genitive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le décollage est prévu à 8 h 15.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The takeoff is scheduled for 8:15.

definitions.note: Most often used for a plane leaving the ground (or more generally, starting to rise).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion décolle à 8 h 15.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane takes off at 8:15.

definitions.note: Used when something stuck on a surface stops sticking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’étiquette décolle du carton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The label is peeling off the cardboard.

definitions.note: Used for planes/rockets (literal) and also for leaving quickly or starting to succeed (figurative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion va décoller dans dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to take off in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion a décollé à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avait l’air déconcerté par cette question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked confused by that question.

definitions.native: messes around, screws up, talks nonsense
definitions.note: Informal/slang; can be used as an imperative: « Déconne pas ! » = “Don’t mess around / Don’t talk nonsense.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de déconner, on est en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop messing around, we’re late.

definitions.native: to mess up, to screw up
definitions.note: Informal/slang; can be a bit rude depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espère ne pas déconner pendant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I don’t mess up during the exam.

definitions.native: to mess around, to fool around, to joke
definitions.note: Informal/slang; often used like “Arrête de déconner !” = “Stop kidding around!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de déconner, ce n’est pas drôle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop kidding around, it’s not funny.

definitions.note: Informal; often used to tell someone to stop joking/being silly, or that you think what they said is not serious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mais tu déconnes ou quoi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you kidding or what?

definitions.note: Very informal/colloquial; can sound rude depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mais vous déconnez !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you kidding me?!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin déconseille ce médicament.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor advises against this medication.

definitions.note: Often used for the surroundings/background of a place (in real life, theater, film, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le décor de ce film est magnifique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The setting of this movie is magnificent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La décoration de la salle est très jolie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decoration of the room is very pretty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons accroché des décorations dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hung decorations in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il décore la salle pour la fête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decorates the room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va décorer la salle pour la fête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to decorate the room for the party.

definitions.note: Past participle of "décorer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont décoré la salle pour la fête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decorated the room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle découpe une image dans le magazine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cuts out a picture from the magazine.

definitions.native: to cut up, to cut out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais découper le gâteau en parts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to cut the cake into slices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne te laisse pas décourager par cet échec.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t let this failure discourage you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après cet échec, il se sent découragé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After that failure, he feels discouraged.

definitions.note: Used mainly in banking (e.g., « un découvert bancaire »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai un découvert sur mon compte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an overdraft on my account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai découvert un bon restaurant près d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I discovered a good restaurant near here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette découverte a changé notre façon de comprendre l’histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This discovery changed our way of understanding history.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « découvrir »; used with a feminine noun in compound tenses or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vérité est découverte par le journaliste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truth is discovered by the journalist.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les découvertes scientifiques ont changé le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientific discoveries have changed the world.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il découvre la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He discovers the truth.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of « découvrir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu découvres une nouvelle ville aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re discovering a new city today.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present (also used as a polite singular "you" with "vous").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Découvrez notre nouvelle collection en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Discover our new collection online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais découvrir la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to discover the truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in literature and storytelling; often corresponds to the everyday past tense « a découvert ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle découvrit une lettre cachée dans le tiroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She discovered a letter hidden in the drawer.

definitions.note: Present tense of « découvrir » with « nous »; often used as an invitation/suggestion (“let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Découvrons cette ville à pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s discover this city on foot.

definitions.note: Conditional present (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je décrirais cette ville comme très agréable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would describe this city as very pleasant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu décrire ta maison ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you describe your house?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) conditional present form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comment décririez-vous votre ville à un touriste ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How would you describe your city to a tourist?

definitions.note: Present tense form of « décrire » (used with je/tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je décris la scène en détail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I describe the scene in detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle décrit la scène en détail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She describes the scene in detail.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils décrivent le problème en détail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They describe the problem in detail.

definitions.note: Formal or plural form of “describe” (used with vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Décrivez votre maison, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Describe your house, please.

definitions.note: Used for answering a call (literally taking the receiver off the hook).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il décroche le téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picks up the phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il décroche le tableau du mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the picture down from the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va décrocher le tableau du mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to take the painting down from the wall.

definitions.note: Commonly used for answering a phone call.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va décrocher dès la première sonnerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to pick up on the first ring.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (vous form), for example when addressing one person formally or several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Décrochez le tableau, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take down the painting, please.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (vous form), for example when addressing one person formally or several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Décrochez, je vous en prie !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pick up, please!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai décroché le tableau du mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the picture down from the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a décroché dès la première sonnerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up on the first ring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le décès de mon grand-père a beaucoup attristé la famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather’s death saddened the family a lot.

definitions.note: Used especially in formal contexts (e.g., announcements, administrative language).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son grand-père est décédé en 2020.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His grandfather died in 2020.

definitions.note: Usually used to say someone has died; sounds more formal than "mort".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon grand-père est décédé l’année dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather passed away last year.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle (used with a feminine subject, often with « être » in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est décédée hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She died last night.

definitions.note: Used with être in compound tenses; refers to people (more formal than "morts").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont décédés en 2010.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They died in 2010.

definitions.note: Formal term, often used in official contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les deux témoins sont décédés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two witnesses are deceased.

definitions.note: Often used for an inscription in a book written by the author (sometimes with a signature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai eu une dédicace de l’auteur dans mon livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a dedication from the author in my book.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « dédier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dédie ce livre à sa sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dedicates this book to his sister.

definitions.note: Past participle of « dédier », often used with « être » or in passive constructions (e.g., « être dédié à… » = “be dedicated to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est dédié à ma mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is dedicated to my mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une déduction sur mes impôts cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a deduction on my taxes this year.

definitions.note: In logic or reasoning, it can mean a conclusion you draw from information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Par déduction, elle comprend la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By inference, she understands the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On peut déduire la réponse à partir de ces indices.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can deduce the answer from these clues.

definitions.note: Often used for amounts (money, points, taxes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux déduire 10 euros du total.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can deduct 10 euros from the total.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Athéna est une déesse grecque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Athena is a Greek goddess.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La batterie est défaillante, donc le téléphone s’éteint souvent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The battery is faulty, so the phone often turns off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu défaire ce nœud ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you undo this knot?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne défais pas le nœud, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t undo the knot, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « défaire »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai défait… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai défait le nœud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I untied the knot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la défaite, l’équipe est rentrée au vestiaire en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the defeat, the team went back to the locker room in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce téléphone a un défaut : la batterie se vide trop vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This phone has a defect: the battery runs down too fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce produit a plusieurs défauts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product has several defects.

definitions.note: Used for things (products, devices, parts) that don’t work properly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet appareil est défectueux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This device is defective.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle défend son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She defends her friend.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) of « défendre » in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils défendent leur équipe jusqu'au bout.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They defend their team to the very end.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the formal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous défendez votre opinion avec calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You defend your opinion calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais défendre mon ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to defend my friend.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « défendre » (used with « je » or « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te défends contre ces accusations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I defend you against these accusations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a défendu son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He defended his friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La défense de l’équipe est très solide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's defense is very solid.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « se mettre en défense » (to take a defensive stance) or « en état de légitime défense » (in self-defense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il agit en état de légitime défense.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is acting in self-defense.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les défenses de l’équipe sont solides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's defenses are solid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Courir un marathon est un défi pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Running a marathon is a challenge for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le budget est en déficit cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The budget is in deficit this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il défie son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He challenges his friend.

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form of « défier » with « vous » (you plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous défiez les règles sans raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You defy the rules for no reason.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cicatrice défigurait son visage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scar disfigured his face.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les soldats vont défiler dans les rues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers are going to parade through the streets.

definitions.note: Used for scrolling on a screen (a page, a feed, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux défiler vers le bas pour voir la suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can scroll down to see the rest.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « définir » (can mean “I define” or “you define”), and also the imperative “define!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je définis ce mot dans mon cahier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I define this word in my notebook.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Définissez ce mot, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Define this word, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu lire la définition de ce mot ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you read the definition of this word?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision définitive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a final decision.

definitions.note: Often means something is final or permanent (not temporary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a quitté l’entreprise définitivement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the company for good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces défis sont difficiles, mais possibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These challenges are difficult, but possible.

definitions.native: to smash in, to break down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a essayé de défoncer la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to smash the door in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mur est défoncé après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall is smashed in after the accident.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can refer to being very drunk or very high (often crude).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est complètement défoncé ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s completely wasted tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l'accident, l'avant de la voiture était complètement défoncé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the front of the car was completely wrecked.

definitions.note: Informal slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il était défoncé après avoir fumé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was really high after smoking.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean something is badly damaged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porte est complètement défoncée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is completely smashed in.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le travail, je suis défoncée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I'm exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce miroir déforme ton visage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That mirror distorts your face.

definitions.note: Used mainly to talk about a person who has died; often placed before the noun (e.g., « mon défunt mari »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle souvent de son défunt mari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She often talks about her late husband.

definitions.note: Often used as an (informal) order.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dégage !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get out!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce produit dégage une odeur forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product gives off a strong smell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais dégager la table après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to clear the table after dinner.

definitions.native: to give off, emit (a smell, heat, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce fromage va dégager une forte odeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese is going to give off a strong smell.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command: « Dégage ! » = “Get out!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il doit dégager d’ici tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to get out of here right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dégages la table après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You clear the table after dinner.

definitions.note: Often used as an order; can sound rude depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dégagez d’ici !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get out of here!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dégagez la table, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clear the table, please.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that has been cleared (e.g., the sky, a path, a space).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ciel est dégagé aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is clear today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le passage est dégagé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passage is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a un style dégagé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a relaxed style.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La route est dégagée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is clear.

definitions.note: Often describes a person’s attitude or style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une attitude dégagée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a relaxed attitude.

definitions.note: Usually used for drawing a sword, gun, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dégainez votre épée !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw your sword!

definitions.note: Past participle of “dégoter” (to find, often after searching).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai dégoté une bonne affaire sur Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a good deal on the internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La peinture dégoulinait le long du mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paint was dripping down the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment dégoûtant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really disgusting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette odeur est vraiment dégoûtante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That smell is really disgusting.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; it can also agree with a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces aliments sont dégoûtants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These foods are disgusting.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me dégoûtes avec tes mensonges.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You disgust me with your lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis dégoûté par cette odeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disgusted by that smell.

definitions.note: Common in everyday speech to mean you’re upset or disappointed about something (not necessarily physically disgusted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis dégoûté, j’ai raté mon train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m so fed up—I missed my train.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar (strong negative tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sandwich est dégueulasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sandwich is disgusting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour Halloween, j'ai acheté un déguisement de pirate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Halloween, I bought a pirate costume.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour Carnaval, les enfants choisissent des déguisements colorés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Carnival, the children choose colorful costumes.

definitions.note: Also used reflexively: se déguiser = to dress up (in costume).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour entrer sans être reconnu, il a décidé de déguiser sa voix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To get in without being recognized, he decided to disguise his voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour la fête, ils sont tous déguisés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the party, they are all in costume.

definitions.native: to taste; to savor (food or drink appreciatively)
definitions.note: Used for eating or drinking something with attention and appreciation (e.g., wine, a good meal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons déguster un fromage local avec du pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to taste a local cheese with bread.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used for damage in general (e.g., after an accident or storm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tempête a causé de gros dégâts dans la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm caused major damage in the city.

definitions.native: to degenerate; to deteriorate; to get worse
definitions.note: Used for situations, relationships, debates, or events that turn bad or out of control.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans dialogue, la situation peut dégénérer rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without dialogue, the situation can quickly degenerate.

definitions.native: to turn ugly; to spiral out of control (of a situation)
definitions.note: Often implies escalation (e.g., into conflict or violence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La dispute a commencé calmement, puis tout a dégénéré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The argument started calmly, then everything spiraled out of control.

definitions.note: Technical/medical sense: to undergo degeneration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec l’âge, certains tissus peuvent dégénérer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With age, some tissues can degenerate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situation a dégénéré très vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation got worse very quickly.

definitions.note: Informal short form of “déjeuner”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se retrouve pour le déj à midi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shall we meet for lunch at noon?

definitions.note: Commonly written as “déjà”; here kept as “déja” to match the requested spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai déja vu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already seen it.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je déjeunais avec mes collègues tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to have lunch with my coworkers every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je déjeune à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have lunch at noon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se retrouve pour déjeuner à midi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shall we meet up for lunch at noon?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais déjeuner avec mes collègues à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have lunch with my colleagues at noon.

definitions.note: Usually means “have lunch” in the present tense with “tu” (informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu déjeunes à midi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have lunch at noon?

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the polite singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous déjeunez à quelle heure ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time do you have lunch?

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we"), often used as a suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjeunons sur la terrasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s have lunch on the terrace.

definitions.note: Past participle of « déjeuner », used with an auxiliary (e.g., « j’ai déjeuné »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déjà déjeuné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already had lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déjà déjeuné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already had lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai déjà mangé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already eaten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons respecter le délai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to meet the deadline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le délai d'attente est de dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiting time is ten minutes.

definitions.note: Plural of « délai ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons respecter les délais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to meet the deadlines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a délibérément ignoré ma question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deliberately ignored my question.

definitions.note: Often used for things that can break easily or that need careful handling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce vase est très délicat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This vase is very delicate.

definitions.note: Used for situations, topics, or people that require tact or careful treatment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une question délicate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive question.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « délicat ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette situation est très délicate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This situation is very delicate.

definitions.note: Used for situations or topics that require care and tact.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une question délicate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a délicatement posé le verre sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gently placed the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces documents sont délicats et doivent rester confidentiels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These documents are sensitive and must remain confidential.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: « des délices ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau est un délice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is a delight.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette tarte est délicieuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tart is delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau est délicieusement moelleux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is deliciously soft.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces crêpes sont délicieuses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These crêpes are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau est délicieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté deux délinquants hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two offenders last night.

definitions.note: Often used for a state of delirium (medical or from fever), and more generally for talking nonsense or an absurd situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec la fièvre, il est tombé dans le délire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the fever, he fell into delirium.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il délire depuis hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s been delirious since last night.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “you’re talking crazy / that’s ridiculous.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu délires si tu crois que ça va marcher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re talking nonsense if you think that’s going to work.

definitions.note: Often used in official contexts (e.g., délivrance d’un document).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La délivrance du passeport prend environ deux semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The issuance of the passport takes about two weeks.

definitions.note: Can also mean being freed (from something difficult) or feeling relief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’examen, elle a ressenti une grande délivrance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the exam, she felt great relief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le facteur délivre le colis ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mail carrier delivers the package this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce médicament délivre la douleur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine relieves the pain.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for a very large amount of something (e.g., a deluge of emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la tempête, il y a eu un déluge dans la vallée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, there was a flood in the valley.

definitions.note: Often used for an elected or appointed representative (e.g., in a company, union, or at a conference).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le délégué a présenté la proposition au comité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegate presented the proposal to the committee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma peau démange depuis ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My skin has been itching since this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le démarrage de l’ordinateur est très lent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer’s startup is very slow.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a vehicle or a machine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture démarre tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car starts right away.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a machine, vehicle, or process.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais démarrer la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to start the car.

definitions.note: Used with tu (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu démarres la voiture maintenant ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you starting the car now?

definitions.note: Often used for starting a machine, vehicle, or activity; can also be used to mean “get going.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Démarrez l’ordinateur, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Start the computer, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film a démarré à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie started at eight o'clock.

definitions.native: to unmask; to expose (someone/something hidden or deceptive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le journaliste a démasqué le mensonge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist exposed the lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La démence affecte la mémoire et le langage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dementia affects memory and language.

definitions.note: Strong/old-fashioned; can feel harsh. Often used in fixed expressions like « une idée démente » (a crazy idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une idée démente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an insane idea.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts with « être démis de ses fonctions » (to be removed from one’s duties/position).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été démis de ses fonctions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was removed from his duties.

definitions.note: Used about a joint (e.g., shoulder): « se démettre l’épaule ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est démis l’épaule en tombant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dislocated his shoulder when he fell.

definitions.note: Used mainly for leaving a job or official position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a donné sa démission hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handed in his resignation yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le scandale, il démissionna immédiatement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the scandal, he resigned immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il démissionne de son poste demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He resigns from his position tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for leaving a job, office, or official position (often formally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a décidé de démissionner de son poste vendredi dernier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to resign from her position last Friday.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive, 2nd person plural (vous); mostly used in formal/literary French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous démissionniez avant la fin du mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to resign before the end of the month.

definitions.note: Used when someone quits a job or position (often formally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a démissionné de son poste la semaine dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He resigned from his position last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La démocratie repose sur des élections libres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Democracy is based on free elections.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous voulons un système plus démocratique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want a more democratic system.

definitions.native: go out of fashion, go out of style
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces styles démodent vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These styles go out of fashion quickly.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est démodée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is out of fashion.

definitions.note: Past participle of « démolir »; often used with « être » in the passive (e.g., « a été démoli »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ancien immeuble a été démoli l'année dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old building was demolished last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont démolir cet immeuble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to demolish this building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On raconte qu’un démon hante cette vieille maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say a demon haunts that old house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu un rire démoniaque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He let out a demonic laugh.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La légende parle de démons qui vivent dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The legend talks about demons that live in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur a fait une démonstration pour expliquer l’expérience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher did a demonstration to explain the experiment.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « une démonstration » to mean a public demonstration (protest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu une grande démonstration dans le centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a big protest downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va démonter le meuble pour le transporter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to take the piece of furniture apart to transport it.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., a comment or event makes someone lose their confidence or composure).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette remarque l’a fait démonter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That remark threw him off.

definitions.note: Used for changing homes (moving to a new place), not for moving an object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il déménage demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s moving tomorrow.

definitions.native: move (house), move to a new place
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons déménager à Lyon en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to move to Lyon in June.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu). Used for moving to a new home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu déménages quand ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you moving?

definitions.note: Used for changing residence (moving house).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déménagé la semaine dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved last week.

definitions.note: Often used when you find something after searching (like a good deal, a rare item, or a hidden place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déniché un bon restaurant près d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a good restaurant near here.

definitions.note: Often used for reporting someone or something to the authorities (e.g., a crime, fraud).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dénonce une fraude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reports a fraud.

definitions.native: to report (to the authorities); to inform on
definitions.note: Often implies reporting something illegal or unacceptable to an authority; can also suggest informing against someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a décidé de dénoncer le vol à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to report the theft to the police.

definitions.note: Used for openly condemning a person, action, or situation (often in a moral or political sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a voulu dénoncer la corruption lors de la conférence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wanted to denounce corruption at the conference.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la tempête, les arbres étaient dénudés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the trees were bare.

definitions.note: Usually used with "de": "dénué de" + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est dénué de courage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lacks courage.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; commonly used with de + noun (e.g., dénuée de sens).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette explication est dénuée de sens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This explanation is devoid of meaning.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; usually followed by « de » + noun (e.g., « dénuées de courage »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces accusations sont dénuées de preuves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These accusations are devoid of evidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai oublié mon déodorant ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my deodorant this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La dépanneuse arrive pour remorquer la voiture en panne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tow truck is coming to tow the broken-down car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le départ du train est à 8 h 15.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train’s departure is at 8:15.

definitions.note: In France, a « département » is also an administrative area (similar to a county).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon père travaille dans le département informatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father works in the IT department.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette voiture dépasse le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car passes the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les frais dépassent notre budget.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The costs exceed our budget.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sur l’autoroute, une voiture peut dépasser une autre voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the highway, one car can overtake another car.

definitions.note: Often used with amounts, limits, or time (e.g., speed limits, budgets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu ne dois pas dépasser la limite de vitesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not exceed the speed limit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai dépassé la limite de vitesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exceeded the speed limit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce style est dépassé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This style is outdated.

definitions.note: Often used with a person (e.g., "Je suis dépassé") to mean you can’t keep up or don’t know what to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis dépassé par tout ce travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m overwhelmed by all this work.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "ça dépend de…" = "it depends on…").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça dépend du jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It depends on the day.

definitions.note: Often used about being dependent on someone/something (including addiction in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une forte dépendance au café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a strong dependence on coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "dependent on" (e.g., "dépendant de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est dépendant de ses parents pour l’argent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dependent on his parents for money.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural (they) of « dépendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils dépendent de leurs parents pour payer le loyer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They depend on their parents to pay the rent.

definitions.note: First-person plural present ("we"). Often used with "de" (depend on) or "de" + infinitive (it depends on doing something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous dépendons de nos parents pour le logement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We depend on our parents for housing.

definitions.note: Usually used with « de »: « dépendre de » = “to depend on.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout peut dépendre de toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything can depend on you.

definitions.note: Used mainly in legal contexts (often in the phrase « aux dépens de quelqu’un »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été condamné aux dépens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was ordered to pay the legal costs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle dépense beaucoup d’argent au supermarché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spends a lot of money at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne veux pas dépenser trop d'argent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to spend too much money.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos dépenses ont augmenté ce mois-ci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our expenses increased this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai dépensé trop d’argent ce mois-ci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent too much money this month.

definitions.note: Often used in a medical context (e.g., cancer screening, COVID testing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dépistage du cancer du sein est recommandé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breast cancer screening is recommended.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle déplace la chaise dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moves the chair in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon déplacement à Lyon a été annulé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My trip to Lyon was canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le déplacement du meuble a été difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Moving the piece of furniture was difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils déplacent les chaises dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They move the chairs in the room.

definitions.note: Often used for moving something/someone from one place to another (physically or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais déplacer la table près de la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to move the table near the window.

definitions.note: Command form (vous) meaning “move” or “move (something)” addressed to one person formally or to a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déplacez cette chaise, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move this chair, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déplacé la table pour faire de la place.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved the table to make room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa remarque était vraiment déplacée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His remark was really inappropriate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’inondation, plusieurs familles ont été déplacées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flood, several families were displaced.

definitions.note: Often used for comments, jokes, or remarks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses blagues étaient déplacées pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His jokes were inappropriate during the meeting.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mostly used in writing; corresponds to “moved” in English narrative style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il déplaça la chaise près de la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved the chair near the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le déploiement du nouveau site web aura lieu lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deployment of the new website will take place on Monday.

definitions.note: Command form (vous) or present tense with « vous »: « vous déployez » = “you deploy/unfold.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déployez la carte sur la table, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfold the map on the table, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’antenne est déployée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The antenna is deployed.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in literature and formal writing; in conversation you usually see "a déposé".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il déposa son sac sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put down his bag on the table.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in literature and formal writing; in conversation you usually see "a déposé".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle déposa une plainte au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She filed a complaint at the police station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dépose les clés sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the keys down on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dépose une plainte au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He files a complaint at the police station.

definitions.native: to put down, to set down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux déposer ton sac ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can put your bag down here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais déposer les enfants à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to drop the kids off at school.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/legal contexts (e.g., déposer une plainte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va déposer une plainte au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to file a complaint at the police station.

definitions.note: Used with « vous »: “you” (plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déposez le sac sur la table, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the bag down on the table, please.

definitions.note: Usually a formal statement given to the police or in court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le témoin a fait une déposition au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness gave a statement at the police station.

definitions.note: Past participle of « déposer »; often used for leaving something somewhere (e.g., dropping off a package).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déposé le colis à la poste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dropped off the package at the post office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dépotoir municipal est plein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The municipal dump is full.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + noun: "dépourvu de" = "devoid of / lacking".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce quartier est dépourvu de transports en commun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This neighborhood is lacking public transportation.

definitions.note: Usually used with « de » (e.g., « dépourvu de + noun »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est dépourvu de patience.
