definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to endure a lot of pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon enfance était heureuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My childhood was happy.

definitions.note: Old spelling of « enfants »; seen in older texts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce livre ancien, on lit : « Les enfans jouent dans la cour. »
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this old book, you read: “The children are playing in the yard.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet enfant aime lire des histoires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This child likes reading stories.

definitions.note: plural of « enfant »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants jouent dans le parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selon la légende, ce château est hanté et mène à l'enfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the legend, this castle is haunted and leads to hell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enferme son vélo dans le garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He locks up his bike in the garage.

definitions.native: to lock up; to shut in; to confine
definitions.note: Used when someone/something is locked inside a place (room, cage, etc.) or kept confined.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va enfermer le chien dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to lock the dog in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Past participle of « enfermer »; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est enfermé dans sa chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is locked up in his room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien est enfermé dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is locked up in the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porte est enfermée à clé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is locked with a key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont enfermés dans la pièce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are locked in the room.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les animaux sont enfermés dans leur cage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The animals are locked up in their cage.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular; in modern French this tense is mostly used in writing (stories, novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enfila son manteau et sortit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put on his coat and went out.

definitions.note: Often used for putting on clothes or quickly slipping something onto a thread/line.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enfile sa veste avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on his jacket before going out.

definitions.native: to put on (clothes), to slip on
definitions.note: Often used for putting on clothes quickly or easily (e.g., a shirt, a sweater).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais enfiler mon manteau avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put on my coat before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle essaie d’enfiler une aiguille avec ce fil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s trying to thread a needle with this thread.

definitions.note: Used for putting on clothing (or slipping something on), especially by inserting an arm/leg into it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfilez votre manteau, il fait froid dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your coat; it’s cold outside.

definitions.note: Often used to show relief or impatience; can also introduce a correction or a conclusion depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfin, nous sommes arrivés !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, we arrived!

definitions.note: Often expresses relief, impatience, or emphasis (like “well, anyway”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfin, tu es là !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, you're here!

definitions.note: Often used in medical contexts (a swollen area of the body).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une enflure au poignet depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had swelling in my wrist since yesterday.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la piqûre, ses bras sont enflés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the sting, his arms are swollen.

definitions.note: Very vulgar insult in French; avoid in polite conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête, enfoiré !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop it, asshole!

definitions.note: Very vulgar insult (offensive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet enfoiré m’a volé mon portefeuille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That asshole stole my wallet.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un enfoiré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He's an asshole.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar insult; can be used as an adjective or like a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est vraiment enfoiré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s really an asshole.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and insulting (swear word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces enfoirés ont encore cassé la machine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those assholes broke the machine again.

definitions.note: Very vulgar insult (strongly offensive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces enfoirés ont encore menti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those assholes lied again.

definitions.native: to push in; to drive in
definitions.note: For forcing something into something else (e.g., a nail into wood) or pushing part of an object inward.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va enfoncer le clou dans le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to drive the nail into the wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of « enfoncer »; often used for something pressed/forced into place (e.g., a nail, a door).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le clou est bien enfoncé dans le mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nail is firmly driven into the wall.

definitions.note: Used with laws, rules, or agreements (e.g., “enfreindre la loi”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va enfreindre la loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to break the law.

definitions.note: Used for breaking a rule, law, agreement, etc. (not for physically breaking an object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enfreint la loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He breaks the law.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "s'enfuir" (to run away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tu as peur, tu t’enfuis tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re scared, you run away right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il engage un nouveau professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hires a new teacher.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « engager sa parole » (to give/pledge one’s word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il engage sa parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives his word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son engagement envers son équipe est remarquable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His commitment to his team is remarkable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’entreprise va engager deux nouveaux employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to hire two new employees.

definitions.note: Often used with "s'engager" for committing oneself (e.g., to a cause or a project).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va engager sa responsabilité en signant ce document.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to commit his responsibility by signing this document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Engagez un avocat pour ce dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hire a lawyer for this case.

definitions.note: Often addressed to “you” plural or formal (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Engagez-vous à aider demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Commit to helping tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “hired/employed” (not necessarily “engaged” in the sense of being engaged to be married—that’s usually "fiancé(e)").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est engagé comme serveur dans ce restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is hired as a waiter in this restaurant.

definitions.note: Often used for someone actively involved in a cause (social, political, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très engagée dans la protection de l’environnement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very committed to protecting the environment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est engagée par cette entreprise depuis mars.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been hired by this company since March.

definitions.note: Often used with "dans" to mean committed/involved in a cause or activity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est engagée dans une association.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is committed/involved in an association.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très engagée dans la protection de l’environnement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very committed to protecting the environment.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; often used with être (e.g., « elles sont engagées ») or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont engagées dans une association.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are committed to an organization.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; often used in the passive to mean “were hired.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles ont été engagées comme serveuses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were hired as waitresses.

definitions.note: Often used in the passive to mean “hired” or “taken on (for a job)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été engagés hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were hired yesterday.

definitions.note: In French, this commonly means “committed/involved” (e.g., in a cause). It does not usually mean “engaged (to be married)”, which is typically “fiancé(e)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont engagés dans la protection de l’environnement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are committed to protecting the environment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La peur engendre la violence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fear causes violence.

definitions.note: Often refers to a mechanical device or piece of equipment; in everyday speech it can be a vague word for “thing” when talking about a machine or vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet engin est très bruyant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This machine is very noisy.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a body part that has lost feeling (e.g., from cold or staying in one position).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai les doigts engourdis à cause du froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My fingers are numb because of the cold.

definitions.note: Commonly used to describe a person who is not fully awake or alert.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le matin, je suis encore engourdi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning, I’m still groggy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On ajoute de l’engrais au jardin au printemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We add fertilizer to the garden in the spring.

definitions.note: Often used for what is at risk or what matters in a situation (e.g., in politics, business, or a debate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut comprendre les enjeux avant de prendre une décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to understand the stakes before making a decision.

definitions.note: Past participle often used as an adjective (e.g., describing people holding each other closely).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le couple est enlacé sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The couple is entwined on the couch.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in literature and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enleva son manteau avant d’entrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He removed his coat before going in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux enlever tes chaussures, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take off your shoes, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La serveuse va enlever les assiettes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waitress is going to take away the plates.

definitions.note: Command form (addressing one person formally or more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enlevez vos chaussures, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take off your shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai enlevé mes chaussures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took off my shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tache a été enlevée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stain was removed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fille a été enlevée hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl was kidnapped last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les panneaux ont été enlevés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The signs were removed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enlève son manteau en entrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes off his coat when he comes in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le criminel enlève la victime en pleine rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The criminal kidnaps the victim in the middle of the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police enquête sur l’enlèvement d’un enfant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the kidnapping of a child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu enlèves ton manteau, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take off your coat, please?

definitions.note: As an adjective, it agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes (e.g., ennemi / ennemie / ennemis / ennemies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un pays ennemi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an enemy country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet homme est mon ennemi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That man is my enemy.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des forces ennemies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are enemy forces.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective (often used like a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont ennemis depuis longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been enemies for a long time.

definitions.note: Plural form of « ennemi ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont vaincu leurs ennemis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They defeated their enemies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ennui me gagne pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Boredom takes over during the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with an object pronoun (e.g., « m'ennuie » = ‘bores me’). With the reflexive form « s'ennuyer » (e.g., « je m'ennuie »), it means ‘to be bored’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film m'ennuie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie bores me.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (des ennuis) to mean “trouble(s)” or “problems.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu des ennuis avec la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got into trouble with the police.

definitions.note: Often used about things/situations as “boring” and about people/behavior as “annoying.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment ennuyant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really boring.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette émission est vraiment ennuyante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This show is really boring.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces réunions sont vraiment ennuyantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These meetings are really boring.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces cours sont vraiment ennuyants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These classes are really boring.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as "s’ennuyer" = "to be bored".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film va ennuyer tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is going to bore everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit du voisin va m’ennuyer toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbor’s noise is going to annoy me all night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette leçon est ennuyeuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This lesson is boring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment ennuyeux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really boring.

definitions.note: Can also mean “to be bored” in the reflexive form: « vous vous ennuyez » = “you are bored.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous ennuyez votre sœur avec ces blagues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You annoy your sister with those jokes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis ennuyé en classe aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m bored in class today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis ennuyé par ce bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by that noise.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “annoyed”; it usually means “bored” rather than “annoyed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis ennuyé pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am bored during the meeting.

definitions.note: Past participle of the reflexive verb « s’enquérir de » (“to inquire about”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis enquis de son état.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I inquired about how he was doing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police ouvre une enquête après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police open an investigation after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’enquête sur la disparition de ce tableau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m investigating the disappearance of that painting.

definitions.note: Often used for police investigations or formal inquiries (e.g., journalists investigating a story).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police va enquêter sur le vol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to investigate the theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enquêteurs interrogent les témoins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigators question the witnesses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a enquêté sur l'affaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police investigated the case.

definitions.note: Often used in a strong, intense sense; can describe people or animals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il était enragé contre son voisin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was furious with his neighbor.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est enragée contre lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is furious with him.

definitions.note: Often used for a mechanism or object that won’t move properly (e.g., a door, a wheel, a machine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porte est enrayée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is jammed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle enregistre la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She records the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai écouté l’enregistrement de la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened to the recording of the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used for signing up or registering something, especially in official or administrative contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enregistrement du véhicule est obligatoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Registering the vehicle is mandatory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai supprimé les enregistrements de mon téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deleted the recordings from my phone.

definitions.native: to record, to register, to save
definitions.note: Often used for recording audio/video, registering something officially, or saving data/files.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais enregistrer cette émission pour la regarder plus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to record this show to watch it later.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command ("you" plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enregistrez votre travail avant de fermer le document.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save your work before closing the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai enregistré la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recorded the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used for being officially entered into a list/system (e.g., a hotel, an exam, an account).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis enregistré à l’hôtel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked in (registered) at the hotel.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the past participle of « enregistrer »; it agrees with a feminine noun (often used with « être » or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunion est enregistrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is recorded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis enrhumé depuis trois jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had a cold for three days.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis enrhumée depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had a cold since yesterday.

definitions.note: Used literally (to make richer) or figuratively (to make something more interesting/valuable).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce voyage va enrichir mon expérience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That trip is going to enrich my experience.

definitions.note: Past participle of « enrouler »; often used like an adjective to mean something is rolled up or wrapped around something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le câble est enroulé autour du poteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cable is wrapped around the pole.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est revenu ensanglanté après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back bloodstained after the accident.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, il enseignait le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he was teaching French at school.

definitions.note: Used for a teacher in general; often implies a school teacher.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enseignant explique la leçon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the lesson.

definitions.note: female teacher (feminine form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enseignante explique la leçon aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the lesson to the students.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enseignantes de l’école sont très patientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school’s female teachers are very patient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enseignants travaillent à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers work at the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle enseigne le français à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She teaches French at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enseignement est important pour l’avenir des enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Education is important for children’s future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va enseigner le français à l'université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to teach French at the university.

definitions.note: Formal or plural “you” form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous enseignez le français à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You teach French at the university.

definitions.note: Present tense: “we teach” (also used for “let’s teach”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous enseignons le français à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We teach French at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai enseigné le français pendant deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I taught French for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous travaillons bien ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We work well together.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « un ensemble de … » meaning “a set/group of …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet ensemble de livres est pour la classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This set of books is for the class.

definitions.note: Past participle of « enseveler »; often used literally (buried in the ground) or figuratively (hidden/covered under something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le village a été enseveli sous la neige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village was buried under the snow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons dîné, et ensuite nous sommes rentrés à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had dinner, and then we went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une entaille sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a notch on the table.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « entendre »; it can also mean “understands” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entend un bruit étrange dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hears a strange noise in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « entendre » (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'entendais de la musique dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I could hear music in the street.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often implies an ongoing situation in the past (“was hearing/used to hear”) or a repeated past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, j’entendait la musique de la rue tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I heard the music from the street every evening.

definitions.note: Present participle of « entendre »; often means “while hearing” or “upon hearing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entendant son nom, elle s’est retournée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hearing her name, she turned around.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after « il faut que »). Not related to English “intend.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que j'entende la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hear the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils entendent un bruit dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hear a noise in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils entendent la question, mais ils ne savent pas la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They understand the question, but they don’t know the answer.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense; also used as a formal singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous entendez la musique ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you hear the music?

definitions.note: Used with « vous » (plural or formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous entendiez la musique depuis la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could hear the music from the street.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « entendre »; in everyday speech, French usually uses « a entendu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entendit un bruit derrière la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He heard a noise behind the door.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “to understand” or “to intend,” but it primarily means “to hear.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous entendons de la musique dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hear music in the street.

definitions.note: Simple future (3rd person singular) of « entendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entendra la musique depuis sa chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will hear the music from his room.

definitions.note: Often used for actually hearing a sound (not just listening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu entendre la musique dans la rue ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you hear the music in the street?

definitions.note: In French, “entendre” can also mean “to understand” (often in the sense of grasping what someone means).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’arrive pas à entendre ce que tu veux dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t understand what you mean.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present tense of « entendre » (used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu entends la musique ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you hear the music?

definitions.note: Past participle of « entendre »; commonly used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai entendu… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai entendu un bruit dans le couloir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a noise in the hallway.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « entendre » (used with avoir when the direct object is feminine and comes before the verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai entendue dans le couloir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard her in the hallway.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « entendre » (used with avoir when the direct object is feminine and comes before the verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai bien entendue, mais je ne suis pas d’accord.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood her well, but I don’t agree.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « entendre ». Often used in the passive (e.g., « ont été entendues » = “were heard”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les paroles ont été entendues par tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The words were heard by everyone.

definitions.note: Past participle of « entendre »; depending on context it can also mean “understood.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous les avons entendus dans le couloir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard them in the hallway.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 1st person plural ("we"); mainly used in literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous entendîmes un bruit étrange dans la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard a strange noise in the night.

definitions.note: Often used for good relations or mutual understanding between people, groups, or countries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une bonne entente entre les voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a good understanding between the neighbors.

definitions.note: Looks like English “enter,” but it means “bury.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enterre le trésor dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He buries the treasure in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’enterrement aura lieu samedi matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The funeral will take place on Saturday morning.

definitions.note: Often used for burying a person (a funeral) or burying something in the ground.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont enterrer leur chien dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to bury their dog in the garden.

definitions.note: Command form ("you" plural/formal), and also the present tense for "you" plural/formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enterrez ce trésor dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bury this treasure in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est enterré au cimetière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is buried in the cemetery.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « enterrer »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été enterrée hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was buried yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle used as an adjective, masculine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les trésors sont enterrés sous le sable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasures are buried under the sand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle de son projet avec beaucoup d’enthousiasme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She talks about her project with a lot of enthusiasm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très enthousiaste à l’idée de commencer ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very enthusiastic about the idea of starting this project.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont enthousiastes à propos du voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are enthusiastic about the trip.

definitions.note: Often used for things that are complete or not divided (e.g., a whole cake, an entire day).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mangé le gâteau entier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons mangé des légumes entiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate whole vegetables.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mangé la pizza entière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis entièrement d’accord avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entirely agree with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis fait une entorse à la cheville en courant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sprained my ankle while running.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une clôture entoure le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fence surrounds the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les arbres entourent la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trees surround the house.

definitions.note: Past participle of « entourer »; often used with « être » in the passive (e.g., « il est entouré de… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le château est entouré de douves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle is surrounded by a moat.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « entourer »; often used with « être » (e.g., « elle est entourée… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est entourée d'amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is surrounded by friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont entourés d'amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are surrounded by friends.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past form (passé simple), common in books and stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entra dans la pièce sans faire de bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entered the room without making a sound.

definitions.note: Often used with a plural subject or in the pronominal form « s’entraider ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette équipe, on doit entraider les nouveaux collègues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this team, we have to help the new colleagues (and support one another).

definitions.note: Often used in the plural; can also be used figuratively for the inside of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin examine ses entrailles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines his intestines.

definitions.note: Imperfect form (past, ongoing or habitual action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entrait dans la salle quand le professeur a commencé à parler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was entering the room when the teacher started speaking.

definitions.note: Used as the present participle of « entrer » (often meaning “as/while entering”). Not to be confused with the English noun “entrant” (a participant/competitor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En entrant dans la pièce, j'ai vu Paul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As I entered the room, I saw Paul.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle entraîne l’équipe deux fois par semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She coaches the team twice a week.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like “des problèmes”, “un retard”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce changement entraîne des problèmes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This change causes problems.

definitions.note: Often used for sports practice; can also mean training in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l’entraînement de football ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to soccer practice tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va entraîner l’équipe de football deux fois par semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to coach the soccer team twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le manque de sommeil peut entraîner des problèmes de santé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lack of sleep can lead to health problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon entraîneur est très motivant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My coach is very motivating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous entraînez l’équipe chaque semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You train the team every week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est bien entraîné pour le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is well trained for the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est bien entraînée pour le match de demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is well trained for tomorrow’s game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été entraînée par le courant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was dragged along by the current.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont bien entraînés pour le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are well trained for the match.

definitions.note: Used for both space and time; can mean “between” (two) or “among” (several), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le café est entre la banque et la pharmacie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café is between the bank and the pharmacy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entre dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enters the house.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural present tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils entrent dans la salle de classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They enter the classroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est entrepreneur et il a créé sa propre entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an entrepreneur and he created his own company.

definitions.note: Past participle of « entreprendre »; often used with « avoir » or in the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le projet a été entrepris en 2020.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project was undertaken in 2020.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère travaille dans une grande entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother works in a big company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup d’entreprises dans cette ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many businesses in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les colis sont stockés dans un entrepôt près de la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The packages are stored in a warehouse near the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux entrer ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come in?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il entrera dans la salle à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will enter the room at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with "tu" (informal "you"); can also mean "go in" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu entres dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You enter the house.

definitions.note: Often used for maintaining something (a car, a building) or looking after someone/something (a garden, a child).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut entretenir la voiture régulièrement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to maintain the car regularly.

definitions.note: Past participle of « entretenir » (masculine singular); often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce jardin est bien entretenu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This garden is well maintained.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « entretenir »; often used like an adjective (e.g., « bien entretenue »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison est bien entretenue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is well maintained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un entretien demain pour ce poste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an interview tomorrow for that job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’entretien de la voiture coûte cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car’s maintenance is expensive.

definitions.note: Common in French; in Canada it’s especially frequent for a job interview.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une entrevue demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an interview tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Formal/plural command form ("vous") of "entrer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entrez, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come in, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect indicative (nous): used to describe an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand le professeur est arrivé, nous entrions déjà dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the teacher arrived, we were already entering the room.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (que nous): used after expressions like « il faut que », « je veux que », etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que nous entrions maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to enter now.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present of « entrer »; often used as a suggestion/command (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entrons dans le musée maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go into the museum now.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fenêtre est restée entrouverte toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window stayed half-open all night.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in writing (stories, literature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils entrèrent dans la salle en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They entered the room in silence.

definitions.note: past participle of « entrer »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est entré dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entered the room.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « entrer »; used with « être » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est entrée dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came into the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’entrée du musée est gratuite aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum entrance is free today.

definitions.note: In French, an “entrée” is the first course (not the main dish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comme entrée, je prends la salade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a starter, I’ll have the salad.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « entrer », used with « être » (e.g., « Elles sont entrées »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont entrées dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came into the house.

definitions.note: Past participle of « entrer » used with « être »; agrees in number/gender (here plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont entrés dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They entered the room.

definitions.note: Acronym: ENT (“espace numérique de travail”), used in schools/universities for the online portal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves se connectent à leurs ENTs pour voir les devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students log in to their school portals to see the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est vraiment entêté : il refuse de changer d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s really stubborn: he refuses to change his mind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pays a été envahi pendant la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country was invaded during the war.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « envahir »; used with « être » in the passive or in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ville a été envahie pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was invaded during the night.

definitions.note: (military/political) to enter and occupy a country or territory by force
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'armée ennemie va envahir le pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The enemy army is going to invade the country.

definitions.note: (by people/things) to spread into a place in large numbers
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des touristes vont envahir le centre-ville cet été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tourists are going to overrun the city center this summer.

definitions.note: (plants/insects) to spread everywhere in a harmful or unwanted way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les moustiques peuvent envahir la maison après la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mosquitoes can infest the house after the rain.

definitions.native: to overwhelm; to be overcome (by a feeling)
definitions.note: (figurative) said of emotions or sensations
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une grande tristesse peut envahir son esprit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A great sadness can overwhelm his mind.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mostly used in literature; in everyday speech, French usually uses the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle enveloppa le cadeau dans du papier rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrapped the gift in red paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai mis la lettre dans une enveloppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the letter in an envelope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il enveloppe le cadeau dans du papier bleu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wraps the gift in blue paper.

definitions.note: Plural form of « enveloppe ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des enveloppes pour envoyer les invitations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought envelopes to send the invitations.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’enverrai un message ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will send you a message tonight.

definitions.note: Often used with feelings/attitudes: « envers quelqu’un » = toward someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très gentil envers ses voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very kind toward his neighbors.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « avoir envie de » to mean “to feel like (doing something)” or “to want (something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai envie d’un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il envie son collègue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He envies his coworker.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "envieux de") to say what someone is jealous of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est envieux de son succès.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is jealous of his success.

definitions.note: Used with numbers to mean an approximate amount or time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a environ dix minutes de marche jusqu'à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s about a ten-minute walk to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons protéger l’environnement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must protect the environment.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural, often with an article: «les environs».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous habitons dans les environs de Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the vicinity of Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’envisage de changer de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m considering changing jobs.

definitions.note: Used for considering a plan, possibility, or course of action (often future-oriented).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons envisager une solution plus simple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to consider a simpler solution.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about plans or possible options.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Envisagez-vous de déménager cette année ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you considering moving this year?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il envoie un message à sa mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sends a message to his mother.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « envoyer » used with « ils/elles ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils envoient un email au professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They send an email to the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu envoies un message à ton ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You send a message to your friend.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular of « envoyer »; mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il envoya une lettre à son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sent a letter to his friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais t’envoyer un message ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send you a message tonight.

definitions.note: Often used as a command ("Send...") or as the "you" (plural/formal) form ("you send").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Envoyez-moi un message, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send me a message, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai envoyé un e-mail à mon professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent an email to my teacher.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « envoyer »; used with « être » or when agreeing with a direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettre a été envoyée hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was sent yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « envoyer »; used with « être » in compound tenses or to agree with a direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les lettres ont été envoyées hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letters were sent yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les e-mails ont été envoyés ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The emails were sent this morning.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; often used in fixed phrases like « les chevaliers errants » (“knights-errant”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a croisé des animaux errants près de la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We came across wandering animals near the road.

definitions.note: Often used in a literary sense (to wander without a clear direction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils errent dans les rues la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wander through the streets at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait une erreur dans le calcul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake in the calculation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait des erreurs dans mes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made mistakes in my homework.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette information est erronée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is wrong.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form of être, used with the informal “you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu es en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are late.

definitions.note: Often used for climbing steep things (like a wall, a mountain, or a fence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont escalader la montagne demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to climb the mountain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « escalader »; often used with « avoir » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a escaladé la montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed the mountain.

definitions.note: Used for an intermediate stop during a trip (often by plane, ship, or train).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons une escale de deux heures à Amsterdam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a two-hour layover in Amsterdam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’escalier est juste à côté de l’ascenseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The staircase is right next to the elevator.

definitions.note: Plural form of « escalier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les escaliers sont très raides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stairs are very steep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un escargot dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a snail in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous mangeons des escargots au restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating snails at the restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au XVIIIe siècle, beaucoup d’esclaves travaillaient dans les plantations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the 18th century, many slaves worked on plantations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les esclaves travaillent dans les champs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slaves work in the fields.

definitions.note: Most often refers to a protective escort (e.g., police or security).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a assuré l’escorte du convoi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police provided an escort for the convoy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été escorté par deux policiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was escorted by two police officers.

definitions.note: Often used in military or police contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une escouade de policiers est arrivée rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A squad of police officers arrived quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet escroc a volé l’argent de plusieurs personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That con artist stole money from several people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a pas assez d’espace dans ma chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn’t enough space in my room.

definitions.note: Plural of « espace ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des espaces entre les mots.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are spaces between the words.

definitions.note: Describes something/someone from Spain; also used for the Spanish language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je parle espagnol à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Spanish at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'apprends l'espagnol à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or to describe a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma voisine est espagnole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’espion écoute derrière la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spy is listening behind the door.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « espion ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une espionne très discrète.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very discreet spy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espionne mon voisin par la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spy on my neighbor through the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va espionner ses voisins pendant des semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to spy on his neighbors for weeks.

definitions.note: Usually said about “you” (tu): « tu espionnes » = “you spy on …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pourquoi tu espionnes tes voisins ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you spying on your neighbors?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les espions observent la situation en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spies are watching the situation in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet enfant est très espiègle : il cache toujours mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That child is very mischievous: he always hides my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a encore de l’espoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is still hope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos espoirs sont grands pour l’année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our hopes are high for next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un esprit très curieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a very curious mind.

definitions.note: Plural form of « esprit »; often refers to minds, attitudes, or (depending on context) supernatural beings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette maison, on dit qu’il y a des esprits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this house, they say there are spirits.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette espèce vit dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This species lives in the forest.

definitions.note: Common in everyday French, often in expressions like « une espèce de… » (“a kind of…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une espèce de soupe aux légumes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a kind of vegetable soup.

definitions.note: Often used in the fixed phrase « en espèces » (= paying in cash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux payer en espèces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can pay in cash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il existe beaucoup d’espèces d’oiseaux ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many species of birds here.

definitions.note: Also commonly means "expects" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espère que tu vas bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you’re doing well.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils espèrent trouver une solution bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hope to find a solution soon.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « espérer » used with « tu » (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu espères venir ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you hope to come tonight?

definitions.note: This is commonly a misspelling of «espèce» (with the accent on the second “e”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle espéce de musique tu écoutes ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of music do you listen to?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je): used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espérais te voir ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was hoping to see you this weekend.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (was hoping / used to hope), third-person singular (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il espérait trouver un travail rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hoped to find a job quickly.

definitions.note: Present participle of « espérer »; often used to express a hope while doing something else (like “hoping that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espérant avoir une réponse bientôt, je vérifie mes e-mails tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hoping to get an answer soon, I check my emails every day.

definitions.note: Someone who speaks or supports Esperanto.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon oncle est espérantiste depuis l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle has been an Esperanto speaker since university.

definitions.note: A constructed international language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprend l’espéranto depuis deux mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been learning Esperanto for two months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais espérer que tu vas bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to hope that you’re doing well.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense; also used as a polite singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'espère que vous espérez une bonne nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that you hope for good news.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous espériez finir tôt, mais la réunion a duré longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hoped to finish early, but the meeting lasted a long time.

definitions.note: First-person plural present of « espérer » (used with « nous » or as a suggestion: « let’s… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espérons que tout se passera bien demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s hope everything goes well tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « espérer »; often used with « avoir » to form the past tense (e.g., « j’ai espéré »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai espéré te revoir bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped to see you again soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a esquivé la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dodged the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais faire un essai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to make an attempt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous faisons un essai de la nouvelle machine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are doing a test of the new machine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'écris un essai pour mon cours de français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm writing an essay for my French class.

definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can mean “I try,” “(he/she) tries,” or the command “try!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'essaie de comprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to understand.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « essayer » used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils essaient de parler français tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They try to speak French every day.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future form of « essayer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle essaiera encore demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will try again tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, j’essaierai de me lever plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will try to get up earlier.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « essayer » used with « tu » (you, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu essaies encore ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you trying again?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après plusieurs essais, j’ai réussi à ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After several attempts, I managed to open the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle essaya d’ouvrir la porte, mais elle était fermée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tried to open the door, but it was closed.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essayais de t’appeler, mais tu ne répondais pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was trying to call you, but you weren’t answering.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle essayait d’ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was trying to open the door.

definitions.note: Present participle (used like “trying …” or “while trying …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En essayant, tu vas y arriver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By trying, you’ll manage to do it.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "essayer" (often used with "il/elle/on").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaye de comprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais essayer demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to try tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu form) of « essayer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu essayes cette veste ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you trying on this jacket?

definitions.note: Usually used to address more than one person (vous) or as a polite/formal command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essayez ce gâteau, il est délicieux !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try this cake; it’s delicious!

definitions.note: Used with "nous" as an invitation/suggestion (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essayons cette recette ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s try this recipe tonight.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person plural (they). Mostly used in literature and formal writing; in everyday speech, French usually uses "ils/elles ont essayé".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils essayèrent d’ouvrir la porte, mais elle était bloquée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to open the door, but it was stuck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai essayé cette chemise, mais elle est trop petite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried on this shirt, but it’s too small.

definitions.note: Common in France for car fuel; in Québec, “essence” can also mean “gas” (as in gas or gasoline).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais mettre de l’essence dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put gas in the car.

definitions.note: More formal/abstract sense: the fundamental nature of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’essence de ce problème est simple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The essence of this problem is simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est essentiel de boire assez d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is essential to drink enough water.

definitions.note: Often used as “l’essentiel” to mean what matters most or the most important part.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’essentiel, c’est d’être en bonne santé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main thing is to be in good health.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’eau est essentielle à la vie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is essential to life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après avoir couru, je suis essoufflé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After running, I am out of breath.

definitions.note: Common in Canadian French (short for words like "essuie-main").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passe-moi un essuie, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me a towel, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essuie la table avec un chiffon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wipes the table with a cloth.

definitions.note: Literary simple past (passé simple) of « essuyer »; common in writing, especially stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essuya ses lunettes avec un mouchoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wiped his glasses with a handkerchief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va essuyer la table avec un chiffon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to wipe the table with a cloth.

definitions.note: Formal/instruction form: ‘you’ (plural or polite) in the present tense (also used for commands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essuyez la table, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wipe the table, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai essuyé la table après le repas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wiped the table after the meal.

definitions.note: Usually used with the article: l’Est (e.g., dans l’Est de la France).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habite dans l’est de la France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in the east of France.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary to form compound tenses with certain verbs and reflexive verbs
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est déjà partie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has already left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selon mon estimation, le trajet prendra environ deux heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to my estimate, the trip will take about two hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a beaucoup d’estime pour son professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a lot of esteem for his teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il estime le coût des travaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He estimates the cost of the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’estime beaucoup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I respect you a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons estimer le coût total à 200 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to estimate the total cost at 200 euros.

definitions.note: Often used to express an opinion or judgment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’estime qu’il faut estimer les risques avant d’agir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think we need to assess the risks before acting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu estimes le coût des travaux à 2 000 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You estimate the cost of the work at 2,000 euros.

definitions.note: Addressing “vous”: either to one person formally, or to multiple people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vous remercie : vous estimez vraiment mon travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you: you really value my work.

definitions.note: Past participle of “estimer” (e.g., in the passive voice or in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le coût est estimé à 200 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cost is estimated at 200 euros.

definitions.note: Can describe a person who is well regarded.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très estimé dans son équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very respected in his team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à l’estomac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My stomach hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai un frère et une sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a brother and a sister.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary verb in the imperfect tense (e.g., to form the past perfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il etait parti avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had left before noon.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or several people to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: eteignez la lumière, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the light, please.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « éteindre » (used with tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu eteins la lumière, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You turn off the light, please.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with certain verbs (often verbs of movement) and with all reflexive verbs in the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous etes arrives.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have arrived.

definitions.note: Past participle of « avoir » (“to have”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai eu de la chance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have had some luck.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the past participle of « avoir » (used when the past participle agrees, usually with a preceding direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chance qu’elle a eue était incroyable.
