definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The luck she had was incredible.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « avoir »; it agrees with a preceding direct object (e.g., « les choses que tu as eues »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les occasions que tu as eues étaient rares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The opportunities you had were rare.

definitions.note: Used as a hesitation filler when thinking or unsure; common in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Euh… je ne sais pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um… I don't know.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural of « avoir »; mainly used in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils eurent très peur quand la porte s’ouvrit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were very afraid when the door opened.

definitions.note: masculine noun; feminine form: « européenne »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est européen, mais il vit au Canada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is European, but he lives in Canada.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les Européens voyagent souvent en train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Europeans often travel by train.

definitions.note: Plural of euro (the currency).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça coûte vingt euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It costs twenty euros.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past) of « avoir » (1st/2nd person singular: je eus, tu eus); used mainly in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je eus à peine terminé que je sortis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had barely finished when I went out.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past) form of « avoir », used mainly in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il eut peur en entendant ce bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was afraid when he heard that noise.

definitions.note: Stressed pronoun used for emphasis, after prepositions (avec eux, pour eux), or on its own (as in “them!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais avec eux au cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the movies with them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evidemment, je suis d’accord avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Obviously, I agree with you.

definitions.note: Used before a noun to mean a previous partner/spouse/job, etc. Often written with a hyphen (ex-mari) or as two words (ex copain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est mon ex copain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s my ex-boyfriend.

definitions.note: Informal; short for « ex-petit ami / ex-petite amie » or « ex-partenaire ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon ex habite à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ex lives in Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est le nombre exact.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the exact number.

definitions.note: Often used in conversation to show strong agreement or to confirm what someone just said.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu es prêt ? — Exact !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you ready? — Exactly!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ta réponse est exacte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is exact.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est exactement ce que je voulais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly what I wanted.

definitions.note: Common as a short reply to agree or confirm what someone just said.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu viens demain ? — Exactement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tomorrow? — That’s right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il exagère toujours quand il raconte ses histoires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always exaggerates when he tells his stories.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu exagères : ce n’est pas si grave !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re exaggerating: it’s not that serious!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu vas exagérer si tu dis que c’est la pire journée de ta vie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re going to exaggerate if you say it’s the worst day of your life.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous exagérez : ce n’est pas si grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re exaggerating: it’s not that serious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un peu exagéré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a bit exaggerated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un examen demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an exam tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai trois examens cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three exams this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle examina le document avant de signer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She examined the document before signing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il examine le document avant de le signer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He examines the document before signing it.

definitions.note: Present tense (3rd person plural): « ils/elles examinent ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les médecins examinent le patient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors examine the patient.

definitions.native: to examine, to inspect, to look at closely
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin va examiner le patient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is going to examine the patient.

definitions.note: Command form (vous) or present tense with vous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Examinez ce document avant de signer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Examine this document before signing.

definitions.note: Often used as the "nous" imperative to mean "let's ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Examinons les résultats ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's examine the results together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai examiné le document avant de le signer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I examined the document before signing it.

definitions.note: Used mostly in formal or literary French, especially for prayers or wishes ("exaucer une prière / un vœu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son vœu a été exaucé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His wish was granted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous visons l’excellence dans notre travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We aim for excellence in our work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant est excellent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is excellent.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette idée est excellente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This idea is excellent.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces idées sont excellentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These ideas are excellent.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces restaurants sont excellents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These restaurants are excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une exception à cette règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an exception to this rule.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant est exceptionnel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is exceptional.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une opportunité exceptionnelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an exceptional opportunity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux une explication claire.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The outside door is closed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to carry out the boss’s instructions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalement, on a trouvé une solution.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, we found a solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille dans la finance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in finance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le financement du projet est assuré par la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project's funding is provided by the city.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural to talk about a person’s or organization’s money situation overall.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois organiser mes finances ce mois-ci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to organize my finances this month.

definitions.note: Often used for things related to money, finance, or funding.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons besoin d’un soutien financier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need financial support.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les marchés financiers ont beaucoup bougé aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The financial markets moved a lot today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situation financière de l’entreprise est difficile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Financièrement, je ne peux pas acheter cette voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Financially, I can't buy that car.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « fin ». Often means “thin/slim” rather than English “fine” (= okay/good).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a slim waist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a répondu avec finesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She answered with finesse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le travail est fini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The work is finished.

definitions.note: Past participle of « finir »; often used in « C’est fini ! » to mean something is finished/over.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est fini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s finished.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is over.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « finir »; it agrees with a feminine singular direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tâche que j’ai finie est difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task that I finished is difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois finir mes devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish my homework before dinner.

definitions.note: Third-person singular simple future of « finir » (used for “he/she/it will …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il finira ses devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will finish his homework tonight.

definitions.note: First-person singular (je) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je finirai mes devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will finish my homework tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would finish her work earlier if she started on time.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense of « finir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu finiras tes devoirs après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will finish your homework after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les travaux sont finis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The work is finished.

definitions.note: Usually used with “tu” (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu finis tes devoirs ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you finishing your homework tonight?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « finir » (used after expressions of doubt, necessity, emotion, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je finisse ce travail aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish this work today.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « finir » used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils finissent leurs devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They finish their homework before dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense: used with « vous » (you plural or polite singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous finissez vos devoirs après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You finish your homework after dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense: «nous finissons» = “we finish / we are finishing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous finissons nos devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finish our homework before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film finit à minuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie ends at midnight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’apprends le finnois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Finnish.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective « fin ». Often used to describe something delicate in texture (e.g., hair).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont des cheveux fins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have thin hair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous approchons de la fin, mais il y aura encore deux fins possibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re getting close to the end, but there will still be two possible endings.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural: used mainly in literature and formal writing; in speech it’s usually replaced by « ils/elles ont fait ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils firent un gâteau pour l’anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They made a cake for the birthday.

definitions.note: Often used in a business or professional context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle travaille pour une firme internationale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works for an international firm.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) of « faire » used mainly in writing (literature, formal narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fis une erreur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake.

definitions.note: Very vulgar slang; refers to a sexual act.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, il fiste quelqu’un.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, he fists someone.

definitions.note: Informal/affectionate; often used to address a boy or young man directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alors, fiston, comment s'est passée ta journée ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So, son, how was your day?

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple) form of « faire », used mainly in written narratives (e.g., novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fit une erreur, puis il s’excusa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a mistake, then he apologized.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in literature; often corresponds to “fixed” or “set” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fixa la date du rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He set the date of the appointment.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fixait un rendez-vous pour le lendemain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was setting an appointment for the next day.

definitions.note: Often used for setting/deciding something (a date, a time, a meeting, a price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fixe un rendez-vous pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set an appointment for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fixe la porte en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stares at the door in silence.

definitions.note: Often used for setting a time/date or arranging something (e.g., a meeting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va fixer une date pour la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to set a date for the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used as the past participle of « fixer » (e.g., « j’ai fixé… » = “I set/arranged…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fixé un rendez-vous pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set up an appointment for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les horaires sont fixés depuis lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schedules have been set since Monday.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « fier ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis fière de toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "fier".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont très fières de leur travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very proud of their work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai de la fièvre depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had a fever since yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis hier soir, je suis fiévreux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since last night, I’ve been feverish.

definitions.note: Often used for a small container for perfume, medicine, or cosmetics.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a acheté un flacon de parfum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought a bottle of perfume.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a un excellent flair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has an excellent sense of smell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La flamme de la bougie vacille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle flame is flickering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les flammes montaient très haut dans la cheminée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flames were rising very high in the fireplace.

definitions.note: Often used for the side of a person/animal or the side of something (like a hill).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has pain in his right side.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la pluie, il y avait une grande flaque devant la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, there was a big puddle in front of the door.

definitions.note: Often used in French for a camera flash or a quick news update ("un flash info").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le flash de l'appareil photo est trop fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The camera flash is too strong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me flatte pour obtenir ce qu’il veut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He flatters me to get what he wants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n'aime pas la flatterie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't like flattery.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very flattering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis flatté par ton compliment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m flattered by your compliment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une fleur pour ma mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a flower for my mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au printemps, les arbres commencent à fleurir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the trees start to bloom.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the cherry trees bloom.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the florist to buy some roses.

definitions.note: Plural of « fleur ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like flowers in the spring.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Seine is a river that goes through Paris.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon emploi du temps est flexible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My schedule is flexible.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These hoses are flexible.

definitions.note: Informal/slang (often mildly pejorative).

definitions.note: Informal/slang (often a bit negative).

definitions.note: Informal/slang.

definitions.note: Informal. Often used about something that gives you the creeps. Not the same as English “flippant” (= not serious, cheeky).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La flotte est prête à partir.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In strong wind, you watch the flag wave above the building.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The image is blurry.

definitions.note: Very informal; can sound crude depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is crazy with joy.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a civil servant at a town hall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These machines work very well.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer dark green.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate melts in the sun.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Freedom of speech is fundamental in a democracy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le fondateur de l’entreprise a présenté le nouveau projet.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house’s foundations are solid.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple) form; used mainly in literature for narration.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow melted in the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le beurre fondre dans la poêle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butter melts in the pan.

definitions.note: Past participle of « fondre ».

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chocolat est fondu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate is melted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fondé une entreprise en 2018.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He founded a company in 2018.

definitions.note: Often used with “sur” (e.g., “fondé sur”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est fondé sur des faits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s based on facts.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « fonder »; used with « être » or as an adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This school was founded in 1950.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This organization was founded in 2010.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "faire" used with "ils/elles" (they).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They do their homework after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une fontaine sur la place.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a fountain in the square.

definitions.note: In French, this is short for « football » (the sport).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je joue au foot le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play soccer on Saturdays.

definitions.note: In France, "football" usually refers to soccer (American football is typically called "football américain").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je joue au football avec mes amis le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play soccer with my friends on Saturdays.

definitions.note: In France, this typically refers to a player of football (soccer), not American football.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est footballeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a soccer player.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’a plus la force de marcher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He no longer has the strength to walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La force du vent a cassé une branche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The power of the wind broke a branch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il force la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forces the door open.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (forcer quelqu’un à faire quelque chose = to force someone to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va forcer son collègue à partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to force his colleague to leave.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a utilisé toutes ses forces pour soulever la boîte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used all his strength to lift the box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai été forcé d’accepter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was forced to accept.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun or with être for a feminine subject)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été forcée de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was forced to leave.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “not necessarily” when negated: « pas forcément ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce n’est pas forcément une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s not necessarily a good idea.

definitions.note: Past participle of « forcer »; also used as an adjective meaning “forced.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont forcés de partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are forced to leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le forgeron fabrique des outils en métal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blacksmith makes tools out of metal.

definitions.note: Often used for an official requirement or administrative step.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut remplir cette formalité avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to complete this formality before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used for professional training or courses (e.g., job training).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis une formation en ligne pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking an online course to learn French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette table a une forme ronde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table has a round shape.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je forme un cercle avec mes mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I form a circle with my hands.

definitions.note: Used especially with a person or group as the direct object (e.g., former quelqu’un).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle forme les nouveaux employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She trains the new employees.

definitions.note: Present tense (they form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces élèves forment un groupe de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These students form a work group.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons former un groupe pour le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to form a group for the project.

definitions.note: Often used for training people (e.g., employees, students).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle doit former les nouveaux employés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to train the new employees.

definitions.note: Plural of « forme ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les formes géométriques sont faciles à reconnaître.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Geometric shapes are easy to recognize.

definitions.note: Present tense (vous form) of « former ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous formez une équipe très efficace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You form a very effective team.

definitions.note: In everyday French, it usually means something positive (not just “formidable” in the sense of intimidating).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est formidable !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is fantastic!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tes idées sont formidables !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your ideas are great!

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense used to make a suggestion (like “let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Formons une équipe pour ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's form a team for this project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous devez remplir ce formulaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to fill out this form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous devez remplir ces formulaires avant la date limite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to fill out these forms before the deadline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle est la formule pour calculer l’aire d’un cercle ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the formula to calculate the area of a circle?

definitions.note: Common in marketing (e.g., phone plans, travel offers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a choisi une formule avec petit-déjeuner inclus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We chose a package with breakfast included.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu formuler ta question plus clairement ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you phrase your question more clearly?

definitions.note: Often used with être: « être formé » = to be trained (e.g., for a job).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est formé pour ce travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is trained for this job.

definitions.note: Past participle used for feminine singular (e.g., with « être » or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est bien formée pour ce travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is well trained for this job.

definitions.note: Also used to mean “loud” (e.g., parler fort = to speak loudly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very strong.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like « parler » or « travailler » to mean doing something with intensity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parle fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils visitent un fort près de la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are visiting a fort near the sea.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « fort ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très forte en maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very good at math.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “a lot” in the sense of intensity (e.g., to be strongly affected, to smell strongly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est fortement influencé par ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is strongly influenced by his friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils visitent une forteresse médiévale sur la colline.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are visiting a medieval fortress on the hill.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont très fortes en maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very strong in math.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces hommes sont très forts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These men are very strong.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used especially for sounds (music, voices, noises).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les voisins sont trop forts le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbors are too loud in the evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu la fortune de trouver un appartement près du métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had the good luck to find an apartment near the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a hérité d’une grande fortune.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She inherited a great fortune.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form of « forcer », mostly found in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il força la porte avec un pied-de-biche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forced the door with a crowbar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nous promenons dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are taking a walk in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural of « forêt ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les forêts couvrent une grande partie du pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Forests cover a large part of the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une fosse le long de la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a ditch along the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un fossé le long de la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a ditch along the road.

definitions.note: Commonly used informally to mean “crazy” in a neutral or positive way (like “That’s crazy!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est fou !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s crazy!

definitions.note: Can sound insulting; often used informally to talk about someone who seems crazy or acts wildly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un fou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He's a crazy person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foudre est tombée près de la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lightning struck near the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dresseur tient un fouet dans la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trainer is holding a whip in his hand.

definitions.note: Also commonly used in cooking for beating/whisking (e.g., eggs or cream).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va fouetter la crème jusqu'à ce qu'elle soit ferme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to whip/whisk the cream until it is stiff.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form, used mainly in writing (stories, novels, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fouilla dans son sac et trouva ses clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He searched in his bag and found his keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fouille dans son sac pour trouver ses clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rummages through his bag to find his keys.

definitions.note: Often used for searching through things (a bag, a drawer) or searching an area; can also mean to frisk/search someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a fouiller son sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police searched his bag.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) command or present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fouillez vos poches, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Search your pockets, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « fouiller » (to search through, rummage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai fouillé mon sac, mais je n'ai pas trouvé mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I searched my bag, but I didn’t find my keys.

definitions.note: Usually a lighter scarf (often a neck scarf), not a thick winter scarf.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte un foulard bleu autour du cou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a blue scarf around her neck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une foule attend devant le stade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A crowd is waiting in front of the stadium.

definitions.note: Past participle of « fouler », often used with « avoir » (e.g., « a foulé »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a foulé l’herbe humide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stepped on the wet grass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le four est chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oven is hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mets la fourchette à gauche de l’assiette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the fork to the left of the plate.

definitions.note: Plural form of « fourchette ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des fourchettes dans le tiroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are forks in the drawer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le fourgon est garé devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The van is parked in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une fourmi sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an ant on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des fourmis dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are ants in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fourni les documents demandés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I provided the requested documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pouvez-vous fournir une preuve d’identité ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you provide proof of identity?

definitions.note: Present tense form of « fournir » (used with tu, il/elle/on, or je in inversion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu fournis les documents nécessaires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You provide the necessary documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils fournissent de l’eau potable aux villages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They provide drinking water to the villages.

definitions.note: Plural form of « fournisseur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons changé de fournisseurs cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We changed suppliers this year.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with “vous” (you, formal/plural), from the verb “fournir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: S’il vous plaît, fournissez votre adresse e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please provide your email address.

definitions.note: Also used as a literary past tense (passé simple) meaning “provided/supplied.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise fournit des logiciels aux écoles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company supplies software to schools.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « fourrer »; common in books, rare in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fourra la lettre dans sa poche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stuffed the letter into his pocket.

definitions.note: Often implies putting something in quickly or messily (more casual than “mettre”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fourre mon téléphone dans mon sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stuff my phone into my bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte un manteau en fourrure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a fur coat.

definitions.note: Often implies doing it quickly or carelessly, like stuffing something into a bag or pocket.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai fourré les papiers dans mon sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stuffed the papers into my bag.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of « fou ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont complètement fous !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re completely crazy!

definitions.note: Plural form of the noun "fou".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette histoire, les fous disent la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this story, the crazy people tell the truth.

definitions.note: Very informal and often vulgar/rough; commonly used in expressions like « s’en foutre » (= to not care).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu fous tes chaussures dans l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You throw your shoes in the entryway.

definitions.note: Informal; can sound rude depending on context. Also used in expressions like « s’en foutre » = “to not care.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fout son manteau sur la chaise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He throws his coat on the chair.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de dire des foutaises !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop talking nonsense!

definitions.note: Very informal and often vulgar. Depending on context, it can also mean “fuck.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils foutent le bazar dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re making a mess in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Very informal and often rude/vulgar (slang). Common in questions like « Qu’est-ce que vous foutez ? » = “What are you doing?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qu’est-ce que vous foutez ici ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing here?

definitions.note: Vulgar/explicit slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il l’a envoyé promener et lui a dit d’aller se foutre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told him to get lost and said to go fuck himself.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; often sounds rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais foutre les clés sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to throw the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Colloquial and often vulgar; used to strongly emphasize an adjective or adverb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait foutrement froid dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s damn cold outside.

definitions.note: Informal and often vulgar (from the verb “foutre”). Common in expressions like “C’est foutu” (= it’s over / it’s hopeless).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est foutu, on a raté le dernier train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re screwed; we missed the last train.

definitions.note: Informal; often considered vulgar (from the verb "foutre").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon ordinateur est foutu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My computer is messed up.

definitions.note: Informal; can be a mild swearword depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette foutue porte ne ferme pas !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This damned door won’t close!

definitions.note: Informal; can sound rude/vulgar depending on context. Used to mean something is ruined or not working anymore.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes chaussures sont foutues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are ruined.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans billets, nous sommes foutus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without tickets, we're screwed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veut fonder un foyer avec elle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to start a home with her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les foyers français consomment moins d’énergie cet hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: French households are using less energy this winter.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard a loud crash in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fracassé son téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smashed his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une fracture au poignet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a fracture in his wrist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce verre est fragile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This glass is fragile.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces verres sont fragiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These glasses are fragile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai trouvé des fragments de verre sur le sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found fragments of glass on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce pain est frais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread is fresh.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « frais de livraison » (shipping fees) or « frais de dossier » (processing/administration fees). Not the same as English “fresh” (that’s the adjective « frais »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les frais de livraison sont inclus dans le prix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shipping fees are included in the price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais une fraise, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a strawberry, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange des fraises au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat strawberries for breakfast.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cueille des framboises dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m picking raspberries in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je préfère une réponse franche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer a frank answer.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « franc ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été franche avec moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was frank with me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Franchement, je ne comprends pas cette règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Frankly, I don’t understand this rule.

definitions.note: Past participle of « franchir » (often used with « avoir » in the passé composé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai franchi la frontière hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crossed the border yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing a boundary/obstacle (a street, a border, a threshold, a fence, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons franchir la frontière demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to cross the border tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je franchis la frontière à pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cross the border on foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a ouvert une franchise de café près de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She opened a coffee franchise near the train station.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « avec franchise ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m’a parlé avec franchise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke to me honestly.

definitions.note: Plural form; can refer to the former French currency or other countries' francs, depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the euro, people paid in francs in France.

definitions.note: Informal/slang (like “bro”); often refers to your actual brother, but can also mean a close male friend.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frangin arrive ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is coming tonight.

definitions.note: Describes something from France, or the French language (often used with the article: « le français »).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak French.

definitions.note: Also used as an adjective meaning “French” (e.g., un livre français).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'apprends le français à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning French at school.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est française.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is French.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chansons sont françaises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These songs are French.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) of « frapper »; mostly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il frappa à la porte et attendit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knocked on the door and waited.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelqu’un frappait à la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone was knocking at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son visage est frappant, mais sa voix est encore plus frappante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His face is striking, but his voice is even more striking.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « frappe aérienne » (air strike).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La frappe a détruit le pont.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The strike destroyed the bridge.

definitions.note: Often used for knocking on a door: « Il frappe à la porte. »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il frappe le ballon avec son pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the ball with his foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils frappent le ballon très fort.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle gagne souvent aux cartes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She often wins at cards.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est déjà habillé.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the door open.

definitions.native: was leaving, was letting, was allowing

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle laissait la porte ouverte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was leaving the door open.

definitions.note: present participle of « laisser »; often used to mean “while leaving” or “by leaving” in context

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This reader likes detective novels.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The readers like this book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lecture avant de dormir m’aide à me détendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reading before sleeping helps me relax.

definitions.native: the next day, the following day

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bus est très lent.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The connection is slow today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marche lentement parce qu’il est fatigué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walks slowly because he is tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lenteur du service nous a énervés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slowness of the service annoyed us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais cuire des lentilles pour le dîner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je porte des lentilles quand je fais du sport.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These snails are very slow.

definitions.note: Interrogative/relative pronoun used to refer to a specific item; it agrees in gender and number (lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which one do you prefer?

definitions.note: plural definite article, used with both masculine and feminine plural nouns

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are playing in the park.

definitions.note: direct object pronoun for plural people or things; usually placed before the verb

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see them every day.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective; used to describe a woman or something related to lesbians.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est lesbienne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lesbian.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « lequel »; used after a preposition (e.g., « avec », « sur », « pour »).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parmi ces livres, lesquels préfères-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Among these books, which ones do you prefer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut acheter de la lessive pour faire une machine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy laundry detergent to do a load of laundry.

definitions.note: Can mean a letter (message) or a letter of the alphabet; the example uses the message meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai reçu une lettre de ma grand-mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a letter from my grandmother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprend les lettres à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He learns the letters at school.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural for written correspondence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai reçu des lettres de mes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received letters from my friends.

definitions.note: Medical term.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was diagnosed with leukemia.

definitions.note: Used before a singular noun; before a plural noun, French uses « leurs ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leur voiture est garée devant la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their car is parked in front of the house.

definitions.note: Indirect object pronoun (used before the verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je leur parle tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talk to them every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pêcheur utilise un leurre pour attraper un poisson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman uses a lure to catch a fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chasseurs ont placé des leurres près de l’étang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunters placed decoys near the pond.

definitions.note: Plural form of the possessive determiner (used before a plural noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leurs enfants sont à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their children are at school.

definitions.note: Plural form of the possessive pronoun/determiner meaning “their,” used before a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leurs amis arrivent ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their friends are arriving tonight.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « lever »; common in books and stories, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il leva la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He raised his hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Verb. Common in phrases like « lever la main » (raise your hand) and « lever les yeux » (look up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais lever la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to raise my hand to ask a question.

definitions.native: to get up; to stand up
definitions.note: Often used as « se lever » (to get up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois lever tôt demain pour prendre le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get up early tomorrow to catch the train.

definitions.native: to lift (a restriction); to remove; to cancel
definitions.note: Used for bans, sanctions, curfews, etc. e.g., « lever une interdiction ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont lever l’interdiction dès lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to lift the ban starting Monday.

definitions.native: to pick up; to collect (money, a tax)
definitions.note: Often used with money: « lever des fonds » (raise funds), « lever un impôt » (levy a tax).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’association espère lever des fonds pour le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The organization hopes to raise funds for the project.

definitions.note: Nautical usage: « lever les voiles » (set sail), « lever l’ancre » (weigh anchor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À l’aube, le capitaine va lever l’ancre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At dawn, the captain is going to weigh anchor.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., lever la main = to raise your hand). Used reflexively: se lever = to get up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais lever la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to raise my hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Usually used with « vous » (formal or plural) or as a command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levez la main, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Raise your hand, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec ce levier, tu peux soulever la caisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this lever, you can lift the crate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous levons la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We raise our hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils levèrent la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They raised their hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Past participle of « lever ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai levé la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I raised my hand.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun (e.g., « le bras levé », « les mains levées »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a le bras levé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has his arm raised.

definitions.note: feminine form of « levé ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La barrière est levée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The barrier is raised.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « lever ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les bras sont levés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The arms are raised.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai une leçon de français cet après-midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a French lesson this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deux leçons aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two lessons today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une liaison directe entre Paris et Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a direct connection between Paris and Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces liaisons sont nécessaires pour le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These connections are necessary for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La liberté est importante pour tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Freedom is important for everyone.

definitions.note: A "libraire" works in a bookstore ("librairie"), not a library.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je demande conseil au libraire du quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask the neighborhood bookseller for advice.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “library”; the French word for “library” is “bibliothèque”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à la librairie pour acheter un roman.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the bookstore to buy a novel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis libre ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m free tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous pouvez parler librement ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can speak freely here.

definitions.note: Plural form of “libre.” Often used about people being free (not busy) or things being available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes libres ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are free tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libère l’oiseau de sa cage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He frees the bird from its cage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La libération des otages a eu lieu ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hostages' release took place this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont libérer l’oiseau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to free the bird.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle libérera l’oiseau demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will free the bird tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Libérez le passage, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clear the way, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est enfin libéré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is finally free.

definitions.note: Often used after a noun (e.g., « un homme libéré »).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After ten years in prison, he is finally freed.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural masculine) of « libérer »; used with « être » or in passive voice/adjectival use.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are finally freed.

definitions.note: Often used for official permissions (e.g., a driver’s license, a work permit, a software license).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut une licence pour conduire une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need a license to drive a car.

definitions.note: Often used for an internet link (URL).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lieutenant gives orders to his unit.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plays in a soccer league.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le lilas sent très bon au printemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lilac smells very good in the spring.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “kind of not OK / going too far.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une limite à ne pas dépasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a limit you must not go beyond.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went beyond the limits.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will read this book on the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime lire avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to read before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have a few liras in a drawer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You read a book before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was reading a novel when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand je suis entré, il lisait un livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I came in, he was reading a book.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They read a book before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We read a book every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reads a book before sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lis un livre avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read a book before going to sleep.
