definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces idées sont liées entre elles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These ideas are linked to each other.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces deux problèmes sont liés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These two problems are linked.

definitions.note: Not a standard French word; likely a misspelling of « ils » (3rd person plural subject pronoun for a group of males or a mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: lls arrivent à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re arriving at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce magasin est un commerce local.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shop is a local business.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « local ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une spécialité locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a local specialty.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous cherchons des entreprises locales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for local businesses.

definitions.note: Often used in more technical contexts (e.g., GPS, finding where something is, or placing something on a map).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La localisation de mon téléphone est désactivée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The location of my phone is turned off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu localiser mon téléphone ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you locate my phone?

definitions.note: Past participle of « localiser »; often used in the passive voice (e.g., « est localisé » = « is located »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le musée est localisé près de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is located near the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le locataire a signé le bail hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tenant signed the lease yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les locataires paient le loyer chaque mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tenants pay the rent every month.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like « location de voiture » (car rental). Not the same meaning as English “location” (place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La location de cette voiture coûte 30 euros par jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rental of this car costs 30 euros per day.

definitions.note: Plural of « local » meaning a place/building used by an organization (not « locals » = local people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les locaux de l’école sont fermés le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school’s premises are closed on weekends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La locomotive tire tout le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The locomotive pulls the whole train.

definitions.note: Often refers to a small private seating area in a theater/opera (a box).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons des places dans une loge au théâtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have seats in a box at the theater.

definitions.note: Often used with "chez" to mean staying/living at someone’s place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il loge chez sa tante à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stays at his aunt’s place in Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette famille loge deux étudiants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This family houses two students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous cherchons un logement près du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for housing near the city center.

definitions.note: Used when someone provides lodging for someone else (e.g., a host, a hotel, a family).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette famille peut loger des étudiants étrangers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This family can house foreign students.

definitions.note: Used when talking about where someone is staying (often temporarily, e.g., while traveling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant le week-end, je vais loger chez une amie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over the weekend, I’m going to stay at a friend’s place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai installé un nouveau logiciel sur mon ordinateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I installed new software on my computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai installé plusieurs logiciels sur mon ordinateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I installed several programs on my computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une réponse logique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a logical answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne comprends pas la logique de cette décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand the logic behind this decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette loi protège les enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This law protects children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon école est loin d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My school is far from here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces lois protègent les consommateurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These laws protect consumers.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (les loisirs) to talk about leisure activities or free-time pursuits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant mes loisirs, je lis et je fais du sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my free time, I read and I play sports.

definitions.note: A constructed language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'apprends le lojban.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning Lojban.

definitions.note: Placed after the noun in French (e.g. une route longue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film est très long.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is very long.

definitions.note: Often used after verbs in expressions like « attendre longtemps » (to wait a long time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a attendu long avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waited a long time before answering.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed expression « le long de » meaning “along” (literally “the length of”). Often confused with English “long”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous marchons le long de la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are walking along the river.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of « long ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes cheveux sont longs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hair is long.

definitions.native: a long time, for a long time
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas vu Paul depuis longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven’t seen Paul in a long time.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of « long ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte une longue robe noire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a long black dress.

definitions.native: at length, for a long time
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons longuement parlé de ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked about this project at length.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a de longues jambes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has long legs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La longueur de la table est de deux mètres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The length of the table is two meters.

definitions.note: Used in French (often as « le look ») to talk about someone’s style or appearance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime ton look aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your look today.

definitions.note: In modern French, this is mainly used as an English title or as a character name (often capitalized: « Lord »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lord Smith habite à Londres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lord Smith lives in London.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the fixed expression « lors de » (“during”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lors de la réunion, j’ai pris des notes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the meeting, I took notes.

definitions.note: Slightly more formal than "quand"; used to introduce a subordinate clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’appellerai lorsque j’arriverai à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you when I get home.

definitions.note: Informal (borrowed from English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de te traiter de loser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop calling yourself a loser.

definitions.note: In French, often used in expressions like « un lot de… » (“a bunch/lot of…”) or to mean a set/batch of items.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un lot de trois cahiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a set of three notebooks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai gagné un petit prix à la loterie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won a small prize in the lottery.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a lottery game (often like bingo) in France.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a joué au loto samedi soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We played the lottery on Saturday night.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « louer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur loua son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher praised his work.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « louer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il loua un appartement près de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rented an apartment near the train station.

definitions.note: Mostly used in formal or religious contexts; often found in the expression « faire des louanges (de) » (“to sing someone/something’s praises”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur a fait des louanges à propos de son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher praised his work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet homme a l'air louche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That man looks shady.

definitions.note: In French, louer can mean to rent (as a tenant) or to rent out (as an owner); context makes it clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle loue un appartement près du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rents an apartment near downtown.

definitions.note: Less common than the “rent” meaning in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il loue le courage de son équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He praises his team’s courage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons louer une voiture pour le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to rent a car for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a entendu un loup hurler dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard a wolf howl in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural of « loup ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On entend des loups dans la forêt la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can hear wolves in the forest at night.

definitions.note: Common in informal French (from the verb « louper »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai loupé le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette valise est trop lourde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase is too heavy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « lourd ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette valise est lourde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase is heavy.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « lourd ». Not to be confused with Lourdes (the town in France).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les valises sont lourdes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are heavy.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of lourd.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces sacs sont très lourds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These bags are very heavy.

definitions.note: Figurative; often said of jokes, remarks, or an atmosphere. Masculine plural form of lourd.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses commentaires sont lourds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comments are crass/awkward.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a vu une loutre nager dans la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw an otter swimming in the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La louve protège ses petits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The she-wolf protects her cubs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai loué un appartement à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rented an apartment in Paris.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal or literary style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son travail a été loué par le jury.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His work was praised by the jury.

definitions.note: past participle of louer
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chambre est déjà louée pour le mois d’août.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is already rented for the month of August.

definitions.note: past participle of louer
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son idée a été louée par toute l’équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her idea was praised by the whole team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les appartements sont déjà loués.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartments are already rented.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses efforts ont été loués par tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His efforts were praised by everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est loyale envers ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is loyal to her friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa loyauté envers ses amis est admirable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His loyalty to his friends is admirable.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont loyaux envers leurs amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are loyal to their friends.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the rent paid for housing (apartment, house, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le loyer est trop cher dans ce quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rent is too expensive in this neighborhood.

definitions.note: Past participle of « lire » (used with auxiliaries like « avoir/être » and in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai lu ce livre en une semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read that book in a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Même après une longue journée, elle reste lucide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even after a long day, she stays clear-minded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En été, on voit des lucioles dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, you can see fireflies in the garden.

definitions.note: Proper noun (place name): a commune in northeastern France (Marne).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous passons par Ludes demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re passing through Ludes tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « lire »; used with « être » or with « avoir » when the direct object is feminine and placed before the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai lue hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read it yesterday.

definitions.native: him, her, to him, to her
definitions.note: can be an indirect object pronoun or a stressed pronoun, depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lui parle tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talk to him every day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "lumineux".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette pièce est lumineuse le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room is bright in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a room, space, or day with a lot of light.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet appartement est très lumineux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment is very bright.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de lumière dans cette pièce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of light in this room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les lumières de la ville sont magnifiques la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city lights are beautiful at night.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to describe someone who seems spaced out or dreamy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un paysage lunaire entoure le volcan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A lunar landscape surrounds the volcano.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a l’air lunaire aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks spaced out today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se voit lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je travaille souvent les lundis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often work on Mondays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce soir, la lune est très brillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight, the moon is very bright.

definitions.note: Plural of « lune » (moon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On peut voir deux lunes dans ce jeu de science-fiction.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can see two moons in this science-fiction game.

definitions.note: Usually plural in French when referring to eyeglasses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai oublié mes lunettes à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my glasses at home.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural) of « lire »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces livres ont été lus par beaucoup d’étudiants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books have been read by many students.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past form (passé simple) of « lire »; common in books and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il lut la lettre en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He read the letter in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lutte contre le réchauffement climatique est urgente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fight against global warming is urgent.

definitions.note: Often used with "contre" (against) or "pour" (for) to talk about fighting for/against an idea, problem, or cause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle doit lutter contre la maladie depuis des années.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has had to fight the illness for years.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous luttez pour vos droits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are fighting for your rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a lutté contre la maladie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fought against the illness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet hôtel est un vrai luxe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hotel is real luxury.

definitions.note: In France, a lycée is the school for students roughly ages 15–18 (after collège).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma sœur est au lycée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is in high school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les lycéens préparent un exposé pour le cours d’histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The high school students are preparing a presentation for history class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons vu un lynx dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a lynx in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un lys blanc pour la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a white lily for the table.

definitions.note: Often means "there"; in everyday speech it can also mean "here" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le livre est là.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is there.

definitions.note: Nonstandard spelling; standard French is « là ». Used to indicate a place/position (“there”), often in pointing or location contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le café est lá, sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is there, on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está lá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is there.

definitions.note: Often insulting when used about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je le trouve lâche de ne rien dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it’s cowardly of him not to say anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ta chaussure est trop lâche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your shoe is too loose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne sois pas un lâche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a coward.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lâche la corde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let go of the rope.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (lâcher quelque chose/quelqu’un) or with "lâcher prise" (to let go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux lâcher ma main maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can let go of my hand now.

definitions.note: Can mean letting something fall accidentally or deliberately.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a lâcher le verre et il s’est cassé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dropped the glass and it broke.

definitions.native: to loosen, to slacken (e.g., pressure, a grip)
definitions.note: Used for easing tension or reducing pressure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois lâcher un peu la corde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to loosen the rope a bit.

definitions.native: to let out / to blurt out (words, an insult, a secret)
definitions.note: Informal in many contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a lâcher une insulte devant tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He let out/blurted out an insult in front of everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des lâches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are cowards.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu lâches ma main !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re letting go of my hand!

definitions.note: Command form ("vous") of "lâcher".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lâchez ma main !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let go of my hand!

definitions.note: Past participle of « lâcher ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai lâché la corde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let go of the rope.

definitions.note: Informal/slang, usually in the expression « faire de la lèche » (to suck up to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il en a marre de faire de la lèche au patron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s fed up with sucking up to the boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien lèche ma main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog licks my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lève la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I raise my hand.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun: se lever.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se lève tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets up early.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « lever » (they raise/lift).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils lèvent la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They raise their hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « lever » (they get up/stand up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se lèvent tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They get up early in the morning.

definitions.note: Simple future (3rd person singular) of "lever".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle lèvera la main pour poser une question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will raise her hand to ask a question.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of « lever ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu lèves la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You raise your hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une coupure sur la lèvre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cut on my lip.

definitions.note: Plural form of « lèvre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle se met du rouge à lèvres sur les lèvres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She puts lipstick on her lips.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien lécha ma main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog licked my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien va lécher la main de son maître.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is going to lick his owner's hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a léché ma main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog licked my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est légal en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s legal in France.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “légal.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette procédure est légale en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This procedure is legal in France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes légalement responsable de vos actes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are legally responsible for your actions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce joueur est légendaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That player is legendary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selon la légende, ce château est hanté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the legend, this castle is haunted.

definitions.note: Text explaining a photo, illustration, map, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lis la légende sous la photo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Read the caption under the photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les légendes racontent l’histoire du village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The legends tell the story of the village.

definitions.note: Often used for the text under a photo, image, or figure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux lire les légendes sous les photos ?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, je mangeais souvent des céréales le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I often ate cereal in the morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing, background, or habitual action in the past); 3rd person singular of « manger » (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais petit, il mangeait souvent des céréales le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he often ate cereal in the morning.

definitions.note: Present participle (often used like “while eating” or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En mangeant, elle a renversé son verre d’eau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While eating, she knocked over her glass of water.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with ils/elles (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils mangent une pizza ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They eat a pizza tonight.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with “nous” (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous mangeons au restaurant ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating at the restaurant tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime manger des pommes après l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to eat apples after school.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (il/elle/on) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mangera après l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will eat after school.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, je mangerai plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will eat earlier.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mangerais une pizza ce soir si j'avais faim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would eat a pizza tonight if I were hungry.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu mangeras une pomme après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will eat an apple after school.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form, used for polite or plural “you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous mangerez à quelle heure ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time will you eat tonight?

definitions.note: Simple future tense, 1st person plural ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, nous mangerons au restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, we will eat at the restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils mangeront au restaurant ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will eat at the restaurant tonight.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « manger » used with « tu » (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu manges une pomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You eat an apple.

definitions.note: Used with "vous"; it can be formal singular or plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangez votre soupe, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat your soup, please.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the simple past (passé simple), mostly used in literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous mangeâmes en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate in silence.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (you ate / were eating).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand vous étiez enfants, vous mangiez souvent des bonbons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were children, you often ate candy.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « manger » (used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous étions enfants, nous mangions souvent des crêpes le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we often ate crepes on Sundays.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in written/narrative French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils mangèrent rapidement avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ate quickly before leaving.

definitions.note: past participle of « manger » (often used with « avoir » in the passé composé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai mangé une pomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate an apple.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « manger »; often used in the passive (with « être ») or when the past participle agrees with a preceding direct object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pomme est déjà mangée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple is already eaten.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pommes sont déjà mangées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apples are already eaten.

definitions.note: past participle of « manger »; used with an auxiliary verb and may agree in gender/number depending on the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les gâteaux ont été mangés très vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cakes were eaten very quickly.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe someone who is very particular or overly focused on something (e.g., cleanliness or order).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est maniaque de la propreté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is obsessive about cleanliness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un maniaque du rangement : tout est parfaitement aligné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a neat freak: everything is perfectly lined up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle manie bien le couteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She handles the knife well.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean handling/operation of an object, tool, machine, or weapon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maniement de cette machine est facile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Handling this machine is easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une grande manifestation dans le centre-ville aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big demonstration in the city center today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a eu des manifestations dans la ville ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were demonstrations in the city this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a manifestement oublié notre rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He clearly forgot our appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils manifestent contre la nouvelle loi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are protesting against the new law.

definitions.note: Often used for taking part in a street protest (une manifestation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont manifesté contre la réforme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They protested against the reform.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a manifesté son intérêt pour le poste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed her interest in the position.

definitions.note: Often implies something secretive or underhanded.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manigance quelque chose derrière notre dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s plotting something behind our backs.

definitions.note: Usually implies doing something secretive or dishonest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu manigances encore un plan pour tricher ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you scheming up another plan to cheat?

definitions.note: Often implies something secretive or underhanded.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout a été manigancé en secret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything was plotted in secret.

definitions.note: Often used for physically handling an object; it can also mean manipulating people (controlling them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manipule la machine avec précaution.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handles the machine carefully.

definitions.note: Often used for handling objects; when used about people or information, it implies influencing in a dishonest or unfair way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut manipuler ce produit avec précaution.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to handle this product with care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est senti manipulé par ses collègues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt manipulated by his coworkers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fais-le de cette manière, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it this way, please.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « avoir des manières » (to have manners) or « les bonnes manières » (good manners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a de bonnes manières.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has good manners.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a fashion model (male or female).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mannequin porte une robe bleue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The model is wearing a blue dress.

definitions.note: A human-shaped figure used to display clothing in a store.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont mis le manteau sur un mannequin dans la vitrine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put the coat on a mannequin in the shop window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont visité un vieux manoir à la campagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They visited an old manor in the countryside.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), mostly used in writing; in everyday speech you’ll usually see/hear the passé composé (a manqué).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manqua son train et arriva en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He missed his train and arrived late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manquait deux chaises, et elles manquaient encore ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two chairs were missing, and they were still missing this morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manquait deux chaises dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two chairs were missing in the room.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manque une page : elle est manquante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A page is missing: it’s missing.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manque encore deux documents : ils sont manquants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two documents are still missing: they are missing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un manque de temps pour finir ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lack of time to finish this project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je manque mon train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m missing my train.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "manquer de temps" = "to lack time").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manque de temps aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t have enough time today.

definitions.note: Often used with the indirect object to mean “to be missing from/to someone” (e.g., “Tu me manques” = “I miss you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manque deux chaises, donc elles me manquent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two chairs are missing, so I’m lacking them.

definitions.note: Often used as “manquer à + person” to mean “to miss someone” (the person missed is the subject in French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais manquer à mes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are going to miss me.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: « manquer quelque chose » = to miss something (a bus, an appointment, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle manquera le train si elle ne part pas tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will miss the train if she doesn’t leave right away.

definitions.native: will lack, will run out of
definitions.note: Often used with « de »: « manquer de + noun » = to lack (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manquera de temps pour finir ce travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will lack time to finish this work.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object: « Tu me manqueras » = “I will miss you” (literally “you will be missing to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te manquerai quand je serai loin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will miss me when I’m far away.

definitions.native: will lack, will run out of
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je manquerai de temps demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will lack time tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle manquerait sa famille si elle partait longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would miss her family if she left for a long time.

definitions.native: would be missing, would be lacking
definitions.note: Often used to say something is missing (e.g., an item, money, time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manquerait une chaise dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A chair would be missing in the room.

definitions.note: Future tense (tu form). Can mean either missing someone/something or failing to do something, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu manqueras beaucoup à ta famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your family will miss you a lot.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural or formal singular future of « manquer ». Commonly: « vous manquerez (qqn/qqch) » = “you will miss (someone/something)”. Also: « manquer à + personne » = “to be missed by someone” (e.g., « vous manquerez à votre famille » = “your family will miss you”, literally “you will be missing to your family”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous manquerez beaucoup à votre famille pendant votre absence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your family will miss you a lot during your absence.

definitions.note: With people, French often uses an inverted structure: « Tu me manques » means « I miss you » (literally: “you are missing from me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me manques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss you.

definitions.note: Can mean “you miss (something/someone)” or “you are missing/lacking (something)”; it also appears in expressions like « Vous manquez de ... » (“You lack ...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous manquez de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You lack time.

definitions.note: Can mean “we miss” (someone/something) or “we lack” (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous manquons de temps aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We lack time today.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing; can mean either “missed” (failed to catch/attend) or “were missing” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils manquèrent le train de quelques minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They missed the train by a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai manqué le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis mon manteau parce qu’il fait froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my coat because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En hiver, je porte souvent des manteaux chauds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, I often wear warm coats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai acheté un manuel de français pour débutants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a beginner French manual.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une tâche manuelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a manual task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai acheté les manuels pour le cours de français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought the textbooks for the French class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai lu le manuscrit avant sa publication.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the manuscript before it was published.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants font un tour de manège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids go for a ride on the carousel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pilote a réussi la manœuvre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pilot succeeded in the maneuver.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « manœuvre (de chantier) » for an unskilled construction worker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils cherchent un manœuvre pour le chantier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are looking for a laborer for the construction site.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au marché, j’achète un maquereau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the market, I’m buying a mackerel.

definitions.note: Informal/insulting meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté un maquereau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a pimp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle met un peu de maquillage avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She puts on a little makeup before going out.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: « se maquiller » = to put on makeup.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle se maquille tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She puts on makeup every morning.

definitions.native: to put on makeup; to apply makeup (to)
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: « se maquiller » = to put on makeup.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va se maquiller avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to put on makeup before going out.

definitions.native: to make up (someone), to do someone’s makeup
definitions.note: Used with a direct object person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maquilleur va maquiller l’actrice avant le tournage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The makeup artist is going to do the actress’s makeup before filming.

definitions.native: to doctor, to falsify (figures, accounts, evidence)
definitions.note: Figurative/extended meaning: to manipulate to make something look better or different from reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont tenté de maquiller les chiffres du rapport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to doctor the figures in the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup d’oiseaux dans le marais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are lots of birds in the marsh.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’entraîne pour courir un marathon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is training to run a marathon.

definitions.note: Often used in a mildly old-fashioned or playful way, but it can also be insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce petit maraud a encore caché mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That little rascal hid my keys again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sol de la salle de bain est en marbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom floor is made of marble.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « marcher »; commonly used in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marcha jusqu’à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walked to the station.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils marchaient ensemble après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were walking together after school.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of « marcher » (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je marchais vers l’école quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was walking to school when it started to rain.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marchait vers l’école quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was walking toward the school when it started to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le marchand vend des fruits au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The merchant sells fruit at the market.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (des marchandises), especially in shipping and trade contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les marchandises arrivent demain au port.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goods arrive tomorrow at the port.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural, especially in shipping/trade contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces marchandises viennent d’Espagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These goods come from Spain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les marchands vendent des fruits et des légumes au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The merchants sell fruit and vegetables at the market.

definitions.note: Present participle of « marcher »; often used with « en » (e.g., « en marchant » = “while walking”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je parle souvent au téléphone en marchant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often talk on the phone while walking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention, cette marche est glissante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, this step is slippery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On fait une marche après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go for a walk after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je marche jusqu’à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I walk to school.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « ça marche » meaning “it works / it’s working.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon téléphone marche maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone works now.

definitions.note: Also commonly means “work/run” (for a machine or device), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils marchent jusqu’à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They walk to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais marcher jusqu'à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to walk to the train station.

definitions.note: Often used for machines, devices, or plans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon téléphone ne peut pas marcher sans batterie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone can't work without a battery.

definitions.note: Simple future (3rd person singular) of « marcher »; can also mean « will work » when talking about something functioning (e.g., a device).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, elle marchera jusqu'à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, she will walk to school.

definitions.note: Conditional present ("would"), used for hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si elle avait plus de temps, elle marcherait jusqu’au travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If she had more time, she would walk to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les marches sont glissantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The steps are slippery.

definitions.note: Often translated as “walk,” not “march” (unless it’s specifically about marching like soldiers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu marches vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You walk fast.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marchez jusqu’au parc, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Walk to the park, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nous). Often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand nous étions enfants, nous marchions jusqu'à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we walked to school.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) present; often used to make a suggestion or invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marchons jusqu'au parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's walk to the park.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 1st person plural: used mainly in literature and storytelling; in speech you’d usually use "nous avons marché".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le dîner, nous marchâmes jusqu’au village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, we walked to the village.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; mainly used in writing (stories, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils marchèrent toute la nuit pour atteindre le village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They walked all night to reach the village.

definitions.note: Past participle of « marcher » (usually used with « avoir » to form the past tense). Often confused with English “march”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai marché jusqu’à l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I walked to the school.

definitions.note: Often refers to a street market or open-air market, but can also mean the general idea of a market (e.g., the job market).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va au marché le samedi matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go to the market on Saturday morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se voit mardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you Tuesday.

definitions.note: English loanword used in French; the common everyday word for “mare” is usually “jument”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce cheval est une mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This horse is a mare.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écris ton nom dans la marge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write your name in the margin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son mari travaille à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her husband works in Paris.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), mostly found in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le roi maria sa fille à un prince étranger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king married his daughter to a foreign prince.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mariage a eu lieu samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wedding took place on Saturday.

definitions.note: Plural form of « mariage ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont assisté à deux mariages cet été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They attended two weddings this summer.

definitions.note: Verb form of « marier » (not the name « Marie »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prêtre marie les deux amoureux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest marries the two lovers.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as « se marier » = “to get married.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se marient en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re getting married in June.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive pronouns: « se marier » = to get married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont se marier en juin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle se mariera en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will get married in June.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You marry your sister to Julien.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you getting married in June?

definitions.note: Informal/common term for cannabis.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marijuana is illegal in some countries.

definitions.note: Often used for things related to the sea (e.g., life, air, animals).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sea air is very fresh this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le marin rentre au port ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sailor is coming back to the port tonight.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « la Marine » (the Navy) or « biologie marine » (marine biology).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rêve d’une carrière marine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dreams of a naval career.

definitions.note: Often refers to a country’s naval forces (e.g., la Marine française = the French Navy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère travaille dans la marine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother works in the navy.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les forces marines protègent la côte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Naval forces protect the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les marins rentrent au port ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sailors are coming back to the port tonight.

definitions.note: As a noun, this refers to the color (short for "bleu marine").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime les marins pour l'hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like navy blues for winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants jouent avec des marionnettes après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children play with puppets after school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses deux sœurs ont des maris très gentils.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her two sisters have very nice husbands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sécurité maritime est très importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maritime safety is very important.

definitions.note: Past participle of « marier »; often used with « être » or « se marier » to mean “(to be/get) married.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est marié en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got married in June.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form (use « mariée » for feminine).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been married for ten years.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « marier » (often used with « être » to describe someone’s marital status).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est mariée depuis deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been married for two years.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est mariée depuis trois ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been married for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mariée porte une robe blanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bride is wearing a white dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mariée arrive à l’église.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bride arrives at the church.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of « marier »; used with « être » to describe women who are married
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont mariées depuis cinq ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been married for five years.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont mariées depuis dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been married for ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont mariés depuis dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been married for ten years.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont mariés depuis dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been married for ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mariés dansent toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newlyweds dance all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mariés attendent leurs femmes devant l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The husbands are waiting for their wives in front of the school.

definitions.note: In everyday French, people often say "confiture" for jam in general; "marmelade" is specifically a citrus fruit spread.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange de la marmelade d’orange au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat orange marmalade for breakfast.

definitions.note: Often refers to a large pot used for soups or stews.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La soupe mijote dans une marmite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is simmering in a pot.

definitions.note: often used for speaking in a low, unclear voice (sometimes complaining under one’s breath)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marmonnait une réponse sans me regarder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was mumbling an answer without looking at me.

definitions.note: Often used when speaking quietly and unclearly, sometimes to complain under your breath.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il commence à marmonner quelque chose, mais je ne comprends pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He starts to mumble something, but I don’t understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette marque est très populaire en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This brand is very popular in France.

definitions.note: Often used for a mark/sign left on something, like a stain or scratch.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une marque sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a mark on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il marque un point.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He marks a point.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais marquer la date sur le calendrier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to mark the date on the calendar.

definitions.note: Used especially for scoring points or goals in sports or games.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veut marquer deux buts pendant le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to score two goals during the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il connaît bien les marques de chaussures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knows shoe brands well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des marques sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are marks on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai marqué la date sur le calendrier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I marked the date on the calendar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma marraine m'a offert un livre pour mon anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My godmother gave me a book for my birthday.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment marrant !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really funny!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est vraiment marrante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is really funny.

definitions.note: Almost always used in the expression « en avoir marre (de…) » = “to be fed up (with…)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'en ai marre de ce bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm fed up with this noise.

definitions.note: Almost always used in the expression « en avoir marre (de ...) » meaning “to be fed up (with ...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’en ai marre !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fed up!

definitions.note: Informal; most often used reflexively as « se marrer » (to have a good laugh).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va se marrer ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to have a good laugh tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for the color of hair, eyes, or clothes; it’s usually invariable (often not changing for feminine/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses yeux sont marron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her eyes are brown.

definitions.note: The month of the year.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon anniversaire est en mars.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in March.

definitions.note: The planet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mars est une planète très froide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mars is a very cold planet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’un marteau pour accrocher ce tableau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a hammer to hang this picture.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les arts martiaux demandent de la discipline.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Martial arts require discipline.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les martiens arrivent sur Terre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the Martians arrive on Earth.

definitions.note: Often used in set titles, e.g. « maréchal de France » (a high military rank).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il admire le maréchal de France dans les livres d’histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admires the Marshal of France in history books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La marée monte vite ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tide is rising quickly tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En français, « livre » est un nom masculin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In French, “livre” is a masculine noun.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with a plural masculine noun or mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les noms masculins finissent souvent par une consonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Masculine nouns often end with a consonant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je porte un masque dans le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wear a mask on the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils portent des masques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wearing masks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le massacre a choqué tout le pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The massacre shocked the whole country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il massacre ses adversaires au débat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He destroys his opponents in the debate.

definitions.note: Often used for killing people or animals; can also be used more loosely to mean doing something very badly (e.g., “massacrer une chanson” = to butcher a song).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont décidé de massacrer les civils pendant la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to massacre civilians during the war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été massacrés pendant la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were massacred during the war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis offert un massage après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I treated myself to a massage after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La masse de cette pierre est très grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mass of this stone is very large.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te masse les épaules.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I massage your shoulders.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le sport, je vais masser mes épaules.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After working out, I’m going to massage my shoulders.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une table en bois massif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a table made of solid wood.

definitions.note: Used especially for a sports match.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On regarde un match de foot ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a soccer match tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux matchs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two matches tonight.

definitions.note: Used in chess (from the verb « mater »). Not related to English “mate” meaning “friend.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aux échecs, il mate son adversaire en deux coups.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In chess, he checkmates his opponent in two moves.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un nouveau matelas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new mattress.

definitions.native: to watch; to check out; to eye (someone/something)
definitions.note: Informal (slang). Used for watching something (a film, a video) or looking at someone/something with interest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va mater un film ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are we going to watch a movie tonight?

definitions.note: Short for « école maternelle » (nursery school) in France.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma fille va à la maternelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My daughter goes to kindergarten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est en congé de maternité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is on maternity leave.

definitions.note: Informal; often used like “check it out!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Matez ce film, il est génial !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check out this movie, it’s great!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai un contrôle de math demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a math test tomorrow.

definitions.note: Short for « mathématiques »; common in school contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime bien les maths.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like math.

definitions.note: male form (female: mathématicienne)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est mathématicien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a mathematician.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in French when talking about the school subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mathématiques sont ma matière préférée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Math is my favorite subject.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me lève tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get up early in the morning.

definitions.note: Used for things or habits that happen early; for people, it means they’re up and active early.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais une promenade matinale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take an early morning walk.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "matinal"; used to describe something that happens in the morning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une routine matinale simple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a simple morning routine.

definitions.note: Often used for “in the morning” as an adverbial phrase (e.g., « ce matinée » is incorrect; use « ce matin »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je travaille toute la matinée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work all morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette chaise est faite d’une matière solide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is made of a solid material.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma matière préférée, c’est l’histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite subject is history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous étudions les différentes matières et leurs propriétés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We study the different materials and their properties.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes matières préférées sont les maths et l’histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite subjects are math and history.

definitions.note: Informal slang; often refers to equipment (especially for work, sports, music, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai oublié mon matos à la maison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le matou dort sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tomcat is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.note: Used mainly in math/science or technical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette matrice a trois lignes et deux colonnes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très mature pour son âge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very mature for his age.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons besoin de matériaux pour construire la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need materials to build the house.

definitions.note: Often used as an uncountable noun for the things needed to do a task.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re missing some equipment for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je maudis cette journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I curse this day.

definitions.note: Often used as a mild swear word (like “damn” / “damned”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai perdu mes clés dans ce maudit sac !

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; can be used literally (cursed) or as an annoyed emphasis (damned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai perdu mes clés dans cette maudite maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost my keys in this damned house.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces maudits moustiques m'empêchent de dormir.

definitions.note: Often placed before the noun (e.g., un mauvais film).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is bad.

definitions.note: In modern French, « mauvais » is normally an adjective (e.g. « un mauvais film »). For the adverb “badly,” French usually uses « mal ».
