definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a bad movie.

definitions.note: Used as a noun to refer to what is bad in general (often in expressions like « le mauvais »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a du mauvais dans cette histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is something bad in this story.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « mauvais ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une mauvaise idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a bad idea.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « mauvais ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont de mauvaises nouvelles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are bad news.

definitions.note: Informal and often insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de faire ta mauviette !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop being such a wimp!

definitions.note: Plural of « mal »; often used for physical pains or troubles (e.g., « maux de tête » = headaches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des maux de tête aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have headaches today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "maximal".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons atteint la capacité maximale de la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have reached the maximum capacity of the room.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « au maximum » (at most) or « maximum » as an invariable adjective meaning “maximum.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes dix personnes maximum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are ten people at most.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vitesse maximum est de 130 km/h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maximum speed is 130 km/h.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais un sandwich au poulet avec de la mayonnaise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a chicken sandwich with mayonnaise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maçon construit un mur en briques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bricklayer is building a brick wall.

definitions.note: Often used as a title for certain professions (especially lawyers and notaries): Maître + surname.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maître explique la leçon aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the lesson to the students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les maîtres entrent dans la salle de classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers enter the classroom.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to a primary school teacher.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maîtresse explique la leçon aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the lesson to the students.

definitions.note: A woman in a romantic/sexual relationship with someone (often with the idea that the person is not her partner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une maîtresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a mistress.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a (female) primary school teacher in France.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maîtresse explique la leçon aux élèves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the lesson to the students.

definitions.note: Refers to a woman someone is having a romantic/sexual relationship with, often secretly (e.g., outside marriage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une maîtresse depuis des années.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has had a mistress for years.

definitions.native: mastery, command (of a skill or subject)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une bonne maîtrise du français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a good command of French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle maîtrise parfaitement le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She masters French perfectly.

definitions.native: to master; to gain mastery of (a skill/subject)
definitions.note: Used for learning and becoming proficient in something (language, technique, topic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle peut enfin maîtriser le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can finally master French.

definitions.native: to control; to keep in check (a situation/emotion)
definitions.note: Used for controlling reactions, emotions, or managing a difficult situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaie de maîtriser sa colère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to control his anger.

definitions.native: to tame; to bring under control (someone/something)
definitions.note: Can be used for bringing something unruly under control (figuratively or literally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pompiers ont réussi à maîtriser l’incendie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters managed to bring the fire under control.

definitions.note: Usually used with "tu" (2nd person singular): "you (singular, informal) master/control".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu maîtrises bien le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You speak French well (you’ve mastered French).

definitions.note: Present tense form meaning “you master/control” (addressing one person formally, or multiple people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous maîtrisez très bien le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You master French very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a maîtrisé la situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He controlled the situation.

definitions.note: In French, this usually refers to corn/maize as a food (kernels) or the plant in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange du maïs avec du poulet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating corn with chicken.

definitions.note: Unstressed pronoun usually placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me connais déjà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already know me.

definitions.note: Object pronoun (direct or indirect); also used as a reflexive pronoun before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me voit tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees me every day.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un mec sympa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a nice guy.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a trois mecs devant la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are three guys in front of the door.

definitions.note: Used in French mostly in business contexts; often implies a professional meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting with my team at 10 o'clock.

definitions.note: Comparative/superlative form of « bon ». Often used with « le/la/les » to mean “the best.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the best movie I’ve seen this year.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the best person or thing (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est le meilleur de la classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the best in the class.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "meilleur"; used when describing a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est la meilleure idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the best idea.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « meilleur »; often used with plural feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont les meilleures idées.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town is threatened by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont menacés par la tempête.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il menaça de partir si tu continuais.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je reçois un rapport mensuel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I receive a monthly report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous mentais encore, et je le sais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are lying again, and I know it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mentait à ses parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was lying to his parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un effort mental difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a difficult mental effort.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She does mental gymnastics to focus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis mentalement épuisé après cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m mentally exhausted after this week.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils mentent à leurs parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are lying to their parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un menteur.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are liars.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "menteur"; used for a woman or girl.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une menteuse, ne la crois pas.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "mentir" used with "vous" (formal singular or plural).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you lying?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une tisane à la menthe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a mint herbal tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier, j’ai compris qu’il menti à ses parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, I realized that he lied to his parents.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing (e.g., novels, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mentionna son nom dans la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mentioned his name in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais mentionner ton nom dans l’e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to mention your name in the email.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mentionner".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce problème est mentionné dans le rapport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ne faut pas mentir à ses parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not lie to your parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si j’avais peur, je mentirais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I were afraid, I would lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mentit à ses parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lies to his parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une cicatrice sur le menton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a scar on his chin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais le menu, s’il vous plaît.

definitions.note: past participle of « mener »

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The debates were conducted calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mer est calme aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sea is calm today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été engagé comme mercenaire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mercenaires ont quitté la ville après la bataille.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour ton aide !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your help!

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to express gratitude (even though it’s a noun originally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci pour votre aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se voit mercredi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Wednesday.

definitions.note: Vulgar. Used as an exclamation of annoyance, anger, or frustration (similar to “damn!”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit! I forgot my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merde, j’ai oublié mes clés !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit, I forgot my keys!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête d’être un merdeux !

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel merdier dans cette chambre !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a mess in this room!

definitions.note: Informal and vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment merdique.

definitions.note: Plural of « mer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les mers sont calmes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The seas are calm today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est une merveille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is a wonder.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce musée abrite des merveilles du monde entier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This museum houses wonders from all over the world.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette idée est merveilleuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This idea is wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le concert s’est merveilleusement bien passé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert went wonderfully well.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These ideas are wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is wonderful!

definitions.note: used before plural nouns

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mesdemoiselles, écoutez-moi, s’il vous plaît.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The messenger brings a letter to the king.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received three messages this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s presenting his product at an international trade fair.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gentlemen, please come in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Messire Jean, veuillez entrer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to measure the table before buying a tablecloth.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down the measurements of the room.

definitions.note: Usually means “you measure” (informal singular, tu).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You measure the table with a measuring tape.

definitions.note: From the verb « mettre ». Not related to English “met” (past tense of “meet”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the book on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu mets la clé sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the key on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were putting the books on the shelf.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/repeated action); also used for descriptions/background in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mettais la table tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to set the table every evening.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past) of « mettre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mettait son manteau avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was putting on his coat before going out.

definitions.note: Present participle of « mettre »; often used after « en » to mean “by putting/placing.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By putting the book on the table, he made a noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je mette la table avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to set the table before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu) of « mettre »; often used after « il faut que », « pour que », « bien que », etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu mettes tes chaussures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to put on your shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future of « mettre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mettrai les clés sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Conditional present (il/elle/on).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With more time, she would set the table before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu mettras les clés sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Core meaning; also used in many everyday expressions.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put the book on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put on my coat before going out.

definitions.note: Common expression: « mettre la table » = to set the table.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois mettre la table avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to set the table before dinner.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought new furniture for the living room.

definitions.note: Very informal slang (verlan); can sound crude depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans eau, la plante meurt.

definitions.note: Informal; used as an adjective meaning “very small,” often in words like « micro-ondes » (microwave) or « micro-entreprise » (microbusiness).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job is monotonous.

definitions.note: Honorific title of respect, especially for a bishop or other high-ranking church figure (and sometimes for nobility).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Monseigneur, puis-je vous poser une question ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My lord, may I ask you a question?

definitions.note: polite form of address for a man; also used before a surname
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Excusez-moi, monsieur, cette place est libre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, sir, is this seat free?

definitions.note: A Catholic honorific/title for certain clergy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le monsignor a célébré la messe ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The monsignor celebrated Mass this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un monstre dans cette histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a monster in this story.

definitions.note: Plural form of « monstre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants ont peur des monstres sous le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are afraid of the monsters under the bed.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette erreur est monstrueuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This mistake is monstrous.

definitions.note: Used literally for something monster-like, and very often figuratively for something extremely large/excessive or morally shocking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont dépensé une somme monstrueuse, et c’était vraiment monstrueux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They spent a monstrous amount, and it was truly outrageous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mont est couvert de neige en hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mountain is covered with snow in winter.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), most common in written narratives; in everyday speech you usually use « est monté(e) ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il monta l’escalier en courant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ran up the stairs.

definitions.note: Often used for film/video editing (cutting and assembling scenes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le montage du film a pris plusieurs mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The editing of the film took several months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous faisons une randonnée en montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going hiking in the mountains.

definitions.note: Plural of "montagne".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les montagnes sont magnifiques en hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mountains are magnificent in winter.

definitions.native: was going up, was getting on, was climbing
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past) of « monter ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was climbing the stairs slowly.

definitions.note: Often used in administrative/financial contexts (e.g., the amount of money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le montant total est de 50 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The total amount is 50 euros.

definitions.note: Present participle of « monter »; often used with « en » to mean “while going up / as (someone) goes up.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While going up the stairs, I found my keys.

definitions.note: Also used for “gets on/boards” (e.g., a bus) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il monte les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbs the stairs.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prix montent encore cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices are going up again this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais monter les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go up the stairs.

definitions.note: Used when you increase the level of something (like the volume, the heat, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux monter le son, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn up the sound, please?

definitions.note: Present tense form of « monter » with « tu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu montes les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go up the stairs.

definitions.native: go up, come up, get on, climb
definitions.note: Usually used as “you (plural) …” or the formal “you …” (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Montez au troisième étage, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go up to the third floor, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons vu une montgolfière au-dessus des champs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a hot-air balloon above the fields.

definitions.native: let's go up, we go up
definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can be present tense (“we go up”) or an imperative (“let’s go up / let’s get on”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Montons dans le bus !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s get on the bus!

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mostly used in writing (stories, novels, formal history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il montra la photo à ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed the photo to his friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une montre noire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a black watch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle me montre une photo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shows me a photo.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with ils/elles (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils montrent leurs photos à leurs amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They show their photos to their friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te montrer une photo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to show you a photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle montrera ses photos demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will show her photos tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te montrerai la photo demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will show you the photo tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me montreras tes photos demain ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you show me your photos tomorrow?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will show your tickets at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deux montres : une pour le sport et une pour le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two watches: one for sports and one for work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me montres tes photos ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you showing me your photos?

definitions.note: Formal/plural (vous) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Montrez-moi votre passeport, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me your passport, please.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") present tense; often used to make a suggestion ("let's").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Montrons-lui notre plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's show him our plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai montré la photo à mon ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I showed the photo to my friend.

definitions.note: Often used for eyeglass frames or the setting that holds a stone in jewelry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai choisi une monture plus légère pour mes lunettes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chose a lighter frame for my glasses.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person plural of « monter »; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils montèrent au sommet avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went up to the summit before nightfall.

definitions.note: Past participle of « monter »; used with « être » in compound tenses for motion (e.g. « il est monté »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est monté au troisième étage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went up to the third floor.

definitions.note: Often used for furniture or equipment (e.g., something already assembled).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The piece of furniture is already assembled.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « monter » (used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est montée dans le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got on the bus.

definitions.note: Often refers to an upward slope or an uphill part of a road/path.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La montée est difficile, mais la vue en vaut la peine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The climb is difficult, but the view is worth it.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « monter » (used e.g. with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont montées au troisième étage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went up to the third floor.

definitions.note: Past participle of « monter » used with « être » for intransitive uses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont montés au troisième étage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went up to the third floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce monument est très ancien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This monument is very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À Paris, il y a beaucoup de monuments célèbres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Paris, there are many famous monuments.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past form (passé simple), often used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il moqua son accent devant tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mocked his accent in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past). Often used with "de" (se moquer de).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se moquait de mon accent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was making fun of my accent.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the reflexive expression « se moquer de » (to make fun of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se moque de moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s making fun of me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se moquent de lui à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They make fun of him at school.

definitions.native: to make fun of, to mock
definitions.note: Most often used in the reflexive form “se moquer de” (to make fun of someone/something, to not care about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aime moquer l'accent des autres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to make fun of other people's accent.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with « tu » (informal “you”). Often used with « se moquer de » + noun/pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pourquoi tu te moques de moi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you making fun of me?

definitions.note: Usually refers to fitted (wall-to-wall) carpet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le salon, il y a de la moquette grise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the living room, there is gray carpet.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; can be formal singular or plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pourquoi vous moquez-vous de lui ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you making fun of him?

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple); common in stories and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se moquèrent de lui devant toute la classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They made fun of him in front of the whole class.

definitions.note: Often used with « se moquer de » = “to make fun of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s'est moqué de moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made fun of me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été moqués par leurs camarades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were mocked by their classmates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce choix est moral.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This choice is moral.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « moral ». Not to be confused with English “morale” (= spirits, confidence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision morale difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a difficult moral decision.

definitions.note: Refers to the general state of mind/confidence of a person or group; often used in expressions about how people are feeling collectively.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La morale de l’équipe est bonne aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team’s morale is good today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Moralement, je ne peux pas accepter ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Morally, I can't accept that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux un morceau de gâteau, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a piece of cake, please.

definitions.note: Plural of « morceau ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des morceaux de verre par terre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are pieces of glass on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien mord le facteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bites the mailman.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the polite/formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mordez doucement, c’est encore chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bite gently; it’s still hot.

definitions.note: Past simple (literary) form meaning “(he/she/it) bit.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien mordit le facteur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bit the mailman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention, ce chien peut mordre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful, this dog can bite.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « mordre » (used with « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu mords dans la pomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You bite into the apple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est fait mordu par un chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got bitten by a dog.

definitions.native: to take a beating, to get beat up
definitions.note: Informal/slang; can be literal (physically) or figurative (to really suffer or have a hard time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a morflé pendant le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took a beating during the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La morgue de l’hôpital est au sous-sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hospital morgue is in the basement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis quelques jours, il a l’air morose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the past few days, he has seemed morose.

definitions.note: A strong opioid painkiller.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On m’a donné de la morphine à l’hôpital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me morphine at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le morse plonge sous la glace pour chercher de la nourriture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The walrus dives under the ice to look for food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une morsure sur le bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a bite on his arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est mort depuis trois ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been dead for three years.

definitions.note: Interjection used to mean “dead” in games, jokingly, or as slang (e.g., “I’m dead” = “that’s hilarious / I can’t”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dead, I missed the bus!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa mort a bouleversé toute la famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His death shook the whole family.

definitions.note: past participle of mourir (used with être in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon grand-père est mort l'année dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died last year.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La plante est morte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant is dead.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « mourir » (used with « être »).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother died in 2018.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une erreur mortelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a deadly mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes tous mortels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are all mortal.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette maladie est mortelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This disease is fatal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces erreurs peuvent avoir des effets mortels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These mistakes can have deadly effects.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “mere humans” (as opposed to gods, immortals, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous ne sommes que des mortels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are only mortals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous ne sommes que des mortels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are only mortals.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les feuilles sont mortes après l’hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaves are dead after the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trees are dead after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were three deaths on the road this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont morts pendant la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They died during the war.

definitions.note: Informal and a bit gross; common in everyday speech.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have snot running when I’m sick.

definitions.note: Insulting/derogatory term, often said about a child or teenager.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That brat lied to his parents again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne comprends pas ce mot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand this word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les motards portent un casque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The motorcyclists wear a helmet.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We slept in a motel near the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le moteur de la voiture fait un bruit étrange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car’s engine is making a strange noise.

definitions.note: Plural form of « moteur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces moteurs consomment moins d’essence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime le motif de cette robe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the pattern of this dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quels sont vos motifs ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are your reasons?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the patterns on this shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movement is in constant motion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai besoin de motivation pour étudier ce soir.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très motivé aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very motivated today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis motivée pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m motivated to learn French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va au travail en moto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes to work by motorcycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de motos dans cette rue.

definitions.note: Plural of « mouche ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des mouches dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are flies in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes vêtements sont mouillés.

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her shoes are wet after the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la pluie, les vêtements sont mouillés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the clothes are wet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mangé des moules avec des frites.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a cake pan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On mange des moules ce soir.

definitions.note: Past participle of « mémoriser ». Often used with « avoir » to form the past tense (passé composé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mémorisé son numéro de téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I memorized his phone number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais le ménage le samedi matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do the housework on Saturday morning.

definitions.note: Often used with forces/efforts (e.g., « ménager ses forces » = not exhaust yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut ménager ses forces avant la course.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to spare your strength before the race.

definitions.native: to handle carefully, to be considerate (of)
definitions.note: Can mean treating someone gently/with care (physically or emotionally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut le ménager un peu : il est fatigué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to go easy on him: he’s tired.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « tâches ménagères » (household chores).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais les tâches ménagères le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do the household chores on Saturday.

definitions.note: Often used in the reflexive form « se méprendre » (“to be mistaken”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux méprendre ses intentions si je ne lui pose pas de questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can misunderstand his intentions if I don’t ask him questions.

definitions.note: Usually used with "vous" (you plural or formal). Often in the expression "Vous vous méprenez" (You’re mistaken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vous méprenez : ce n’est pas ce que j’ai dit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re mistaken: that’s not what I said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a parlé de son collègue avec mépris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke about his coworker with contempt.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il méprisait ses camarades de classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despised his classmates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te méprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I despise you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils méprisent leurs adversaires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They despise their opponents.

definitions.native: to despise; to scorn; to look down on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais mépriser toute forme d’injustice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will despise every form of injustice.

definitions.native: to disdain; to treat with contempt
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils disent mépriser les règles quand elles les dérangent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say they disdain the rules when they inconvenience them.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous méprisons le mensonge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We despise lying.

definitions.note: Common misspelling of “mère” (mother).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma mére arrive ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother is arriving tonight.

definitions.note: Imparfait (past): “I/you/he/she/it deserved” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu méritais une seconde chance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserved a second chance.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), often used for background description or repeated/ongoing past situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il méritait une meilleure chance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deserved a better chance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a obtenu ce poste au mérite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got that job on merit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle mérite une pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She deserves a break.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) present tense of « mériter ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils méritent une récompense pour leur travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They deserve a reward for their work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux mériter une pause après ce travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can deserve a break after this work.

definitions.native: to be worthy of / to merit
definitions.note: Often used in formal writing: « mériter + nom » (mériter l'attention, mériter une récompense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce résultat semble mériter une explication.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This result seems to merit an explanation.

definitions.native: to earn (in the sense of deserve)
definitions.note: Not the same as earning money (« gagner de l'argent »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Par son courage, il a su mériter le respect de tous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Through his courage, he managed to earn/deserve everyone's respect.

definitions.note: Present tense form with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu mérites une pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserve a break.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous méritez une pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserve a break.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense (“we”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous méritons une pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We deserve a break.

definitions.note: Past participle of « mériter »; used with « avoir » (j’ai mérité) or as an adjective (un salaire mérité).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu as mérité une pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserved a break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bracelet est en métal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bracelet is made of metal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette porte a un bruit métallique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This door has a metallic sound.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce poème, la mer est une métaphore de la liberté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this poem, the sea is a metaphor for freedom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette méthode est facile à apprendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is easy to learn.

definitions.note: Plural form of « méthode ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous utilisons différentes méthodes pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We use different methods to learn French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très méticuleux dans son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very meticulous in his work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Être boulanger, c’est mon métier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being a baker is my job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le système métrique est utilisé dans beaucoup de pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The metric system is used in many countries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends le métro tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the subway every morning.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like « la météo » (the weather/the weather report).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle est la météo aujourd’hui ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s the weather like today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mêle le sucre et la farine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mixes the sugar and the flour.

definitions.note: Often used with "mêler à" (to mix into/with) or reflexively "se mêler de" (to get involved in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais mêler les ingrédients dans un grand bol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to mix the ingredients in a large bowl.

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form of « mêler » used with « vous ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mêlez la farine et les œufs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mix the flour and the eggs.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "mixed with" (e.g. "mêlé de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un sentiment mêlé de joie et de tristesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a feeling mixed with joy and sadness.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « mêler » (often used like an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sauce est bien mêlée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sauce is well mixed.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article: « le/la/les même(s) » = “the same (one/thing/people)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons la même idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same idea.

definitions.note: used to emphasize something surprising or unexpected
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a même oublié mon anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He even forgot my birthday.

definitions.note: Usually used with an article (e.g., « le même », « la même », « les mêmes »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux le même.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want the same one.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons les mêmes idées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same ideas.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons les mêmes idées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same ideas.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un môme sympa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a nice kid.

definitions.note: Informal/familiar (can sound a bit slangy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des mômes qui jouent dans le parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are kids playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette pêche est mûre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This peach is ripe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est mûr pour son âge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is mature for his age.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette banane est mûre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This banana is ripe.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces fraises sont mûres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These strawberries are ripe.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cueille des mûres dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m picking blackberries in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le fruit a mûri au soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fruit ripened in the sun.

definitions.note: Intransitive or transitive; figuratively, can mean to develop/come to fruition (e.g., an idea or plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les tomates vont mûrir au soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tomatoes are going to ripen in the sun.

definitions.note: Shortened form of « me » used before a word starting with a vowel sound (or silent h).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il m‘appelle tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls me every day.

definitions.note: Elided form of “ne” used before a vowel or mute h, in French negation (usually with “pas”, “plus”, “jamais”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’aime pas le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle nage tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She swims every morning.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, mes cousins nageaient dans la rivière tous les étés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, my cousins used to swim in the river every summer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: can mean “was swimming” or “used to swim,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, je nageais tous les étés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I used to swim every summer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for an ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier, il nageait dans la piscine pendant une heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, he was swimming in the pool for an hour.

definitions.note: Present tense ("they" form) of "nager".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En été, ils nagent dans la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, they swim in the sea.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of « nager » (used with « nous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nageons dans la piscine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We swim in the pool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime nager dans la piscine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to swim in the pool.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « nager » used with « tu » (you, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu nages très bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You swim very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le nageur s'entraîne tous les matins à la piscine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The swimmer trains every morning at the pool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les nageurs s'entraînent tous les matins à la piscine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The swimmers train every morning at the pool.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « nageur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma sœur est une nageuse très rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a very fast swimmer.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the formal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nagez jusqu’au bord, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swim to the edge, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing for completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils nagèrent jusqu’à l’autre rive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They swam to the other bank.

definitions.note: Past participle of « nager », used with « avoir » in compound tenses (e.g., « j’ai nagé » = “I swam / I have swum”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai nagé dans la mer hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swam in the sea yesterday.

definitions.note: A language (and the people) originally from central Mexico; usually capitalized in English and often in French (Nahuatl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le nahuatl est encore parlé au Mexique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nahuatl is still spoken in Mexico.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce conte, le nain aide la princesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this fairy tale, the dwarf helps the princess.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans l’histoire, les nains vivent dans la montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the dwarfs live in the mountain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La naissance de mon frère a eu lieu en juillet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother’s birth took place in July.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beaucoup de bébés naissent en été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many babies are born in summer.

definitions.note: Informal interjection used to refuse, disagree, or show lack of interest; common in casual speech.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tonight? — Nah, I'm tired.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can sound a bit casual or dismissive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une nana sympa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She's a nice girl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une nappe blanche pour la table.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) of « naître »; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il naquit à Paris en 1902.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was born in Paris in 1902.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like « pays natal » (home country) and « ville natale » (birthplace).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lyon est sa ville natale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lyon is his birthplace.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « langue natale » (native language) or « ville natale » (hometown).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le français est sa langue natale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: French is her native language.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La natation est mon sport préféré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swimming is my favorite sport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nation est très diverse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This nation is very diverse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une fête nationale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a national holiday.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une fête nationale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a national holiday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle est votre nationalité ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your nationality?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime la nature.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like nature.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “without makeup” or “with a natural look” when talking about someone’s appearance.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prefers natural-looking makeup.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This color is natural.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Naturellement, je peux t’aider demain.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « naturel »; used with feminine plural nouns.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le naufrage a eu lieu pendant la tempête.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « avoir la nausée » (“to feel nauseous”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had nausea since this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les navires arrivent au port ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ships are arriving at the port tonight.

definitions.note: Often used to express regret or apology; more formal than "désolé" in some contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cleans the kitchen after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new car.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog sleeps in its doghouse.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company found a niche in the market.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can sound crude.

definitions.note: Informal/slang: used to say something is in very good condition or that everything is fine.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are nests in the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nie les faits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denies the facts.

definitions.note: Verb (infinitive). Often followed by a direct object or by "nier que" + clause.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « nier » for « vous ».

definitions.note: Usually insulting; can be a bit old-fashioned.

definitions.note: Borrowed from English; used mainly in sports reporting to mean “zero” (often with a score).

definitions.note: Used in technical contexts (e.g., programming) to mean “null / no value,” similar to English “nil.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this language, the variable is nil if it hasn’t been initialized.

definitions.note: Less common outside sports/tech; can be used stylistically to mean “nothing/none,” but sounds marked in everyday French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’incident, il ne restait plus que du silence et nil d’autre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the incident, nothing remained but silence and nothing else.

definitions.note: Very vulgar slang. Often used as an insult or in commands (e.g., “Nique ça !”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nique ça !

definitions.native: to screw (someone over), to mess up

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re going to mess everything up if you touch that.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar slang; can mean something is ruined/broken or that someone is in trouble.

definitions.note: Often used for a person’s ability/skill level, or the level/standard of something.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My level of French is improving.

definitions.note: Plural of « niveau ».

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma nièce habite à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My niece lives in Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a nié les faits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denied the facts.

definitions.note: Not a standard French form; likely a typo or nonstandard spelling of « je ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sorry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision noble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a noble decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le roi a invité un noble au château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king invited a nobleman to the castle.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are noble people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pluie noie les fleurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain drowns the flowers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le noir est ma couleur préférée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Black is my favorite color.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « nombreux ».

definitions.note: used before plural nouns

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took notes during class.

definitions.note: Often used in a neutral or formal way to mean “well-known/undeniable,” not necessarily negative like English “notorious.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down your number.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam is graded out of 20.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier soir, on a fait une nouba chez Léa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, we had a party at Léa’s place.

definitions.note: Informal, familiar word.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fais un pas en avant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime peindre des paysages.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (for example, prison sentences or fines).

definitions.note: Present tense (je).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is painted blue.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is painted blue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une pellicule pour mon appareil photo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a roll of film for my camera.

definitions.note: Often used for a very thin layer on a surface (for example on food or skin).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A thin layer of dust covers the table.

definitions.note: Often used for the main pack of riders in a bicycle race.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular of « pencher »; mostly used in writing (e.g., novels).

definitions.note: Used to indicate duration in time.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (from the verb « pendre »). Not to be confused with « pendant » meaning “during/for” or the noun “pendant”.

definitions.note: Often used for something hanging (or hanging up), e.g. a coat.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ton manteau est pendu derrière la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your coat is hung up behind the door.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « pendu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La robe est pendue dans le placard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress is hanging in the closet.

definitions.note: In everyday French, this usually refers to a pendulum wall or mantel clock (a “pendulum clock”), not just the pendulum itself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pendule du salon sonne à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pendulum clock in the living room chimes at noon.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in literature and formal writing; in everyday speech, French usually uses the passé composé instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pensa à son enfance pendant le voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thought about his childhood during the trip.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), third person plural (“they”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils pensaient que le magasin était fermé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the store was closed.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or states).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pensais souvent à toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often thought about you.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), often used for ongoing or habitual thoughts in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle pensait à ses vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was thinking about her vacation.

definitions.note: present participle / gerund form of « penser » (often means “while thinking”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En pensant à toi, je souris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thinking about you, I smile.

definitions.note: Often used as “penser à” (to think about) or “penser que” (to think that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pense que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils pensent que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Often followed by « à » (think about) or « que » (think that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais penser à toi ce soir, et je dois aussi penser à appeler ma mère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to think about you tonight, and I also have to remember to call my mother.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive: « penser + infinitif » = intend/plan to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pense partir demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to leave tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often with « que » to introduce an opinion or belief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pense que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think you’re right.

definitions.note: first-person singular ("I") in the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je penserai à toi demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will think about you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional present (used for polite requests, suggestions, or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je penserais que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would think that it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Conditional present (often used for a hypothetical idea, or to report information with uncertainty: “is said to think”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je penserait que c’est une bonne idée, mais je ne suis pas sûr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would think it’s a good idea, but I’m not sure.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu penseras à moi demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will think about me tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural future simple (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils penseront à toi demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will think about you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensez-vous que c’est une bonne idée ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you think it’s a good idea?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (you were thinking / you used to think).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous pensiez que le musée était fermé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You thought the museum was closed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were thinking about you last night.

definitions.note: First-person plural present ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous pensons que c’est une bonne idée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Past participle of « penser », often used with « avoir » to form the past tense (passé composé).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about you last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai une pensée pour toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a thought for you.

definitions.note: Plural form of "pensée".

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils perdent souvent leurs clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They often lose their keys.
