definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai tiré un pique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew a spade.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « une petite pique » (a little jab).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a lancé une petite pique à son collègue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a little dig at his coworker.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le moustique me pique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mosquito is biting me.

definitions.note: Often used for insect stings (mosquitoes, bees) or a sharp prick (needle, thorn).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les moustiques aiment piquer quand il fait chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mosquitoes like to bite/sting when it’s hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis piqué le doigt avec une aiguille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pricked my finger with a needle.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « piquer ». It can look like English “piqued” (as in “piqued my interest”), but in French it usually means physically “stung/pricked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s'est piquée avec une aiguille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pricked herself with a needle.

definitions.note: Often used for an insect bite or sting; also used for a needle prick (like a shot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une piqûre de moustique sur le bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a mosquito bite on my arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des piranhas dans cette rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are piranhas in this river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pirates attaquent le navire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pirates attack the ship.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pirates attaquent le navire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pirates attack the ship.

definitions.note: Comparative form of « mauvais » (“bad”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est pire que je ne le pensais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's worse than I thought.

definitions.note: Often used after "encore" to mean "even worse".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est pire qu'hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's worse than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pire est derrière nous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The worst is behind us.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns or when referring to more than one thing/person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses résultats sont pires cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His results are worse this year.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « au pis » (“if worst comes to worst”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au pis, on restera à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If worst comes to worst, we’ll stay at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va à la piscine après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the swimming pool after school.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a de la pisse dans l’allée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s piss in the alley.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal way to say “to pee.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien pisse dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog pees outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des pissenlits dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are dandelions in the garden.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal; often considered rude. More neutral: « uriner ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai trop bu, je dois pisser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drank too much; I have to pee.

definitions.note: Very informal/vulgar in French; used like English “to piss.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai pissé derrière l'arbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I peed behind the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On suit la piste dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow the trail in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion atterrit sur la piste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane lands on the runway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a trouvé une nouvelle piste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a new lead.

definitions.note: Plural of « piste ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a plusieurs pistes de ski ouvertes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several ski runs open today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a un pistolet dans le tiroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a pistol in the drawer.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone/something that looks sad or in a bad state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la pluie, le chat avait l'air piteux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the cat looked pitiful.

definitions.note: Used in the expression « pitié ! » to beg or plead (like “mercy!” or “please!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pitié ! Ne me laisse pas tout seul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mercy! Don’t leave me all alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu pitié de ce chien abandonné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took pity on that abandoned dog.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « pitié ! » to beg someone to stop or to ask for kindness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pitié, arrête de crier !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, stop yelling!

definitions.note: Often expresses contempt or strong criticism; can also mean 'pitiable' (deserving pity) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est pitoyable de mentir comme ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s pathetic to lie like that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce village est pittoresque, avec ses maisons en pierre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This village is picturesque, with its stone houses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons visité plusieurs villages pittoresques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited several picturesque villages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange une pizza ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm eating a pizza tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons commandé deux pizzas ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered two pizzas tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On mange dans une pizzeria ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating at a pizzeria tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il manque une pièce du puzzle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One piece of the puzzle is missing.

definitions.note: Often used for a room in a home (e.g., une pièce = a room).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet appartement a deux pièces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment has two rooms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'appartement a trois pièces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment has three rooms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n'ai pas de pièces pour le parking.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have any coins for the parking meter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a cassé le verre en plusieurs pièces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the glass into several pieces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La souris est tombée dans le piège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mouse fell into the trap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des pièges dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are traps in the forest.

definitions.note: Often used to criticize the quality or level of something (e.g., a “piètre résultat”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait un piètre discours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave a poor speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont piéger le renard près de la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to trap the fox near the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le renard est piégé dans le filet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fox is trapped in the net.

definitions.note: Often used with être: « être piégé » = to be trapped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis piégé dans l’ascenseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trapped in the elevator.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used for a woman or a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est piégée dans l’ascenseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is trapped in the elevator.

definitions.note: past participle used as an adjective (masculine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont piégés dans l’ascenseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are trapped in the elevator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le placard est plein de manteaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The closet is full of coats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une place libre ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a free spot here.

definitions.note: Used for a town/city square, often named (e.g., place de la Concorde).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se retrouve sur la place du village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet in the village square.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je place le livre sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « placement de produit » (product placement) or in finance for an investment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le placement de ce produit dans le film est très visible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The placement of this product in the movie is very noticeable.

definitions.note: Common in finance: « un placement » = money you put into an investment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce placement rapporte 3 % par an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This investment yields 3% per year.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something in a particular position or for arranging/placing something somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais placer les chaises près de la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to place the chairs near the window.

definitions.note: Plural of "place" meaning a seat or spot (often in a theater, restaurant, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a plus de places pour le concert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no more seats for the concert.

definitions.note: Formal singular or plural form of “placer” (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Placez le livre sur la table, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on the table, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vase est placé sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vase is placed on the table.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., a comment or joke that is well-timed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une remarque très bien placée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a very well-placed comment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les invités sont placés à table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guests are seated at the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les livres sont placés sur l’étagère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are placed on the shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le plafond est très haut dans cette pièce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ceiling is very high in this room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va à la plage cet après-midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the beach this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En été, les plages sont souvent bondées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the beaches are often crowded.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts: plaider une cause = to plead/argue a case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'avocat va plaider demain au tribunal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer is going to plead in court tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « plaider »; often used in legal contexts or with « avoir » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a plaidé sa cause devant le juge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pleaded his case before the judge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une plaie au bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a wound on his arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a nettoyé ses plaies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor cleaned his wounds.

definitions.note: From « plaindre » (without « se »), meaning to feel sorry for someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle plaignait son ami après l'accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt sorry for her friend after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se plaignent tout le temps du bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They complain all the time about the noise.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (used with “vous”, also for polite singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vous plaignez tout le temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You complain all the time.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), used mostly in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se plaignit du bruit toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complained about the noise all night.

definitions.native: to pity, to feel sorry for
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais plaindre mon voisin, car il traverse une période difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to pity my neighbor, because he is going through a difficult time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La plaine est très grande et plate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plain is very big and flat.

definitions.note: Form of « plaindre » used with a direct object (e.g., « Je plains quelqu’un » = “I feel sorry for someone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je plains ton ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel sorry for your friend.

definitions.note: Often used for a formal complaint (e.g., to a company or to the police).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déposé une plainte au commissariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filed a complaint at the police station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons reçu plusieurs plaintes des clients.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We received several complaints from customers.

definitions.note: Plural noun; often used in expressions like « des plaints » in legal/administrative contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les plaints ont été déposés au commissariat ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The complaints were filed at the police station this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’espère que ce cadeau te plaira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you’ll like this gift.

definitions.note: Conditional form of « plaire » (to please; to be liked). Often used in polite questions or suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Est-ce que ce film te plairait ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like this movie?

definitions.native: to please; to appeal to; to be liked (by)
definitions.note: Most commonly used as « plaire à + [person] » (the thing that pleases is the subject; the person pleased is an indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film peut plaire à tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie can appeal to everyone.

definitions.note: Used with “je” (e.g., « je plais ») to mean “I please” (I am liked).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je plais beaucoup à ses parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His parents like me a lot.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « plaire »; often used like “to like” (literally “to please”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film me plaisait beaucoup quand j’étais enfant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked that movie a lot when I was a child.

definitions.note: Often means “funny/amusing” (not “pleasant” in the everyday English sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une histoire plaisante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a funny story.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je plaisantais, ne le prends pas mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was joking; don’t take it the wrong way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il plaisantait avec ses amis pendant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was joking with his friends during dinner.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “(someone) is kidding.” It can look like English “pleasant,” but it doesn’t mean that.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il plaisante, ne t’inquiète pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s joking, don’t worry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aime plaisanter tout le temps en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to joke all the time in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était une plaisanterie !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a joke!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses plaisanteries font rire tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His jokes make everyone laugh.

definitions.note: Often used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu plaisantes !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're kidding!

definitions.native: are you joking, are you kidding
definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous plaisantez ? Ce n’est pas possible !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you kidding? That’s not possible!

definitions.note: Used mostly in fixed, formal expressions like « s’il vous plaise »; it’s from the verb « plaire » (to please).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: S’il vous plaise, parlez plus lentement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Used mainly in expressions like « s’il vous plaît » (“please”) and « plaire à » (“to be liked by / to please”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chansons me plaisent beaucoup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these songs a lot.

definitions.note: Formal or plural form (vous) of « plaire ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous plaisez beaucoup à mes parents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents like you a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un plaisir de vous rencontrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les petits plaisirs de la vie comptent beaucoup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The small pleasures of life matter a lot.

definitions.note: Noun, masculine: « un plait » is a fold/pleat in cloth (often spelled « pli » in modern French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sur la jupe, on voit un plait bien marqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the skirt, you can see a clearly defined pleat.

definitions.note: Verb form from « plaire » is « plaît » (with circumflex), but « plait » (without accent) can appear as a form of « plaire » in older texts or without proper accents; it can also be from « plaire »/« plaire à » depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce qui lui plait, c’est la simplicité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What pleases him is simplicity.

definitions.note: Most often used for a plan (what you intend to do); for a map/floor plan, French often uses the same word in context (e.g., un plan de la ville).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a un plan pour ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a plan for this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pose une planche en bois sur le sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts a wooden board on the floor.

definitions.note: Usually means the (wooden) floor inside a building.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le plancher de la chambre est en bois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bedroom floor is made of wood.

definitions.note: Plural form of « planche ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a empilé des planches dans le garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stacked boards in the garage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion plane au-dessus de la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane glides over the city.

definitions.native: to glide, to soar, to hover
definitions.note: Often used for birds, aircraft, or something moving smoothly through the air.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’aigle peut planer au-dessus de la vallée pendant des minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The eagle can glide above the valley for minutes.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après avoir fumé, il dit qu’il peut planer pendant des heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After smoking, he says he can be high for hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je planifie mes vacances pour juillet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning my vacation for July.

definitions.note: Past participle of « planifier »; often used with « avoir » to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons planifié le voyage pour juillet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We planned the trip for July.

definitions.note: Common in French, especially in work contexts, to mean a schedule/timetable (often weekly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je consulte le planning de la semaine avant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I check the week’s schedule before the meeting.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a trouvé une planque pour se cacher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He found a hiding place to hide.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can mean to hide someone/something or to stash/put away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je planque les cadeaux dans le placard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hide the gifts in the closet.

definitions.note: Informal (colloquial). Often used with a direct object (e.g., planquer quelque chose).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a planqué les clés sous le tapis pour bien les planquer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hid the keys under the rug to hide them well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des plans pour ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have plans for this weekend.

definitions.note: Often used for a drawing or diagram (for example, a building plan or a city map).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les plans du musée sont à l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum maps are at the entrance.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), mainly used in writing (stories, novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il planta un arbre dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He planted a tree in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai une plante verte dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a green plant in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je plante des tomates dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plant tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais planter des tomates dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to plant tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des plantes dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are plants in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a planté un arbre dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He planted a tree in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used with "être" (e.g., "je suis planté") to mean you’re stuck or left somewhere (like when a car breaks down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis planté à la gare sans batterie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m stuck at the station with no battery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le jardin est bien planté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden is well planted.

definitions.note: Often used informally with être: être planté = to be stuck/stranded (e.g., in traffic or after being left somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis planté dans les embouteillages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m stuck in traffic.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used to agree with a feminine noun). Often used to mean something is stuck and can’t move.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture est plantée dans la boue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is stuck in the mud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les arbres sont plantés dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trees are planted in the garden.

definitions.note: Informal when used about people (e.g., being left waiting or unable to move on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On est plantés à la gare sans train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re stuck at the station without a train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La Terre est une planète.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Earth is a planet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les planètes tournent autour du Soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The planets orbit around the Sun.

definitions.note: Often used for a sign or nameplate (e.g., on a wall or door), or for a vehicle license plate depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a accroché une plaque sur la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hung a plaque on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette bouteille est en plastique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bottle is made of plastic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La table est plate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is flat.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a prepared dish/meal (not the physical plate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce plat est délicieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dish is delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prenait le bus tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was taking the bus every morning.

definitions.note: Present participle of « prendre ». It can also be used like an adjective meaning “engaging/compelling” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En prenant le métro, tu arriveras plus vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By taking the subway, you'll arrive faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prend le bus tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus every morning.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of « prendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prendra le train demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will take the train tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prendrai le train demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take the train tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Conditional present form (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prendrais un café, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would take a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional present (3rd person singular) of « prendre »; used for hypothetical situations, reported speech, or polite/hedged statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prendrait un café, s’il y en avait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would have a coffee if there were any.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense of « prendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu prendras le train à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will take the train at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais prendre le train demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take the train tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous prendrez le train à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will take the train at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) future tense of « prendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous prendrons le train demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take the train tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils prendront le train demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will take the train tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu prends le bus chaque matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You take the bus every morning.

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form used with “vous” (you plural or polite singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenez votre temps, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take your time, please.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) imperfect subjunctive of « prendre »; often used in « il fallait que vous… »-type sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous preniez le train plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to take the train earlier.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (je/il/elle/on). Often used after expressions like « il faut que… ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je prenne ce médicament.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take this medicine.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « prendre » used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils prennent le bus tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take the bus every morning.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form (tu) of "prendre"; used after expressions of necessity, doubt, emotion, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu prennes ton manteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to take your coat.

definitions.note: First-person plural present of « prendre »; often used to make a suggestion (like “let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenons le métro !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take the subway!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin prescrit un antibiotique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribes an antibiotic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un traitement prescrit par le médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a treatment prescribed by the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis presque prêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m almost ready.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; common in books and narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pressa le bouton rouge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pressed the red button.

definitions.note: Usually refers to newspapers/journalists and the news media (not a physical printing press).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La presse parle beaucoup de cette affaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The press is talking a lot about this case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presse le citron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He squeezes the lemon.

definitions.note: Often means an intuition that something (often bad) is going to happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un pressentiment que quelque chose ne va pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a feeling that something isn’t right.

definitions.note: Often used as « se presser » (= to hurry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On doit presser le pas si on veut arriver à l’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to hurry if we want to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Often used for squeezing (e.g., fruit) or pressing something with your hands or a tool.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais presser une orange pour faire du jus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to squeeze an orange to make juice.

definitions.note: (vous) form: used with “you” (plural or formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pressez le citron dans un bol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Squeeze the lemon into a bowl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de pression au travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of pressure at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai pressé le citron pour faire du jus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I squeezed the lemon to make juice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très pressé ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in a big hurry this morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis pressée, je dois partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in a hurry; I have to leave now.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont pressés parce qu'ils ont un rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re in a hurry because they have an appointment.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., a service provided by a company or professional).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise propose une prestation de nettoyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company offers a cleaning service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a aucune preuve contre lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no evidence against him.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a pas de preuves contre lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no evidence against him.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « prier »; in some contexts it can also mean “asked/begged.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pria en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prayed in silence.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je): describes an ongoing/habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je priais tous les soirs avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to pray every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chaque soir, il priait avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each evening, he was praying before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prie tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pray every evening.

definitions.note: Often used in polite or formal requests ("Je vous prie de...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te prie de m’écouter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m begging you to listen to me.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils prient pour leur famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They pray for their family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais prier pour toi ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to pray for you tonight.

definitions.note: Often used in polite requests, especially in the form « je vous prie de… ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vous prie de prier de patienter un instant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask you to wait a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prierai pour toi ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will pray for you tonight.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present subjunctive or imperative of « prier » (used for “you” plural/formal, and also as a polite request like “please”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: S'il vous plaît, priez pour nous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, pray for us.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the expression « le primaire » to refer to the primary school level.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon fils est en primaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son is in primary school.

definitions.note: Often used in politics: « une primaire » (e.g., to choose a party’s candidate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le parti organise une primaire en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party is holding a primary election in June.

definitions.note: Often refers to an extra payment added to a salary (e.g., a year-end bonus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a reçu une prime de fin d'année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He received a year-end bonus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette tribu utilise des outils primitifs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tribe uses primitive tools.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prince vit dans un grand château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prince lives in a big castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La princesse vit dans un grand château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The princess lives in a big castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre objectif principal est d'apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our main goal is to learn French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le principal parle aux élèves dans la cour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal talks to the students in the courtyard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le principal, c’est de rester calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main thing is to stay calm.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La raison principale, c’est le manque de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main reason is the lack of time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange principalement des légumes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mainly eat vegetables.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les raisons principales sont simples.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main reasons are simple.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les principaux problèmes sont déjà identifiés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main problems have already been identified.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une question de principe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a matter of principle.

definitions.note: Plural form of "principe".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses principes sont très importants pour lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His principles are very important to him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au printemps, il fait souvent beau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the weather is often nice.

definitions.note: First-person plural present ("nous") form, often used to suggest or invite an action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prions pour la paix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s pray for peace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sécurité est notre priorité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Safety is our priority.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons définir nos priorités avant de commencer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to define our priorities before starting.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person plural of « prendre »; common in literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils prirent le train pour Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the train to Paris.

definitions.note: Past participle of « prendre »; often used with « avoir » to form the past tense (passé composé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai pris le train ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the train this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Désolé, ce siège est déjà pris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, this seat is already taken.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « prendre » (used with an auxiliary like « être » or « avoir », depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La photo est déjà prise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo is already taken.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective “pris”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Désolé, cette place est déjà prise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, this seat is already taken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a une bonne prise sur la corde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good grip on the rope.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « prise de courant ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a pas de prise près du lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn’t an outlet near the bed.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (past participle) of « prendre », used with feminine plural subjects or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont prises au piège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are trapped (lit. they are taken in the trap).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été envoyé en prison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sent to prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prisonnier a été libéré après dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was released after ten years.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prisonniers rentrent chez eux après la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoners go home after the war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux prisons dans cette région.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two prisons in this region.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), mostly used in writing (stories, formal narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prit son manteau et sortit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took his coat and went out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te prive de dessert ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m depriving you of dessert tonight.

definitions.note: Usually used with "de" + thing taken away: "priver quelqu’un de quelque chose".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On ne peut pas priver un enfant de sommeil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t deprive a child of sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un privilège de travailler avec vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a privilege to work with you.

definitions.note: Past participle of « priver », often used with « être »: « être privé de … » = “to be deprived of …”. Not the same as English “private” (that’s « privé » as an adjective meaning “private”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été privé de ses droits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was deprived of his rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une conversation privée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a private conversation.

definitions.note: Often used for places or events that are not open to the general public.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une soirée privée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a private (exclusive) party.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « privé ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une salle privée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a private room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel est le prix de ce livre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the price of this book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a gagné un prix pour son film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She won an award for her film.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle fait une prière avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She says a prayer before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont dit leurs prières avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They said their prayers before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a prié pour sa famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prayed for his family.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or polite requests (e.g., « je vous ai prié de… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai prié de rester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked him to stay.

definitions.note: Often used in polite notices or formal instructions (e.g. « Vous êtes priés de… » = “You are kindly asked to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les passagers sont priés de garder leurs billets à portée de main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Passengers are kindly asked to keep their tickets within reach.

definitions.note: Often used informally, sometimes with a hyphen (e.g., pro-européen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis pro-vélo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in favor of bikes.

definitions.note: Informal: used to describe someone who is a professional or very skilled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est pro, pas amateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a professional, not an amateur.

definitions.note: Informal abbreviation used in expressions like « un pro de … »; also used to mean being in favor of something (e.g., « les pros et les antis »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un pro de l’informatique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a computer pro.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une forte probabilité de pluie demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a high probability of rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les probabilités de pluie sont élevées aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The probability of rain is high today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est probable qu’il pleuve demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is likely that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va probablement pleuvoir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will probably rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un problème avec mon ordinateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a problem with my computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons plusieurs problèmes à résoudre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have several problems to solve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une procession traverse le village pendant la fête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A procession goes through the village during the festival.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce processus prend beaucoup de temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This process takes a lot of time.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun: «la semaine prochaine» = “next week.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pars lundi prochain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm leaving next Monday.

definitions.note: Usually used with an article (e.g., « le prochain »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends celui-ci, et tu prends le prochain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take this one, and you take the next one.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « aimer son prochain » (“love your neighbor”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut aider son prochain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should help your neighbor / your fellow human being.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "prochain".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La semaine prochaine, je commence un nouveau travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week, I’m starting a new job.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used as a noun after a feminine noun is implied (e.g., « la prochaine » = “the next one”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prochaine, c’est Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next one is Marie.

definitions.note: Often used in announcements about something that will happen or be available in the near future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film sortira prochainement au cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will be released in theaters soon.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "prochain"; used with feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes prochaines vacances sont en juin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My next vacation is in June.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prochains jours seront très chargés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next few days will be very busy.

definitions.note: Often used with de to mean “close to / near (to)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon école est proche de chez moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My school is close to my home.

definitions.note: As a noun, it means a person close to you (often a family member or close friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un proche m'a appelé hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A relative (a loved one) called me last night.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes amis habitent proches d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends live close to here.

definitions.note: Refers to people close to you (family members, close friends).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais passer les fêtes avec mes proches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to spend the holidays with my loved ones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai tendance à procrastiner quand je suis stressé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tend to procrastinate when I'm stressed.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (me/te/lui/nous/vous/leur) to mean “gives/provides (someone) with.” Slightly formal compared to “donne.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce médicament me procure du soulagement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine gives me relief.

definitions.note: Often used for getting something (sometimes with the idea of getting it for someone else).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois procurer un document avant demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get a document before tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., procurer quelque chose à quelqu’un = to provide someone with something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette association peut procurer un logement aux familles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This organization can provide housing to families.

definitions.note: In France this is a public prosecutor (a magistrate) who represents the state in court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le procureur demande une peine plus sévère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prosecutor is asking for a harsher sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a procuré un billet pour le concert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got a ticket for the concert.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of « procéder ». Often used with « à »: « procéder à » = to proceed with / carry out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il procède à la vérification des documents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He proceeds with the verification of the documents.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a court trial (legal proceeding).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le procès commence demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trial starts tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, especially in expressions like « procéder à » + noun (e.g., to carry out an action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons procéder à une vérification.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to carry out a check.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons suivre la procédure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to follow the procedure.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., court cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une procédure est en cours contre l’entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Legal proceedings are underway against the company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce jeune musicien est un prodige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This young musician is a prodigy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le producteur du film cherche un nouveau réalisateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The film’s producer is looking for a new director.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis plus productif le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am more productive in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used for making goods, but also for artistic works like a film or a play.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La production a augmenté cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Production has increased this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est très productive au travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very productive at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette usine produira plus d’énergie l’an prochain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This factory will produce more energy next year.

definitions.note: Conditional present (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec plus de temps, elle produirait de meilleurs résultats.
