definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que ce traitement prévienne les infections.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This treatment has to prevent infections.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “let me/you/them know” (give a heads-up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Préviens-moi si tu es en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me know if you’re late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selon les prévisions météo, il va pleuvoir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the weather forecast, it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils prévoient une réunion demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are planning a meeting tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: to foresee; to anticipate; to expect
definitions.note: Used for predicting or expecting something in the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois prévoir une hausse des prix cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to anticipate a rise in prices this year.

definitions.native: to plan; to schedule; to arrange
definitions.note: Used for planning ahead or making arrangements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais prévoir un rendez-vous pour demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to schedule an appointment for tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: to provide for; to allow for; to budget for
definitions.note: Often used when making preparations for needs, costs, or contingencies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut prévoir un budget pour les imprévus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to budget for unexpected expenses.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « prévoir » (used with « je » or « tu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prévois une réunion demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning a meeting tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle prévoit de partir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She plans to leave tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « prévoir » used with « vous » (you plural/formal) or as an imperative (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous prévoyez un voyage cet été ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you planning a trip this summer?

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") present tense; often used to mean "let’s" when suggesting a plan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prévoyons une solution simple avant demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s plan a simple solution before tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « prévoir »; often used in phrases like « c’était prévu » (it was planned) or « comme prévu » (as expected).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était prévu depuis longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It had been planned for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce retard était prévu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This delay was planned.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « prévoir »; often used with « être » to mean something is planned/scheduled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunion est prévue demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is scheduled for tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" + infinitive (e.g., "prêt à partir" = ready to leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis prêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai contracté un prêt pour acheter une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took out a loan to buy a car.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « prêt ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis prête à partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ready to leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te prête mon stylo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m lending you my pen.

definitions.note: Used with an object: prêter quelque chose à quelqu’un (to lend something to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux te prêter mon stylo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can lend you my pen.

definitions.note: Conditional present ("je"): used for polite requests, hypothetical situations, or advice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te prêterais ma voiture, mais je n’ai plus d’essence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would lend you my car, but I don’t have any gas anymore.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont prêtes à partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are ready to leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous prêtes votre livre à Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You lend your book to Marie.

definitions.note: "vous" form (plural or formal); can also be used as a command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prêtez-moi votre stylo, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lend me your pen, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prêtre parle aux fidèles dans l’église.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest speaks to the faithful in the church.

definitions.note: Plural of « prêtre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prêtres parlent avec les familles après la messe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priests talk with the families after Mass.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont prêts à partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are ready to leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je lui ai prêté mon stylo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lent him my pen.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past) form of « prendre »; corresponds to “we took” and is mainly used in writing (stories, novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous prîmes le train à six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the train at six o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il écrit sous un pseudonyme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He writes under a pseudonym.

definitions.note: Informal shortening of « psychologue »; can refer broadly to a mental health professional.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais voir mon psy demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to see my therapist tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle suit une psychanalyse depuis plusieurs mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been doing psychoanalysis for several months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le psychiatre m’a posé beaucoup de questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The psychiatrist asked me a lot of questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle étudie la psychologie à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is studying psychology at university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est très psychologique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is very psychological.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vois une psychologue une fois par semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a psychologist once a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On dit que le tueur est un psychopathe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say the killer is a psychopath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin pense qu'il traverse un épisode psychotique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor thinks he is going through a psychotic episode.

definitions.note: Past participle of « pouvoir », used with « avoir » to express having been able to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai pu finir mes devoirs à temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was able to finish my homework on time.

definitions.note: Past participle of « pouvoir », typically used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai pu… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai pu finir mes devoirs hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was able to finish my homework last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier soir, la poubelle puait dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, the trash can stank in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used in a strong, negative sense (very unpleasant smell).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce couloir est puant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hallway stinks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle puanteur dans la cuisine !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a stench in the kitchen!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va au pub après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We're going to the pub after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un jardin public.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a public garden.

definitions.note: Refers to a group of people (e.g., spectators, readers, customers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le public applaudit à la fin du spectacle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauds at the end of the show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette publication est disponible en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This publication is available online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette publicité passe à la télévision tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This advertisement is on TV every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a trop de publicités sur ce site.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many ads on this website.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les jardins publics sont ouverts aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The public gardens are open today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va publier un article demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to publish an article tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une école publique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a public school.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les écoles publiques sont gratuites.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Public schools are free.

definitions.note: past participle of « publier »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'article a été publié ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The article was published this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La photo a été publiée hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo was published yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de pubs dans ce quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of pubs in this neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon chien a attrapé une puce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dog caught a flea.

definitions.note: Common in tech contexts (e.g., une puce électronique).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette carte contient une puce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This card contains a chip.

definitions.note: Describes a male who has not had sex; the feminine form is "pucelle".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dit qu’il est encore puceau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he’s still a virgin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon chien a des puces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dog has fleas.

definitions.note: Used mainly in cooking; commonly refers to a dessert (often a sweet cream) in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour le dessert, je prends un pudding au chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dessert, I’m having a chocolate pudding.

definitions.note: Often refers to a sense of decency or reserve about the body, intimacy, or personal matters.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle parle de ce sujet avec pudeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She talks about that subject with modesty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce fromage pue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese stinks.

definitions.note: Often used informally to talk about a strong, unpleasant smell.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tes chaussures puent !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your shoes stink!

definitions.note: Often used as an insult when addressed to someone directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu pues la sueur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stink of sweat.

definitions.note: Less common than « peux » in everyday speech; « je puis » is more formal or literary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je puis vous aider maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can help you now.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary form of « je peux » (from « pouvoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je puis vous aider si vous voulez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can help you if you want.

definitions.note: Often used to list actions in order (e.g., “d’abord…, puis…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une douche, puis je m’habille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a shower, then I get dressed.

definitions.note: Used to link two actions in sequence (often like “and then”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je finis, puis je pars.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finish, and then I leave.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a cause that is already known or considered obvious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puisque tu es là, aide-moi, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since you're here, help me, please.

definitions.note: Can mean physical power/strength, electrical power, or a country's power/influence, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La puissance du moteur est impressionnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The engine’s power is impressive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un moteur puissant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a powerful engine.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une voiture puissante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a powerful car.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des femmes puissantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are powerful women.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces moteurs sont très puissants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These engines are very powerful.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « pouvoir », used after expressions like « il faut que… », « pour que… », « bien que… ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je puisse partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to be able to leave now.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of « pouvoir », often used after expressions like « il faut que » (it’s necessary that) or « bien que » (although).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je puisse finir ce travail aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to be able to finish this work today.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, often used after expressions like « il faut que » or « pour que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’ils puissent venir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have to be able to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form (used after expressions like « il faut que… », « pour que… », « avant que… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu puisses venir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to be able to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form used with "vous".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux que vous puissiez venir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to be able to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after « il faut que », « pour que », « bien que »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que nous puissions partir tôt demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to be able to leave early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually means a water well.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un vieux puits dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an old well in the garden.

definitions.note: Commonly used in everyday French for a sweater; short for « pull-over ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis un pull parce qu’il fait froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on a sweater because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Past participle of « punir »; often used with « être » (e.g., « il est puni »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est puni parce qu’il a menti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is punished because he lied.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « punir »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été punie pour avoir menti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was punished for lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur va punir les élèves qui trichent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is going to punish the students who cheat.

definitions.note: Present tense form (also used for the imperative with “tu”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tu triches, je te punis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you cheat, I punish you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tu arrives en retard, tu auras une punition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you arrive late, you will get a punishment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est de l’eau pure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s pure water.

definitions.note: This form is not recognized as a standard/common French noun; it may be a misspelling or a very regional/obsolete term.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne comprends pas le mot « purains » dans cette phrase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the word “purains” in this sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’eau est pure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is pure.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts to mean "only" for one reason (e.g., purely theoretical, purely for information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je le fais purement par curiosité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m doing it purely out of curiosity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pureté de l’eau est très importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The purity of the water is very important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le système a été purgé de toutes les erreurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The system was purged of all errors.

definitions.note: Often refers specifically to mashed potatoes in everyday French ("purée de pommes de terre").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux de la purée avec le poulet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want mashed potatoes with the chicken.

definitions.note: Can also mean a smooth mash/puree made from other foods (e.g., vegetables or fruit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette purée de carottes est très bonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This carrot puree is very good.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « pouvoir », used with an infinitive to express ability/possibility in the past (often as background or habitual).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand tu étais enfant, tu pus rester dehors plus longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a child, you could stay outside longer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne put pas venir hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: Very vulgar slang; used as an intensifier (often in “putain de + noun”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce putain de bus est encore en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That fucking bus is late again.

definitions.note: Vulgar swear word; very common in informal speech and can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Putain, j’ai oublié mes clés !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I forgot my keys!

definitions.note: Very vulgar/derogatory term; use with caution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a insulté cette femme en la traitant de putain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insulted that woman by calling her a prostitute.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; used as a strong exclamation (anger, frustration, surprise).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I missed the bus again!

definitions.note: Also commonly used as a vulgar insult/exclamation; literal meaning is “prostitute.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les putains attendent près du bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prostitutes are waiting near the bar.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive; commonly used as an insult. Avoid using it.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was punished for insulting someone by saying “whore.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fini le puzzle hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finished the puzzle last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je trouve cette dispute puérile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find this argument childish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mets mon pyjama avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my pajamas before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Plural form; in French, you can also say « un pyjama » for one set.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes pyjamas sont dans l’armoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My pajamas are in the closet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons visité une pyramide en Égypte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited a pyramid in Egypt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a visité les pyramides en Égypte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the pyramids in Egypt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la maladie, il était très pâle.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he hears the news, he turns pale.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m making pizza dough.

definitions.note: Plural form; usually refers to pasta as a food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce soir, on mange des pâtes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight, we're eating pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the pastry shop to buy an éclair.

definitions.note: Informal/vulgar.

definitions.note: A serious and highly sensitive term; used to describe an adult sexually attracted to children.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté un pédophile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a pedophile.

definitions.native: fag (offensive slur for a gay man)
definitions.note: Very offensive French slur; avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a dit : « Il est pédé. »
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said, “He’s a fag.”

definitions.note: Very offensive, derogatory slang (a homophobic insult). Avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne dis pas « pédé » : c’est une insulte homophobe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say “pédé”: it’s a homophobic insult.

definitions.note: Very offensive and derogatory slang; a homophobic insult. Avoid using.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sont fait traiter de pédés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were called fags (a slur).

definitions.note: Very offensive French slur targeting gay men; avoid using it except when discussing or quoting it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce mot est une insulte : « pédés » ; ne l’emploie pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That word is an insult: “faggots”; don’t use it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pélicans volent au-dessus de la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pelicans are flying above the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail est pénible, mais important.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This work is difficult, but important.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or situation that gets on your nerves.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête, tu es pénible !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop it, you’re annoying!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a gravi la colline péniblement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed the hill with difficulty.

definitions.note: Anatomical term; may be considered rude or too direct in casual conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin examine le pénis du patient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines the patient’s penis.

definitions.note: A person who feels sorry for their sins or wrongdoings, often in a religious context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pénitent demande pardon au prêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The penitent asks the priest for forgiveness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une pénurie de médecins dans cette région.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a shortage of doctors in this region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pénètre dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enters the house.

definitions.note: Can also be used in a figurative sense (e.g., an idea, a smell, light).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lumière pénètre par la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light penetrates through the window.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple); mostly used in written storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pénétra dans la pièce sans faire de bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entered the room without making a sound.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; can also be used figuratively (e.g., to enter a place or a situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a pénétré dans la salle en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entered the room silently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les policiers ont pénétré dans le bâtiment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police entered the building.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the seeds inside fruit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a recraché les pépins de la pomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spat out the apple seeds.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a eu des pépins avec la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had trouble with the car.

definitions.note: Informal; often used by children or within the family.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon pépé habite près de la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa lives near the sea.

definitions.note: This is usually a misspelling of « père » (with a grave accent: è).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon pére travaille beaucoup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad works a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle of « périr »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « a péri »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau a péri pendant la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat perished during the storm.

definitions.note: Slightly formal; often used in expressions like « au péril de sa vie » (“at the risk of his/her life”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les randonneurs étaient en péril à cause de la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hikers were in danger because of the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont affronté de grands périls en mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They faced great dangers at sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Calcule le périmètre de ce rectangle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calculate the perimeter of this rectangle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je traverse une période difficile en ce moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going through a difficult period right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pétales de cette fleur sont très délicats.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The petals of this flower are very delicate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On entend des pétards dans la rue ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can hear firecrackers in the street tonight.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive insult; avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a traité sa collègue de pétasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called his colleague a bitch.

definitions.note: Informal / slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais péter si je mange encore des haricots.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to fart if I eat more beans.

definitions.note: Informal; used for things breaking suddenly (e.g., a tire) or for an explosion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pneu risque de péter sur l’autoroute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire might burst on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai signé une pétition pour protéger ce parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I signed a petition to protect this park.

definitions.note: In the common expression « être dans le pétrin » = to be in trouble / in a mess.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis dans le pétrin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in trouble.

definitions.note: Usually refers to crude oil/petroleum (not cooking oil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix du pétrole augmente cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price of oil is going up this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pétrolier est entré dans le port ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oil tanker entered the port this morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une compagnie pétrolière très puissante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a very powerful oil company.

definitions.note: Slang/vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai pété dans l’ascenseur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I farted in the elevator.

definitions.note: Informal slang (e.g., for a device/object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon téléphone est pété.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange une pêche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm eating a peach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pêche est interdite ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fishing is forbidden here.

definitions.note: Verb form of « pêcher » (not to be confused with « pêche » meaning “peach” as a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pêche dans la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fishes in the river.

definitions.note: Not to be confused with “pécher” (with an accent), which means “to sin.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons pêcher dans la rivière ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to fish in the river this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté des pêches au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought peaches at the market.

definitions.note: In French, "pêche" can also mean "peach" (the fruit), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pêches sont interdites ici en hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fishing is forbidden here in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pêcheur part en mer avant l’aube.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman goes out to sea before dawn.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pêcheurs partent en mer très tôt le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fishermen head out to sea very early in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai pêché toute la matinée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fished all morning.

definitions.note: Abbreviation for « quartier général » (military/police/organizational headquarters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le général retourne au qg ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The general is going back to HQ tonight.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like Chinese medicine, tai-chi, or acupuncture.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En médecine traditionnelle chinoise, on cherche à faire circuler le qi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In traditional Chinese medicine, people try to get the qi flowing.

definitions.note: Meaning depends on context: at a station it’s a train/metro platform; along a river/port it’s a quay/wharf.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le train part du quai 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves from platform 3.

definitions.note: Often used to mean having the required skills or credentials.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est qualifiée pour ce poste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is qualified for this position.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La qualité de ce produit est excellente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The quality of this product is excellent.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses meilleures qualités sont la patience et la gentillesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His best qualities are patience and kindness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand arrives-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you arriving?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je téléphone à ma mère quand j'ai le temps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call my mother when I have time.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed expression « quant à ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quant à moi, je préfère rester ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As for me, I prefer to stay here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle quantité de sucre veux-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much sugar do you want?

definitions.note: Often used with “en” (e.g., “en quarantaine” = “in quarantine”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est en quarantaine depuis lundi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been in quarantine since Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quarante ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am forty years old.

definitions.note: Often used to mean one fourth (1/4), especially in set phrases like « un quart d’heure » (15 minutes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai attendu un quart d’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited fifteen minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’habite dans un quartier calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a quiet neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de restaurants dans ces quartiers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many restaurants in these neighborhoods.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quasi fini mes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve almost finished my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai quasiment fini mes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve almost finished my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quatorze ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fourteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quatre frères.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have four brothers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est la quatrième fois que je viens ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the fourth time I’ve come here.

definitions.note: Often used as an ordinal number (e.g., “le/la quatrième” = “the fourth [one/person]”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est arrivée quatrième.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came in fourth.

definitions.note: Often spelled « quatrième » (with è).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est ma quatriéme année en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my fourth year in France.

definitions.note: Used in exclamations (often with an adjective), meaning “how …!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que c’est beau !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How beautiful it is!

definitions.note: Often used with “ne … que” to mean “only.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai que dix euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have ten euros.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamative determiner, often in the pattern « que de / que d’ + noun » to express a large quantity (more common in writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que de monde dans le métro !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So many people in the subway!

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to show surprise or emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que ! Tu pars déjà ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What! You’re leaving already?

definitions.note: Used as an interrogative pronoun, often at the beginning of a question.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que veux-tu manger ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you want to eat?

definitions.note: Used as a relative pronoun for things or ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le livre que je lis est intéressant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book that I am reading is interesting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pense que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that you are right.

definitions.note: used after a comparative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il travaille plus que je ne pensais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works more than I thought.

definitions.note: Can refer to the Quechua language or a Quechua person/people, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle apprend le quechua à l’université.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is learning Quechua at university.

definitions.note: used before a masculine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel livre veux-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which book do you want?

definitions.note: used in exclamations before a masculine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel beau jour !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a beautiful day!

definitions.note: Used in questions to ask for a choice or to identify something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel est ton préféré ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which one is your favorite?

definitions.note: Used to mean it doesn’t matter which one; often after the noun (e.g., "un livre quelconque").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous pouvez choisir un jour quelconque de la semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose any day of the week.

definitions.note: Often means something is unremarkable or mediocre; can sound slightly negative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un restaurant quelconque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an ordinary restaurant.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used after the noun in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous pouvez choisir des couleurs quelconques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose any colors.

definitions.note: used before a feminine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle heure est-il ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time is it?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « quel » (used before a feminine singular noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle couleur préfères-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which color do you prefer?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “quel”; used before a feminine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelles couleurs préfères-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which colors do you prefer?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelles sont tes couleurs préférées ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which are your favorite colors?

definitions.note: Used before a number or quantifier to mean “approximately” (e.g., quelque vingt minutes = about twenty minutes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est resté quelque vingt minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed about twenty minutes.

definitions.note: Used before a plural noun or a number (e.g., « quelque(s) jours », « quelque trois minutes »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté quelque livres pour le cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some books for the class.

definitions.note: Often implies a small number (commonly with « quelques »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reste quelque minutes avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a few minutes left before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « quelque chose » (“something”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quelque chose à te dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something to tell you.

definitions.note: Often written as two words: « quelque chose ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quelquechose à te dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something to tell you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais quelquefois au cinéma le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sometimes go to the movies on Sundays.

definitions.note: Used before a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai quelques questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a few questions.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "quel"; used before a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quels livres veux-tu lire ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which books do you want to read?

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "quel"; used in questions and exclamations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quels films veux-tu voir ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movies do you want to see tonight?

definitions.note: Often implies a dispute or squabble, sometimes ongoing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont eu une querelle au sujet de l’argent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had an argument about money.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal or literary; more common everyday verbs are "se disputer" or "se quereller".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils passent leur temps à quereller pour des détails.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They spend their time quarrelling over details.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une question pour toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a question for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rempli le questionnaire en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled out the online questionnaire.

definitions.note: Often implies questioning someone closely or in a challenging way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le policier va questionner le témoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer is going to question the witness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deux questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une longue queue devant la boulangerie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a long line in front of the bakery.

definitions.note: Often used for an animal’s tail.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien remue la queue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is wagging its tail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chiens remuent leurs queues quand ils sont contents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dogs wag their tails when they are happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a de longues queues devant le cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are long lines in front of the movie theater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qui est là ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who is there?

definitions.note: often introduces a relative clause
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La femme qui parle est ma professeure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman who is speaking is my teacher.

definitions.note: Used mostly in formal or written French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiconque veut participer doit s'inscrire avant vendredi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whoever wants to take part must register before Friday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à la quincaillerie pour acheter des vis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the hardware store to buy some screws.

definitions.note: Often used to mean an approximate period of 15 days (not necessarily exactly 15).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pars en voyage pour une quinzaine de jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going on a trip for about two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quinze ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fifteen years old.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), most common in writing (stories, literature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il quitta la ville au lever du soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the city at sunrise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je quitte la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils quittent la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving a place or stopping an activity/job; with a person, it can mean “to leave” (e.g., end a relationship).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois quitter la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Simple future (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle quittera Paris demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will leave Paris tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je quitterai la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je quitterais ce travail si je trouvais mieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would quit this job if I found something better.

definitions.note: Conditional form (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il quitterait son travail si on lui offrait un meilleur salaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would quit his job if they offered him a better salary.

definitions.note: Usually used with "être" in the expression "être quittes" meaning each person has paid what they owed, so nobody owes anything anymore.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maintenant que tu m’as remboursé, nous sommes quittes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Now that you’ve paid me back, we’re even.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu quittes la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used as a command or instruction ("Leave!" / "Please leave.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quittez la salle, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous quittons la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: In French, this often means “to leave” a place or “to stop” an activity; it doesn’t match English “quit” in all contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous quittons le travail plus tôt aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We leave work earlier today.

definitions.note: Past participle of « quitter »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai quitté… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quitté la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « quitter »; often used with « être » (e.g., « elle est quittée ») or when agreeing with a preceding direct object (e.g., « la maison qu’elle a quittée »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison qu’elle a quittée était très ancienne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house she left was very old.

definitions.note: past participle (plural masculine); used in compound tenses or the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été quittés par leur guide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were left by their guide.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to show surprise or disbelief (like “What?!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quoi ? Tu pars déjà ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What? You’re leaving already?

definitions.note: Used after prepositions and often at the end of informal questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De quoi as-tu besoin ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you need?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you back after work.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rapplique au bout de cinq minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shows up again after five minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai lu le rapport ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the report this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rapporte le livre à la bibliothèque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brings the book back to the library.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle rapporte un accident à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reports an accident to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux rapporter le livre à la bibliothèque demain ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring the book back to the library tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used with information, results, or facts (e.g., in news, police, or work contexts).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to report the incident to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rapportera les clés demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will bring back the keys tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle rapportera ce qu’elle a vu à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will report what she saw to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail rapportera plus d’argent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job will earn more money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai lu les rapports ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the reports this morning.

definitions.note: Often used for relationships between people, groups, or countries (e.g., "rapports avec" = "relations with").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les rapports entre les deux pays se sont améliorés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Relations between the two countries have improved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rapporté du pain à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought back some bread to the house.

definitions.note: Often used for telling what someone said or for reporting information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a rapporté les faits à la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reported the facts to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rapproche les deux chaises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moves the two chairs closer together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rapprochent les chaises pour faire de la place.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They move the chairs closer together to make room.

definitions.native: to bring closer; to move closer
definitions.note: Often used transitively (rapprocher quelque chose de...) or reflexively (se rapprocher de...) meaning “to come/get closer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu rapprocher la chaise de la table, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you move the chair closer to the table, please?

definitions.note: Can be used literally (physically closer) or figuratively (bring people/ideas closer together).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rapprochez les chaises, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bring the chairs closer, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté une nouvelle raquette de tennis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new tennis racket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En hiver, on peut marcher en raquettes dans la montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, you can walk with snowshoes in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On met des raquettes pour marcher dans la neige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put on snowshoes to walk in the snow.

definitions.note: Used for sports like tennis or badminton.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai oublié mes raquettes de tennis à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my tennis rackets at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une espèce rare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a rare species.

definitions.note: Used especially for meat (like "steak rare" in English).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer my steak rare (undercooked).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va rarement au cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rarely goes to the movies.

definitions.note: Plural form (feminine or masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces livres sont rares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are rare.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se coupe en rasant sa barbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cuts himself while shaving his beard.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « raser ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rase sa barbe tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaves his beard every morning.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively (se raser) when talking about shaving oneself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais raser ma barbe ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to shave my beard tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for buildings or places (e.g., a house, a neighborhood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont raser l'ancien immeuble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to demolish the old building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu te rases tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shave every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous rasez votre barbe chaque matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shave your beard every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’un rasoir pour me raser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a razor to shave.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), often used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rassembla les documents sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gathered the documents on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle rassemble ses affaires avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gathers her things before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used for a public gathering (meeting, rally, or crowd).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un rassemblement sur la place ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a gathering in the square tonight.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rassemblent les documents pour le dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gather the documents for the file.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va rassembler tous les documents sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to gather all the documents on the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a command to a group ("you" plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rassemblez vos affaires et suivez-moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gather your things and follow me.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), third-person plural (they); common in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rassemblèrent les documents sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gathered the documents on the table.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rassembler ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout le monde est rassemblé dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone is gathered in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont rassemblés devant l’entrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are gathered in front of the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa voix est rassurante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her voice is reassuring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette musique me rassure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This music reassures me.

definitions.note: Often used for calming someone down or making them feel less worried.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te rassurer : tout va bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to reassure you: everything is fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis rassuré après avoir reçu ses nouvelles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reassured after getting news from him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis rasé ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shaved this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est rasé de près.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is clean-shaven.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le travail, je suis rasé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I'm exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un rat dans la cave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a rat in the basement.

definitions.note: Infinitive form; commonly used with a direct object: rater un train / un examen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais rate le train si je ne pars pas maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to miss the train if I don’t leave now.

definitions.native: to miss (e.g., a bus, a train); to fail to catch
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais rater le bus si je ne pars pas tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to miss the bus if I don’t leave right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a raté son examen, mais il va le repasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He failed his exam, but he’s going to retake it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai raté ce gâteau parce que j’ai oublié le sucre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I messed up this cake because I forgot the sugar.

definitions.native: to miss (a target); to not hit
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tireur a raté la cible de peu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shooter missed the target by a little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision rationnelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a rational decision.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave a rational explanation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In wartime, there were rations of bread and sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des rats dans le sous-sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are rats in the basement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je rattrapai mon retard avant la fin de la semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught up on my delay before the end of the week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rattrape le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He catches the bus.

definitions.note: Often used for catching up after being behind (time, work, level) or for catching someone who is ahead or running away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois rattraper mon retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to catch up on my delay.

definitions.note: First-person singular simple future ("I will...") of rattraper.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te rattraperai bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will catch up with you soon.

definitions.note: Often used for catching up to someone/something, or catching something that’s falling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rattrapez-moi !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Catch up with me!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai rattrapé dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught up with him in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai raté le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai raté l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for an attempt, plan, or event that didn’t work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon examen est raté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My exam is a failure.

definitions.note: Informal; can be insulting when used to describe a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se croit raté, mais il a déjà beaucoup réussi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thinks he's a failure, but he has already achieved a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le concert, j’avais la voix rauque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, my voice was hoarse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le village a été ravagé par la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village was ravaged by the storm.

definitions.note: Often used with "être" (e.g., "je suis ravi(e)"). Feminine form: "ravie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis ravi de te voir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m delighted to see you.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « ravi »; used mainly with « être » (e.g., « je suis ravie »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis ravie de te voir !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m delighted to see you!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sentier descend dans un ravin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path goes down into a ravine.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange des raviolis ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating ravioli tonight.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes ravis de vous rencontrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re delighted to meet you.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est ravissante dans cette robe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is charming in that dress.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving a scratch mark on a surface (like a screen, glass, or a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais rayer l’écran de mon téléphone si je le mets avec mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to scratch my phone screen if I put it with my keys.

definitions.note: Used for crossing out words or items on a list.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A ray of sunshine is coming in through the window.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun was shining on the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les rayons du soleil entrent par la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun’s rays come in through the window.

definitions.note: Used for the part of a store where certain products are displayed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pâtes sont dans les rayons italiens, juste à côté des sauces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pasta is in the Italian aisles/sections, right next to the sauces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime ton pull à rayures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your striped sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai rayé ton nom de la liste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crossed your name off the list.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le rebelle refuse d’obéir aux ordres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rebel refuses to obey orders.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rebels are advancing toward the capital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La balle rebondit sur le sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball bounces on the ground.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They threw the waste in the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an easy recipe for making crêpes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai écrit mes recettes dans un cahier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote my recipes in a notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will receive an email tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to receive a message from my friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il recevra une réponse demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will receive an answer tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous recevrez un e-mail de confirmation demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will receive a confirmation email tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une pièce de rechange pour ma voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a replacement part for my car.

definitions.note: Often used for charging a phone or battery ("recharger").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il recharge son téléphone avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He recharges his phone before going out.

definitions.native: was looking for, was searching for

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais une recherche sur les animaux marins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m doing research on marine animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle recherche ses clés partout.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are looking for an apartment near downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to look for my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes recherches sur ce sujet commencent aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My research on this topic starts today.

definitions.note: Formal/informal plural (vous) command or present tense form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please look for your ticket.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rechercher » (used with an auxiliary like « avoir »).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police searched for the suspect all night.

definitions.native: to glue back on, to stick back together
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais recoller l’étiquette sur la bouteille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to stick the label back on the bottle.

definitions.note: Often used for catching up in progress or position (e.g., in a race or at school).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to work this weekend to catch up with the others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai suivi ta recommandation et j’ai appelé le médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed your recommendation and I called the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te recommande ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recommend this movie to you.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you recommend this restaurant?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant est recommandé par mes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is recommended by my friends.

definitions.note: Used for registered letters/parcels ("envoyer en recommandé").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai envoyé une lettre en recommandé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent a letter by registered mail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il recommence demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He starts again tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la pause, nous allons recommencer l'exercice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the break, we're going to start the exercise again.

definitions.native: will start again, will begin again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, elle recommencera son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, she will start her work again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tu te trompes, tu recommences.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you make a mistake, you start again.

definitions.note: Past participle of « recommencer » (used with an auxiliary like « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai recommencé le cours hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I restarted the course yesterday.

definitions.native: let's start again, let's begin again

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's start again tomorrow morning, when we’ll be less tired.

definitions.note: Often used for taking someone back (e.g., driving them home or walking them to the door).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to drive you back home.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « reconnaître » (used with tu/je depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je reconnais ta voix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognize your voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te remercie pour ta reconnaissance.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thank you for your gratitude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis reconnaissant pour ton aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis très reconnaissante pour ton aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes reconnaissants pour votre aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous reconnaissez cette chanson ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you recognize this song?

definitions.note: Can mean recognizing a person/thing or admitting/acknowledging something, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle reconnaît sa voix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She recognizes his voice.

definitions.note: to identify someone/something previously known; to acknowledge
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais reconnaître ton écriture tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will recognize your handwriting right away.

definitions.note: to accept as true or valid

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to acknowledge his mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pays va reconnaître le nouveau gouvernement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country is going to recognize the new government.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai reconnu tout de suite.
