definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est reconnue pour son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is recognized for her work.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « reconnaître ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces artistes sont reconnues dans le monde entier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These artists are recognized worldwide.

definitions.note: Often the masculine plural past participle of « reconnaître » (used with an auxiliary like « avoir » or « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été reconnus par la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were recognized by the police.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular of « reconnaître »; often used in formal/literary narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il le reconnut tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He recognized him right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais reconsidérer ma décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to reconsider my decision.

definitions.note: Often used for rebuilding something from pieces or evidence (e.g., an event, a document, a scene).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police essaie de reconstituer la scène de l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are trying to reconstruct the scene of the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reconstruction de la ville a pris plusieurs années après la guerre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reconstruction of the city took several years after the war.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of « reconstruire »; used with « être » or to agree with a feminine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison a été reconstruite après l’incendie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house was rebuilt after the fire.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a best performance or achievement (e.g., a world record).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a battu le record du monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the world record.

definitions.note: Often used with the preposition « à »: « recourir à » = to resort to, to turn to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En cas de problème, vous pouvez recourir à un spécialiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In case of a problem, you can resort to a specialist.

definitions.note: Often used in legal/administrative contexts (e.g., making an appeal or seeking a remedy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait un recours contre la décision du tribunal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He filed an appeal against the court’s decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sol est recouvert de neige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ground is covered with snow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « recouvrir » (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La table est recouverte d'une nappe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is covered with a tablecloth.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La neige recouvrait la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow was covering the road.

definitions.note: Means to cover (often completely) a surface (snow, paint, dust, etc.). Not the same as English “recover” (= get better).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La neige va recouvrir la route pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Snow is going to cover the road during the night.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'armée forme de nouvelles recrues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army trains new recruits.

definitions.note: Past participle of « recruter ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été recruté par une grande entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was recruited by a large company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin examine le rectum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines the rectum.

definitions.note: Often used for collecting things like information, testimony, donations, or harvests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons recueillir des informations avant de décider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to collect information before deciding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faites un pas de recul, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a step back, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture recule lentement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is backing up slowly.

definitions.note: Used for stepping or moving backward (literal); can also be used figuratively (e.g., to back down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux reculer un peu, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you back up a little, please?

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to address one person formally or more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reculez, s'il vous plaît !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move back, please!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le recyclage est important pour protéger l’environnement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Recycling is important to protect the environment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut recycler le papier et le plastique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to recycle paper and plastic.

definitions.native: goes back down, comes back down
definitions.note: Often used for going down again (stairs, a mountain, etc.) or returning to a lower level.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il redescend les escaliers en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes back down the stairs in silence.

definitions.native: go back down, come back down
definitions.note: Often used for descending again after having gone up (stairs, a mountain, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais redescendre les escaliers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go back down the stairs.

definitions.native: go back down, come back down
definitions.note: Often means going down again or returning downstairs/down a slope.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu redescends tout de suite !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You come back down right away!

definitions.note: Often used with "à" to say you owe someone money or gratitude (e.g., "redevable à quelqu’un").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis redevable à mon ami pour son aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am indebted to my friend for his help.

definitions.note: Often used for returning to a previous state or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après les vacances, je veux redevenir plus organisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vacation, I want to become more organized again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu redeviens sérieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re becoming serious again.

definitions.note: A classic, long, fitted coat (often associated with formal or historical style).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte une redingote noire pour la cérémonie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wearing a black frock coat for the ceremony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais redire la question plus lentement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to repeat the question more slowly.

definitions.note: Form of the verb « redire »; it can mean “I repeat” (je redis), “you repeat” (tu redis), or “repeat!” as a command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je redis que je ne suis pas d’accord.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repeat that I don’t agree.

definitions.note: Usually used with "vous" (you plural or formal you). Often an imperative meaning "repeat!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Redites après moi : « Bonjour ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Repeat after me: “Hello.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me redonne mon livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives me my book back.

definitions.note: Often used for someone or something that inspires fear or respect because it is very strong or dangerous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un adversaire redoutable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a formidable opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il redoute l'examen de demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fears tomorrow's exam.

definitions.note: Can refer to physically straightening something or correcting a mistake/problem, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il redresse la chaise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He straightens the chair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu redresser la chaise, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you straighten the chair, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut redresser cette erreur avant d’envoyer le document.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to correct this mistake before sending the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux redémarrer ton ordinateur ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you restart your computer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois refaire cet exercice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to redo this exercise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je refais le gâteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm making the cake again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il refait le lit tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remakes the bed every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a refait le lit avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remade the bed before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Refaites l'exercice, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Redo the exercise, please.

definitions.note: Conditional form of « refaire » (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si j’avais plus de temps, je le referais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, I would do it again.

definitions.note: From the verb « refermer »; « referme » is often used as an instruction (command) or as “closes” with he/she/it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Referme la porte, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Close the door again, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu refermer la porte, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you close the door again, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vois mon reflet dans le miroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see my reflection in the mirror.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette vitrine reflète la lumière du soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shop window reflects the sunlight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les miroirs reflètent la lumière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mirrors reflect the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pouvez-vous reformuler votre question, s’il vous plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you rephrase your question, please?

definitions.note: In songs or poems: the repeated line(s) or section.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le refrain de cette chanson reste dans la tête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chorus of this song sticks in your head.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le café a déjà refroidi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee has already cooled.

definitions.note: Often used for something becoming cooler in temperature (food, drink, weather).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laisse la soupe refroidir avant de la manger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the soup cool down before eating it.

definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can mean “I cool down/cool” (je), “you cool down/cool” (tu), or it can be the command “cool down/cool!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je refroidis la soupe avant de la servir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cool the soup before serving it.

definitions.note: Formal/plural command (vous) and also the present tense form for “you cool down” (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Refroidissez la soupe avant de la servir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cool the soup down before serving it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La soupe refroidit sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is cooling down on the table.

definitions.note: Often used for a place where someone is protected or safe (e.g., during danger or bad weather).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’orage, ils ont trouvé refuge dans une grange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, they found shelter in a barn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son refus de venir a surpris tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His refusal to come surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il refusa l’offre sans hésiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He refused the offer without hesitating.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person singular: “I refused.” Mostly used in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je refusai poliment son invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I politely refused his invitation.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il refusait de répondre aux questions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He refused to answer the questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je refuse cette proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I refuse this proposal.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) form of « refuser » in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils refusent de répondre à la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They refuse to answer the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais refuser cette offre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to refuse this offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu refuses de répondre à la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You refuse to answer the question.

definitions.note: Used with "vous" (formal or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous refusez ma proposition ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you refusing my offer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a refusé mon invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He refused my invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’accident, il a dû regagner la confiance de son équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he had to regain his team’s trust.

definitions.native: to go back, to return (to a place)
definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts than "retourner".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons regagner la maison avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to go back home before nightfall.

definitions.note: Usually used with an object: regagner quelque chose = regain/get something back (e.g., confidence, strength).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Regagnez confiance en vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regain confidence in yourself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son regard est triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His look is sad.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing (stories, novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle regarda par la fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked out the window.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 1st person singular (“I”). Mostly used in writing; in speech French usually uses the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je regardai la mer pendant longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked at the sea for a long time.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils regardaient un film quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were watching a movie when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je regardais la télévision quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was watching TV when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il regardait la télévision quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was watching TV when I arrived.

definitions.note: Present participle of « regarder ». It can also look like English “regarding” (“concerning”), but here it’s the verb form meaning “looking/watching.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu, regardant la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him, looking at the sea.

definitions.note: This is a false friend with English "regard"; it usually means "look at" or "watch."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle regarde la télévision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is watching television.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « regarder » (used with « ils/elles »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils regardent la télévision après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watch TV after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais regarder la télévision ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to watch television tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il regardera le film ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of « regarder » (je regarderai).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demain, je regarderai ce film avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, I will watch this movie with you.

definitions.note: Future tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils regarderont un film ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will watch a movie tonight.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of « regarder ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu regardes la télé tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You watch TV every evening.

definitions.note: Formal or plural form of the command (“Look!” / “Watch!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Regardez ce film ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch this movie tonight.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous regardiez la télévision quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were watching TV when I arrived.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form used to make a suggestion: "let's …".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Regardons ce film ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's watch this movie together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a reçu des regards curieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got curious looks.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils regardèrent le film en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watched the movie in silence.

definitions.note: Past participle of « regarder ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai regardé un film hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched a movie last night.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of “regarder”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai regardée hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched her last night.

definitions.note: Often means “watched/looked at,” not “regarded” in the sense of “considered.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai regardées hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched them last night.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « regarder ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les oiseaux qu’ils ont regardés étaient magnifiques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds they watched were magnificent.

definitions.note: Often refers to an official log/book where information is recorded.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a écrit son nom dans le registre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrote her name in the register.

definitions.native: is full of, is teeming with
definitions.note: Often used with « de »: « regorger de » = to be full of / abound with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette ville regorge de cafés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This city is full of cafés.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai aucun regret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no regrets.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in common phrases like « avoir des regrets » (to have regrets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des regrets.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have regrets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il regretta sa décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He regretted his decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est regrettable, mais nous devons annuler la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s regrettable, but we have to cancel the meeting.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “regretter”; it can express regret or an apology depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je regrette de ne pas pouvoir venir ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry I can’t come tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais regretter mes paroles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to regret my words.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of missing a person, place, or time in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vas-tu me regretter ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to miss me?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu regretteras tes mots.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will regret your words.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous regretterez votre décision plus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will regret your decision later.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous regrettez votre décision ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you regret your decision?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin examine ses reins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines his kidneys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reine arrive au château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The queen is arriving at the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses reins lui font mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His kidneys hurt.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rejeta la proposition sans hésiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rejected the proposal without hesitating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le comité va rejeter la proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee is going to reject the proposal.

definitions.note: Often used for refusing an idea, offer, request, or proposal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle rejette sa proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rejects his proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont rejeté la proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rejected the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa demande a été rejetée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her request was rejected.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa proposition a été rejetée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her proposal was rejected.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « rejoindre » (used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je te rejoigne devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to meet up with you in front of the station.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « rejoindre » (they join / they are joining).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rejoignent leurs amis au café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet up with their friends at the café.

definitions.note: Often used to invite someone to come and meet you somewhere ("join us").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rejoignez-nous au café à 15 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Join us at the café at 3 p.m.

definitions.native: will join, will meet, will catch up with
definitions.note: First-person singular simple future of « rejoindre » (I will…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te rejoindrai à la gare à 18 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll meet you at the train station at 6 p.m.

definitions.native: will join, will meet, will catch up with
definitions.note: Future simple (tu form) of « rejoindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu rejoindras tes amis au café après les cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will meet your friends at the café after class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te rejoindre à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to meet you at the station.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « rejoindre » (usually used with « tu » or « je » depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te rejoins à la gare dans dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll meet you at the train station in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nous rejoint au café après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He joins us at the café after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans la course, je passe le relais à mon coéquipier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the race, I pass the relay (baton) to my teammate.

definitions.note: Often used for a place where you stop (e.g., on a trip) or where something/someone is relayed onward.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous faisons un relais dans un petit village avant de continuer la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We make a stopover in a small village before continuing the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une bonne relation avec mes voisins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good relationship with my neighbors.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts for a link between things (e.g., cause and effect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une relation entre le stress et le sommeil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a connection between stress and sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a de bonnes relations avec ses collègues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has good relationships with his colleagues.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est relativement facile de s’y habituer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s relatively easy to get used to it.

definitions.note: Common in everyday French to mean “fairly/quite” (often softer than “very”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le film est relativement long.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is fairly long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai remercié pour son aide.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives my book back to me tomorrow.

definitions.native: was giving back, was returning, was making
definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing/repeated past action or a past state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rendait le livre à la bibliothèque chaque semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was returning the book to the library every week.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « il faut que… » (subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je te rende ton livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to give you back your book.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « rendre » (used with ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rendent les clés au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They return the keys to the owner.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective: « rendre + complément + adjectif » (e.g., rendre heureux = make happy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces nouvelles rendent ma sœur très heureuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news makes my sister very happy.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present indicative of « rendre » (tu rendes)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me rendes mon livre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you giving me my book back?

definitions.note: Also used in fixed expressions like « rendre visite » (to visit) or « rendre service » (to do someone a favor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous rendez le livre demain ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you giving the book back tomorrow?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous rendiez les clés après chaque visite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You gave back the keys after each visit.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in writing/storytelling; corresponds to “they returned/gave back.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rendirent les clés au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They returned the keys to the owner.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 2nd person singular (tu). Mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu rendis les clés au concierge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You gave the keys back to the concierge.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), often used in novels and history writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rendit le livre à la bibliothèque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He returned the book to the library.

definitions.note: 1st person plural ("we") present, often used to make a suggestion ("let's...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rendons ce livre à la bibliothèque demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's return this book to the library tomorrow.

definitions.native: fall asleep again, go back to sleep
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le bruit, j’ai eu du mal à me rendormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the noise, I had trouble falling asleep again.

definitions.note: Simple future, 3rd person singular (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il te rendra ton livre demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will give you back your book tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular (je) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te rendrai ton livre demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give you back your book tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il me rendrait mon livre demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would give me my book back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective to mean “would make” (e.g., rendre + adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça rendrait le projet plus simple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That would make the project simpler.

definitions.note: Often means “give back” (e.g., return an item). Not the same as English “render” (a false friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me rendras mon livre demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will give me back my book tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux me rendre mon livre demain ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me my book back tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective: “rendre + object + adjective” (e.g., rendre quelqu’un heureux = to make someone happy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nouvelle va me rendre très heureux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That news is going to make me very happy.

definitions.note: Future tense (vous form). Often used for returning an object or giving something back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous rendrez les clés demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will return the keys tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) future tense of « rendre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous rendrons les clés demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will return the keys tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te rends ton livre demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give you back your book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective: « rendre + adjective ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me rends heureuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You make me happy.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rendre »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai rendu… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rendu mon devoir ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I handed in my homework this morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « rendre » (used with être or to agree with a preceding direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La monnaie m’est rendue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The change is returned to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les clés ont été rendues au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were returned to the owner.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective: « rendre + adjectif » = to make (someone/something) + adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces bonnes nouvelles les ont rendues très heureuses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That good news made them very happy.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rendre » (masculine plural), often used with homework or documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les devoirs ont été rendus demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The homework was turned in tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rendre » (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les clés ont été rendus au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were returned to the owner.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past), “we” form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous rendîmes les clés au propriétaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We gave the keys back to the owner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette loi renforce la sécurité des écoles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This law strengthens school safety.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette équipe veut renforcer sa défense cette saison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team wants to strengthen its defense this season.

definitions.note: Often used for extra support or additional personnel (e.g., police or military reinforcements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a demandé des renforts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police asked for reinforcements.

definitions.note: Often used for extra people sent to help (e.g., police, military, a team at work).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des renforts arrivent pour nous aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reinforcements are arriving to help us.

definitions.native: same old story, same old line
definitions.note: Often used to complain about something repetitive or overused.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nous ressort toujours la même rengaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always trots out the same old story.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il renifla et reprit son chemin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sniffed and continued on his way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien a reniflé la piste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog sniffed the trail.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts to mean someone’s good reputation or public recognition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce chef jouit d’une grande renommée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chef enjoys a great reputation.

definitions.note: Often used with « à » (e.g., « renoncer à quelque chose » = to give something up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je renonce à mon projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving up on my project.

definitions.native: give up; give up on; abandon
definitions.note: Usually used with “à” or “à + infinitive”: renoncer à quelque chose / renoncer à faire quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a décidé de renoncer à son projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to give up on his project.

definitions.note: Past participle of « renoncer » (often used with « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a renoncé à son projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave up on his plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois renouveler mon passeport bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to renew my passport soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle me renseigne sur les horaires du musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gives me information about the museum’s opening hours.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (renseignements) to mean “information” in general, especially practical info or details (e.g., at an information desk).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cherche un renseignement sur les horaires du musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for some information about the museum’s opening hours.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural in French, especially for practical info (e.g., travel or administrative details).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour plus de renseignements, contactez l’accueil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For more information, contact the reception desk.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « se renseigner » = to find out / get information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pouvez-vous me renseigner sur les horaires ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me information about the schedule?

definitions.note: Past participle of « renseigner »; often used to mean “well informed” (bien renseigné).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis bien renseigné sur le sujet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am well informed about the subject.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form, mostly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rentra tard ce soir-là.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back late that evening.

definitions.native: was coming back, was going back, was coming home
definitions.note: Often used for returning home; meaning can be ‘come back’ or ‘go back’ depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je rentrais chez moi quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was coming home when it started to rain.

definitions.native: was coming back, was going back in, was going home
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rentrait chez lui tous les soirs à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to come home every evening at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of « rentrer »; often used like “on returning/when coming back.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En rentrant chez moi, j’ai appelé ma sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On my way back home, I called my sister.

definitions.native: comes back, goes back (in), comes home
definitions.note: Often used to mean “to go/come home” (to return to where you live).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rentre à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes home.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can also mean “go in/enter” (e.g., going inside a building).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rentrent à la maison après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They come home after school.

definitions.note: Often used for returning home or going back inside.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais rentrer à la maison à six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to come home at six o'clock.

definitions.native: will come back, will go back (home)
definitions.note: Often used to mean returning home (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rentrera à la maison ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will come back home tonight.

definitions.native: will come back, will go back, will return, will go in
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je rentrerai tôt ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will come back early tonight.

definitions.native: will come back, will go back, will return
definitions.note: Future tense (tu form) of « rentrer ». Often used for returning home or going back inside.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu rentreras à la maison après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will come back home after school.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « rentrer » (e.g., « tu rentres », « il/elle rentre »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu rentres à la maison ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming home tonight?

definitions.note: Usually used with “vous” (formal or plural) as a command or present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rentrez à la maison, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go back home.

definitions.native: let’s go back, let’s come back
definitions.note: First-person plural ("nous") present-tense form, often used to make a suggestion (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rentrons à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go home.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rentrer »; commonly used with « être » (e.g., « il est rentré »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est rentré tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back late.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « rentrer » (used with être for intransitive movement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est rentrée tard hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came back late last night.

definitions.native: back-to-school, start of the school year
definitions.note: Commonly refers to the start of the school year (and more broadly the return to work and cultural life after summer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rentrée a lieu en septembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Back-to-school happens in September.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « rentrer » (often used with « être » in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont rentrées tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came home late.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « rentrer », often used with « être » (e.g., « ils sont rentrés »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont rentrés à la maison après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came back home after school.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple) form; common in writing (stories, books).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il renversa son verre sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knocked over his glass on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a renversé son verre d’eau en voulant s’asseoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knocked over his glass of water while trying to sit down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai renversé du café sur ma chemise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spilled coffee on my shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voiture a renversé un cycliste au carrefour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car ran over a cyclist at the intersection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le peuple a renversé le régime après des mois de protestations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The people overthrew the regime after months of protests.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like a card, a page, or an item on a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renversez la carte pour voir la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn the card over to see the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai renversé mon café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knocked over my coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bouteille est renversée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is knocked over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je renvoie le colis demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending the package back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for dismissing someone from a job (like “to fire”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le patron le renvoie après l’incident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss fires him after the incident.

definitions.note: Often used for returning something (e.g., a product) to where it came from.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais renvoyer ce colis à l’expéditeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send this package back to the sender.

definitions.note: Used with a person as the object: renvoyer quelqu’un.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le patron va renvoyer un employé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is going to fire an employee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renvoyez ce colis, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send this package back, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le colis a été renvoyé au magasin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package was sent back to the store.

definitions.note: Often used about being fired from a job or dismissed from school.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été renvoyé de son travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fired from his job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettre a été renvoyée à l’expéditeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was sent back to the sender.

definitions.note: Often used about losing a job (passive: « être renvoyé(e) »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été renvoyée après plusieurs retards.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was fired after several times being late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les colis ont été renvoyés au magasin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The packages were sent back to the store.

definitions.note: Often used for being fired from a job or expelled from a place (like school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont été renvoyés de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were expelled from school.

definitions.note: Often used for a place where criminals or dangerous animals hide.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a trouvé le repaire du gang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found the gang’s hideout.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can also be the informal command “talk again!” (to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reparle après l’opération.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can speak again after the operation.

definitions.note: Often used with de (reparler de) to mean “talk about again.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On pourra reparler de ce sujet demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can talk about this topic again tomorrow.

definitions.note: future tense, “we” form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous reparlerons de ce problème demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will talk about this problem again tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je repars demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving again tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il repart demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaves again tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often means “you leave again” (vous) or can be used as an order: “leave again!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous repartez déjà ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you leaving again already?

definitions.note: Past participle of « repartir », often used with « être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est reparti tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left again right away.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « repartir » (used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est repartie à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She left again at noon.

definitions.native: to leave again, to set off again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois repartir tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave again right away.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (repartir quelque chose) like tasks, roles, or money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va repartir les tâches entre nous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to divide up the tasks among us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je repartis tôt le lendemain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left again early the next morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On prend un repas en famille le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a meal as a family on Sundays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle repassait une chemise quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was ironing a shirt when you called.

definitions.native: was coming back, was passing by again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il repassait par ici tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was coming by here again every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il repasse sa chemise avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He irons his shirt before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle repasse par la boulangerie après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She goes back to the bakery after work.

definitions.note: Often used for reviewing a lesson or material.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il repasse la leçon ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reviews the lesson tonight.

definitions.note: Used for ironing clothes (removing wrinkles with an iron).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois repasser ma chemise avant le rendez-vous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to iron my shirt before the appointment.

definitions.native: to go back, to come back
definitions.note: Often means returning to a place or doing something again ("to stop by again").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais repasser demain pour récupérer mon livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come back tomorrow to pick up my book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je repasserai la chemise demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will iron the shirt tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: will come back, will stop by again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je repasserai te voir après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will come back to see you after work.

definitions.note: Often used for reviewing lessons or going over something again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je repasserai ma leçon ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will review my lesson tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai repassé la chemise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ironed the shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis repassé par ici hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came back here last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va repeindre la cuisine ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to repaint the kitchen this weekend.

definitions.note: Present tense (il/elle/on) of « repeindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il repeint la porte d’entrée en bleu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He repaints the front door in blue.

definitions.note: Past participle of « repeindre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mur a été repeint hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall was repainted yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for folding something back onto itself (e.g., paper, a sleeve, a map). Not related to English “reply”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il replie la carte et la met dans sa poche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He folds the map and puts it in his pocket.

definitions.note: Command form (vous) or present tense with “vous” (you plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Repliez la carte et rangez-la dans votre sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fold the map up and put it in your bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai vu un reportage sur les incendies à la télévision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a news report about the fires on TV.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le reporter écrit un article sur l’événement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reporter is writing an article about the event.

definitions.note: Often means “to postpone,” not “to report” (which is usually "rapporter" or "signaler" in French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons reporter la réunion à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are going to postpone the meeting until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le match a été reporté à cause de la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The match was postponed because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’incident a été reporté au journal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The incident was reported to the newspaper.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “postponed” (not “reported” in the news sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunion est reportée à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is postponed until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin de repos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need rest.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense), most often seen in books and stories; in conversation you usually use "a reposé".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le voyage, il reposa quelques minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, he rested for a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reposait sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was resting on the sofa.
