definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to stay at home tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle restera à Paris demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will stay in Paris tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je resterai à la maison ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will stay at home tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je resterais à la maison s'il pleuvait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would stay at home if it rained.

definitions.note: Future tense (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu resteras ici pendant que je vais chercher de l’aide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will stay here while I go get help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous resterez ici jusqu’à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will stay here until tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous resterons ici jusqu’à la fin du film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will stay here until the end of the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils resteront ici jusqu’à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will stay here until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je garde les restes pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m keeping the leftovers for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « rester » used with « tu » (informal singular) or as the imperative « (tu) reste » + -s before « en »/« y ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu restes ici ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you staying here tonight?

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or several people to stay.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Restez ici, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay here.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form): can describe an ongoing or habitual past situation, or a polite/softened suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pensais que vous restiez à la maison ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you were staying at home tonight.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial abbreviation of « restaurant ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On mange au resto ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating at a restaurant tonight.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("nous") present; often used as a suggestion ("let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Restons ici encore cinq minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s stay here five more minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’accès est restreint aux membres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Access is restricted to members.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person plural; common in writing (stories, history), less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils restèrent silencieux pendant un moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They remained silent for a moment.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rester » (often used with « être » in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est resté à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed at home.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « rester » (used with « être » or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est restée à la maison toute la journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stayed at home all day.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of « rester » (used with « être » in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont restées à la maison toute la journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stayed at home all day.

definitions.note: Past participle of "rester"; agrees with a masculine plural subject (or a mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont restés à la maison toute la journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stayed at home all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le train a dix minutes de retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is ten minutes late.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a command meaning “delay!” (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bus retarde à cause du trafic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is delayed because of traffic.

definitions.note: Often used for delays in schedules, projects, or actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mauvais temps va retarder le vol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bad weather is going to delay the flight.

definitions.note: Past participle of "retarder" (used with avoir, or with être in the passive). Not to be confused with the English word "retarded" (offensive term).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vol a été retardé à cause du brouillard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight was delayed because of the fog.

definitions.note: Present participle of « retenir »; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avançait en retenant son souffle, retenant sa peur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved forward holding his breath, holding back his fear.

definitions.note: Also commonly used to mean “hold back” or “keep,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retenez bien cette règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remember this rule well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais retenir ton nom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to remember your name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaie de retenir ses larmes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to hold back his tears.

definitions.note: Past participle of « retentir » (often used with « avoir »: « a retenti »). Not related to « retenir » (“to keep/retain”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un cri a retenti dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A shout rang out in the street.

definitions.note: Can be present tense ("it rings out") or the literary simple past ("it rang out") in narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une sirène retentit dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A siren rings out in the street.

definitions.note: Past participle of « retenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai retenu ton numéro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kept (remembered) your number.

definitions.note: Feminine form (past participle) of « retenir »; used with a feminine noun (or when the subject/object is feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa colère est retenue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her anger is held back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait preuve de retenue pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed restraint during the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used for an amount kept back (for example from a salary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une retenue sur mon salaire ce mois-ci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a deduction from my salary this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retiens mon souffle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hold my breath.

definitions.note: In everyday French, retenir is often used to mean “to remember” (e.g., retenir un nom, un numéro).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retiens ton nom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember your name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retient une partie de son salaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He keeps (retains) part of his salary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle retient facilement les numéros de téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remembers phone numbers easily.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form of « retenir », mostly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retint son souffle pendant quelques secondes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He held his breath for a few seconds.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « retirer » (he/she/it withdrew/removed/took off). Often replaced by « a retiré » in spoken French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retira son chapeau en entrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took off his hat as he came in.

definitions.note: Usually means “remove/take out/withdraw,” not “retire” (stop working).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retire son argent au distributeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He withdraws his money at the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu retirer ton manteau, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take off your coat, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais retirer de l'argent au distributeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to withdraw money from the ATM.

definitions.note: Often means “remove/withdraw” in French; it does not usually mean “retire” (stop working).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu retires ta main du feu !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You take your hand away from the fire!

definitions.note: Usually used with "vous" (formal singular or plural) as an instruction or request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retirez la carte de la machine, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remove the card from the machine, please.

definitions.note: Often used for taking something out (e.g., money from a bank account) or removing something from a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai retiré de l'argent au distributeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I withdrew money from the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’annonce a été retirée du site.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ad was removed from the website.

definitions.note: Past participle of « retirer ». It can look like English “retired,” but it usually means “removed/taken out” in this form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les documents ont été retirés du dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were removed from the file.

definitions.native: to fall again, to fall back down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ballon va retomber dans l’herbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball is going to fall back down into the grass.

definitions.native: to fall back into (a habit), to relapse
definitions.note: Often used with "dans" + a noun (e.g., retomber dans une addiction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il risque de retomber dans ses mauvaises habitudes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He may relapse into his bad habits.

definitions.note: Often used for coming back or a trip back (e.g., "aller-retour" = round trip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais mon retour à Paris demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m returning to Paris tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular; used mainly in literature and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retourna la carte pour lire le message.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned the card over to read the message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retourne à la maison après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes back home after school.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about turning something to the other side (it can also be used as an imperative: “Retourn(e) !” = “Turn/Flip it over!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il retourne la feuille pour lire l’autre côté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turns the sheet over to read the other side.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois retourner à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go back home.

definitions.note: Often used for flipping something (e.g., a pancake) so the other side faces up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois retourner la crêpe, s'il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to flip the pancake, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retournerai en France l'année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will go back to France next year.

definitions.note: Often used for physically turning something over (e.g., a card, a pancake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retournerai la crêpe dans une minute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will flip the crêpe in a minute.

definitions.note: Can mean either “to go back/return” or “to turn (something) over,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu retournes à la maison après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go back home after school.

definitions.note: Often used as an instruction (formal or plural “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retournez à la maison, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go back home, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous retourniez à la maison avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to go back home before nightfall.

definitions.note: Used with an object (e.g., a page, a card).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voulais que vous retourniez la carte pour voir l’image.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted you to flip the card over to see the picture.

definitions.note: First-person plural present ("we" / "let’s").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retournons à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go back home.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple), used mostly in writing (stories, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le dîner, ils retournèrent à l’hôtel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, they went back to the hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est retourné chez lui après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went back home after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tapis est retourné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rug is turned over.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « retourner », often used with « être » to mean “was returned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettre est retournée à l'expéditeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was returned to the sender.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le retrait d’argent au distributeur est impossible aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cash withdrawal at the ATM is impossible today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon père est à la retraite depuis deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad has been retired for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon père est retraité depuis deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad has been retired for two years.

definitions.note: Often used for finding something/someone again or meeting someone at a place ("meet up").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retrouve mes clés dans mon sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find my keys again in my bag.

definitions.note: Often used for finding something you lost, or discovering something again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais retrouver mon livre ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find my book again tonight.

definitions.native: to meet again, to see again
definitions.note: Used for getting together with someone after some time apart.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons retrouver nos amis demain au café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to meet our friends again tomorrow at the café.

definitions.native: will find again, will meet again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle retrouvera ses clés dans son sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will find her keys again in her bag.

definitions.native: will find again, will meet again
definitions.note: First person singular future tense (je).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je retrouverai mes clés demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find my keys again tomorrow.

definitions.native: will find again, will meet again
definitions.note: Future tense (tu form): used with "you" (singular, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu retrouveras tes clés dans ton sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find your keys again in your bag.

definitions.native: will find again, will meet again, will get back
definitions.note: Second-person plural future tense (vous). Often used for “see you again” in a formal or plural context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous retrouverez vos clés sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find your keys on the table.

definitions.native: will find again, will meet again
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous retrouverons nos amis demain au café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will meet our friends again tomorrow at the café.

definitions.note: Form used with “vous” (you plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retrouvez votre mot de passe avec votre adresse e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Find your password again using your email address.

definitions.native: let's meet (up), let's get back together
definitions.note: 1st person plural ("nous") present; often used to suggest meeting again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retrouvons-nous à 18 h devant le cinéma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's meet at 6 p.m. in front of the movie theater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai retrouvé mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys again.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « retrouver ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai retrouvée au café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found her again at the café.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « retrouver ». It often means ‘to find again’ or ‘to rediscover’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai retrouvés dans le tiroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found them again in the drawer.

definitions.note: Often used in the set phrase « prendre sa revanche » (“to get your revenge / get even”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veut prendre sa revanche après cette défaite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to get his revenge after that defeat.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « revenir »; often implies an ongoing, repeated, or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il revenait souvent tard le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often came back late in the evening.

definitions.note: Often used after « en » to mean “on the way back / when returning.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En revenant, j’ai acheté du pain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the way back, I bought bread.

definitions.native: to claim; to assert (a right); to demand
definitions.note: Used for formally asserting a right, responsibility, or ownership, or for demanding something (often in a collective/social context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les employés revendiquent une augmentation de salaire : ils vont revendiquer cette hausse jusqu’au bout.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees are demanding a pay raise: they will keep demanding it to the end.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as the polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revenez demain, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come back tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais revenir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to come back tomorrow.

definitions.native: let’s come back, we’re coming back
definitions.note: Present tense form of « revenir » used with « nous » (we); can also be used as an imperative meaning “let’s come back / let’s return.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revenons à la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s come back to the question.

definitions.note: Past participle of « revenir », usually used with « être » (e.g., « il est revenu »). Not related to English « revenue ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est revenu à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son revenu est faible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His income is low.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « revenir » (typically used with « être »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est revenue à la maison tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came back home late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont revenues tard hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came back late last night.

definitions.note: Past participle of « revenir » used with « être »; agrees in number/gender (here: masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont revenus tard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came back late.

definitions.note: Plural form of "revenu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses revenus ont augmenté cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His income has increased this year.

definitions.native: will see again, will meet again
definitions.note: Future tense (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il te reverra demain au bureau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will see you again tomorrow at the office.

definitions.note: Future tense of "revoir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te reverrai demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will see you again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple future (tu form) of « revoir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me reverras demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will see me again tomorrow.

definitions.native: will see again, will see you again
definitions.note: Second-person plural future tense (vous). Often used to address one person formally or multiple people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous reverrez vos amis demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will see your friends again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future tense form of « revoir » (used for seeing someone or something again).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nous reverrons demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will see each other again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for the back side of clothing or fabric; in set phrases like « à l’envers et à l’endroit ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a mis son pull à l’envers : on voit le revers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put his sweater on inside out: you can see the back side.

definitions.note: Simple future (3rd person singular) of « revenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reviendra demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will come back tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") future tense of "revenir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je reviendrai demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will come back tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Conditional ("would") form of « revenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je reviendrais demain si je pouvais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would come back tomorrow if I could.

definitions.note: Conditional form of « revenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il reviendrait demain si c’était possible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would come back tomorrow if it were possible.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense of « revenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu reviendras demain matin ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you come back tomorrow morning?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense of « revenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous reviendrez demain matin ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you come back tomorrow morning?

definitions.note: Future tense ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous reviendrons demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will come back tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils reviendront demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will come back tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « revenir » (used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux qu’elle revienne demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want her to come back tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils reviennent demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are coming back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « revenir » (used with « tu » or « je » depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je reviens tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il revient demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” to give a total amount (e.g., “Ça revient à…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça revient à dix euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It comes to ten euros.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple) form; common in books and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il revint chez lui avant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back home before nightfall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il revit son amie après dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees his friend again after ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne veux pas revivre ce moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to relive that moment.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of « revoir », often used after « que » (e.g., « il faut que… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je revoie mes notes avant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to look over my notes again before the exam.

definitions.native: here we are again, there you are again
definitions.note: Used to point out that someone/something has come back or reappeared.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revoilà Paul !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s Paul again!

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « au revoir » (“goodbye”), literally “until we see each other again.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais revoir mes amis ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to see my friends again this weekend.

definitions.note: Commonly used for studying (e.g., to review a lesson).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois revoir mes notes avant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to review my notes before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te revois demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll see you again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for going over information again (for example, notes for an exam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je revois mes notes avant l’examen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fabric is rough to the touch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces remarques sont rudes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live on a quiet alley behind the bakery.

definitions.note: Used especially for a horse rearing or bucking.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That mistake is going to ruin my chances.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les ruines du château sont impressionnantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle ruins are impressive.

definitions.note: Often used to mean financially broke.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “financially broke” or “bankrupt” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après cet accident, il est ruiné.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After that accident, he is ruined.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A stream runs through the village.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are rumors about their divorce.

definitions.note: Usually used for the end of a romantic relationship.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After two years, they announced their breakup.

definitions.note: Used for a break, split, or rupture (for example in medicine or a material).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin a confirmé une rupture des ligaments.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor confirmed a ligament rupture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a utilisé une ruse pour entrer sans billet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used a trick to get in without a ticket.

definitions.note: Describes a person or thing from Russia.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Russian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est un Russe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is a Russian.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes voisins sont russes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are Russian.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les Russes parlent souvent russe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Russians often speak Russian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très rusé et il trouve toujours une solution.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very cunning and he always finds a solution.

definitions.note: masculine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Foxes are very cunning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime le rythme de cette chanson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the rhythm of this song.

definitions.note: Often implies complaining in an annoyed way.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going to complain again when it rains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette école, il y a une règle importante : on arrive à l’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this school, there is an important rule: you arrive on time.

definitions.note: A measuring tool used to draw straight lines or measure length.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une règle pour mesurer cette feuille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a ruler to measure this sheet of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je règle la température.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I adjust the temperature.

definitions.note: often used for paying a bill or settling an amount owed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je règle l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay the bill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois respecter le règlement de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to follow the school rules.

definitions.note: Often used for paying a bill or settling an amount due.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le règlement se fait en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Payment is made online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois suivre les règlements de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to follow the school rules.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like paying an invoice or settling an amount owed (e.g., "règlement d’une facture").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les règlements se font par carte ou en espèces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Payments are made by card or in cash.

definitions.note: Plural form of « règle ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois suivre les règles de l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to follow the school rules.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the plural (« les règles ») to mean menstruation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a ses règles aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has her period today.

definitions.note: Verb form used with "tu" (e.g., "tu règles"). Not to be confused with the noun "règles" meaning "rules" or "period".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You adjust the radio volume.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le règne de Louis XIV a duré plus de soixante-dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reign of Louis XIV lasted more than seventy years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il règne sur son royaume depuis dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has reigned over his kingdom for ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le réacteur de la centrale a été arrêté par sécurité.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His reactions are normal.

definitions.note: Past participle of « réagir » (used with « avoir » in compound tenses).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reacted too quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" to mean "react to".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to react to this news calmly.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « réagir » used with « tu » (informal “you”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reacts calmly to the bad news.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), third-person singular; used mainly in literature and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle réalisa son rêve de voyager autour du monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She achieved her dream of traveling around the world.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce projet est réalisable en deux semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This project is feasible in two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce réalisateur a gagné un prix au festival.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This film director won a prize at the festival.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about what someone has achieved (e.g., on a CV). Not the same as English “realizations” (= becoming aware of something).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On my résumé, I describe my main achievements.

definitions.note: Often used with a clause like « que… » to mean becoming aware/understanding something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je réalise que j’ai oublié mes clés.

definitions.note: Can mean doing/producing something concrete (e.g., a project, a film).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle réalise un film pour l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is making a film for school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils réalisent ce projet ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They carry out this project together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle veut réaliser son rêve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to achieve her dream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais réaliser que j’ai oublié mes clés.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils réaliseront ce projet l’année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will carry out this project next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils réaliseront bientôt qu’ils se sont trompés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will soon realize that they were wrong.

definitions.note: Can mean “to become aware/understand” or “to do/complete” depending on context.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense (also used as the formal singular “you”).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce plan est réaliste.

definitions.note: plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your goals are realistic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai réalisé une affiche pour l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a poster for school.

definitions.note: Often used for suddenly understanding something or becoming aware of something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut accepter la réalité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to accept reality.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai déménagé récemment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved recently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un film récent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a recent movie.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "récent".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une nouvelle récente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a recent piece of news.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went to the hotel reception to ask for my key.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have mutual respect.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave us an account of his trip.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the piano recital tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She recites a poem in front of the class.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filed a complaint with customer service.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The harvests were poor this year because of the drought.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apples were harvested in September.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu auras une récompense si tu finis tes devoirs.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees were rewarded for their work.

definitions.native: to reconcile; to bring back together (people, ideas, groups)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mediator is going to reconcile the two neighbors.

definitions.note: Often used for emotional comfort or solace.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After that bad news, I needed comfort.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce thé chaud est très réconfortant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hot tea is very comforting.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tries to comfort her friend after the bad news.

definitions.note: Addressed to “you” in the plural (vous), or as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réconfortez votre ami, il en a besoin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Comfort your friend; he needs it.

definitions.note: In school context, it usually means “recess” (the break time between classes).

definitions.note: Often used for reusing materials or objects instead of throwing them away.

definitions.note: Often used about getting better after being tired or ill.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la grippe, il doit récupérer.

definitions.note: Often used as an instruction (e.g., “récupérez vos affaires” = “get your things back”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pick up your luggage at the exit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai récupéré mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got my keys back.

definitions.note: Often used for a written assignment (like an essay) or the act of writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour demain, nous devons faire une rédaction en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For tomorrow, we have to write a French composition.

definitions.note: Often used for writing something fairly formal (a report, a letter, a contract, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois rédiger un rapport pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write a report for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rédiger » (used with être/avoir or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le contrat est rédigé en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract is written in French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons obtenu une réduction sur le prix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got a reduction on the price.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to reduce waste.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The speed is reduced in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les prix ont été réduits cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prices were reduced this week.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are real problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais réessayer demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to try again tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for a school, convent, monastery, or boarding house dining room.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We all have lunch together in the dining hall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai eu le réflexe de vérifier la porte avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the reflex to check the door before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses réflexes sont rapides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His reflexes are quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après un moment de réflexion, j’ai changé d’avis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a moment of thought, I changed my mind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après quelques réflexions, j’ai accepté son invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After some thought, I accepted his invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai réfléchi à ta proposition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about your proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois réfléchir avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to think before answering.

definitions.note: Often used as an order or suggestion (as in “Think!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réfléchis avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think before you answer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for an ongoing or repeated action in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was thinking about that problem all night.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form; can also mean “reflect” (think about something carefully).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je réfléchisse avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to think before answering.

definitions.note: Used as “you” (plural or formal singular) in the present tense, or as a command (“think!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réfléchissez avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think before you answer.

definitions.note: Present tense form (3rd person singular) of « réfléchir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il réfléchit avant de répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thinks before answering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le réfrigérateur est presque vide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The refrigerator is almost empty.

definitions.note: Most often used reflexively: « se réfugier » = to take refuge (somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant l’orage, ils vont réfugier leurs enfants dans la cave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the storm, they will shelter their children in the cellar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les réfugiés cherchent un endroit sûr où vivre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The refugees are looking for a safe place to live.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” (référer à) to mean “to refer to.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often refers to that book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu me donner une référence pour ce livre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a reference for this book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis les références à la fin du document.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the references at the end of the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle nous régale avec un gâteau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She treats us with a cake.

definitions.note: Often used with an object pronoun: « Je te régale » = “It’s my treat / I’m treating you.” It can also mean to really delight someone (often with food, but not only).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te régaler avec un bon dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to treat you to a good dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for an eating plan, sometimes specifically to lose weight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis au régime en ce moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm on a diet right now.

definitions.note: In politics, it refers to a government or political system, often with a negative tone.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The regime banned demonstrations.

definitions.note: a military unit
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon grand-père a servi dans un régiment d’infanterie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather served in an infantry regiment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette région est très montagneuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This region is very mountainous.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les régions de France ont chacune leurs traditions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The regions of France each have their own traditions.

definitions.note: Often used for paying a bill or settling a matter (e.g., a problem or dispute).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais régler l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to pay the bill.

definitions.native: will settle, will pay, will set
definitions.note: Simple future (3rd person singular) of « régler ». Depending on context, it often means to settle a bill (pay) or to resolve a problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il réglera la facture demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will pay the bill tomorrow.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally, or multiple people, to set/adjust something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réglez le volume, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Adjust the volume, please.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally, or multiple people, to pay/settle (a bill, an amount).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réglez la note à la caisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pay the bill at the checkout.

definitions.note: Informal/slang (often used to say something is acceptable or that someone is fair/honest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: T’inquiète, c’est réglo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’s okay.

definitions.note: Often used with "nous" ("nous réglons" = "we adjust/set") or as the "let’s" form ("Réglons..." = "Let’s adjust/set...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réglons la hauteur du siège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s adjust the seat height.

definitions.note: Often used with "nous" ("nous réglons" = "we pay/settle") or as the "let’s" form ("Réglons..." = "Let’s pay/settle...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réglons l'addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s pay the bill.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase « C’est réglé » to mean something is settled/handled (and no longer a problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne t’inquiète pas, c’est réglé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’s taken care of.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « C’est réglé » (“It’s settled / taken care of”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne t’inquiète pas, tout est réglé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, everything is settled.

definitions.note: Common for bills/invoices (e.g., « facture réglée »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le restaurant est réglé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant bill is paid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’affaire est réglée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The matter is settled.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À cette époque, le roi régnait sur le pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that time, the king ruled over the country.

definitions.note: Often used for monarchs; also used more generally for a situation or feeling that ‘prevails’ (e.g., silence, chaos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendant des siècles, des rois ont tenté de régner sans partage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For centuries, kings tried to reign without sharing power.

definitions.note: Often means “at a steady/consistent rhythm” (e.g., trains, hours, habits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bus est régulier le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is regular in the morning.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons des horaires réguliers cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have regular schedules this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais du sport régulièrement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exercise regularly.

definitions.note: Commonly used to mean “often” in everyday speech (not necessarily on a fixed schedule).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is often late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Certaines religions croient en la réincarnation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some religions believe in reincarnation.

definitions.note: Usually used in the reflexive form « se réjouir » (to be happy/glad about something).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to see you again.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form, commonly used to suggest doing something together ("let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réjouissons-nous de cette bonne nouvelle !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s rejoice at this good news!

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object: « Ça me réjouit » = “That makes me happy.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nouvelle me réjouit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news makes me happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rénovation de l’appartement coûte cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The renovation of the apartment is expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’appartement a été rénové l’année dernière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment was renovated last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rumeur se répand vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rumor spreads quickly.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple), mostly used in writing (stories, novels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une odeur de fumée se répandit dans la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A smell of smoke spread through the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rumeur s’est rapidement répandue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rumor spread quickly.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mainly used in formal writing (e.g., literature).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réparation de ma voiture coûte très cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The repair of my car is very expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les réparations prennent plus de temps que prévu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The repairs are taking longer than expected.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repaired my bike.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is repaired.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a busy week, I finally have a little respite.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a répliqué immédiatement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replied immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result was replicated by another team.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answers the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il répondait toujours très vite aux messages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always used to answer messages very quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a reservation under the name Martin.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very reserved in class.
