definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to solve this problem together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il résout le problème rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He solves the problem quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le résultat est positif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result is positive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les résultats seront affichés demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The results will be displayed tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “resume” (= continue) or “résumé” (= CV).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle résume l’histoire en deux phrases.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She summarizes the story in two sentences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu résumer cet article en deux phrases ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you summarize this article in two sentences?

definitions.note: Often used for a summary of a text, report, or situation. For “CV/résumé” in the job-application sense, French usually uses “CV” (curriculum vitae).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu me faire un résumé de ce chapitre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a summary of this chapter?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La résurrection est un thème important dans certaines religions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Resurrection is an important theme in some religions.

definitions.note: often used to say someone is back to good health after being ill
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la grippe, il est enfin rétabli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flu, he’s finally recovered.

definitions.note: Often used for restoring something to its previous state (e.g., order, peace, a service, electricity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ville va rétablir l’électricité demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is going to restore electricity tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Used reflexively as "se rétablir" to mean to recover (from an illness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la grippe, il a réussi à rétablir sa santé progressivement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flu, he managed to recover his health gradually.

definitions.note: Present tense form (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin rétablit le calme dans la salle d’attente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor restores calm in the waiting room.

definitions.note: A (now uncommon/old-fashioned) job: someone who repairs metal pots and pans by re-tinning them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le rétameur répare les vieilles casseroles du village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tinker repairs the village’s old saucepans.

definitions.note: Often used with « à » + infinitive (e.g., « réticent à faire quelque chose »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est réticent à parler de ce sujet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is reluctant to talk about this topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je règle le rétroviseur avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I adjust the rearview mirror before leaving.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rétrécir »; used with « être » in compound tenses and as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pull a rétréci au lavage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sweater shrank in the wash.

definitions.note: Past participle of « réunir »; often used with « être » to mean that a group has met or is assembled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le comité est réuni ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee is meeting this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunification du pays a eu lieu en 1990.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reunification of the country took place in 1990.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une réunion à 10 heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting at 10 o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons deux réunions aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two meetings today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va réunir toute l’équipe pour parler du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to bring the whole team together to talk about the project.

definitions.note: Used for a group of people (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous nous réunis ce soir pour parler du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting tonight to talk about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette association réunit des voisins tous les mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This group brings neighbors together every month.

definitions.note: Often used with an object to mean “passed” (e.g. réussir un examen = to pass an exam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai réussi l'examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle veut réussir dans la vie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to succeed in life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle réussira si elle étudie régulièrement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will succeed if she studies regularly.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu réussiras ton examen si tu révises un peu chaque jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will pass your exam if you review a little each day.

definitions.note: First-person plural future (nous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous réussirons si nous travaillons ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will succeed if we work together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je réussis à finir mes devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I succeed in finishing my homework before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle réussit toujours ses examens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always succeeds in her exams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa réussite est le résultat de beaucoup de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His success is the result of a lot of work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je règle mon réveil à sept heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set my alarm clock for seven o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le réveil est difficile le lundi matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Waking up is hard on Monday morning.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se réveilla en sursaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He woke up with a start.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: « se réveiller » = to wake up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me réveille à sept heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Can be used reflexively: « se réveiller » = to wake up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te réveiller à sept heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to wake you up at seven o'clock.

definitions.native: will wake up, will wake (someone) up
definitions.note: Can be used either intransitively (wake up) or transitively (wake someone up), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit la réveillera demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise will wake her up tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Used with "tu" (informal singular): « tu réveilles ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me réveilles trop tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're waking me up too early.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command to one person you address with « vous » (formal or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Réveillez-vous, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up, please.

definitions.native: late-night holiday meal, Christmas/New Year’s Eve dinner
definitions.note: Refers especially to a festive meal eaten late on Christmas Eve (réveillon de Noël) or New Year’s Eve (réveillon du Nouvel An).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On fait un grand réveillon en famille le 24 décembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a big late-night Christmas Eve dinner with the family on December 24th.

definitions.note: Past participle of « réveiller »; often used with « être » (and often reflexively: « se réveiller »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis réveillé tôt ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early this morning.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (it’s originally the past participle of « réveiller »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis réveillé depuis six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « réveiller » (often used with « être » or in the reflexive « se réveiller »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me suis réveillée tôt ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early this morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est déjà réveillée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is already awake.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « réveiller » (often used with « être » in compound tenses, or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles se sont réveillées tôt ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They woke up early this morning.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of « réveiller ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont déjà réveillés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re already awake.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants sont déjà réveillés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are already awake.

definitions.note: Often used for studying/reviewing lessons (especially for an exam). It can also mean “revise” in the sense of checking/updating something (a text, a plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je révise pour l’examen de demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying for tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Often used for studying for an exam ("réviser pour un examen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois réviser pour l’examen de demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to review for tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « le temps est révolu » to mean something is over and belongs to the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette époque est révolue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That era is gone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La Révolution française a commencé en 1789.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The French Revolution began in 1789.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses idées étaient vraiment révolutionnaires pour l’époque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His ideas were truly revolutionary for the time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle révèle la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reveals the truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mostly used in writing (stories, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il révéla la vérité au dernier moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He revealed the truth at the last moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette révélation a surpris tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This revelation surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va révéler la vérité à tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to reveal the truth to everyone.

definitions.native: to unveil; to bring to light (a secret, information, identity)
definitions.note: Often used for secrets, information, or something previously hidden.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le journaliste doit révéler ses sources avant de publier l’article.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist must reveal his sources before publishing the article.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le secret a été révélé hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secret was revealed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vérité a été révélée hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truth was revealed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À la fin du spectacle, les danseuses font une révérence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the show, the dancers take a bow.

definitions.note: Used as a title for a member of the clergy (especially in some Christian churches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le révérend arrive pour la cérémonie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Reverend is arriving for the ceremony.

definitions.note: Feminine form, used as a title or descriptor for a member of the clergy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La révérende Martin prend la parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reverend Martin is speaking.

definitions.note: Past participle of « réélire »; often used with « être » (e.g., « il a été réélu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maire a été réélu pour un second mandat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor was re-elected for a second term.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for ongoing or habitual actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je rêvais que je pouvais voler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was dreaming that I could fly.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il était petit, il rêvait souvent de voyager.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was little, he often dreamed of traveling.

definitions.note: Often implies letting your mind wander rather than focusing on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime rêvasser pendant le cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to daydream during class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait un rêve étrange cette nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a strange dream last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rêve souvent la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often dreams at night.

definitions.note: Present tense of « rêver » (used with ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rêvent de voyager en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They dream of traveling to France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime rêver quand je suis en vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to dream when I’m on vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait de beaux rêves cette nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had beautiful dreams last night.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu form) of « rêver ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu rêves de voyager en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You dream of traveling to France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un rêveur : il parle toujours de ses projets impossibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He's a dreamer: he always talks about his impossible plans.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with vous (you, formal or plural); can also be an imperative meaning “dream!” addressed to vous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rêvez-vous souvent la nuit ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you often dream at night?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « rêver » (used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand tu étais petit, vous rêviez souvent de voyager.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were little, you often dreamed of traveling.

definitions.note: Past participle of « rêver »; used with « avoir » in compound tenses and can agree when used as an adjective (e.g., « un voyage rêvé »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rêvé de vacances au soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dreamed of a vacation in the sun.

definitions.note: Often used for someone or something moving around with no clear purpose, sometimes in a suspicious way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un homme rôde autour de la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A man is prowling around the house.

definitions.note: Often used for people or animals moving around (sometimes suspiciously) without a clear purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des chats rôdent près des poubelles la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cats prowl near the trash cans at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel est ton rôle dans ce projet ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your role in this project?

definitions.note: Plural of « rôle ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les acteurs ont des rôles importants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the actors have important roles.

definitions.note: Often used for food (meat, vegetables, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pommes de terre sont rôties.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The potatoes are roasted.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a piece of meat cooked as a roast.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour le dimanche, on prépare un rôti de bœuf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Sunday, we’re making a roast beef.

definitions.note: used before a feminine singular noun; it agrees with the thing possessed, not the possessor
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a perdu sa veste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lost his jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a du sable dans mes chaussures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is sand in my shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelqu’un veut saboter le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone wants to sabotage the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a saboté le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sabotaged the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sabre est une arme tranchante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The saber is a bladed weapon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis mes livres dans mon sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put my books in my bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'appartement a été saccagé pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment was trashed during the night.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “sachant que …” meaning “knowing that … / given that …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sachant qu’il pleuvait, elle a pris un parapluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Knowing it was going to rain, she took an umbrella.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of « savoir », often used after expressions like « il faut que » (it’s necessary that…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je sache la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to know the truth.

definitions.note: Usually used in the present subjunctive (je/il/elle/on). It can also be the imperative (tu) meaning “know!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je sache la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to know the truth.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (they) of « savoir »; often used after expressions like « il faut que », « je veux que », « bien que », etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut qu’ils sachent la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have to know the truth.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, often used after "que" (e.g., "il faut que tu saches...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que tu saches la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to know the truth.

definitions.note: Often used for a small sealed packet containing a single portion (e.g., tea, sugar, shampoo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends un sachet de thé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking a tea bag.

definitions.note: Formal or plural command form (“you” as vous): “know … / be aware …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sachez que je suis là pour vous aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Know that I am here to help you.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present subjunctive of « savoir » (used with « vous »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que vous sachiez la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to know the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faire un sacrifice demande parfois beaucoup de courage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Making a sacrifice sometimes takes a lot of courage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont fait beaucoup de sacrifices pour leurs enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They made many sacrifices for their children.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: sacrifier quelque chose (to sacrifice something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va sacrifier son temps pour aider ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to sacrifice his time to help his friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a sacrifié son temps libre pour aider sa famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sacrificed his free time to help his family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pour eux, critiquer ce livre est un sacrilège.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For them, criticizing this book is a sacrilege.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un lieu sacré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sacred place.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette tradition est sacrée pour ma famille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tradition is sacred for my family.

definitions.note: Common informal use to emphasize a noun (often before it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une sacrée surprise !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s one heck of a surprise!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des chansons sacrées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are sacred songs.

definitions.note: Informal; often used to emphasize an adjective or to mildly swear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fait sacrément froid aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s really cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des lieux sacrés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are holy places.

definitions.note: Plural of « sac ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai deux sacs dans la voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two bags in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu un plaisir sadique à se moquer de lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took a sadistic pleasure in making fun of him.

definitions.note: A spice (and also the yellow-orange color made from it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ajoute une pincée de safran dans le riz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I add a pinch of saffron to the rice.

definitions.note: Often means sensible or reasonable; it can also describe someone who gives wise advice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un conseil sage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's wise advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tout le monde écoutait le sage du village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone listened to the wise person of the village.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces enfants sont très sages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These children are very well-behaved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avec l’âge, on acquiert souvent plus de sagesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With age, you often gain more wisdom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son nez saignait depuis dix minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His nose had been bleeding for ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon doigt saigne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My finger is bleeding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes mains saignent à cause du froid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hands are bleeding because of the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La coupure a commencé à saigner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cut started to bleed.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “you’re bleeding” (tu saignes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu saignes ! Appelle un médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re bleeding! Call a doctor.

definitions.note: “vous” form (you plural or formal). Can be present (“you are bleeding”) or an imperative (“bleed!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous saignez beaucoup ; il faut appeler un médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're bleeding a lot; we need to call a doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un repas sain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a healthy meal.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « sain ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette salade est saine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This salad is healthy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il essaie de manger sainement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to eat healthily.

definitions.note: Also used in some fixed expressions (e.g., "Saint-" in place names) and as a title before names (Saint Paul).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un lieu saint pour beaucoup de gens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a holy place for many people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saint Martin est le saint patron de cette église.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Saint Martin is the patron saint of this church.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « saint »; often used in names (e.g., Sainte Marie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une femme sainte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a holy woman.

definitions.note: Used for a female saint; often capitalized as part of a name or title (e.g., Sainte Marie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle prie Sainte Thérèse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prays to Saint Thérèse.

definitions.note: Plural form of « saint » (a holy person recognized by the Church).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette église, on prie souvent les saints.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this church, people often pray to the saints.

definitions.note: Often used with a following clause (e.g., “Je sais que…” = “I know that…”). It can look like English “says,” but it does not mean that.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sais que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know that you’re right.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was my savior when I got lost in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chat est sauvé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is saved.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « sauver » (also used with « être » in compound tenses or as an adjective).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were rescued by the firefighters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants sont enfin sauvés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are finally saved.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you formal/plural).

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « savoir » (to know).

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « savoir » (used for past ongoing/habitual states like knowing).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knew that you were right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il savait la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knew the answer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « savoir » (used for an ongoing/past habitual state of knowing).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knew the answer.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone with a lot of knowledge, especially in a particular field.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a respected scholar in his field.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils savent la réponse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They know the answer.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of « savoir » (used with « ils/elles »).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette glace a une saveur de vanille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ice cream has a vanilla flavor.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present form; also used for formal singular “you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous savez où il habite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You know where he lives.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense of "savoir" (used with "vous").

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous) of "savoir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous saviez que le musée était fermé.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense ("we" form) of "savoir".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We knew the answer.

definitions.note: Used mostly in formal contexts; for everyday “knowledge” you often hear "connaissance(s)".

definitions.note: used for knowing facts or information

definitions.note: used before another verb

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me lave les mains avec du savon.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can speak a little French.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play the saxophone in a band.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses propos sont scandaleux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His remarks are scandalous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un scanner pour numériser mes documents.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like science, especially biology.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used for school subjects or academic fields (e.g., the sciences).

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists study the climate.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: School activities start at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist got an exclusive about the election.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a points total in a game or sport.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s the score?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des scorpions dans le désert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are scorpions in the desert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu me passer le scotch, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the tape, please?

definitions.note: Usually refers to a member of the Scout movement (often a Boy Scout) in French.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother has been a Boy Scout for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film a des scènes très émouvantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie has very moving scenes.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned or literary; can be used jokingly.

definitions.note: Plural of « sein » (breast).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed tired after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sembles fatigué aujourd’hui.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel that you are tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sens une bonne odeur dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smell a nice smell in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai eu une sensation étrange en entrant dans cette maison.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong enthusiasm (similar to “fantastic!”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These plants are sensitive to the cold.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « sentir » (used for ongoing/past habitual actions).

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « sentir » (used for ongoing/past habitual actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sentais le café et je trouvais ça délicieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tasted the coffee and I found it delicious.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « sentir »; can also mean “felt” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuisine sentait bon quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen smelled good when I arrived.

definitions.note: Present participle of « sentir »; often used after « en » to mean “by/while smelling.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En sentant le café, je me réveille tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By smelling the coffee, I wake up right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je comprends cette sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understand this sentence.

definitions.note: Usually used about something giving off a smell; it can be good or bad depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces fleurs sentent bon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These flowers smell good.

definitions.note: Used with "tu" (informal "you"); present tense of "sentir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu te sentes mieux aujourd’hui ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel better today?

definitions.note: Present tense form of "sentir" used with "vous" (you) or as a polite/formal command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous sentez le café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you smell the coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai senti une grande joie en la voyant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great joy when I saw her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai senti l’odeur du café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smelled the smell of coffee.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle, often used with « se sentir » (to feel) in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s’est sentie mieux après le repos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt better after resting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle; can agree with a feminine direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est l’odeur qu’elle a sentie dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the smell that she smelled in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On suit un sentier dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow a trail in the forest.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (vous) of « sentir »; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity (e.g. « Il fallait que… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous sentiez la différence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to feel the difference.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai un mauvais sentiment à propos de cette situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a bad feeling about this situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des sentiments pour toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have feelings for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais enfant, nous sentions la peur avant même d'entrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, we felt fear even before going in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans la cuisine, nous sentions l'odeur du pain chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the kitchen, we smelled the scent of warm bread.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: sentir quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux sentir une odeur de fumée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can smell a smell of smoke.

definitions.native: to smell (to give off an odor)
definitions.note: Used without an object or with a complement: Ça sent… / Ça sent bon/mauvais.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette pièce va sentir le renfermé si on n’aère pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room will smell musty if we don’t air it out.

definitions.note: Used with a noun: sentir une douleur, sentir le froid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la course, je vais sentir une douleur dans les jambes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, I’m going to feel pain in my legs.

definitions.note: Used with an emotion or clause: sentir la peur; sentir que…
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je commence à sentir que quelque chose ne va pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m starting to feel that something is wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sentiras la différence demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will feel the difference tomorrow.

definitions.note: future tense (vous form): either noticing an odor or smelling something intentionally, depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous sentirez tout de suite l’odeur du café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will smell the coffee right away.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu) form of "sentir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sentis une bonne odeur de café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You smell a nice coffee scent.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) of « sentir »; in everyday speech you usually use « a senti » instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sentit une douleur dans le dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a pain in his back.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) of « sentir »; in everyday speech you usually use « a senti » instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle sentit la fumée dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She smelled smoke in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai sept ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am seven years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon anniversaire est en septembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in September.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est mon septième jour de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my seventh day of work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sera arrivé avant nous.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will have arrived before us.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect (futur antérieur) with verbs that take « être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je serai arrivé à midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will have arrived at noon.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary in the conditional to form the conditional perfect (like English “would have” + past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans la pluie, ils seraient partis plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without the rain, they would have left earlier.

definitions.note: Conditional, 1st or 2nd person singular (je/tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je serais très content de t’aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would be very happy to help you.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary verb « être » to form the conditional perfect (e.g., with certain intransitive/reflexive verbs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il serait parti plus tôt si tu l’avais appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would have left earlier if you had called him.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary verb être in the futur antérieur (future perfect), with a past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu seras parti avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will have left before noon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Malgré la pluie, il est resté serein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the rain, he stayed calm.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense of "être".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous serez prêts demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will be ready tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon cousin est sergent dans l’armée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin is a sergeant in the army.

definitions.note: Used with “vous” (you plural or formal) in the conditional mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous seriez surpris de voir combien de temps ça prend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would be surprised to see how long it takes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous serions partis plus tôt, mais il pleuvait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have left earlier, but it was raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a prêté serment devant le juge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took an oath in front of the judge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prêtre a donné un sermon après la lecture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest gave a sermon after the reading.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nous) future tense of « être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous serons prêts à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will be ready at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Third-person plural ("they") in the future tense of être.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils seront prêts demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will be ready tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a peur du serpent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is afraid of the snake.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that winds like a snake (e.g., a road or river).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La route serpente dans la montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road winds through the mountain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des serpents dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are snakes in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai nettoyé la cuisine avec une serpillière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the kitchen with a mop.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form of « serrer », often used in writing rather than everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il serra les dents et ne dit rien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He clenched his teeth and didn’t say anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous faisons pousser des tomates dans la serre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We grow tomatoes in the greenhouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il serre la main de son ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He squeezes his friend's hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va serrer ma main très fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to squeeze my hand very tightly.

definitions.native: to tighten (a screw, a bolt, a strap)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dois serrer la vis pour que ça tienne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to tighten the screw so it holds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle vient serrer son enfant contre elle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She comes to hold her child tight against her.

definitions.native: to press together; to pack closely
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut serrer les livres sur l’étagère pour faire de la place.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to pack the books together on the shelf to make space.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mécanicien va serrer la pièce dans l’étau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mechanic is going to clamp the part in the vise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les tomates poussent dans les serres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomatoes grow in the greenhouses.

definitions.note: Commonly means “you tighten/you squeeze” (with tu), and it can also appear after que in the subjunctive (e.g., « que tu serres… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu serres la main de ton ami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You squeeze your friend's hand.

definitions.note: Also used as the formal (vous) command form, and as the present tense form for "vous".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Serrez bien le bouchon, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tighten the cap well, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La serrure de la porte est cassée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lock on the door is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons changé les serrures de la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We changed the locks on the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai appelé un serrurier pour ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called a locksmith to open the door.

definitions.note: Past participle of « serrer »; often used with « avoir » (j'ai serré…) or as an adjective meaning “tight.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai serré la main du médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shook the doctor’s hand tightly.

definitions.note: Often used for clothing or something close-fitting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce pantalon est trop serré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These pants are too tight.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est très serrée à la taille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very tight at the waist.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont serrés dans le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are packed tightly together on the subway.

definitions.note: Usually the present tense form with « tu » (you): « tu sers » = « you serve ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sers le dîner à 19 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You serve dinner at 7 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette clé sert à ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This key is used to open the door.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il servait le dîner quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was serving dinner when I arrived.

definitions.note: Feminine form of « servant ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La servante travaille dans une grande maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maid works in a big house.

definitions.note: Feminine form; can sound old-fashioned depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La servante apporte le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maid brings the coffee.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after « il faut que », « je veux que »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je serve le dîner à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to serve dinner at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils servent le dîner à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They serve dinner at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le serveur apporte l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter brings the bill.

definitions.note: Often used for a computer/server (IT).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le site est en panne : le serveur ne répond pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The website is down: the server isn’t responding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les serveurs apportent les plats à table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiters bring the dishes to the table.

definitions.note: Usually refers to computer/network servers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les serveurs du site sont en maintenance ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The website's servers are under maintenance tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La serveuse apporte l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waitress brings the bill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La serveuse nous apporte l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waitress brings us the bill.

definitions.note: Plural form of "serveuse" (female).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les serveuses sont très sympathiques dans ce café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waitresses are very friendly in this café.

definitions.note: Used with “vous” (you formal / you plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous servez le café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you serving the coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai servi le dîner à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I served dinner at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: More common in the negative: « pas très serviable » (“not very helpful”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le voisin est très serviable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbor is very helpful.

definitions.note: Often used for customer service or a service provided; also used in restaurants for “service” (the act of serving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le service est inclus dans l’addition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Service is included in the bill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise propose des services en ligne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company offers online services.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the past participle of « servir » (e.g., with « être » or to agree with a feminine direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La soupe est servie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is served.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu me passer une serviette, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me a napkin, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai oublié ma serviette à la piscine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my towel at the pool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pouvez-vous apporter des serviettes, s’il vous plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring napkins, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des serviettes propres dans la salle de bains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are clean towels in the bathroom.

definitions.note: Often used for serving food/drinks, or for being useful (e.g., « Ça sert à… » = “It’s used for…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je peux vous servir un café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I serve you a coffee?

definitions.note: Third-person singular simple future of « servir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce restaurant servira le dîner à 19 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant will serve dinner at 7 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça servirait à quoi de partir maintenant ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would be the point of leaving now?

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form of « servir » (literary; often replaced by passé composé in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je servis le dîner à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I served dinner at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past tense) of « servir »; in everyday speech, French usually uses « a servi » instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le serveur servit le café en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter served the coffee in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le serviteur apporte le thé à la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The servant brings the tea to the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les serviteurs apportent le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The servants bring dinner.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous servons le dîner à sept heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We serve dinner at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: used before plural nouns; in French, this agrees with the thing possessed, not the owner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle cherche ses clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is looking for her keys.

definitions.note: Often used for a class, meeting, or a period of work (e.g., a training session).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La session commence à 9 heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The session starts at 9 o’clock.

definitions.note: Most commonly used for a tennis set (and sometimes other sports).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nadal a gagné le premier set.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nadal won the first set.

definitions.note: Often used literally (door threshold) and figuratively (a minimum level or limit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit dépasse le seuil acceptable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise exceeds the acceptable threshold.

definitions.note: After the verb, it often means "alone."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il se sent seul ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels alone tonight.

definitions.note: Before a noun, it often means "only."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est le seul café ouvert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's the only café open.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « seul ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est seule à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is alone at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux seulement un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only want a coffee.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « seul ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont seules à la maison ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are alone at home tonight.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "seul"; agrees with a plural masculine noun or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont seuls à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are alone at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sexe est encore un sujet tabou pour certaines personnes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sex is still a taboo subject for some people.

definitions.note: Used especially in official/administrative contexts to refer to the category recorded on documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veuillez indiquer votre sexe sur le formulaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please indicate your gender on the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On parle de sexualité à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: People talk about sexuality at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’éducation sexuelle est importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sex education is important.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “sexuel.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une relation sexuelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sexual relationship.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ne sont pas sexuellement compatibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are not sexually compatible.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “sexuel”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces photos contiennent des contenus sexuelles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These photos contain sexual content.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont des rapports sexuels protégés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have protected sexual intercourse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est très sexy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very sexy.

definitions.note: Spanish form of address used for a man; used in French mainly when referring to Spanish-speaking contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bonjour, señor García.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello, Mr. García.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un shampoing pour cheveux secs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a shampoo for dry hair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’achète un shampooing doux pour les cheveux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying a gentle shampoo for my hair.

definitions.note: Used to chase someone or something away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sho ! Va-t'en !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shoo! Go away!

definitions.note: Commonly used in French as an English loanword, especially in the expression « faire du shopping ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On fait du shopping samedi après-midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going shopping on Saturday afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mets un short en été.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wear shorts in the summer.

definitions.note: Informal; English loanword, used for a small serving of strong alcohol.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a bu un shot de tequila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drank a shot of tequila.

definitions.note: Common loanword in French, especially for an entertainment performance (music, TV, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le show commence à 20 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The show starts at 8 p.m.

definitions.note: Used for the (often American) law-enforcement role; in French it can also refer to a traditional “sherif” (a Muslim leader) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce western, le shérif protège la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this western, the sheriff protects the town.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est si fatigué ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is so tired tonight.

definitions.note: used to contradict a negative question or statement
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu n'as pas faim ? — Si, j'ai faim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aren't you hungry? — Yes, I am hungry.

definitions.note: Used to contradict a negative statement or question (e.g., “You didn’t go?” “Si, I did.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu n’aimes pas le café ? — Si, j’aime ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — You don’t like coffee? — Yes, I do.

definitions.note: In French fixed-do solfège, « si » is the note B (equivalent to « ti » in some English-speaking systems).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le morceau commence sur un si.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The piece starts on a B.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne sais pas si elle vient ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know whether she's coming tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tu as le temps, on peut se voir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time, we can see each other tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to contradict a negative question or statement (answering “yes” when the question is negative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu n’aimes pas le café ? — Si, j’adore ça.
