definitions.note: Often used for the remaining balance in a bank account or what is left to pay.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le solde de mon compte est de 50 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balance of my account is 50 euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le soleil brille aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun is shining today.

definitions.note: Often used with "être solidaire de" (to support someone / stand with someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis solidaire de mes collègues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in solidarity with my coworkers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’inondation, la solidarité du quartier a aidé les familles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flood, the neighborhood’s solidarity helped the families.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette table est solide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table is solid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaises sont solides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These chairs are solid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis son déménagement, il est un peu solitaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since his move, he’s a bit lonely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après son déménagement, il a ressenti une grande solitude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After his move, he felt great loneliness.

definitions.note: Often refers to being alone in a calm, chosen way (not necessarily feeling lonely).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle aime la solitude pour lire et réfléchir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes solitude to read and think.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il joue un solo de guitare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plays a guitar solo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les sols de cette maison sont en bois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floors in this house are wooden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons trouvé une solution au problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found a solution to the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous cherchons des solutions simples.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are looking for simple solutions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette forêt, il fait sombre même en plein jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this forest, it’s dark even in broad daylight.

definitions.note: Often used literally (a ship sinking) or figuratively (e.g., sinking into despair).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau va sombrer pendant la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat is going to sink during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après cette mauvaise nouvelle, il va sombrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After that bad news, he is going to collapse.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils portent des vêtements sombres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wearing dark clothes.

definitions.note: Past participle of « sombrer »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « a sombré »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau a sombré pendant la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat sank during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La somme est trop élevée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The total amount is too high.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin de sommeil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sommeille sur le canapé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dozing on the couch.

definitions.note: Used with “nous” (1st person plural) as the present tense of “être” (“to be”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes prêts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons atteint le sommet de la montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached the summit of the mountain.

definitions.note: Used for a high-level official meeting, especially between leaders.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chefs d’État se retrouvent pour un sommet international.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Heads of state are meeting for an international summit.

definitions.note: Describes someone who sleepwalks; can also be used as a noun meaning “sleepwalker.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il était enfant, il était somnambule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was a child, he was sleepwalking.

definitions.note: Used before a singular noun; it agrees with the thing possessed, not the owner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle cherche son sac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is looking for her bag.

definitions.note: Not to be confused with English “son” (male child).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’entends un son bizarre dans la cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear a strange sound in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used for opinion polls (e.g., in politics or the media).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selon un sondage, la plupart des Français sont favorables à cette mesure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to a poll, most French people are in favor of this measure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin utilise une sonde pour examiner l’estomac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor uses a probe to examine the stomach.

definitions.note: Used for measuring/exploring (for example, the depth of water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont fait une sonde pour mesurer la profondeur du lac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took a sounding to measure the depth of the lake.

definitions.note: Somewhat literary/poetic; in everyday French, "rêve" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait un songe étrange cette nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a strange dream last night.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" ("songer à") to mean "to think about / consider"; can also mean "to dream of" in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je songe à changer de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm thinking about changing jobs.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (songer à) meaning "to think about / consider".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je songe à changer de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm thinking about changing jobs.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary; often used with "à" ("songer à" = to think about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu songes à changer de travail ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you thinking about changing jobs?

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « songez à… » (“think about…”) and can sound slightly formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Songez à prendre votre passeport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think about bringing your passport.

definitions.note: Past participle of « songer », often used with « avoir » (e.g., « j’ai songé à… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai songé à toi toute la journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about you all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mainly in written storytelling; in conversation you usually use “a sonné”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À midi, la cloche sonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At noon, the bell rang.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le téléphone sonnait quand je suis entré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone was ringing when I came in.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; used to describe how something sounded in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa voix sonnait étrange au téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His voice sounded strange on the phone.

definitions.note: Often used for phones, doorbells, and alarms (e.g., « Le téléphone sonne. »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le téléphone sonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is ringing.

definitions.note: Used for bells, phones, alarms, doorbells, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le téléphone va sonner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is going to ring.

definitions.note: Often refers to the sound of a bell/phone, or the ringtone/alert sound on a phone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai changé la sonnerie de mon téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my phone’s ringtone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai entendu la sonnette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard the doorbell.

definitions.note: Usually used to mean “ring (a bell/doorbell/phone)” or “sound” (an alarm, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sonnez à la porte, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ring the doorbell, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « sonner » (used with « avoir »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le téléphone a sonné toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone rang all night.

definitions.note: This form is not standard French; it looks like a typo for « sonne » (from « sonner », “to ring”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le message, il a écrit « mon téléphone sonr ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the message, he wrote “my phone rings.”

definitions.note: Plural of « son ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’entends des sons étranges dans la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear strange sounds at night.

definitions.note: Plural of « son » (the outer layer of grain, used in food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange des céréales avec des sons de blé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat cereal with wheat bran.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary to form compound tenses with some verbs
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont déjà arrivés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have already arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un restaurant très sophistiqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very sophisticated restaurant.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une solution sophistiquée, mais facile à utiliser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sophisticated solution, but easy to use.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce conte, la sorcellerie transforme les gens en animaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this tale, witchcraft turns people into animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sorcier lance un sort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wizard casts a spell.

definitions.note: Usually spelled with an accent: « sorcière ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le conte, la sorciere vit seule dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the witch lives alone in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural of « sorcier » (male wizards).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les sorciers préparent une potion magique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wizards are preparing a magic potion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le conte, la sorcière habite dans la forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the witch lives in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On raconte qu’il y a des sorcières dans cette forêt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: People say there are witches in this forest.

definitions.native: go out, come out, get out, leave
definitions.note: Present tense form of « sortir » (e.g., « je sors », « tu sors »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sors ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going out tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est le sort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's fate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sort de la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaves the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je sortais). Often describes an ongoing or habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sortais de l’école quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was leaving the school when it started to rain.

definitions.native: was going out, was coming out
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « sortir » (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sortait tous les soirs après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was going out every evening after dinner.

definitions.note: Present participle of « sortir »; often means “while leaving/going out,” or can describe someone/something that is leaving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu sortant du métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him leaving the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle sorte de musique tu aimes ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of music do you like?

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of « sortir », often used after expressions like « il faut que » (it’s necessary that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je sorte maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to leave now.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural of « sortir » (they go out/come out/leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sortent de la maison à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il existe plusieurs sortes de fromages en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several kinds of cheeses in France.

definitions.note: Can be used with « tu » (informal ‘you’) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sortes ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going out tonight?

definitions.note: Present tense form of “sortir” for “vous” (you plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sortez, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go out.

definitions.note: Past participle of « sortir »; often used with « être » for going out/leaving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est sorti à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went out at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Past participle of « sortir »; can be used with « avoir » when « sortir » takes a direct object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai sorti la poubelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took out the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sortie est à droite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exit is on the right.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a planned activity outside (with friends, class, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On fait une sortie au musée demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going on an outing to the museum tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « sortir » (used with être in compound tenses). Not the same as the English noun “sortie”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est sortie à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went out at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Plural form of « sortie ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous faisons souvent des sorties le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We often go on outings on the weekend.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of « sortir » (used with « être », or to agree with a feminine plural direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont sorties hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went out last night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, used with "vous" (you plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il pleuvait, vous ne sortiez pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it was raining, you weren’t going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sorcière lance un sortilège sur le château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witch casts a spell on the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sorcier a lancé des sortilèges sur le château.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wizard cast spells on the castle.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 1st person plural (nous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il pleuvait, nous ne sortions pas le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it was raining, we didn’t go out in the evening.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "to get out of" a place (e.g. "sortir de la maison").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais sortir ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go out tonight.

definitions.native: will go out, will come out, will leave
definitions.note: Future tense (third-person singular): “he/she/it will …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sortira ce soir avec ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will go out tonight with his friends.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of « sortir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je sortirai après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will go out after work.

definitions.note: Simple future, 2nd person singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sortiras ce soir avec tes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will go out tonight with your friends.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past) for “they went out/left”; in everyday speech you usually use “ils/elles sont sortis(es)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le dîner, ils sortirent dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, they went out into the garden.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) future tense form of "sortir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous sortirez après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will go out after dinner.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural), often used with « être » in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont sortis à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went out at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: past simple (passé simple), 2nd person singular; mainly found in literature
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu sortis du cinéma en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the movie theater in silence.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in writing (stories, books) rather than everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sortit de la maison sans faire de bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went out of the house without making a sound.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present ("nous"); often used as a suggestion/command (imperative "Let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sortons un peu prendre l’air.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go out for a bit to get some fresh air.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « contrarier les sorts » (to thwart fate) or « les sorts en sont jetés » (the die is cast). Not the same as English “sorts” = “kinds/types”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont connu des sorts très différents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They experienced very different fates.

definitions.note: In the sense of magic/witchcraft; not the same as English “sorts” = “kinds/types”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sorcière a lancé plusieurs sorts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witch cast several spells.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who looks very similar to another person (a celebrity's look-alike, for example).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a croisé le sosie de Brad Pitt dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ran into a Brad Pitt look-alike on the street.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or behavior in a mildly insulting way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était sot de dire ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was silly to say that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de dire des sottises !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop saying nonsense!

definitions.note: An old French coin; today it’s mostly used in set phrases like « ne pas avoir un sou » (“not to have a penny”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas un sou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have a penny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas de souci pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not worried about tomorrow.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in the reflexive form: « se soucier de » = to worry about, to care about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me soucie de toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worry about you.

definitions.note: Most often used in the reflexive form: « se soucier de » = to care about / to worry about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu ne dois pas te soucier de ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don't have to worry about that.

definitions.note: Usually used in the reflexive form: « se soucier de » (to worry about / care about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu te soucies trop de ce que les autres pensent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You worry too much about what other people think.

definitions.note: Often used with de to mean “concerned about.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est soucieux de son avenir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is worried about his future.

definitions.note: Plural of « souci ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai pas de soucis en ce moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any worries right now.

definitions.note: Usually the small dish that goes under a cup.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pose la tasse sur la soucoupe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the cup on the saucer.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like « tout à coup » or « soudainement » for “suddenly.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un silence soudain est tombé dans la salle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A sudden silence fell over the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soudain, il s’est mis à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, it started to rain.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "soudain".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa colère était soudaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her anger was sudden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soudainement, il s'est mis à pleuvoir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, it started to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le soudeur porte un masque de protection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The welder wears a protective mask.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont essayé de soudoyer le fonctionnaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to bribe the official.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a beaucoup souffert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffered a lot.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple) of « souffler » (he/she/it blew); common in books and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vent souffla toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind blew all night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vent soufflait très fort hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind was blowing very hard last night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; can be used for blowing out candles, etc., in an ongoing/repeated past context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il soufflait les bougies quand tout le monde a applaudi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was blowing out the candles when everyone applauded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin de reprendre mon souffle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to catch my breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je souffle sur la soupe pour la refroidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I blow on the soup to cool it down.

definitions.note: Used for blowing air (wind, breathing out, blowing on something) and for blowing out (a candle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vent va souffler très fort aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind is going to blow very strongly today.

definitions.note: Past participle of « souffler » (to blow). Don’t confuse with the noun « un soufflé » (a type of baked dish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a soufflé sur la soupe pour la refroidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He blew on the soup to cool it down.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il souffrait depuis des semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was suffering for weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a vécu beaucoup de souffrance après l'accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went through a lot of suffering after the accident.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses souffrances ont duré des années.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His suffering lasted for years.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone is not feeling well (health-related).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne viens pas travailler aujourd'hui : je suis souffrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not coming to work today: I’m unwell.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’accident, elle était encore souffrante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, she was still suffering (in pain).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je souffre depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been suffering since yesterday.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « souffrir » used with « ils/elles » (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils souffrent beaucoup après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are suffering a lot after the accident.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « souffrir » used with « tu » (informal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu souffres encore ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you still suffering?

definitions.note: Usually used with “vous” (formal singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous souffrez encore ?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed the online course.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « suivre » (often used with « être » in the passive, or as an adjective meaning “monitored/followed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est suivie par un médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is monitored by a doctor.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural masculine) of « suivre »; used with auxiliary verbs (e.g., « sont/ont »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves sont suivis par une tutrice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are followed/monitored by a tutor.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form of « suivre » for « je » or « tu »; mainly used in written/literary French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suivis le guide jusqu'au musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed the guide to the museum.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mainly used in written French (e.g., novels, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suivit le guide dans le musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He followed the guide into the museum.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense, used with "nous" (often as an invitation: "let's...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suivons ce chemin jusqu’au village.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s follow this path to the village.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of « suivre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suivra le guide jusqu’au musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will follow the guide to the museum.

definitions.note: First person singular simple future of « suivre » (je suivrai).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suivrai tes conseils.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will follow your advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais suivre le guide jusqu'à la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to follow the guide to the station.

definitions.note: third-person plural future tense of « suivre »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants suivront le professeur en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children will follow the teacher in silence.

definitions.note: Often used with "à" (e.g., "sujet à") to mean "liable/prone to" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce plan est sujet à des changements.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This plan is subject to change.

definitions.note: Commonly used for the topic of a conversation, book, essay, etc.; also for the subject of a sentence (grammar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel est le sujet de ce livre ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the subject of this book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons deux sujets à traiter aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two subjects to deal with today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces sujets reviennent souvent dans nos discussions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These topics come up often in our discussions.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often followed by « à ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est sujette à des migraines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is prone to migraines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il regarde un combat de sumo à la télévision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s watching a sumo match on TV.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial abbreviation of « super ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est sup !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is awesome!

definitions.note: Informal; often used on its own as a positive reaction (like “Great!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ton idée est super !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is great!

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ton idée est super !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is great!

definitions.note: Informal; used to express enthusiasm or approval.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Super ! On a fini plus tôt que prévu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Great! We finished earlier than expected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vue depuis la terrasse est superbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from the terrace is magnificent.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine), used to describe more than one person or thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces fleurs sont superbes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These flowers are superb.

definitions.note: Describes something that lacks depth or is only on the surface (can be about people, comments, knowledge, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son analyse est trop superficielle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His analysis is too superficial.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son analyse est superficielle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her analysis is superficial.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses excuses étaient superficielles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her apologies were superficial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais au supermarché pour acheter du pain et des fruits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the supermarket to buy bread and fruit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlez à votre superviseur si vous avez un problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to your supervisor if you have a problem.

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form; often used in stories and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il supplia le roi de lui pardonner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He begged the king to forgive him.

definitions.note: Often used in a strong or figurative sense (e.g., “c’est un supplice” = “it’s torture”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attendre sans nouvelles, c’est un vrai supplice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Waiting with no news is real torture.

definitions.note: Strong/formal way to ask; often used to express desperation or urgency.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te supplie de m'aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm begging you to help me.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to beg/implore” (not “to supply” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te supplier de m’aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m begging you to help me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a supplié sa mère de le laisser sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He begged his mother to let him go out.

definitions.note: Often used for an additional fee (e.g., un supplément de 5 €).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un supplément de 5 € pour la livraison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an extra charge of €5 for delivery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais une couverture supplémentaire, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like an extra blanket, please.

definitions.note: Plural form; agrees with a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des frais supplémentaires pour les bagages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are additional fees for luggage.

definitions.native: was enduring, was putting up with
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À l'époque, il supportait mal le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the time, he didn’t handle the noise well.

definitions.native: can’t stand, puts up with, supports
definitions.note: Often used to mean “can’t stand / tolerate” (especially with ne...pas), but it can also mean “support” in the sense of helping someone emotionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne supporte pas le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t stand the noise.

definitions.native: to put up with, to tolerate
definitions.note: Commonly used for enduring something unpleasant (e.g., noise, pain, waiting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais supporter le bruit pendant les travaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put up with the noise during the construction work.

definitions.note: Can mean to support someone (emotionally or financially), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te supporter pendant cette période difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to support you during this difficult time.

definitions.native: will support, will tolerate, will put up with
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te supportera i si tu me dis la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will put up with you if you tell me the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu supportes bien le bruit ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you tolerate the noise well?

definitions.note: Second-person plural present ("vous"). Often used for polite singular or for a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supportez-vous le bruit ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you put up with the noise?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suppose que tu as raison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He assumes you're right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une supposition, pas une certitude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an assumption, not a certainty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses suppositions étaient fausses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His assumptions were wrong.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a hypothetical situation; it corresponds to “we suppose/assume” in form, but often translates as “let’s suppose/assume.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supposons qu’il pleuve demain : on restera à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s suppose it rains tomorrow: we’ll stay at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai supposé que tu étais déjà parti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assumed you had already left.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is assumed or claimed, but not certain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un trésor supposé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a supposed treasure.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cause supposée de la panne est une batterie vide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supposed cause of the breakdown is a dead battery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les faits supposés sont difficiles à vérifier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supposed facts are hard to verify.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle supprime le message.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She deletes the message.

definitions.note: Often used for deleting files, messages, accounts, or removing information/content.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais supprimer ce fichier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to delete this file.

definitions.note: Past participle of « supprimer ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le fichier a été supprimé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The file was deleted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une décision suprême.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a supreme decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bureau du directeur est à l’étage supérieur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal’s office is on the upper floor.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons to mean “better” or “superior (to)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce modèle est supérieur à l’ancien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This model is better than the old one.

definitions.note: Used for a person who has authority over you at work or in an organization.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois en parler à mon supérieur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk about it with my superior.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre chambre est au troisième étage, à la fenêtre supérieure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our room is on the third floor, at the upper window.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used for rank, quality, or authority.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a une qualité supérieure à celle des autres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has superior quality compared to the others.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces résultats sont supérieurs à ceux de l’an dernier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These results are better than last year’s.

definitions.note: Plural noun; often used to mean people who have authority over you (e.g., at work).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois en parler à mes supérieurs avant de prendre une décision.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk about it with my superiors before making a decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le livre est sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on the table.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai lu un article sur le climat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read an article about the climate.

definitions.note: Common in Canadian French; in France people usually say allumé(e) instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La télé est sur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is on.

definitions.note: This form is masculine singular. It comes from the adjective « sûr » (feminine: « sûre »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis sur que c’est la bonne adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sure it’s the right address.

definitions.note: Often used in informal speech instead of « sûr » (with the accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu es sure de toi ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you sure of yourself?

definitions.note: Often spelled "sûrement" in modern French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il viendra surement demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will surely come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais du surf le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go surfing on the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La surface de la table est propre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surface of the table is clean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En été, j’aime surfer tous les week-ends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the summer, I like to surf every weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon frère est surfeur et il va à la plage tous les week-ends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a surfer and he goes to the beach every weekend.

definitions.note: Past participle of « surgir », usually used with « être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est surgi de nulle part.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He popped up out of nowhere.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « surmenage professionnel » (work-related overwork/burnout).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a fait un surmenage et son médecin lui a conseillé de se reposer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a burnout and his doctor advised him to rest.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est surmenée depuis des semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been overworked for weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle doit surmonter sa peur de parler en public.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She must overcome her fear of speaking in public.

definitions.note: Past participle of « surmonter »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « a surmonté »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a surmonté ses peurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcame her fears.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son surnom au lycée était "Léo".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His nickname in high school was “Léo.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette équipe surpasse toutes les autres cette saison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team surpasses all the others this season.

definitions.note: Often used for something physically higher than and above something else (like a cliff or balcony).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le balcon surplombe la mer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balcony overlooks the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin m’a dit que je suis en surpoids.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor told me that I am overweight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un résultat surprenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a surprising result.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa réponse est surprenante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her answer is surprising.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette nouvelle me surprend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news surprises me.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça me surprendrait s’il arrivait à l’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would surprise me if he arrived on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais te surprendre avec une bonne nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to surprise you with some good news.

definitions.native: to catch (someone) off guard; to catch (someone) in the act
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a réussi à surprendre le voleur en train de voler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police managed to catch the thief stealing.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (someone/something you surprise), or in the reflexive form « se surprendre à + infinitive » (“to catch yourself + -ing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me surprends !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You surprise me!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis surpris par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am surprised by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis surpris par cette nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am surprised by this news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça me surprise de te voir ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It surprises me to see you here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a l’air surprise par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looks surprised by the news.

definitions.note: Feminine form (of "surpris").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est surprise par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is surprised by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une surprise pour toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a surprise for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu me surprises toujours avec tes idées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always surprise me with your ideas.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles sont surprises par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are surprised by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai eu quelques surprises cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a few surprises this week.

definitions.note: Past simple (passé simple) form, mostly used in writing/literature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa réponse me surprit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her answer surprised me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va sursauter quand le téléphone va sonner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s going to startle when the phone rings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime les desserts, surtout le chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like desserts, especially chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des caméras de surveillance dans le magasin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are surveillance cameras in the store.

definitions.note: Often used for a staff member in a school who supervises students (e.g., in hallways, during study hall, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le surveillant du collège surveille les élèves dans la cour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school monitor supervises the students in the courtyard.

definitions.native: watches, keeps an eye on, monitors
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle surveille les enfants dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She watches the children in the garden.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of « surveiller » (used with « ils/elles »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils surveillent l'entrée du bâtiment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watch the entrance of the building.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping an eye on someone/something (e.g., a child, a patient, a situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois surveiller les enfants pendant que tu cuisines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to watch the kids while you cook.

definitions.note: Form used with “vous” (formal singular or plural) and for giving instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Surveillez les enfants pendant que je cuisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch the children while I cook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est surveillé par la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is being watched by the police.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « surveiller »; often used in the passive with « être » (e.g., « est surveillée »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison est surveillée par une caméra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is monitored by a camera.

definitions.note: Often used for unexpected events or incidents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un accident peut survenir à tout moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An accident can happen at any time.

definitions.note: Past participle of « survenir »; often used with « être » (e.g., « est survenu »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un incident est survenu pendant le cours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An incident occurred during the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l'accident, sa survie dépendait des secours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, his survival depended on the rescue services.

definitions.note: Often used for unexpected events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des problèmes surviennent parfois pendant le voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Problems sometimes happen during the trip.

definitions.note: Often used for unexpected events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un problème survient pendant le voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A problem happens during the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il survit à l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He survives the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a qu’un survivant après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is only one survivor after the accident.

definitions.note: Masculine plural (can also be used for a mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les survivants ont été emmenés à l’hôpital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The survivors were taken to the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans eau, les plantes ne survivent pas longtemps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, plants don’t survive for long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il survivra à cette épreuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will survive this ordeal.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("je") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je survivrai à cette épreuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will survive this ordeal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu survivras à cette épreuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will survive this ordeal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont réussi à survivre à l'accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They managed to survive the accident.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as the polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous survivrez à cette épreuve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will survive this ordeal.

definitions.note: Past participle of « survivre »; used with « avoir » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a survécu à l'accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He survived the accident.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il survécut à l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He survived the accident.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who gets upset or hurt easily.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très susceptible, alors je fais attention à mes mots.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very sensitive, so I’m careful with my words.

definitions.note: Usually followed by « à » + noun or infinitive: « susceptible à … ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce métal est susceptible à la rouille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This metal is susceptible to rust.

definitions.note: Adjective plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont très susceptibles quand on les critique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very sensitive when people criticize them.

definitions.note: Plural form of "sushi" in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons commandé des sushis pour dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered sushi for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son comportement est suspect.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior is suspicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté un suspect.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suspecte qu’il me cache quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspect that he’s hiding something from me.

definitions.note: Plural adjective (masculine or mixed gender).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les résultats sont suspects.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The results are suspicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police interroge deux suspects.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are questioning two suspects.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été suspecté de vol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was suspected of theft.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « suspendre » (also used for figurative meanings like suspending an activity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suspends mon manteau au crochet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hang up my coat on the hook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le match est suspendu à cause de la pluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The match is suspended because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le service est suspendu jusqu’à nouvel ordre.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn’t knock on the door if it’s open.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You knock on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You type your name here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a attrapé la tapette pour tuer la mouche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabbed the fly swatter to kill the fly.
