definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say that: “tapette” is an insult.

definitions.note: Plural of « tapette ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté deux tapettes pour les mouches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two fly swatters for the flies.

definitions.note: Also used as the polite/formal command (vous) form of « taper ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tapez votre mot de passe, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please type your password.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un grand tapis dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big rug in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a tapé à la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knocked on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai tapé le message sur mon ordinateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I typed the message on my computer.

definitions.note: Often used in a friendly way (to joke with someone), but it can also be annoying depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aime taquiner sa sœur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to tease his sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis arrivé tard hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived late last night.

definitions.note: From the verb « tarder »: to take a long time (to do something), to be slow to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça tarde !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s taking a long time!

definitions.native: to delay; to be late (to do something)
definitions.note: Common in « ne pas tarder » (“won’t be long / will be along soon”). Also used as « tarder à + infinitif ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a tardé à répondre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was late to reply.

definitions.native: to take a long time (to do something); to linger
definitions.note: Often with « tarder à + infinitif » to mean something is slow to happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le printemps tarde à arriver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spring is taking a long time to arrive.

definitions.native: to be long (in coming); to not be long (in negative form)
definitions.note: In « ne pas tarder », meaning “soon / any moment now.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ne va pas tarder à rentrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’ll be home soon.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « tardif »; often used in formal contexts (e.g., “late response,” “late diagnosis”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa réponse tardive a retardé le projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His late reply delayed the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel est le tarif pour un aller simple ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the fare for a one-way ticket?

definitions.note: Often refers to an open-faced pie (a tart), but can also be used for some pies depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une tarte aux pommes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having an apple tart.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté deux tartes aux pommes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two apple pies.

definitions.native: slice of bread (with toppings), open-faced sandwich
definitions.note: Often means a slice of bread (usually buttered) with something spread on it (jam, Nutella, cheese, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une tartine de beurre et de confiture au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a slice of bread with butter and jam for breakfast.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; can be insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce mec est complètement taré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That guy is completely crazy.

definitions.note: Informal and often insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne l’écoute pas : c’est un taré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t listen to him: he’s a nutcase.

definitions.note: Informal and often insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des tarés partout sur Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are crazies everywhere on the internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un tas de vêtements sur le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a pile of clothes on the bed.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase « un tas de + noun » (informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a un tas de choses à faire aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a lot of things to do today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je bois un café dans une tasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m drinking a coffee in a cup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons acheté deux tasses pour le café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought two cups for coffee.

definitions.note: informal (often used by children or within the family)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma tata habite à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt lives in Lyon.

definitions.note: Informal, affectionate term for "aunt" (often used by children).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais chez ma tatie ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to my auntie’s this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un tatouage sur le bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a tattoo on her arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a plusieurs tatouages sur le bras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has several tattoos on his arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vivent dans un taudis depuis des années.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been living in a slum for years.

definitions.note: Very informal slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a passé la nuit en taule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spent the night in jail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une taupe a creusé un trou dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A mole dug a hole in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le taureau est dans le pré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bull is in the meadow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des taureaux dans le champ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are bulls in the field.

definitions.note: Often used for things like interest rates, tax rates, unemployment rates, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le taux de chômage a baissé cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The unemployment rate went down this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une taxe sur l’alcool.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a tax on alcohol.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais prendre un taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take a taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de taxis devant la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are lots of taxis in front of the train station.

definitions.note: Informal spelling of “chat” for online messaging.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a eu un long tchat hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a long online chat last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est tchèque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Czech.

definitions.note: Noun for a person; the language is usually called « tchèque » too, but that would be a different entry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est tchèque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Czech.

definitions.note: informal singular object pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te comprends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understand you.

definitions.note: informal singular reflexive pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux te regarder dans le miroir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can look at yourself in the mirror.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le technicien répare l’ordinateur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technician repairs the computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un problème technique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a technical problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il apprend une nouvelle technique de dessin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is learning a new drawing technique.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Techniquement, c’est possible, mais ce sera difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Technically, it’s possible, but it will be difficult.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des questions techniques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are technical questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle apprend de nouvelles techniques de dessin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is learning new drawing techniques.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette technologie rend les téléphones plus rapides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This technology makes phones faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette entreprise propose des solutions technologiques innovantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company offers innovative technological solutions.

definitions.note: Usually takes a direct object (e.g., teindre un tissu, teindre les cheveux).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va teindre ses cheveux en noir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to dye her hair black.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il teint le tissu en bleu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dyes the fabric blue.

definitions.note: Refers to the color/appearance of someone’s skin (especially the face).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un teint pâle aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a pale complexion today.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written French, especially in expressions like « tel quel » or « un tel + noun ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai jamais vu un tel spectacle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have never seen such a show.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases or comparisons (e.g., “tel …, tel …” = “like …, like … / such …, such …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tel père, tel fils.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Like father, like son.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons or to refer to something of that kind; it agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai jamais vu un tel spectacle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen such a show.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "tel"; often used in "une telle..." / "telle que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai jamais vu une telle situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen such a situation.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify an adjective or adverb; can also be used with a verb to mean “so much.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis tellement fatigué aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m so tired today.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « tel »; used before a noun (or in phrases like « de telles… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai jamais vu de telles erreurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen such mistakes.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of « tel »; used before a feminine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De telles erreurs peuvent arriver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such mistakes can happen.

definitions.note: Plural form of « tel »; agrees with a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De tels problèmes arrivent parfois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such problems happen sometimes.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "tel"; agrees with a plural masculine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De tels problèmes sont difficiles à résoudre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such problems are difficult to solve.

definitions.note: Not the same as a religious building (that’s usually "temple").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il s’est cogné la tempe contre la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bumped his temple against the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils visitent un temple ancien en Asie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are visiting an ancient temple in Asia.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont visité plusieurs temples en Asie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They visited several temples in Asia.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal aux temples.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My temples hurt.

definitions.note: Used mainly in music, but also more generally for pace/rhythm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chef d’orchestre ralentit le tempo à la fin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conductor slows the tempo at the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une solution temporaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a temporary solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n'ai pas beaucoup de temps aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have much time today.

definitions.note: Commonly used in expressions like « Quel temps fait-il ? » for “What’s the weather like?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel temps fait-il aujourd'hui ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What's the weather like today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a un tempérament calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a calm temperament.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La température est basse ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperature is low this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les températures vont baisser cette nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperatures are going to drop tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une tempête approche, alors on reste à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A storm is coming, so we’re staying home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les tempêtes sont de plus en plus fortes chaque hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Storms are getting stronger and stronger every winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est tenace et n’abandonne jamais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is tenacious and never gives up.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense ("ils/elles"): often describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils tenaient une pancarte devant l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were holding a sign in front of the school.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « tenir » (je/tu): used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je tenais la porte pendant que tu entrais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was holding the door while you were coming in.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « tenir » (often used for an ongoing past action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tenait la porte ouverte pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was holding the door open for me.

definitions.note: Present participle of « tenir ». Not to be confused with the English word “tenant” (renter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il avançait, tenant une lampe dans la main.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was moving forward, holding a lamp in his hand.

definitions.note: Often used with body parts or objects (e.g., "tendre la main" = to hold out your hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tend la main pour dire bonjour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He holds out his hand to say hello.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; can also be used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous tendez le bras ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you stretching out your arm?

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) of « tendre »; often used in writing instead of « a tendu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tendit la main pour dire bonjour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He held out his hand to say hello.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette viande est très tendre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This meat is very tender.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est très tendre avec ses enfants.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very affectionate with his children.

definitions.note: Often used with body parts or objects (e.g. « tendre la main » = to hold out your hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va tendre la main vers moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to hold out his hand toward me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle lui parle tendrement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks to him tenderly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces légumes sont très tendres après la cuisson.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These vegetables are very tender after cooking.

definitions.note: Often used for physically extending something (a hand, an arm, a piece of fabric, etc.). Not the same as English “to tend” (= take care of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu tends la main pour l’aider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hold out your hand to help him/her.

definitions.note: Past participle of « tendre »; often used with a direct object (e.g., « tendre la main » = to hold out your hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a tendu la main pour dire bonjour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He held out his hand to say hello.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ambiance est tendue ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The atmosphere is tense tonight.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a l’air tendue avant l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looks tense before the exam.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present form of "tenir" (used with "vous").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenez bien le sac, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold the bag tightly, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous): “you were holding/keeping.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous teniez la porte pour moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were holding the door for me.

definitions.note: Used for physically holding something or someone (e.g., « tenir la main de… » = to hold someone’s hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais tenir la main de mon enfant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to hold my child’s hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je joue au tennis le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play tennis on the weekend.

definitions.note: Form of « tenir » used with « nous » (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous tenons la porte ouverte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re holding the door open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a de la tension dans l'équipe aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is tension in the team today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des tensions entre les deux pays.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are tensions between the two countries.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; mainly used in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tenta d’ouvrir la porte, mais elle était verrouillée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to open the door, but it was locked.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; describes an ongoing/repeated attempt in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tentait d'ouvrir la porte, mais elle était bloquée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was trying to open the door, but it was stuck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau est très tentant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is very tempting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa tentative a échoué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His attempt failed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après plusieurs tentatives, il a réussi à ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After several attempts, he managed to open the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On dort dans une tente ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re sleeping in a tent tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tente de résoudre le problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to solve the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais tenter de l'appeler ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to try to call him tonight.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "tenter quelqu'un" / "tenter quelqu'un de faire quelque chose" / "tenter de faire quelque chose"), depending on the structure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau va tenter beaucoup de gens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is going to tempt a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons monté deux tentes près du lac.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put up two tents near the lake.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as a polite singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tentez de le faire aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try to do it today.

definitions.note: Past participle of « tenter »; often used with « être » to mean “to be tempted (to).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai été tenté d’accepter, mais j’ai refusé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was tempted to accept, but I refused.

definitions.note: Often used with « de + infinitive » (e.g., « tenté de faire quelque chose »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis tenté de commander un dessert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tempted to order a dessert.

definitions.note: Past participle of « tenir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai tenu la porte pour toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I held the door for you.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « tenir » (used e.g. in the passive: « est tenue » = “is held”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réunion est tenue dans la salle A.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is held in room A.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'aime bien ta tenue aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like your outfit today.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « tenir »; often used with an auxiliary like « avoir/être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les promesses ont été tenues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The promises were kept.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont tenu leurs engagements : ils les ont tenus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They kept their commitments: they kept them.

definitions.note: Common in the expression « être tenu de + infinitive » (= to be required to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont tenus de respecter les règles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are required to follow the rules.

definitions.note: A type of Mexican distilled alcoholic drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends une tequila, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a tequila, please.

definitions.native: to evade, to dodge the question
definitions.note: Formal; often used when someone avoids giving a clear answer or decision.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de tergiverser et réponds clairement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop evading and answer clearly.

definitions.note: Often used for a word or expression used in a particular context (e.g., a technical term).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne comprends pas ce terme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand this term.

definitions.note: Plural form of "terme".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous sommes d’accord sur les termes du contrat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agree on the terms of the contract.

definitions.note: Passé simple (simple past), mostly used in writing (stories, history) rather than everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il termina son travail avant midi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finished his work before noon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se retrouve à la terminale 2 de l’aéroport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s meet at terminal 2 of the airport.

definitions.note: In France, « la terminale » is the last year of lycée (high school), before the baccalauréat exam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma sœur est en terminale cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is in her final year of high school this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il termine son travail à 18 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finishes his work at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils terminent leurs devoirs avant le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They finish their homework before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois terminer ce travail ce soir.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous traitez ce problème avec sérieux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You handle this problem seriously.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to track down the suspect for three days.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have been tracking down the suspect since this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai beaucoup de travail aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of work today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will work tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les activités universitaires commencent en septembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: University activities start in September.

definitions.note: In France, an « université » is a public higher-education institution; in everyday English you may translate it as “university” or sometimes “college” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle étudie à l’université à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies at the university in Paris.

definitions.note: Masculine plural pronoun form of « un » (feminine: « unes »). Used to mean “some/ones” when replacing a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais prendre des biscuits : j'en veux uns au chocolat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to have some cookies: I want some chocolate ones.

definitions.note: Informal English loanword, often used in expressions like « donner un up » meaning to give someone a boost.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette musique me donne un up.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That music gives me a boost.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « urbain ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une zone urbaine près du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an urban area near the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une urgence : appelez les secours !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an emergency: call the emergency services!

definitions.note: Often used in the plural in French to refer to the hospital ER (service des urgences).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été emmené aux urgences après l’accident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was taken to the emergency room after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est urgent, je dois partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s urgent; I have to leave now.

definitions.note: Plural form (feminine or masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des problèmes urgentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are urgent problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a du sang dans mon urine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is blood in my urine.

definitions.note: A medical/neutral term; in everyday speech, "faire pipi" is often more common (especially with children).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois uriner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pee.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a du sang dans mes urines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is blood in my urine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’usage du téléphone est interdit en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Phone use is forbidden in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les usages de ce produit sont expliqués sur la boîte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The uses of this product are explained on the box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon père travaille dans une usine automobile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father works in a car factory.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle/adjective of « user »; agrees with a masculine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes souliers sont usés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are worn out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est très utile pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very useful for learning French.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces conseils sont très utiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tips are very useful.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), 3rd person singular; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il utilisa une clé pour ouvrir la porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used a key to open the door.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais étudiant, j’utilisait mon ordinateur tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a student, I used my computer every day.

definitions.note: Present participle (often used like “by using …” or “while using …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En utilisant cette application, tu apprendras plus vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By using this app, you will learn faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’utilisation de ce téléphone est très simple.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Using this phone is very simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle utilise son téléphone pour traduire les mots.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She uses her phone to translate words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils utilisent leur téléphone pour traduire ce mot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They use their phone to translate this word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux utiliser mon ordinateur si tu veux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can use my computer if you want.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu utilises cette application tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You use this app every day.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; also used as the polite singular “you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilisez cette application tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Use this app every day.

definitions.note: First-person plural present ("we" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilisons cette application pour apprendre le français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s use this app to learn French.

definitions.note: Past participle of « utiliser ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai utilisé mon téléphone pour appeler un taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used my phone to call a taxi.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « utiliser »; often used in the passive (e.g., « est utilisée »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette méthode est utilisée partout.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is used everywhere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces outils sont déjà utilisés par l’équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tools are already used by the team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne vois pas l’utilité de cette règle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t see the usefulness of this rule.

definitions.note: used to form the near future
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va commencer bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to start soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il va au travail à pied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes to work on foot.

definitions.note: used before an infinitive to form the near future
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va partir demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to leave tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: used as an informal singular command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Va dans ta chambre !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go to your room!

definitions.note: Usually plural in French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je pars en vacances en août.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going on vacation in August.

definitions.note: Often used for housing/rooms/jobs to mean available because nobody is using or occupying it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet appartement est vacant depuis deux mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment has been vacant for two months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y avait un vacarme terrible dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a terrible racket in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai reçu un vaccin contre la grippe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a flu vaccine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On va vacciner les enfants demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to vaccinate the children tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a une vache dans le champ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cow in the field.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for emphasis (similar to “really” or “so” in spoken English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est vachement bon !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s really good!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des vaches dans le champ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are cows in the field.

definitions.note: Often used for something unsteady or about to fall (a person, an object, or even a light/flame).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaise vacille sur le sol inégal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair wobbles on the uneven floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin examine le vagin pendant la consultation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines the vagina during the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ses explications sont vagues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His explanations are vague.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une vague a frappé le bateau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A wave hit the boat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je me souviens vaguement de son nom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I vaguely remember his name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les vagues sont très hautes aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waves are very high today.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form, often used after expressions like « il faut que » or « bien que ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que ça vaille le coup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has to be worth it.

definitions.note: Often used for efforts, hopes, or attempts that don’t succeed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était un effort vain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pointless effort.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed expression « en vain ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai essayé en vain de le joindre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried in vain to reach him.

definitions.note: Simple future (il/elle/on) of « vaincre ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle vaincra ses adversaires demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will defeat her opponents tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle veut vaincre son adversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to defeat her opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le match, il est vaincu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the match, he is defeated.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « vain ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’était une tentative vaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a futile attempt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vainqueur reçoit une médaille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winner receives a medal.

definitions.note: Plural of "vainqueur".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les vainqueurs reçoivent une médaille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winners receive a medal.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont des efforts vains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are futile efforts.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to form the near future (futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais partir dans cinq minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to leave in five minutes.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular of « aller » (je vais).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l’école en bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to school by bus.

definitions.note: Commonly used for large ships (often in a historical or literary context), and also for spacecraft in sci‑fi ("vaisseau spatial").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vaisseau traverse l’océan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship is crossing the ocean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On voit plusieurs vaisseaux au large du port.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can see several ships off the coast near the port.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the dishes/plates/cutlery as a set, or to the task of washing them (faire la vaisselle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je dois faire la vaisselle après le dîner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do the dishes after dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for things like tickets, documents, IDs, coupons, or offers (meaning they can be used and are still in date).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce billet est valable jusqu'à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is valid until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « valoir » (used for value, price, or being worth something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce tableau valait très cher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That painting was very expensive (was worth a lot).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces chaussures valent 80 euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are worth 80 euros.

definitions.note: A male servant, especially in a wealthy household.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valet apporte le manteau du comte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The valet brings the count’s coat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les valets ouvrent la porte aux invités.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The valets open the door for the guests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette bague a une grande valeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ring has great value.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos valeurs sont importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our values are important.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used for numbers, amounts, or worth (e.g., in math, finance, or data).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les valeurs de ce tableau ont changé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The values in this table have changed.

definitions.note: Present tense (vous form) of « valoir »; used to talk about value/price or being worth doing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous valez beaucoup plus que ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are worth much more than that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Votre billet est valide jusqu’à demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your ticket is valid until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait ma valise pour le voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I packed my suitcase for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons deux valises pour le voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two suitcases for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons marché dans la vallée toute la journée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked in the valley all day.

definitions.note: Infinitive form; used to express value or equivalence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce tableau peut valoir très cher, mais je ne sais pas combien il pourrait valoir exactement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting can be worth a lot of money, but I don't know exactly how much it could be worth.

definitions.note: Past participle of "valoir". Often used with "avoir" (e.g., "a valu") or "être" in some expressions (e.g., "a valu la peine").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce vieux vélo a valu cinquante euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That old bike was worth fifty euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, le vampire a peur du soleil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the vampire is afraid of the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les vampires sortent la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the vampires come out at night.

definitions.note: Commonly used in French, borrowed from English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai loué un van pour le week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rented a van for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est vaniteux et parle toujours de ses réussites.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is conceited and always talks about his successes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vantait ses réussites devant tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was bragging about his successes in front of everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle vantait les qualités de ce produit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was praising the qualities of that product.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vante les mérites de ce produit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He praises the merits of this product.

definitions.native: to praise; to extol; to promote
definitions.note: Often used as “vanter + noun” (vanter les mérites de…). Reflexive form: “se vanter de …” = “to boast about …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le guide touristique va vanter les monuments de la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tour guide is going to praise the city’s monuments.

definitions.note: Commonly in the reflexive: “se vanter de …”. Not to be confused with English “vaunt” (rare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il aime se vanter de ses réussites, mais aujourd’hui il préfère vanter le travail de son équipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to boast about his successes, but today he prefers to praise his team’s work.

definitions.note: Informal/modern term (from English) used for vaping and e-cigarettes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les vapes sont interdites dans ce bâtiment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vapes are forbidden in this building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De la vapeur sort de la casserole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Steam is coming out of the pot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais enfant, j’ai eu la varicelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I had chickenpox.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prix varie selon la saison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price varies depending on the season.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette boutique propose une grande variété de thés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shop offers a wide variety of teas.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to form the near future (futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu vas partir maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are going to leave now.

definitions.note: Used with « tu » (informal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu vas à l’école en bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go to school by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un vase pour les fleurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a vase for the flowers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une vaste plaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a vast plain.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something with a lot of space (like a room or apartment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le salon est vaste et lumineux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The living room is spacious and bright.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of « valoir »; used for things being worth a certain amount or being worthwhile.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce tableau vaudra très cher un jour.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting will be worth a lot one day.

definitions.note: Conditional form of « valoir » (often used for advice or hypothetical value).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça vaudrait la peine d’essayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would be worth trying.

definitions.note: Insulting term for a person seen as lazy or worthless.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Arrête de traîner toute la journée, vaurien !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop hanging around all day, you good-for-nothing!

definitions.note: From the verb « valoir »; commonly used with « ça » (e.g., « Ça vaut… »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre vaut dix euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is worth ten euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les vautours tournent au-dessus de la vallée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vultures are circling above the valley.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu vaux beaucoup mieux que ça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are worth much more than that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais un sandwich au veau, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a veal sandwich, please.

definitions.note: Often used for a leading performer or the most famous person in a show or event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est la vedette du film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is the star of the movie.

definitions.note: Used for a small boat, often in a military or police context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une vedette de la police surveille le port.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A police patrol boat is watching the harbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont les vedettes du cinéma français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are the stars of French cinema.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « la veille » (the day before) or « la veille de + date/event » (the eve of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis arrivé la veille du mariage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived the day before the wedding.

definitions.note: Verb form of « veiller » (e.g., « je veille », « il/elle veille »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veille sur les enfants pendant que tu cuisines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch over the children while you cook.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of staying awake to watch over someone/something or to remain vigilant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais veiller sur les enfants ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to watch over the children tonight.

definitions.native: will watch over, will stay awake
definitions.note: Often used with "sur" (veiller sur) to mean "to watch over" someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veillerai sur les enfants ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will watch over the children tonight.

definitions.note: Polite instruction (often in signs, announcements, customer service). Usually followed by an infinitive or by “à + infinitive”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veillez à éteindre votre téléphone, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please make sure to turn off your phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a veillé sur son petit frère toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watched over his little brother all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai veillé jusqu’à minuit pour finir mes devoirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed up until midnight to finish my homework.

definitions.note: Informal; often used like “lucky guy.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel veinard, tu as gagné deux billets !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You lucky guy, you won two tickets!

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes vraiment des veinards !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re really lucky!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le médecin cherche une veine pour faire la prise de sang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is looking for a vein to do the blood test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai des veines très visibles sur les mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have very visible veins on my hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime le velours de cette veste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the velvet of this jacket.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ils/elles): used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past or background description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils venaient tous les jours après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They used to come every day after school.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « venir » (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je venais te voir après le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was coming to see you after work.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « venir »; often describes an ongoing or habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il venait tous les dimanches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came every Sunday.

definitions.note: Present participle of « venir »; often used to mean “coming from …” in phrases like « venant de … ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venant de Paris, elle arrive ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Coming from Paris, she arrives tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vend sa voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sells his car.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (je/tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vendais des légumes au marché le samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to sell vegetables at the market on Saturdays.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vendait des légumes au marché tous les samedis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was selling vegetables at the market every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vendent des fruits au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell fruit at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vendeur m’a aidé à choisir un téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesperson helped me choose a phone.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with « vous » (formal singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vendez des légumes au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sell vegetables at the market.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense (“we sell”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous vendons des fruits au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sell fruit at the market.

definitions.note: Simple future, 3rd person singular (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle vendra sa voiture demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will sell her car tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux vendre ma voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell my car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On se voit vendredi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Friday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je travaille tous les vendredis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work every Friday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will live in Paris next year.

definitions.note: Simple future (futur simple), 1st person singular: “I will live.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to live in France.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) in the simple future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je bois un vodka avec du jus d’orange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m drinking a vodka with orange juice.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "mes vœux" (best wishes) or "faire un voeu" (to make a wish).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make a wish for your birthday.

definitions.note: Plural of « vœu »; often used in set phrases like « meilleurs voeux » (best wishes).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I send you my best wishes for the new year.

definitions.native: here is, here are, this is, these are
definitions.note: Used to introduce or point out something that is present or being presented.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici ton café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your coffee.

definitions.note: Used to present or point to something that is close (often followed by a noun or pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici ton livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your book.

definitions.note: Used to point something out or present something; often followed by a noun or pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici votre reçu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your receipt.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like « voie publique » (public road) or « voie ferrée » (railway track).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the fastest route to get to downtown.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of « voir » (used after expressions like « il faut que », « je veux que », etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que je voie le médecin aujourd'hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to see the doctor today.

definitions.note: Present tense, third-person plural (they) of « voir ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They can see the sea from their room.

definitions.note: Plural of « voie ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These roads are dangerous at night.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form used after expressions like « il faut que… », « je veux que… », « bien que… ».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to see this document before the meeting.

definitions.native: here is, here are; there is, there are; there you go
definitions.note: Used to point out or present someone/something (often written with an accent: « voilà »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: voila ton livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte un voile noir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a black veil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau a une grande voile blanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat has a large white sail.

definitions.native: there you go, here you are
definitions.note: Often used when presenting or handing something to someone, or to indicate that something is done or settled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voilà, c'est prêt !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There you go, it's ready!

definitions.note: used to present or point out someone or something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voilà ton café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your coffee.

definitions.native: there you go, here it is
definitions.note: This is commonly written “voilà” (with a grave accent) in standard French; “voilá” is a misspelling. Used to point something out or to present/show something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: voilá, c’est fini !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There you go, it’s finished!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux voir ce film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see this movie.

definitions.note: Used to correct or strengthen what was just said; often introduces a stronger statement (like “or even”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est gentil, voire généreux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is kind, even generous.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « voir » used with « je » or « tu ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vois la montagne au loin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the mountain in the distance.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it agrees in gender and number (voisine, voisins, voisines).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le village voisin est à dix minutes d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighboring village is ten minutes from here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voisin est très gentil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le voisinage est très calme le soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood is very quiet in the evening.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est la maison voisine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the neighboring house.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "voisin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma voisine est très gentille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) neighbor is very nice.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos maisons sont voisines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our houses are neighboring.

definitions.note: feminine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes voisines sont très gentilles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very nice.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (used with masculine plural nouns, or mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos villages voisins organisent une fête ensemble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our neighboring villages are organizing a festival together.

definitions.note: Plural form of « voisin ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes voisins sont très gentils.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle voit la mer depuis sa fenêtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sees the sea from her window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il voit les photos sur son téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks at the photos on his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’aime ta voix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre vol part à 18 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our flight leaves at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « voler »; mostly used in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'oiseau vola au-dessus de la rivière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird flew over the river.

definitions.note: Literary past tense (passé simple) of « voler »; mostly used in books and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vola mon portefeuille dans le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stole my wallet on the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les oiseaux volaient au-dessus du lac.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were stealing bikes at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’oiseau volait très haut dans le ciel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird was flying very high in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il volait de l’argent dans les sacs des touristes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was stealing money from tourists’ bags.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je tiens le volant à deux mains.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m holding the steering wheel with both hands.

definitions.note: Present participle of « voler ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai vu un oiseau volant au-dessus du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a bird flying over the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une soucoupe volante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a flying saucer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird flies very high.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds fly very high.

definitions.note: Depending on context, « voler » can also mean “to steal.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu voles très haut dans le ciel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re flying very high in the sky.

definitions.note: Usually refers to window shutters.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ferme les volets avant de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I close the shutters before going to sleep.

definitions.note: feminine form of "voleur".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female thief was arrested by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are flying very high today.

definitions.note: Verb form of « voler » for « vous » (present tense or imperative).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t steal in this store.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play volleyball with my friends on Saturdays.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a voluntary choice.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m willing to help tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a volunteer in an organization.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a volontairement ignoré mes messages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deliberately ignored my messages.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These participants are voluntary volunteers to help.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les volontaires aident après la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volunteers help after the storm.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “sure” or “with pleasure” when accepting an offer or invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, gladly!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a la volonté de réussir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has the will to succeed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vols partent à 7 h et à 18 h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our flights leave at 7 a.m. and at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police enquête sur plusieurs vols dans le quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating several thefts in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Often used for the volume of a sound (loudness) or for a book volume.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn the volume down, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’avion a volé toute la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane flew all night.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of "voler" meaning "to steal"; used with an auxiliary verb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a du vomi par terre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is vomit on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw up after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a dû vomir après le trajet en voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to vomit after the car ride.

definitions.note: Past participle of « vomir ». Often written without -s/-e after « avoir » unless a preceding direct object agrees (e.g., « les sandwichs qu’il a vomis »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont les sandwichs qu’il a vomis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the sandwiches he threw up yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand il a mangé trop vite, il vomit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he eats too fast, he vomits.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to form the near future (futur proche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont partir demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to leave tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ils/elles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont à l'école en bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They go to school by bus.

definitions.note: used before plural nouns; can refer to one person formally or to more than one person
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Où sont vos clés ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are your keys?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon vote est secret.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My vote is secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vote à chaque élection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I vote in every election.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils votent pour le nouveau maire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They vote for the new mayor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais voter demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to vote tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les votes seront comptés ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The votes will be counted tonight.

definitions.note: Formal/instruction form (used with “vous”), also used for addressing multiple people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Votez pour votre candidat préféré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vote for your favorite candidate.

definitions.note: used with plural you or formal singular you, before a singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voici votre billet, madame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here is your ticket, ma'am.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai voté aux dernières élections.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I voted in the last election.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular, simple future of « vouloir » (he/she/it will want).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il voudra partir demain matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will want to leave tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'aurai terminé, je voudrai me reposer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I’m finished, I will want to rest.

definitions.note: Conditional, 3rd person plural (ils/elles). Often used for polite requests or to express a wish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils voudraient réserver une table pour ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would like to book a table for this evening.

definitions.note: Conditional form of « vouloir », often used to make requests more polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular conditional of « vouloir » (“he/she/it would like/would want”), often used in reported speech or to express what someone would like under certain conditions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il voudrait un café, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) form; often used for polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voudrez-vous fermer la fenêtre, s’il vous plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you close the window, please?

definitions.note: Conditional form used for polite requests or hypothetical situations (you form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voudriez-vous un café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils voulaient partir plus tôt, mais ils n’ont pas pu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wanted to leave earlier, but they couldn’t.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/habitual): “I wanted” or “I used to want.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voulais te parler hier soir, mais tu étais occupé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to talk to you last night, but you were busy.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « vouloir » (he/she/it wanted, was wanting).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to leave earlier.

definitions.note: Present participle of « vouloir »; often used to mean “wanting to …” or “intending to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voulant partir tôt, il a pris un taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wanting to leave early, he took a taxi.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present (you want). Used with "vous" for either plural "you" or polite/formal singular "you".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous voulez un café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; used with “vous” (you, formal/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous vouliez un café ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense ("nous" form): used for ongoing past situations, habits, or polite requests in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous voulions partir plus tôt, mais il pleuvait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wanted to leave earlier, but it was raining.

definitions.note: Infinitive form; commonly conjugated as je veux, tu veux, il/elle veut, etc.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to want a coffee, please.

definitions.native: to be willing to / to want to (do something)
definitions.note: Often used with another verb in the infinitive: vouloir + infinitif.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to want to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.native: to mean / to intend (in the sense of 'to want to say/do')

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you going to mean by that?

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to learn French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai voulu t’aider, mais je n’ai pas eu le temps.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it often appears in phrases like « non voulu » (“unwanted”).

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular of « vouloir »; mainly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il voulut partir tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to leave right away.

definitions.note: used for more than one person, or as a polite/formal way to address one person
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes prêts pour le voyage ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready for the trip?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon voyage en France a été incroyable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My trip to France was incredible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je voyage souvent pour le travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often travel for work.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to travel by train.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took several trips this year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You travel often in the summer.
