definitions.note: Plural form of « voyageur ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les voyageurs attendent le train sur le quai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The travelers are waiting for the train on the platform.

definitions.note: Present tense (or imperative) form used with “vous” (you, formal/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous voyagez souvent en France.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You travel often in France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a voyagé en Italie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He traveled to Italy.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: “I saw” or “you (singular, informal) saw,” in the sense of “was seeing / used to see.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, je voyais la mer tous les étés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I used to see the sea every summer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of « voir » (3rd person singular: il/elle/on voyait). Used for a habitual action in the past or an ongoing situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, il voyait souvent des lapins dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he often used to see rabbits in the garden.

definitions.note: Present participle of « voir »; often used to mean “upon seeing / when seeing” in context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voyant la pluie, il a pris un parapluie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Seeing the rain, he took an umbrella.

definitions.note: Often used for clothes or colors that really stand out; can have a slightly negative sense (too showy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte une robe voyante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a flashy dress.

definitions.note: Feminine form (a female fortune teller/psychic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La voyante lui a dit qu’il allait changer de travail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fortune teller told him that he was going to change jobs.

definitions.note: Usually used for “you see” (formal/plural) and as an imperative “see!” (formal/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous voyez la tour ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see the tower?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of « voir »; mostly found in formal or literary French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fallait que vous voyiez la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to see the truth.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce what you’re about to check/think about; can also sound like “come on” depending on context and tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voyons ce que ça donne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s see how it turns out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous voyons la mer d’ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can see the sea from here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté un voyou dans la rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a thug in the street.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police a arrêté des voyous près de la gare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested some thugs near the train station.

definitions.note: Agrees in gender and number: vrai (m. sg.), vraie (f. sg.), vrais (m. pl.), vraies (f. pl.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une histoire vraie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a true story.

definitions.note: Used as a noun mainly with an article (e.g., « le vrai » = “the truth / what is true”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dit le vrai, même si c’est difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tells the truth, even if it’s difficult.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "vrai".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une vraie histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a true story.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "vrai"; used with feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont de vraies histoires.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are true stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est vraiment intéressant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's really interesting.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "vrai".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont de vrais amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are true friends.

definitions.note: Past participle of « voir »; used in compound tenses (e.g., « j’ai vu » = “I have seen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vu hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him yesterday.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (often with an article) to mean “considering” or “given.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vu la météo, on reste à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Given the weather, we're staying at home.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of « voir » (used when the past participle agrees with a feminine noun/pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je l’ai vue hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw her yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "avoir une belle vue" (to have a nice view).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depuis la terrasse, la vue est magnifique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From the terrace, the view is magnificent.

definitions.note: Past participle of « voir », feminine plural form (used for agreement, e.g. with a preceding direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai vues hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw them last night.

definitions.note: Often used to describe rude language, manners, or something in bad taste.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je trouve ce commentaire vulgaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find this comment vulgar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sans mot de passe fort, ton compte est vulnérable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without a strong password, your account is vulnerable.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après la tempête, les habitants les plus vulnérables ont reçu de l’aide en premier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the most vulnerable residents received help first.

definitions.note: Past participle of « voir » used with masculine plural objects/subjects (agreement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je les ai vus hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw them yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai vécu à Paris pendant deux ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Paris for two years.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular of « vivre »; mainly used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vécut à Paris pendant dix ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lived in Paris for ten years.

definitions.note: Describes food or a person who avoids all animal products (meat, fish, eggs, dairy, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis végétalien, donc je ne mange pas de viande ni de fromage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm vegan, so I don't eat meat or cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis végétarien, je ne mange pas de viande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m vegetarian; I don’t eat meat.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est végétarienne depuis trois ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been vegetarian for three years.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont végétariens, donc ils ne mangent pas de viande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are vegetarian, so they don't eat meat.

definitions.note: Masculine plural noun (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont végétariens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are vegetarians.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce véhicule est trop grand pour ce garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This vehicle is too big for this garage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a trop de véhicules dans cette rue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many vehicles on this street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l’école à vélo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to school by bike.

definitions.note: Plural of « vélo ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a beaucoup de vélos devant l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of bikes in front of the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce serpent est vénéneux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This snake is venomous.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., discussing whether a statement is true).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je doute de la véracité de cette histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt the truthfulness of that story.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., statements, stories, information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son histoire est véridique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story is true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vérifiais mes e-mails quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was checking my emails when you called.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une vérification des passeports est obligatoire avant l’embarquement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A passport check is mandatory before boarding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vérifie son billet avant d’entrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He checks his ticket before going in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais vérifier l’adresse avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to check the address before leaving.

definitions.note: Form used with "vous" (often a command, but can also be present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vérifiez votre adresse e-mail, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please check your email address.

definitions.note: Past participle of « vérifier »; commonly used with « avoir » in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai vérifié l’adresse avant de partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the address before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est une véritable histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a true story.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize sincerity or certainty; slightly more formal than "vraiment".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis véritablement désolé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am truly sorry.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce sont de véritables amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are real friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est la vérité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a plusieurs vérités dans cette histoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several truths in this story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vétérinaire examine mon chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The veterinarian is examining my dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai acheté un nouveau vêtement pour l’hiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new piece of clothing for the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je range mes vêtements dans l’armoire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put my clothes away in the wardrobe.

definitions.note: More formal/literary than "habiller"; commonly used as "vêtir quelqu’un" (to dress someone) or reflexively "se vêtir" (to get dressed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va se vêtir rapidement avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to get dressed quickly before going out.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal/literary way; common in fixed expressions like « bien vêtu » (well-dressed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est bien vêtu pour l’entretien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is well dressed for the interview.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « vêtu » (often used after « être » or « se trouver »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est vêtue de noir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is dressed in black.

definitions.note: Passé simple (literary past) of « voir » for « nous »; often replaced by « nous avons vu » in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous vîmes la mer au loin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw the sea in the distance.

definitions.note: Possessive pronoun (formal/plural): used with « vous » and stands alone (not before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette place est la vôtre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This seat is yours.

definitions.note: Plural form of the possessive pronoun (refers to more than one thing); formal or plural “your.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces livres sont vôtres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are yours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon vœu, c’est de te revoir bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wish is to see you again soon.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in fixed expressions like « meilleurs vœux » (best wishes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je te présente mes vœux de bonheur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you my wishes for happiness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les wagons sont pleins de voyageurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train cars are full of passengers.

definitions.note: Expresses surprise or admiration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Waouh, c'est incroyable !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that's incredible!

definitions.note: This does not appear to be a common or standard French noun; it may be a name, a borrowing from another language, or a misspelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je ne connais pas le mot « warawara ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know the word “warawara”.

definitions.note: Abbreviation (from “water-closet”); common on signs and in informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les WC sont au fond du couloir, à gauche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restrooms are at the end of the hallway, on the left.

definitions.note: Often also spelled "weekend" in French; both are common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On part à la campagne ce week-end.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the countryside this weekend.

definitions.note: Plural form of « week-end ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous partons souvent à la mer les week-ends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We often go to the seaside on weekends.

definitions.note: Commonly written « week-end » as well; refers to Saturday and Sunday.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On part en weekend avec des amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going away for the weekend with friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je bois un whisky avec des glaçons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m drinking a whiskey with ice cubes.

definitions.note: Used to express surprise, admiration, or excitement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wow, c’est incroyable !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that’s incredible!

definitions.note: Used as a symbol, especially in math, to represent an unknown value or variable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans l’équation, x vaut 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the equation, x equals 3.

definitions.note: replaces a previously mentioned place
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu vas à la bibliothèque ? Oui, j'y vais maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to the library? Yes, I'm going there now.

definitions.note: replaces à + thing(s) or idea(s); often translated as to/about/in it or them in English, and not used for people
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu penses à ton examen ? Oui, j'y pense souvent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you thinking about your exam? Yes, I think about it often.

definitions.note: Very informal spoken form of « il y a » (often written « y a »; here forced as « ya »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya un problème.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a problem.

definitions.note: Informal; common in casual speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu viens ce soir ? — Ya, j’arrive !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tonight? — Yeah, I’m coming!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils louent un yacht pour les vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rent a yacht for the vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mange un yaourt au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat a yogurt for breakfast.

definitions.note: The currency of Japan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le yen est la monnaie du Japon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The yen is the currency of Japan.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai échangé des euros contre des yens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exchanged euros for yen.

definitions.note: Used in English within French (especially informally, e.g. in conversation or text messages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Tu viens ce soir ? — Yes !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tonight? — Yes!

definitions.note: Plural of « œil » (“eye”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai les yeux bleus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have blue eyes.

definitions.note: Informal interjection used to get someone’s attention or greet someone (more common in spoken French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo, tu viens ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yo, are you coming tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je fais du yoga le matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do yoga in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used in an informal, modern way to describe someone’s mood or attitude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le yoga, je me sens très zen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After yoga, I feel very zen.

definitions.note: Very informal (often childlike); can be considered vulgar depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a mal au zizi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His penis hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les zombies attaquent la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the zombies attack the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, les zombies attaquent la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, the zombies attack the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans ce film, des zombis envahissent la ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie, zombies invade the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette zone est interdite au public.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This area is off-limits to the public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a deux zones dans ce parc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two zones in this park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous allons au zoo dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the zoo on Sunday.

definitions.note: A mild exclamation of annoyance or disappointment (like “darn”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zut ! J'ai oublié mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Darn! I forgot my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a zéro message sur mon téléphone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are zero messages on my phone.

definitions.note: A very common preposition; the exact meaning depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l'école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to school.

definitions.note: Common preposition used for destination/location (and often with times).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais á Paris demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to Paris tomorrow.

definitions.native: (non-standard in French) likely intended to be “à” = to, at
definitions.note: In standard French, the correct form is “à” (grave accent). The character “á” (acute accent) is not standard in French and is typically a typo or an encoding/keyboard error.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’écris « á » ici tel quel, mais en français on écrirait « à ».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m writing “á” here as-is, but in French one would write “à”.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel âge as-tu ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How old are you?

definitions.note: Plural of « âge » (age).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les âges des enfants sont indiqués sur le formulaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children's ages are indicated on the form.

definitions.note: Describes a person or animal; often used with "de" + age (e.g., "âgé de 10 ans").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon grand-père est très âgé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is very old.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ma grand-mère est très âgée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother is very elderly.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used for people (and sometimes animals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont âgés de cinquante ans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are fifty years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il croit que son âme est immortelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believes that his soul is immortal.

definitions.note: Plural of « âme ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces âmes généreuses aident les autres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These generous souls help others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’âne mange de l’herbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The donkey is eating grass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des ânes dans le champ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are donkeys in the field.

definitions.note: Informal, very common form of « cela » in everyday French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça ne marche pas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It doesn't work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous entrons dans une nouvelle ère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are entering a new era.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle portait une robe éblouissante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was wearing a dazzling dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a un grand écart entre les deux résultats.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big gap between the two results.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il écarte la chaise pour me laisser passer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moves the chair aside to let me pass.

definitions.note: Command form (plural or formal): said to one person using “vous” or to several people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écartez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please move aside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons eu un échange intéressant en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had an interesting exchange in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’échange mon billet avec toi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exchange my ticket with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On peut échanger nos places si tu veux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can swap seats if you want.

definitions.note: Often used for exchanging goods, services, or information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont échanger des cartes au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to trade cards at the market.

definitions.note: Plural form of « échange ». Often used for exchanging things or for (verbal) exchanges between people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons eu des échanges intéressants pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had interesting exchanges during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous échangions des messages tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were exchanging messages every day.

definitions.note: Used after expressions like « il faut que… » (subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut que nous échangions nos idées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to exchange our ideas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai échangé mon billet contre un autre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exchanged my ticket for another one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons reçu des échantillons gratuits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We received free samples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chat échappe au chien et grimpe dans un arbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat escapes from the dog and climbs into a tree.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” to mean “escape from” or “avoid” something (e.g., échapper à un danger).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog managed to escape from the gardener.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chien s’est échappé du jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog escaped from the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sont échappés pendant la nuit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They escaped during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai oublié mon écharpe à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my scarf at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son projet s’est terminé par un échec.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His project ended in failure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le roi est en échec.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king is in check.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je joue aux échecs avec mon frère le dimanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play chess with my brother on Sundays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il monte sur l’échelle pour changer l’ampoule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbs on the ladder to change the light bulb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai entendu un écho dans la grotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard an echo in the cave.

definitions.note: Past historic (passé simple), 3rd person singular, often used in writing; in everyday speech you usually use the passé composé (a échoué).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau échoua près de la plage.

definitions.note: Used especially for boats/ships that get stuck on sand or rocks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bateau a échoué près de la plage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat ran aground near the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu éclairer ce point, s’il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you clarify this point, please?

definitions.note: Often used for scouting groups (e.g., Boy Scouts).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scouts are going hiking this weekend.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the French pastry.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought chocolate eclairs.

definitions.note: Plural of "éclair" meaning a lightning flash.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw flashes of lightning during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un éclat de lumière a traversé le ciel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A flash of light crossed the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai trouvé un éclat de verre sur le sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a shard of glass on the floor.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), often used in literature and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À ce moment-là, la bombe éclata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that moment, the bomb exploded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ballon éclate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon bursts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ballon va éclater !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon is going to burst!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fire is going to break out in the building.

definitions.note: Usually refers to broken pieces (often of glass, wood, or metal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des éclats de verre par terre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are shards of glass on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like « un éclat de rire ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On a entendu des éclats de rire dans le couloir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard bursts of laughter in the hallway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ballon a éclaté.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon burst.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons regardé une éclipse solaire hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched a solar eclipse yesterday.

definitions.note: Used especially for eggs hatching and flowers blooming; also used figuratively for something appearing or emerging.

definitions.note: Used for eggs hatching (birds, insects, etc.) and for flowers budding/opening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au printemps, les fleurs éclosent dans le jardin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the flowers bloom in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother goes to school at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two schools in this neighborhood.

definitions.note: Describes a person who avoids wasting money or resources.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very thrifty: she always compares prices before buying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’économie du pays se porte bien cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's economy is doing well this year.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural to mean money you have saved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai fait des économies pour acheter une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved up to buy a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La croissance économique est lente cette année.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Economic growth is slow this year.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “good value / not expensive.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is very affordable.

definitions.note: Can mean saving money or conserving resources (like time, energy, water).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saving to buy a new computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essaie d’économiser pour acheter une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to save up to buy a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il porte un kilt écossais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wearing a Scottish kilt.

definitions.note: Often used with time (e.g., « le temps écoulé » = the time elapsed).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over the past year, I learned a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of « écouler », often used with a time period (e.g., weeks, months).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The past weeks have been very busy.

definitions.note: Used mainly to talk about time that has passed (days, weeks, years, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au cours des mois écoulés, nous avons beaucoup appris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over the past months, we have learned a lot.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mostly used in literature; in everyday speech, French usually uses the passé composé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il écouta la chanson en silence.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He listened to the song in silence.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’écoutais la radio quand tu as appelé.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle écoutait la radio quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was listening to the radio when I arrived.

definitions.note: Present participle of « écouter »; often used with « en » to mean “while/by listening.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En écoutant la radio, j’ai appris la nouvelle.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (“Listen!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écoute bien ce que je te dis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Listen carefully to what I’m telling you.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of « écouter » (they listen/are listening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils écoutent la musique dans le salon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are listening to music in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais écouter de la musique dans le bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to listen to music on the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle écoutera la radio ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will listen to the radio tonight.

definitions.note: Often used with “à” before the thing/person you listen to: écouter quelqu’un; écouter à la radio.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il écoutera attentivement ce que tu dis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai oublié mes écouteurs à la maison.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my earphones at home.

definitions.note: Formal or plural command (“Listen!” to one person you address as vous, or to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écoutez bien : le train part à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Listen carefully: the train leaves at eight o'clock.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (vous form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous écoutiez la radio tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were listening to the radio every morning.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present (used with “nous”, often as a suggestion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Écoutons la chanson jusqu'à la fin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s listen to the song until the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai écouté de la musique toute la soirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened to music all evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je regarde un film sur l’écran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m watching a movie on the screen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaleur est écrasante aujourd’hui.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais écraser la canette avec mon pied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai écrasé le papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crushed the paper.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tomato is crushed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons mangé des écrevisses au dîner.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (il/elle/on) in the future tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He writes a letter to his friend.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a message yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une confirmation écrite.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettre est écrite en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter is written in French.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the past participle of « écrire »; often used with « être » or to agree with a preceding direct object.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letters they wrote are very moving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les messages sont écrits en français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The messages are written in French.

definitions.note: plural form

definitions.native: to develop; to draw up; to work out (a plan/idea)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must draw up a plan to reduce expenses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Canada, you can see a moose in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vont élargir la route l’année prochaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to widen the road next year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The electoral campaign starts tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an electronic dictionary.

definitions.note: Often used to describe numbers, prices, or levels that are high.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was eliminated in the semi-final.

definitions.native: moves away, takes away, keeps away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il éloigne la chaise du mur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moves the chair away from the wall.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: éloigner quelque chose/quelqu’un (to move something/someone away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu éloigner la chaise de la porte ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you move the chair away from the door?

definitions.note: Often used with de: éloigner quelqu’un de quelque chose (to keep someone away from something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils essaient d’éloigner les enfants de la route.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are trying to keep the children away from the road.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or multiple people to move/keep something away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Éloignez-vous de la porte, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move away from the door, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’hôtel est un peu éloigné du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is a little far from the city center.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa maison est très éloignée du centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her house is very far from the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils vivent dans des villages éloignés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in faraway villages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son discours était très éloquent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His speech was very eloquent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été élu maire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was elected mayor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le maire élu prendra ses fonctions demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elected mayor will take office tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for explaining something confusing or solving a mystery/problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La police essaie d’élucider l’affaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are trying to clear up the case.

definitions.note: Verb form of « élever » (e.g., he/she raises). Not to be confused with the noun « un/une élève » meaning “student.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle élève ses enfants avec patience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She raises her children with patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet élève est très sérieux en classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This student is very serious in class.

definitions.note: Plural form of « élève ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves écoutent la professeure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students listen to the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son élégance est remarquable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her elegance is remarkable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette robe est très élégante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is very elegant.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle porte une robe élégante pour la soirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing an elegant dress for the evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’eau est composée de deux éléments : l’hydrogène et l’oxygène.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is made up of two elements: hydrogen and oxygen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet élément manque dans le dossier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This part is missing from the file.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les éléments du rapport sont clairs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elements of the report are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'éléphant est un animal très grand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elephant is a very big animal.

definitions.note: Plural of « éléphant ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les éléphants vivent en groupe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elephants live in groups.

definitions.note: Used for a person or device that sends a signal/message (e.g., a radio transmitter or the sender of a payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’émetteur envoie un signal à la radio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transmitter sends a signal to the radio.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le match, une émeute a éclaté dans le centre-ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the match, a riot broke out in the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a émigré au Canada en 2010.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He emigrated to Canada in 2010.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a acquis une grande éminence dans son domaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gained great eminence in his field.

definitions.note: Past participle of « émettre », often used with « être » in the passive (e.g., « a été émis » = “was issued”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un communiqué a été émis ce matin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A statement was issued this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’écoute une émission de radio tous les matins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listen to a radio show every morning.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like emissions of gases/pollution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette usine réduit ses émissions de CO₂.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This factory is reducing its CO₂ emissions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette chanson me donne beaucoup d’émotion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This song gives me a lot of emotion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a du mal à parler de ses émotions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a hard time talking about his emotions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une histoire émouvante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a moving story.

definitions.note: Often used to describe being emotionally affected by something (good or bad news, a story, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il était très ému en entendant la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was very moved when he heard the news.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of « ému » (emotionally affected).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle était émue par ce discours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was moved by that speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’ai plus d’énergie aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any energy left today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une prof énergique.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s an energetic teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bruit m’énerve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise annoys me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bruit va vraiment énerver mon voisin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is really going to annoy my neighbor.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective with "être" (e.g., "Je suis énervé"). It can be a false friend: it does not usually mean "enervated" in the English sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis énervé parce que le bus est encore en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm annoyed because the bus is late again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis énervé par ce bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by that noise.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis énervée parce que le bus est encore en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed because the bus is late again.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils sont énervés parce qu’il y a beaucoup de bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are annoyed because there is a lot of noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette énigme est difficile à résoudre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This riddle is hard to solve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces énigmes sont difficiles, mais amusantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These riddles are difficult, but fun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce gâteau est énorme !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is huge!

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont acheté des légumes énormes au marché.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought huge vegetables at the market.

definitions.native: a lot, a great deal, enormously
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merci énormément pour ton aide !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you so much for your help!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre est très épais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very thick.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « épais ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette soupe est épaisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This soup is thick.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces couvertures sont très épaisses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These blankets are very thick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle épargne pour acheter une voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She saves to buy a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’épargne pour acheter une voiture, mais j’essaie aussi d’épargner chaque mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saving to buy a car, but I also try to save each month.

definitions.note: Form used with “vous” (e.g., commands or polite plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Épargnez un peu d’argent chaque mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save a little money each month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai épargné 50 euros ce mois-ci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved 50 euros this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le village a été épargné par la tempête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village was spared by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces soldats ? Je les ai épargnés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those soldiers? I spared them.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les jouets sont éparpillés dans toute la chambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The toys are scattered all over the room.

definitions.note: Informal and expressive; often used to show enthusiasm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est un film épatant !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an amazing movie!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal à l’épaule droite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right shoulder hurts.

definitions.note: Plural form of « épaule ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mal aux épaules après le sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoulders hurt after sports.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peux-tu épeler ton nom, s'il te plaît ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you spell your name, please?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous): used for "you" (plural) or formal "you".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Épelez votre nom, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spell your name, please.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu épelles ton nom ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you spell your name?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais à l’épicerie pour acheter du lait.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the grocery store to buy milk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce curry est très épicé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This curry is very spicy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette soupe est très épicée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This soup is very spicy.

definitions.note: Plural form; in French it’s commonly used in the plural when talking about the food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je n’aime pas les épinards.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like spinach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai une épine dans le doigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a thorn in my finger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attention, cette plante a des épines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, this plant has thorns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai besoin d’une épingle pour accrocher ce papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a pin to hang up this paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai regardé un épisode de cette série hier soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched an episode of that series last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il épluche une pomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peels an apple.

definitions.note: Often used for peeling fruits/vegetables (and sometimes for shelling things like shrimp).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu peux éplucher les pommes ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you peel the apples?

definitions.note: Command form (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Épluchez les pommes de terre, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Peel the potatoes, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai épluché les pommes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I peeled the apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À cette époque, je vivais à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that time, I was living in Paris.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), used mostly in writing (e.g., novels, history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En 1920, elle épousa un médecin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1920, she married a doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon épouse travaille à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wife works in Paris.

definitions.note: Verb form of « épouser » (to marry). Not to be confused with the noun « une épouse » meaning “wife.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il épouse sa meilleure amie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He marries his best friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veut épouser Marie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to marry Marie.

definitions.note: Plural of « épouse » (wife).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces femmes sont les épouses de mes amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These women are my friends’ wives.

definitions.note: This form is used with "vous" (plural or formal "you"); it can be either present tense ("you marry") or an imperative ("marry!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous épousez Claire ce samedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re marrying Claire this Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a épousé Paul en 2020.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She married Paul in 2020.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce film est vraiment épouvantable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is really terrible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans le champ, il y a un épouvantail pour éloigner les oiseaux.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the field, there is a scarecrow to keep the birds away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon époux travaille à Lyon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My husband works in Lyon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’épreuve de maths est demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The math test is tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les élèves passent des épreuves de mathématiques demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are taking math tests tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used with "de" (épris de + noun/pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est épris d’elle depuis des mois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been in love with her for months.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual feeling/experience in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle éprouvait de la joie en le voyant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt joy when she saw him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle éprouve de la joie quand elle voit ses amis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels joy when she sees her friends.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu éprouves de la joie quand tu joues avec ton chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You feel joy when you play with your dog.

definitions.note: Usually used for feelings, emotions, or sensations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous éprouvez de la joie en apprenant la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You feel joy when you learn the news.

definitions.note: Often used with avoir to mean “felt/experienced” (not “approved,” which is approuvé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai éprouvé une grande joie en apprenant la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great joy when I heard the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce travail est vraiment épuisant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job is really exhausting.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette journée est vraiment épuisante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This day is really exhausting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le travail, je suis épuisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I’m exhausted.

definitions.note: Often used for stock, supplies, or tickets.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Désolé, le stock est épuisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, the stock is sold out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le voyage, je suis épuisé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, I am exhausted.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le travail, elle est épuisée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, she is exhausted.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, they were exhausted.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après le voyage, ils sont épuisés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, they are exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le chevalier tient une épée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knight is holding a sword.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les chevaliers brandissent leurs épées.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knights brandish their swords.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut trouver un équilibre entre le travail et la vie personnelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to find a balance between work and personal life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je cherche une alimentation équilibrée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a balanced diet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’équipage du bateau est prêt à partir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship’s crew is ready to leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre équipe travaille sur ce projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team is working on this project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons tout l’équipement pour faire du camping.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have all the equipment for camping.

definitions.note: Plural form of « équipe ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les équipes sont prêtes pour le match.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teams are ready for the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon équipier m’aide à porter les sacs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teammate helps me carry the bags.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous cherchons une solution équitable pour tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are looking for a fair solution for everyone.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “in a fair/just way,” especially when sharing or distributing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous devons répartir les ressources équitablement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must distribute the resources fairly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a eu une érection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had an erection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’éruption du volcan a recouvert la ville de cendres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volcano’s eruption covered the city in ash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le plan a été établi hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan was established yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils veulent établir une nouvelle entreprise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to set up a new company.

definitions.note: Most commonly the present tense form meaning “you establish” (tu), and it can also be used as an imperative (“establish!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu établis un plan pour demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You set up a plan for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle used as an adjective (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les principes sont établis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principles are established.

definitions.note: Often used for a business or institution (like a school, hotel, or restaurant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cet établissement est très populaire dans le quartier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This establishment is very popular in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Refers to a level of a building (not the ground surface).
