definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the third floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bâtiment a cinq étages.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building has five floors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai mis les livres sur l’étagère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the books on the shelf.

definitions.note: Plural of « étagère ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai rangé les livres sur les étagères.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the books away on the shelves.

definitions.note: Past tense (imperfect) form of the auxiliary verb « être ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils étaient déjà partis quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had already left when I arrived.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle (usually with "je" or "tu") to form the pluperfect (plus-que-parfait).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’étais déjà parti quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already left when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « être » used with « je » or « tu » (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais enfant, j’étais souvent malade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I was often sick.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary to form the pluperfect with verbs that take être
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle était déjà partie quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had already left when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of « être » (used for ongoing states/habits or background description in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j’étais petit, mon chien était très gentil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, my dog was very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette boîte est étanche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This container is watertight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a des canards dans l’étang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are ducks in the pond.

definitions.note: Present participle of « être », often used in more formal or written French (e.g. « étant donné » = “given”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Étant fatigué, il est rentré tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being tired, he went home early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La première étape, c’est de remplir ce formulaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first step is to fill out this form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons terminé les premières étapes du projet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finished the first steps of the project.

definitions.note: More specific than "américain"; it refers to the United States (USA).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est citoyen étasunien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a U.S. citizen.

definitions.note: French term that specifically means people from the United States (as opposed to all people from the Americas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les étasuniens sont arrivés hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Americans arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for the condition or situation something is in (e.g., "en bon état" = "in good condition").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maison est en bon état.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is in good condition.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or multiple people to turn something off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Éteignez la lumière, s'il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the light, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), mainly used in written French; often corresponds to “turned off/put out” in storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il éteignit la lumière avant de sortir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned off the light before going out.

definitions.native: turn off, switch off, put out (a fire)
definitions.note: Used for turning off devices/lights and for extinguishing flames.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: N'oublie pas d'éteindre la lumière en partant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to turn off the light when you leave.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) form; used for switching off devices or putting out a light/fire.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Éteins la lumière, s’il te plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the light, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of « éteindre ». Often used with objects like lights, alarms, devices.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai éteint la lumière.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned off the light.

definitions.note: Used for lights, fires, and other things that are no longer on or burning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lumière est éteinte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La télévision est éteinte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is off.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les lumières sont éteintes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are off.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple) form; common in literature and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il étendit la couverture sur le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spread the blanket out on the bed.

definitions.native: to spread out, to stretch out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va étendre la couverture sur le lit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to spread the blanket out on the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai étendu la nappe sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spread the tablecloth on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le réseau de transports est très étendu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transportation network is very extensive.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nappe est étendue sur la table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tablecloth is spread out on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils rêvent d’un amour éternel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They dream of an eternal love.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son amour est éternelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her love is eternal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je t’aimerai éternellement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will love you forever.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils ont promis une amitié éternels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They promised an eternal friendship.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai l’impression que ça dure une éternité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like it’s lasting an eternity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai éternué toute la matinée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sneezed all morning.

definitions.note: Common misspelling/variant typing of «êtes» (2nd person plural of «être»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous étes en avance aujourd’hui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are early today.

definitions.note: Used with «vous» for plural ‘you’ or polite singular ‘you’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comment étes-vous ce matin ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you this morning?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous étiez déjà prêts quand je suis arrivé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were already ready when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (vous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand vous étiez enfants, vous jouiez souvent dehors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were children, you often played outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Une étincelle a mis le feu au papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A spark set the paper on fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Des étincelles jaillissent du feu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sparks are flying from the fire.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary “être” in compound past tenses (e.g., plus-que-parfait) with certain verbs and with reflexive verbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous étions déjà partis quand tu as appelé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had already left when you called.

definitions.note: Often used for product labels, name tags, or labels on clothing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai arraché l’étiquette de mon pull.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tore off the label from my sweater.

definitions.note: Refers to rules of polite behavior, often in formal situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut respecter l’étiquette à cette cérémonie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to follow proper etiquette at this ceremony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai collé des étiquettes sur les boîtes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stuck labels on the boxes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette étoffe est douce et résistante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fabric is soft and durable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nuit, on voit beaucoup d’étoiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, you can see a lot of stars.

definitions.note: Plural of « étoile ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nuit, on voit beaucoup d’étoiles dans le ciel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, you can see many stars in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Étonnamment, il a accepté tout de suite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surprisingly, he agreed right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est vraiment étonnant !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really surprising!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une découverte étonnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a surprising discovery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce bruit m’étonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise surprises me.

definitions.note: Conditional present (il/elle/on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ça m’étonnerait qu’il arrive à l’heure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d be surprised if he arrived on time.

definitions.note: Often used with "être" (e.g., "être étonné de..." = to be surprised by/at...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis étonné de te voir ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m surprised to see you here.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est étonnée par la nouvelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is surprised by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il étouffe en mangeant trop vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He chokes when he eats too fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce tissu étouffe le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fabric muffles the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fumée a failli étouffer l’homme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke almost suffocated the man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je suis un peu étourdi aujourd’hui : j’ai oublié mes clés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m a bit absent-minded today: I forgot my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'est étrange, je n'ai reçu aucun message.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's strange; I didn't receive any message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Étrangement, il n’a pas répondu à mon message.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Strangely, he didn’t reply to my message.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something/someone from another country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un pays étranger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a foreign country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parle avec un étranger dans le train.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is talking with a stranger on the train.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils se sentent étrangers dans cette ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feel foreign in this city.

definitions.note: Plural form of « étranger ». It can mean people from another country (foreigners) or people you don't know (strangers), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dans cette ville, les étrangers sont bien accueillis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, foreigners are warmly welcomed.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces bruits sont étranges.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These noises are strange.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il a été étranglé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was strangled.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of « étranger ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est étrangère, mais elle parle très bien français.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is foreign, but she speaks French very well.

definitions.note: Feminine form (talking about a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est une étrangère.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a foreigner.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elles lisent des journaux étrangers et des revues étrangères.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They read foreign newspapers and foreign magazines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette rue est trop étroite pour les voitures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This street is too narrow for cars.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of « étroit »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette rue est très étroite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This street is very narrow.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of « étroit »
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les rues de ce village sont très étroites.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The streets in this village are very narrow.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les couloirs sont étroits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hallways are narrow.

definitions.note: Plural form of « étude »; often refers to school/university studies or study (as an activity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mes études commencent en septembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My studies start in September.

definitions.note: Simple past (passé simple), third-person singular; common in writing (stories, formal texts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il étudia toute la nuit pour l’examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He studied all night for the exam.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quand j'étais au lycée, il étudiait tous les soirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was in high school, he studied every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’étudiant pose une question au professeur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The student asks the teacher a question.

definitions.note: feminine form of "étudiant".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mon amie est étudiante à Paris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friend is a student in Paris.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les étudiantes sont dans la salle de classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) students are in the classroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les étudiants arrivent en classe à huit heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students arrive in class at eight o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle étudie le français tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies French every day.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense ("they").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils étudient le français après l’école.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They study French after school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais étudier le français tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to study French every day.

definitions.note: Present tense form of « étudier » used with « tu » (you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu étudies le français ce soir ?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you studying French tonight?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vous) present tense; also used as the formal singular “you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous étudiez le français tous les jours.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You study French every day.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") present-tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Étudions ensemble pour l’examen demain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s study together for the exam tomorrow.

definitions.note: past participle of « étudier »; often used with « avoir » in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai étudié toute la soirée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied all evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En été, il fait souvent chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, it’s often hot.

definitions.note: Past participle of « être »; used with « avoir » in compound tenses (e.g., « a été » = has been).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle a été très gentille avec moi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been very kind to me.

definitions.note: Past participle of « être »; used with auxiliaries to form compound tenses (e.g., « j’ai été » = “I have been”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai été très fatigué hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very tired yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ces étés sont de plus en plus chauds.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These summers are getting hotter and hotter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’évacuation du bâtiment a été ordonnée par la police.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evacuation of the building was ordered by the police.

definitions.native: to evacuate; to clear out/empty (a place)
definitions.note: Used for evacuating people from a place, or clearing out/emptying a room, building, area, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les pompiers ont dû évacuer l'immeuble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters had to evacuate the building.

definitions.note: Command form (vous): used to tell one person formally or several people to evacuate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Évacuez le bâtiment immédiatement !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Evacuate the building immediately!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Après l’accident, il a été évacué à l’hôpital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was evacuated to the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’évaluation de ce projet prendra deux semaines.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evaluation of this project will take two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le professeur va évaluer les devoirs ce soir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is going to evaluate the homework tonight.

definitions.note: Past participle of « évanouir »; also commonly used as an adjective (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est tombé et il s’est évanoui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell and fainted.

definitions.note: Used for a female subject (feminine singular past participle), often with the reflexive verb « s’évanouir ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s’est évanouie dans le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fainted in the subway.

definitions.note: Used for a feminine singular noun or subject (past participle), often with « s’évanouir » meaning “to fade away / vanish.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa voix s’est évanouie dans le bruit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her voice faded away in the noise.

definitions.note: Most commonly used reflexively: « s’évanouir » = to faint.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle va s’évanouir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to faint.

definitions.note: Often used transitively (waking someone else); for waking up yourself, French commonly uses « se réveiller ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essaie d’éveiller les enfants à sept heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to wake the children up at seven o’clock.

definitions.native: to arouse, to awaken (interest, curiosity, feelings)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ce livre va éveiller ma curiosité.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That book is going to awaken my curiosity.

definitions.note: Past participle of « éveiller »; used in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bruit a éveillé le bébé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise woke up the baby.

definitions.note: Often used for being awake (not asleep). In other contexts it can also mean alert/aware.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il est déjà éveillé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is already awake.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle est éveillée depuis six heures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enfants sont encore éveillés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are still awake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle s’évente avec un éventail parce qu’il fait très chaud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fans herself with a hand fan because it’s very hot.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts for a possible outcome or contingency.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il faut envisager toutes les éventualités.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to consider all possibilities.

definitions.note: Often means “possibly” or “if needed,” not “eventually.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: On pourra éventuellement changer de date si tu n’es pas disponible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can possibly change the date if you’re not available.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Évidemment, je ne vais pas oublier ton anniversaire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Obviously, I’m not going to forget your birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il n’y a aucune évidence pour soutenir cette théorie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no evidence to support this theory.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression « il est évident que… » (“it is obvious that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’évidence de sa réponse a surpris tout le monde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The obviousness of his answer surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est évident.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s obvious.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La réponse est évidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is obvious.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les avantages sont évidents.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advantages are obvious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il évite les embouteillages en prenant le métro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He avoids traffic jams by taking the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ils évitent le centre-ville en voiture.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They avoid downtown by car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’essaie d’éviter le sucre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to avoid sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elle évitera les embouteillages en partant plus tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will avoid traffic jams by leaving earlier.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu évites les embouteillages en partant tôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You avoid traffic jams by leaving early.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (to one person formally or to more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Évitez de parler trop fort, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please avoid speaking too loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai évité la question.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I avoided the question.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of « éviter »; used with « être » or to agree with a direct object placed before the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette erreur a été évitée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This mistake was avoided.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situation évolue rapidement.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is evolving quickly.

definitions.note: present tense (3rd person plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les technologies évoluent très vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Technologies evolve very quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for gradual change or progress over time (in ideas, situations, people, organizations, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notre projet doit évoluer avec les besoins des clients.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our project has to evolve with the customers' needs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’évolution de la technologie est très rapide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evolution of technology is very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situation a beaucoup évolué depuis hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation has evolved a lot since yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette photo évoque de beaux souvenirs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This photo evokes beautiful memories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il évoque le problème pendant la réunion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mentions the problem during the meeting.

definitions.note: Plural of « événement ». Spelling variant of « événements » (both are accepted in French).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a plusieurs évènements cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several events this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’est un événement important pour notre ville.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important event for our town.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il y a plusieurs événements cette semaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several events this week.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense of « être »; used with « vous » (formal singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vous êtes en retard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are late.

definitions.note: used with some verbs, and with reflexive verbs, to form past tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il doit être arrivé maintenant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He must have arrived by now.

definitions.note: used before a past participle to form the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dîner va être servi bientôt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dinner is going to be served soon.

definitions.note: Used as a noun to mean a living being or a person/creature, often in phrases like « un être humain ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chaque être humain mérite le respect.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every human being deserves respect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je veux être honnête.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to be honest.

definitions.note: Plural of « être » as a noun (often used in phrases like « êtres humains » = human beings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les êtres humains ont besoin de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Human beings need to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous passons nos vacances sur une île.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spend our vacation on an island.

definitions.note: Plural of « île ».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous visitons trois îles pendant les vacances.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are visiting three islands during the vacation.

definitions.note: Literary/poetic interjection, often used to address someone/something or to express emotion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ô mon ami, écoute-moi !
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh my friend, listen to me!

definitions.note: Literary/simple past (passé simple) form meaning “(he/she/it) took off/removed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ôta son chapeau en entrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took off his hat as he came in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ôte mon manteau en entrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off my coat when I come in.

definitions.note: Often used for removing something from a place or taking something off (like clothing), similar to “enlever.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je vais ôter mon manteau, il fait chaud ici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take off my coat; it’s warm in here.

definitions.note: Command form (vous) of « ôter »: used to tell one person politely, or several people, to remove something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ôtez vos chaussures, s’il vous plaît.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take off your shoes.

definitions.note: Past participle of « ôter »; often used with « avoir » (e.g., « a ôté »).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J'ai ôté mon manteau en entrant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took off my coat when I came in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: J’ai quelque chose dans l’œil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something in my eye.

definitions.note: Plural of « œuf » (egg).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je prends deux œufs au petit-déjeuner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two eggs for breakfast.

definitions.note: Often used for an artist’s/author’s work (a painting, a book, a piece of music, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cette œuvre est célèbre dans le monde entier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This work is famous all over the world.

definitions.note: Plural of « œuvre »; often used for works of art or an artist’s complete works.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nous avons vu plusieurs œuvres au musée.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw several works at the museum.
